The FAITH Process for Website v1a
KF Introductory Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF0-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Introductory Meeting  KF0 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain,   and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  When we use the term   orientation   in Karis Fellowships, we are talking about realigning with our Creator and living within the realities of our created design. If you are in this group, you have probably been able to admit to yourself that you have deviated from the Creator and from your created design through neurosis. Sometimes the word   neurosis   is a little confusing for our generation, so in KF we use the term  misorientation   instead. Misorientation is a kind of rebellion against our Creator and our design. We have misoriented away from our true purpose and calling by trying to save the life of our idealized self. Our goal is to reorient back to God as His creatures, to learn what is pleasing to Him, and to fulfill our created purpose in this material world, which is to be in relationship with Him.  0:03   PRESENTING  In Karis Fellowships, we encourage anonymity. There is no need to share your last name, and you can even make up a name to maintain your privacy. Only you know   your privacy needs,   and we want to protect them as much as we wish to protect our own. Similarly, we protect those close to us by referring to them as   another KF member ,   someone I love , or   someone who is close to me.   Referring to others in this way  helps protect everyone’s privacy , and it avoids the appearance of inside knowledge or cliques. It also reminds us that in the group we each tell our own story and not the story of another. Our story is ours and ours alone.  0:09   KARIS CIRCULATION  Karis Fellowships is an organization run completely by volunteers, but our website and the other services that we use require financial support. If you receive gifts of training from Karis Fellowships that enhance your well-being and your connection to God, return regular financial gifts to the Fellowships. By doing so, you invite more well-being and connection into your life. Your gifts say,   “Thank you.”   In KF, we refer to this principle as   circulation . It is the essence of kari s .  0:11   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  Since we are committed to adhering to time restraints, we will always begin our meetings on time and end on time, or before. If, however, from time to time, you need to join the group late, please call in anyway. Although the call-in prompt asks you to immediately announce your presence, wait until the facilitator acknowledges you. If the facilitator forgets, go ahead and announce yourself when there is a pause in the meeting. If you should join the meeting and find   yourself in the middle of silence,   it is probably because the group is in mindfulness training. Just be patient and wait a minute for someone to start

2  karisfellowships.com   KF0-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  speaking again. You will know that the group is meeting because the call-in prompt will tell you how many people are gathered on the call.  0:13   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Karis Fellowships is more than an education. Over the years, we have seen that regular attendance will actually start to orient members and set them on a path toward real glory. One of our tools for orientation is the practice of mindfulness and Christian meditation. Although the words   meditation   and   mindfulness  are often used interchangeably, the practice of each has a distinct purpose. In KF, mindfulness training simply means that we train our minds and bodies to notice, without judgment, what is happening inside and around us in the moment. We define   meditation as training ourselves to quiet our minds and connect with God beyond words or images. We learn to dwell alone with Him in silence and stillness. Christians have been meditating for centuries, but we have largely lost the tradition of meditation in the Protestant church.  Mindfulness and meditation are difficult for everyone.   That’s   why they are called spiritual disciplines. Disciples are learners, and a discipline is something that you have to learn. It takes time to learn any new skill, and Karis Fellowships supports you in the process of learning. Think of your mind as a new puppy learning to sit still on command. Everything distracts the puppy at first; a puppy can only focus on a command for a few seconds. The trainer knows that. He does n’t   punish the puppy for not doing what it is not yet trained to do. Instead, he rewards the puppy   for what it tries to do. Pat yourself on the head every time you make an effort to practice these new skills. Your lasting reward will be added control over your mind and emotions, which will lead to more peace, strength, and stability in your life.  You can find the mindfulness and meditation scripts from these meetings on the KF website.  Let’s begin learning the   3-Minute Breathing Space . 1   Follow these basic instructions as I guide you.  We start with   AWARENESS .  Bring yourself into the present moment by adopting an appropriate posture. Sit upright, if you can, and straighten your neck. Lower your chin a little, and let your shoulders fall back naturally. Think of the crown of your head reaching toward the heavens and your tailbone reaching toward the earth. Plant the entire sole of each foot on the ground or sit cross-legged on the floor. If possible, close your eyes.   (Pause)   Now ask yourself:   What is my experience right now — in thoughts, in feelings, and in my physical sensations?  (Repeat)   (Pause)   Get to know yourself   a little. As you breathe, acknowledge   and register your experience, even if it is unwanted or uncomfortable. Notice the thoughts within your mind, your feelings, and what your body is sensing. Breathe, and simply observe for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Move to   GATHERING .  Gently direct your full attention to your breathing — to each in-breath and each out-breath as they follow one after the other. Your breath can function as an anchor to bring you into the present moment, to help you focus your awareness, and to guide you into stillness. Observe your breathing for thirty seconds.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  And now we will move to   EXPANDING .  Expand the field of your awareness around your breathing so that you sense your body as a whole. Notice how your body moves with the breathing. Notice your posture. What is your face doing? Ob serve and breathe for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

3  karisfellowships.com   KF0-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Pause, and gently redirect your mind back to the meeting.  The   3-Minute Breathing Space   provides a way to step out of the habitual reactions of automatic pilot mode. When events occur, a breathing space can help you thoughtfully reconnect with yourself and with God. Maintaining awareness in the moment, without making judgments, is the key skill to learn through this practice.  Begin your own daily practice this week, spending one minute on each of the three steps. Try following the instructions for the   3-Minute Breathing Space   in the morning and then again later in the day. This will help you learn to be aware of what you are experiencing in the present moment — right here, right now. You can practice this mindfulness exercise using the teaching notes to guide you, or you can download the instructions under the   Toolbox   menu on the KF   website. Alternatively, you can call this meeting’s  playback number and follow along with the group again.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:22   KARIS CONFESSION  At each meeting, we listen to the KF Confessions to remind ourselves of what we learned in the   Neurosis  and Human Growth   book study and, also, to take us beyond the study into the promise and vision that God has for each of us. There are twelve Confessions because there are twelve months. Each month we look in detail at one of the Karis Confessions.  0:24   TOOLBOX  This week we will explore how Karis Fellowships works . Let’s begin with how   the meetings are structured.  Each meeting is divided into the same sequence   of introductions and training. Bring a copy of the   Meeting Schedule   with you to the meeting so that you can help by reading one of the introductions. During the  Toolbox   segment of the meeting, we explore integration techniques, worksheets, and practical training exercises that help us process our anxieties, conflicts, and self-hate in very practical ways. We learn to interrupt the autopilot of our neurotic solution, which drives our chronic reactions, and we train ourselves to use that same energy to make healthy choices, building the glorious life God intends for each of us.  L et’s   now look at five points that describe our work in Karis Fellowships.  1.   The   real self   is the   True Self  In the book study, we learned that our present solution for anxiety and conflicts is neurotic, or misoriented. In Karis Fellowships, we believe that the   real self   that Dr. Horney talks about is the   True Self,   which God created. 2   We use the term True Self because this self is congruent with the truth. We know that God is true and that Jesus is the Way, the Truth, and the Life. 3   As we follow the way of Jesus, we grow into our True Self, and we become the truth of who He created us to be. We learn to build a life that declares the glory of God.  2.   The   idealized self   is the   Idol Self  In the Fellowships, we call the   idealized self   the   Idol — I-D-O-L — or   Idol   Self . Someday you might want to go through the Bible looking at the characteristics of idols, graven images, and false gods. You may

4  karisfellowships.com   KF0-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  find it striking, as Nancy did, to see the similarity between the characteristics of the idealized self and an idol. To dismantle this Idol, we must commit to the goal of learning real love.  3.   Karis Fellowships is a training program  During the year of training, you will be introduced to many tools that will help restore your True Self. The training will feel overwhelming. Depending on your neurotic development, you will want to master it all immediately, feel chronic self-judgment, or feel rebellious and do as little as possible. Remember that you are like a puppy and can only learn at your own pace. You learn by taking small puppy steps toward developing endurance and self-management, which prepares you to take up more training in the future. You   can’t   learn it all or know it all at once, and   that’s   why many KF members continue to train with KF for several years.  4.   Showing up  Members of Karis Fellowships have reported that just showing up for the meetings each week has changed their lives. We would encourage you to use whichever KF tools you can during the week, but if you are an overly busy puppy or a puppy that feels frozen and overwhelmed, your first step will be to simply attend the meetings. If you miss a meeting, you can join other meetings during the week or listen to your regular meeting through the playback number provided on the KF website. Scripts and contact numbers for other meetings are also provided on the website.  5.   Take your work seriously  It is God’s desire   that you learn to love. As you learn to love,   God’s love   is able to flow through you to your family, to your community, and to this messed-up world. You can learn to stop being part of the mess. By restoring your True Self, you allow   God’s   will of love to be done through you, on earth as it is in heaven. 4  Our prayer might go something like this:  God, my Father and Creator, I choose to begin this journey of love with You. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  Before we start the sharing segment of the meeting, you might wish to have some purified drinking water available. Water helps our bodies process our experience during the meetings.  Let’s   talk about the   Meeting Preparation Guide   for a moment. Some members have a ring binder in which they store completed and blank preparation guides, KF documents, and worksheets. With a completed preparation guide, you are ready to efficiently offer your story in the meeting, and you also have a record of your own restoration. Alternatively, you can download the guides and keep a record of your recovery and progress on your computer. The DOC version will allow you to modify your document.  In the   Meeting Preparation Guide,   we use the terms   oriented   and   misoriented . To keep things simple, Nancy has reduced lots of Greek words down to those two basic concepts. Essentially, these Greek words express the idea of living in harmony and correspondence with God and His Creation, or not. When we are oriented,   we make choices that are in harmony with God’s desires and promises. Orientation is the

5  karisfellowships.com   KF0-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  work of the True Self. Oriented people are supported by God and connected to His resources, and they consistently produce the Fruit of the Spirit. 5   By living their lives   God’s way , they contribute to the Creation and to the community. The Greek words that Nancy has summarized as   orientation   are often translated in our Bibles as   righteousness ,   justice ,   love ,   faith ,   walking by the Spirit , and   goodness .  When we are misoriented, we are out of harmony with God, ourselves, and the Creation, and we actively create harm, often without realizing it. Misorientation through pride is the work of the Idol Self, and God will always oppose our pride. As a result, we sense deep down that we   are neither supported by God nor connected to His resources. When we lack this support and connection, we cannot consistently produce the Fruit of the Spirit in our lives — we are neurotic. The Greek   words that Nancy has bundled   into the term  misorientation   are translated in our Bibles as   sin ,   transgression ,   unrighteousness ,   the flesh ,   disobedience , etc. Basically, these words mean missing the mark, wandering from the path, stumbling, error or delusion, and failure.  The other items in the   Meeting Preparation Guide   are self-explanatory. However, thankfulness, which is at the end of the guide, is very important in the process of reorientation and is well worth highlighting here. We will see in the KF Romans study that misoriented people do not honor God, nor do they give thanks. Gratitude reminds us that we are not God. It also helps us be aware of how God is supporting us, even when our feelings are telling us a tale of woe. Gratitude is physically and spiritually beneficial. Learning to be thankful in all things is part of the reorientation process.  If you are new to the group, feel free just to listen during the sharing time. When you are ready, it is to your advantage, and it also benefits the group, if you give the gift of sharing your experience while you train. If you wish to share, we encourage you to set a timer to remind you of the 5-minute time limitation. This is simply an opportunity to share your own work. We do not give counsel; neither do we ask for advice. When a member has finished sharing, we simply say   “Thank you”   to acknowledge his or her contribution.  Let’s begin our sharing.  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  We encourage you to read your Bible throughout the week and look for examples of   what you are learning in KF. If you have your Bible with you now, turn to the Gospel of John, chapter 17. The whole of this chapter is our text for the introductory lesson. Here, Jesus is praying for His followers. His prayer is an astounding revelation of the true glory that He has in mind for us. Before we look at the nature of this true glory,   let’s review what we learned in the book study about   our self-manufactured glory.  We learned that we have a neurotic need to search for personal glory. Our backgrounds, our conflicts about other people, our deep anxiety, our natural strengths and weaknesses, and our need for self- confidence all pressed us into seeking an imagined safe place. We then tried to make that safe place our identity — we created an Idol Self. That Idol Self can never feel safe because   it is false. It is a house built on sand, but it gives us an illusion of glory. 6   The Idol uses our powerful imagination to validate this false glory by exaggerating evidence that perpetuates our illusions and by dismissing any evidence that might call us back to reality. Chronic insecurity regarding our real attributes presses us beyond what is rational into an imagined identity characterized by superior attributes and abilities.

6  karisfellowships.com   KF0-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  In our Bible passage, however, we discover that we are designed by God to grow into the true glory that He intended for us. Consequently, deep within, we are seeking the natural fulfillment of our original design. We were created to be glorious, and through revealing   our glory as God’s creatures , we declare  God’s   glory in our own unique way. This brings us to the big question: What is glory?  In John 17, Jesus prays to His Father about Himself and about us, His followers.   Let’s consider   some of the aspects of Biblical glory that this intimate prayer reveals.  1.   Glory is of primary importance  Jesus talks to the Father about glory right from the start. He wants His Father to glorify Him so that He can glorify His Father. The ultimate purpose of our true glory is to enhance   God’s reputation.  2.   Glory has to do with giving  In verses 2 and 4, we see between the Father and the Son a dynamic relationship of giving, which overflows to us in the gift of eternal life. J esus tells the Father, “I have brought glory to   You, Father, by fulfilling the work that Y ou gave me to do.” 7   The Father gave Jesus authority and, also, a glorious mission, and by fulfilling that mission, Jesus returned a gift that glorified His Father. This almost incomprehensible generosity between   the Father and the Son is a demonstration of glory , and we are invited to participate in this glorious relationship of mutual giving that overflows into the lives of others.  3.   Glory is revealed through joyful lives  Jesus prays that His disciples will be filled with His joy. His joy in us is an expression of His glory.  4.   Glory is doing things God’s way  In verse 14 we learn that, along with His glory, Jesus has given   God’s word to His followers . This is the  logos.   We can translate this Greek word as   God’s way of doing things . Jesus is our only example of a human being who has accomplished the mission God designed for him while remaining fully integrated with his True Self. Jesus gave us the great gift of showing us how to fulfill our own glory by  doing things God’s way.   The natural result of our glory is that others can learn something about God by watching us.  5.   Glory offers the potential for unity  With regard to our KF work, the particular aspect of this glory that Nancy would like you to notice is in verse 22. Jesus affirms , “I   have given to them the very same glory that You gave to Me so that they may be one just as We are one. ”   God gave Jesus glory, and Jesus has passed that same glory on to us. He has done this for the sake of unity, not primarily with each other but with Him and within ourselves. In Jesus, we are no longer a kingdom divided against itself, fighting to suppress the True Self and actualize the Idol Self; we are no longer at war with ourselves and at war with God. 8   Now, because of the work of Jesus Christ, we can stand unified. It is only in being unified, just as He is, that we can act with consistent power, love, and confidence in this world.  Consider revisiting this chapter and see if you can make more connections between giving, glory, unity, and love.  We might pray this very bold prayer together:  Lord Jesus, glorify me so that I might glorify You. (Repeat)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF0-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Bring some purified water to the meetings. Water helps your body process what it is experiencing. You may also wish to take some notes on the back of your   Meeting Preparation Guide , or you might start a KF journal. Assume an alert and upright posture, whatever works for you, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  The FAITH Process  We always end our meetings with the   FAITH Process . F-A-I-T-H is an acronym for Feelings, Awareness, Inquiry, Talk to Jesus, and Heal.  Here is our integration focus:   Consider God’s generous gifts.   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  F is for Feelings  As you   consider   God’s generous gifts ,   how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  A is for Awareness without judgment  As you breathe and   consider   God’s generous gifts,   allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush our feelings and thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us.   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  I is for Inquiry:   What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what is it doing when you   consider   God’s   generous  gifts .   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. Perhaps you will find unfairness or resentment in your body; perhaps hope or joy. Just explore.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  T is for Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  God’s generous gifts . Do you feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe.  (Pause)   When you consider   God’s   gifts, what story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something? Do you hope for something? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath, like a sigh.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  H is for Heal  For thousands of years, human beings have had very strong feelings when they   have   considered God’s  generous gifts . You also are a human creature, and you are not alone in your feelings.   (Pause)   You can

8  karisfellowships.com   KF0-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  breathe rather than reacting and getting caught up in explanations. Breathe with compassion for our human condition, and help your body release with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. Take a deep breath .  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank you for this time together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our glory and to the truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  If you have completed the prerequisites for joining KF and wish to begin training in the next cycle, please register on the website under the Registration tab or email   admin@karisfellowships.com   for assistance. If your registration is approved, the admin team will allow you access to the KF website where you will find the meeting days and times, call-in numbers, and various guides and worksheets. We would like to remind everyone that Karis Fellowships is a gift offered by volunteers and that no one is under any obligation.  1   Zindel Segal, J. Mark G. Williams and John D Teasdale,   Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy for Depression   (New York: Guilford Press, 2013), 208. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  2   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).  3   John 14:6.  4   Matt. 6:10.  5   Gal. 5:22 – 23.  6   Matt. 7:24 – 27.  7   John 17:4.  8   Matt. 12:25.

title: KF1 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF1-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF1 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me   in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Karis Fellowships is more than an education. We anticipate that regular attendance at the weekly KF meetings will actually change you and set you on a glorious path, the path that God intended for you. At these meetings, you will learn to use tools that will help you in your daily life. One of these tools is the practice of mindfulness and Christian meditation. In Karis Fellowships, mindfulness means that we train our minds to be aware of what is happening inside and around us. In meditation, we train ourselves to rest in stillness and connect with God. It is a kind of waiting before the Lord. Although, to a great extent, we have lost the traditions of mindfulness and meditation in the modern church, Christians have used these practices for centuries to help them walk with God.  Mindfulness and meditation are difficult for everyone.   That’s   why they are called spiritual disciplines. Disciples are learners, and a discipline is something that you have to learn. Learning any new skill takes time, patience, and practice. Karis Fellowships supports you in the process of learning. Think of your mind as a young puppy learning to sit still on command.  We begin with the   3-Minute Breathing Space . 1   This mindfulness exercise teaches us important skills. First, we learn to give our physical bodies permission to talk to us; second, we learn to notice our breathing; and third, we learn that mindful breathing helps us experience ourselves as unified material and spiritual creatures. The   3-Minute Breathing Space   trains us to connect to our breathing when we are under stress and, also, to disconnect from our compulsive judgments, reactions, and stories. We can simply breathe and observe.  Follow these basic instructions as I guide you. When you notice that your mind is drifting, as it certainly will, gently recall your thoughts by observing your breath.  We start with   AWARENESS .  Prepare your body for mindfulness practice. Sit up straight, if you can. Imagine the crown of your head reaching toward the heavens and your tailbone reaching toward the earth. Lengthen your spine by straightening the back of your neck and drop your chin a little. Plant your feet on the ground or, if you are sitting on the floor, plant your tailbone into the earth. If possible, close your eyes. Then ask yourself:   What

2  karisfellowships.com   KF1-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  is my experience right now — in thoughts, in feelings, and i n my body’s sensations?   (Repeat)   Get to know yourself as you are right now. Observe for thirty seconds, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Move to   GATHERING .  Notice your breathing, just as it is. Notice each in-breath and each out-breath as they follow one after the other. Use your breath as an anchor to bring you into the present moment and to help you find a place of stillness and unbiased awareness. Observe your breathing without judgment and release any thoughts of right or wrong. Breathe and observe for another thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now move to   EXPANDING .  Expand your awareness to include a sense of yourself as a composite whole of mind, emotions, and physical sensations, including the part of you that is observing all of those things.   (Pause)   Notice how your body moves with each breath.   (Pause)   Notice your posture and what your face is doing.   (Pause)   Observe and breathe for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now pause, and redirect your mind back to the meeting. It takes a long time to learn how to make the most of the   3-Minute Breathing Space , and most of us are still learning .   Be kind to yourself as you train and learn.  We practice mindfulness to maintain our awareness of who we are and what we are experiencing in the present moment, no matter what is going on around us.   If you haven’t already   done so, begin your own daily practice this week, spending one minute on each of the three steps. Try to set aside time in the morning and then again later in the day. It might help to attach this practice to a habit that is already in place. You can practice the   3-Minute Breathing Space   using these teaching notes to guide you, or you can download the instructions under the   Toolbox   menu on the KF website. Alternatively, you can call this  meeting’s playback number and follow along with the group again.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  We hope that you will review the notes from the   KF Introductory Meeting . You can also read the  Expanded   Version   of the introductory lesson to get a more detailed explanation of what we do in KF. Bold print in the body of the text indicates documents, information, and KF tools that are available on the website.  At this point, you might ask yourself the question:   How do I know when I am misoriented?  In the   KF Introductory Meeting , you learned that in Karis Fellowships we use the term   misorientation  when referring to our neurotic behaviors and compulsive drives. We often cannot spot the signs that indicate misorientation because our misoriented behaviors and reactions seem so normal to us. When you are misoriented, you are no longer oriented toward God and His design but have oriented toward the demands and pride of the Idol Self. Your habitual ways of thinking, feeling, and reacting have become an autopilot system that short-circuits your ability to make conscious choices and, also, your ability to consider the consequences of the choices you make; you   don’t   even notice what you are actually doing.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF1-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  You automatically defend your reactions as justified and rational, and any evidence to the contrary is immediately flushed from your awareness because it   doesn’t   fit your ideas of right and wrong, good and bad, fair and unfair. When you are misoriented, you become hardened and must engage with life through a closed system that can only filter and evaluate what it already believes and knows.  Judging creates tension and anxiety, and tension and anxiety trigger self-protection. You cannot learn in that environment. In mindfulness training, however, you learn to observe without judgment, which allows real evidence to penetrate your conscious mind. When you stop judging information as good or bad, right or wrong, fair or unfair, you can relax, observe, and learn. Your goal is to stop evaluating and simply observe what is true about yourself in this moment. How misoriented are you?  Your first step toward recognizing misorientation is to notice yourself. You observe what you are doing right now within your own mind and body, and in your choices. With mindful observation, you explore and compare your reactions in similar situations and look for patterns. As you continue in your training, you might also look for signs of positive change. Step by step, you will learn to identify healthy and unhealthy behaviors, feelings, and thoughts. For a moment, you lay aside the idea that others are the cause of your misorientation. You begin to accept that you yourself are the cause.  Feelings seem like a good place to start, but do you know that most of us   don’t   know what we are actually feeling? We have suppressed our real and, perhaps, unacceptable feelings to prevent them from coming to our awareness. When we were young, we suppressed our feelings to protect our True Self; we now suppress our feelings to protect our Idol Self.  Here are a few examples of the feelings offered by experienced KF members that could very well indicate misorientation:  •   Strain or tension  •   Lack of gratitude  •   Chronic discontent or envy  •   Contempt for oneself or for others  •   Suddenly falling in love or plunging into hate  •   Rage or despair  •   A sense of worthlessness  •   Helplessness  •   Defensiveness  •   A strong desire to control  •   A strong desire to rescue  •   A strong desire to escape  •   Irritability  •   Stagnation or fatigue  •   Hurt feelings  •   Fears, phobias, and panic  •   Craving, addictive behaviors  •   Euphoria  •   Numbness or no feelings  •   Paralyzing doubt

4  karisfellowships.com   KF1-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Behaviors can also indicate that something is amiss. Here are a few red flags to consider:  •   Blaming others for how we feel  •   Judging or evaluating with strong feelings  •   Obsessing or nagging  •   Irrational resistance  •   Disregard for balance and limitations, like overspending or overcommitting  •   Choosing instant gratification  •   Avoiding change, exploration, or personal development  •   Using force or going into battle mode  •   Abrupt efforts to extricate ourselves  •   Creating drama or soap opera scenarios  •   Victimizing ourselves or others  •   Reacting in old unproductive patterns  •   Sacrificing ourselves or others to avoid conflict, to please, or to win  •   Creating suffering  •   Refusing to take responsibility  •   Taking too much responsibility for everything  •   Carelessness or recklessness  •   Procrastination  •   Restlessness, like compulsive activity or compulsive talking  These are just a few of the symptoms of misorientation, but this list is a good place to start! Bear in mind that misorientation is always egocentric, meaning that nothing and no one else matters except what you need or want. There is a kind of heedlessness, a disregard for other factors in your decisions and activities. Only your feelings or needs count. You might think:   “I’ve got to do this now to feel better. It’s all up to me. Only I know what is right. I have to change this because . . .”   Misorientation has the feeling of an impulsive, compelling priority, unplanned and without balance,   in which no one else’s opinion matters— not even God’s.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Compassionate Father, I present myself now, as I am, to become what You would have me be. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  This month we are considering KF Confession 1:  We confess that we have worshipped and served an Idol Self that we have created.  How did we turn from the real God who created us and create a god of our own? In the NHG book study, which we all endured together, we learned that our backgrounds, our conflicts about other people, our

5  karisfellowships.com   KF1-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  deep anxiety, and our need for self-confidence all pressed us into seeking an imagined safe place that could only be maintained and defended with certain behaviors. These behaviors seemed to give us some degree of relief from our anxiety, but they still did not provide the security and self-confidence that we dreamed of. We then believed that   more   would be better, so we took those behaviors to an extreme. We became convinced that if we could perform perfectly, we would have what we seek. That dream hardened into a chronic search for glory, an imagined place of perfect security and effortless superiority. We became completely egocentric in this search. We no longer took any real interest in other people, nor did we notice their struggles with the same problem.  The search for glory uses up a lot of energy. Our goal in Karis Fellowships is to redirect that creative and abundant energy toward our true glory. As we learned in the   KF Introductory Meeting , our true glory reveals our original design, and our original design reveals the glory of our Creator. Our glory is this:   to  fulfill our design as creatures who uniquely represent God’s character in this material world. (Repeat)  How does the Bible first describe our glory?   Let’s look at   Genesis 1:26 – 28 . This translation is from the  New American Standard Bible . 2  26 Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness; and let them  rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the sky and over the cattle and over all  the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”   27 God created man in His own image, in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.  28 God blessed them; and God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth,  and subdue it; and rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the sky and over every living thing that moves about   on the earth.”  Take a deep breath.  First, we see in this passage that all human bein gs are created in God’s image— men and women, boys and girls. Both sexes reveal the image of God. Human beings were designed to offer to this world the  likeness of God’s character, trustworthiness, and creative wealth. We   are not designed to mold ourselves into an image that we then worship and serve.  Next, we see in this passage that we have work to do. In the   KF Introductory Meeting , we learned that Jesus glorified God by finishing His work, and we glorify God by finishing ours. Our job is to rule over other creatures and subdue the material world. In other words, we are called to influence this world according  to God’s mercy and truth.   Note that we were not designed to rule over each other. That feels a little scary for the neurotic!  Finally, we are designed to be fruitful and multiply. Our ability to create other eternal souls is similar to  God’s creative   ability .   However, unlike God, we cannot do it alone; we need a partner. Sex differences reveal the nature of our relationship with God. Paul teaches that the communion between male and female in the marriage relationship represents and explores the communion that human creatures have with Christ. 3   This is so important. The unity of one sex with the other reflects our unity with a Divine Being quite different from ourselves but with similar characteristics. Just as we cannot generate children by ourselves, we cannot be saved or be complete by ourselves. We need to co-labor with God in our own restoration; we cannot do it alone. Only God knows what our glory will look like.  Our prayer might go something like this:

6  karisfellowships.com   KF1-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Lord of Glory, I am ready to explore my glory. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  A list of the Fruit of the Spirit is found in Galatians 5:22 – 23. Our goal in Karis Fellowships is to consistently experience and produce this Fruit in our lives, and to do that, we need healing. In the KF meetings, we heal personally and, also, as a group. During this portion of the meeting, we integrate what we have learned so that the Fruit of the Spirit can flow naturally out of our healing. This opportunity for healing and integration makes KF attendance your best friend right now. On the KF website, you can read about the vision that Karis Fellowships has for you as a child of God. We believe that you can become a powerful and creative instrument for good in this world.  Following the regular meeting integration, Nancy is sometimes able to share with the group something that she is aware of. This is not an arbitrary guess on her part, but a gift given by God to this community. Just allow the gift to work. You may feel a physical sensation, get very sleepy, or feel like you need to stretch or move. Simply let your experience be what it is. If you feel nothing, that is perfectly all right too.  We will begin with a mindfulness practice that helps us allow our feelings and passing thoughts to come to our awareness without judging or reacting to them. We learn to explore rather than suppress. Nancy calls this practice the   FAITH   Process . We learn to practice our faith while we feel our feelings.  F   is for Feelings  A   is for Awareness without judgment  I   is for Inquiry: What is my body saying?  T   is for Talk to Jesus  H   is for Heal  During this part of the meeting, you might like to take some notes. You could use the back of your   Meeting Preparation Guide , or you might want to start a KF journal. Now assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider fulfilling your created design .   (Repeat)   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider fulfilling your created design , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Graciously allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush thoughts or feelings from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us. Observe whatever tension you may be feeling

7  karisfellowships.com   KF1-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  as you   consider fulfilling your created design.   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing as you   consider fulfilling your created design.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what resistance, confusion, or even terror feels like in your body. Perhaps you feel joy or curiosity.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  fulfilling   your created design .   (Pause)   Are your thoughts pleasant, unpleasant, or vague and slippery? Just breathe and observe.   (Pause)   What do you believe when you consider your created design? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Do you feel compelled to judge your design as good or evil?   (Pause)   Observe whatever you are experiencing as just information. Breathe deeply, and allow your exhale to be long and relaxed.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created you to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you do when they have   considered   fulfilling their created design . You can read about that in the Psalms. You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   You can observe and learn something from what you have just experienced. When a fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up in explanations and reactions. Breathe with compassion for yourself and for the whole human race. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I check for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are so grateful for this time together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our glory and to the truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS

8  karisfellowships.com   KF1-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Karis Fellowships sends out regular emails during the week with portions of the   Expanded Version   of the KF teaching notes. We call this gift the   KF Compass . Please write to   admin@karisfellowships.com   if you would like to receive these emails.  1   Zindel Segal, J. Mark G. Williams, and John D. Teasdale,   Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy for Depression   (New York: Guilford Press, 2013), 208.
