title: KF2 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF2-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF2 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  We hope that during your training you will develop a daily or weekly routine that includes a review of the  week’s teaching and an exploration of the   Karis Fellowships tools. You can also further your training by reading the   Expanded Version   or by listening to the playback of this meeting.  Habits are mindfully cultivated, or they are mindlessly accumulated. In KF, we begin the challenging work of cultivating new habits of personal development, and on that journey, we discover ways to make the work easier. You can take a free course for developing new habits at   tinyhabits.com .  When we practice our new disciplines, we are rewarded with growing stability and peace. Our goal is to stabilize our lives so that we can redirect our abundant resources toward launching our glorious potential in Christ.  Let’s continue   practicing the   3-Minute Breathing Space . 1   Follow these instructions as I guide you.  We start with   AWARENESS .  Sit upright and bring yourself into the present moment. Try stretching the crown of your head toward the heavens and your tailbone toward the earth. If you are sitting in a chair, plant the entire soles of your feet on the floor. If possible, close your eyes. Then ask yourself:   What is my experience right now — in thoughts, in feelings, and   in my body’s sensation s?   Breathe and get to know yourself.   (Pause)   What is my experience right now — in thoughts, in feelings, and   in my body’s sensation s?   Observe and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  At this stage, your mind might be bouncing all over the place like an active and easily distracted puppy. Observe where your thoughts are going and then gently draw them back to connect with your body and your breath.   (Pause)  Let’s move to   GATHERING .  Redirect your full attention to your breathing — to each in-breath and each out-breath as they follow one after the other. Your breath functions as an anchor to bring you into the present moment, to help you

2  karisfellowships.com   KF2-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  find stillness, and to tune your awareness. Observe your breathing for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now we will go to   EXPANDING .  Expand the field of your awareness around your breathing so that you have a sense of yourself as a composite whole of mind, body, and emotions, including the part of you that observes those things.  (Pause for 10 seconds)   Notice how your body moves as you breathe.   (Pause)   Notice your posture and your face.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now pause, and notice how you feel.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Redirect your mind back to the meeting. We hope that you have begun your own daily practice of this technique. Any athlete or musician knows that a skill is only useful if you practice it regularly. Regular practice makes the skill available to you in the crush or crisis of the moment. The skill   won’t be   there if  you don’t practice it.   Train yourself in mindfulness with the   3-Minute Breathing Space   in the morning and again later in the day. Your goal is to maintain awareness in the present moment without judging who you are or what you are experiencing.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask,   “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  Let’s continue to explore KF   Confession 1:  We confess that we have worshipped and served an Idol Self that we have created.  You might wonder why, in KF, we decided to change the language of familiar Bible translations and introduce a vocabulary that may seem strange to some of you.   Let’s look at some of the thinking behind  this decision to retranslate. If you have grown up in the church, you will have heard certain words repeated over and over again, and you will have learned their theological definitions. Your mind goes on autopilot when you see or hear these familiar words and also the verses in which they appear. You believe that you already know what it all means.  The Bible is a rich text that illustrates how the neurotic pride of the Idol Self militates against the True Self, the person God created you to be. Our goal in Karis Fellowships is to dismantle this Idol Self and reorient to our True Self and to God. With this goal in mind, Nancy has retranslated Bible passages from the original Greek using vocabulary that highlights what the Scriptures say about the Idol Self and the redemption of our True Self. This new vocabulary helps us understand the working out of our salvation in Jesus as a process of reorientation. 2  Here is an example of our unique vocabulary. In the NHG book study, we learned that the idealized self has the characteristics of the idols, or graven images, described in the Bible. Both the words   idol   and   ideal  come from the Greek word for an   imagined thing . So, in KF, we call the idealized self by a more reprehensible and, for us, a more accurate name — the Idol Self. Through Karis Fellowships training, we learn how to stop investing in this Idol Self and grow into our True Self, the only s elf that can express God’s

3  karisfellowships.com   KF2-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  love. This isn’t the love that we   see in movies or read about in books. Rather, it is a precisely defined set of attributes and choices described   in chapter 13 of Paul’s first letter to   the Corinthians. 3  You really cannot recover your True Self without help.   That’s   why we created Karis Fellowships. The KF training program is designed to be a one-year effort toward recovery, but many of us continue to train together year after year. We recognize the tendency to slip back into idolatry, especially when faced with new challenges and opportunities. We are not so very different from the Old Testament nations that resisted the discomforts of personal development and then, when afraid or euphoric, turned back to their idols.  Regularly review the   Love or Pride?   list. Compare your choices and behaviors with the items on that list and record them on your   Meeting Preparation Guide . When you are acting out of pride, you are often in fear. So, this week, under question two on your guide, record whatever triggered your fear and how you tried to defend your pride.  The book   The Art of Victory   gives us our KF motto,   Train hard. Fight easy. 4   (Repeat the motto)   In KF, we learn to train hard.   That isn’t always   fun, but we train hard so that we are able to fight easy when we find ourselves up against the Idol Self, spiritual opposition, or fear — not only in ourselves but in others. Without training you cannot fight your Idol; in adversity you will succumb to its demands. With training, however, you will have the skills to overcome. You will be able to fight easy and be more than conquerors through Christ Jesus —and that’s exciting! 5  Our prayer might go something like this:  Captain of the hosts, teach me to train hard that I might fight easy.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Now   let’s look at John’s first letter , toward the back of the New Testament. This is   Nancy’s translation   of  1 John 4:16 – 19 .  16 We have come to know and have trusted the love which God has in us. God is love, and the one who dwells in love dwells in God, and God dwells in that one.   17 By this, love is perfected with us, so that we may have boldness in the day of judgment, because as He is, so also are we in this world.   18 There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear, because fear involves punishment or torment, and the one who fears is not perfected in love.   19 We love because He first extended love to us.  Take a deep breath.  1.   Agape   love, when oriented, is God’s love expressed through our lives  Our poor Idol Self cannot love others or God because it is constantly reacting to outside threats and fiercely defending its ego, its stories, and its pride. Oriented agape love is responsive not reactive; it

4  karisfellowships.com   KF2-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  is not swayed by circumstances, nor is it determined by the merits of the one who is loved. This love is generated within the redeemed True Self through its correspondence, or co-responding, with God. It only exists in our world because someone has done the hard work necessary to become the love of God on earth. So, this love is really about your character and your connection to God. We have been created in   God’s   image; therefore, each one of us is uniquely designed to express His love. When you express   God’s   love through who you are and how you live, you display to the world both   your Creator’s  glory and your own.  2.   The meaning of perfect  Now that we are looking closely at these verses in First John,   it’s   important to clarify the meaning of the word   perfect , which is repeated several times in this passage. When we read the word perfect in English versions of the New Testament, we get the feeling that nothing is valuable unless it meets a certain standard. We must act perfectly, look perfect, think perfect thoughts, and, in this case, love perfectly — otherwise, all our efforts have no value. There is no invitation for growth or training. If you have been raised this way, you know how painful and destructive it is. Anything less than perfect is judged as worthless.  However, these idealized standards of perfection are not what John is talking about. The word perfect is a translation of the Greek word   telos , meaning the fulfillment of an intention or design. We could also translate   telos   using words like mature, accomplished, fulfilled, or fully developed. When John talks about a perfect love, he is referring to a love that is fully developed; it is fulfilling its purpose, and that purpose is to cast out fear. When your love starts casting out fear, you will know that your love is perfect — it is doing its job.  3.   People of no fear  In verse 18 we read,   “ There is no fear in love; but developed love casts out fear, because fear involves punishment or torment, and the one who fears is not fully developed in love. ”   Our tendency is to focus on fighting our fears in order to avoid the torment, but John and God would have us focus on growing our love. As your love grows, your fears will automatically lose their power, and you will experience more freedom. Your goal is not to get rid of your fears; your goal is to grow your love.  4.   Learn to spot the fear  When you are punishing yourself, or punishing someone else, know that fear is motivating you. You are afraid of losing the life that you imagine will keep you safe and happy. When you feel the self-hate of the Idol whipping you from within, stop and remind yourself:   Fear is not my friend. Love is the foundation from which I will deal with self-hate .   (Repeat)   Have that conversation with yourself and then tell your Idol Self to back off.  So, think about this: your Idol Self is motivated by fear; your True Self is motivated by love — and you are learning to recognize the difference.  You   can take this week’s Bible   passage from First John and turn it into a prayer. In fact, l et’s   do that right now.   (Pause)  Lord, lead me to know and trust Your love. Teach me how to dwell in Your love. Mature Your love in me that I may be a person of no fear. (Repeat the last sentence)  Take a deep breath.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF2-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  At these meetings, always try to have some purified water available and be prepared to take some notes. You might like to use the back of your   Meeting Preparation Guide , or perhaps you have started a KF journal. Assume a mindfulness posture, follow these instructions, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider learning to really love. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider learning to really love,   how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. Feelings can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Gently allow whatever you are experiencing to remain in your awareness. We often flush feelings or thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us. Practice holding those feelings and thoughts in your awareness as you   consider learning to really love .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider   learning to really love.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what hopelessness or frustration feels like in your body. Perhaps you feel trust or joy.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  learning   to really love . Does the idea of real love feel pleasant, scary, or vague and slippery? Just observe.  (Pause)   Do you judge your present capacity to love as good or bad?   (Pause)   What do you believe about that? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something — perhaps of yourself, of loss, or of others? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created you to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you do when they have   considered learning to really love . You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   Feelings are just chemical reactions in your body bringing you information. With training, you can choose what you will do with that information.   (Pause)   When fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up

6  karisfellowships.com   KF2-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  in a story and reacting. Breathe with compassion for yourself and for the whole human race as you learn to really love. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I check for further integration.  Take a deep breath, and pause.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are grateful for this time together to train and to heal. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our glory and to the truth about ourselves. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  During the last lesson we mentioned the   KF Compass , which regularly delivers portions of the   Expanded Version   to your inbox. If you would like to receive these emails, write to admin. Try it and see if it works for you. You can cancel at any time.  If you are the Karis Link of a new member, be sure to check in with them and ask how they are doing in KF.  1   Zindel Segal, J. Mark G. Williams, and John D. Teasdale,   Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy for Depression   (New York: Guilford Press, 2013), 208. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  2   Phil. 2:12.  3   1 Cor. 13:1 – 13.  4   en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Alexander_Suvorov .  5   Rom. 8:37.

title: KF3 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF3-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF3 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in   the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  At this early stage in the Karis Fellowships training cycle, we can add this understanding to our KF prayer: the Hebrew word for   pain   or   sorrow   is a word that also means   idol . This alternative translation is particularly meaningful for us in KF as we learn to contend with the Idol Self. So, I am now going to pray this prayer incorporating what we have just learned.  “Examine me, O God, and reveal my motivations. Run experiments on me and discover my fearful thoughts. See if there is any hurtful or idolatrous way in me, and lead me in the ways of eternity.”  Take a deep breath.  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:07   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:08   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:09   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Let’s   take a little time to consider why we do mindfulness training. Most of our KF training teaches us to be motivated by principles, by our commitment to doing things God ’s way,   and by what we know to be true about ourselves. We have created an idol, however, and because we are caught up in its pride system, we are often motivated by emotional reactions that restore our pride and relieve our fear. Through training in mindfulness, we are able to step back from these reactions and make informed choices based on real evidence . We learn that we don’t have to run down   misoriented paths, chased by our own fears. Rather, we can stand in the face of those fears and resist our old habitual patterns. We might feel the same desperation or compulsive need, but we   don’t   have to act on it. Mindfulness and meditation are invaluable tools that will help us make this change.  Let’s   practice the   3-Minute Breathing Space . 1  AWARENESS  Place your feet on the ground and lengthen your spine, or you may wish to sit cross-legged on the floor. Be kind to your body. If you are fatigued, prop yourself up with pillows. Close your eyes and take a few seconds to arrive at this moment in your life.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Now, gently explore who you are and where you are. You might notice subtle sensations in your body, or you might recognize thoughts or feelings. Some of these may be unwanted. Experiment with simply observing and acknowledging what is there, without trying to cling to it, explain it, or push it away. Just observe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF3-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  GATHERING  Gently bring your full attention to your breath, observing each in-breath and each out-breath. You   don’t  need to change your breathing. Where do you feel the breath most? In your nose . . . the back of your throat . . . your chest . . . your abdomen?   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Observe your breath circulating in and out, co-responding with the air around you. When your mind wanders, kindly guide it back to your breath.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  EXPANDING  Expand your awareness now to include not only your breathing but also a sense of yourself as a whole person. Observe your mind, body, and heart — the trinity of your entire self — as you breathe for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Close this time by gradually re-engaging with the world around you. Experiment with carrying some of this awareness with you as you move through the rest of the meeting.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  Before we get started, I would like to remind you to check the website   for the week’s   worksheets and teachings. Just click on   Meeting Guides and Teachings   under the   KF   tab. The   Meeting Version   is the version that is read in the meetings. The   Expanded Version   adds information and stories to the meeting notes. Also, during the week, Karis Fellowships sends out regular emails with portions of the   Expanded Version . We call this gift the   KF Compass . Please write to   admin@karisfellowships.com   if you would like to receive these emails.  If you miss a meeting, be sure to read the teaching notes. You can also hear a recording of the meeting through the playback number and participate with the group in the meditations and integrations. KF families and couples might like to listen to the meeting together. Members have experienced healing from just listening to the recordings.  If you select   Healing/Integration   under the   Toolbox   tab on the KF website, you will find the   Tapping Protocol . 2   We will focus on this protocol for two lessons, so you might wish to print out a copy.  This is KF Confession 1:  We confess that we have worshipped and served an Idol Self that we have created.  During the next few weeks, we will look at this first Confession. Let's read it again in the first person singular:   I   confess that   I   have worshipped and served an Idol Self that   I   have created.   (Repeat)   By confessing this to the Lord, we acknowledge that we have violated the First Commandment:   “Thou shalt  have no other gods before Me. ” 3   We understand what this means for us today because we have all studied the book   Neurosis and Human Growth . 4  Fear is not hard to spot in our lives.   That’s   why we start looking at our fears very early in our KF training.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF3-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Some people might say that we should not think about negative things. In KF, we would say that we should think about true things if we want freedom. If we feel fear, then it is true that we feel fear, but we do not need to be afraid of our fear. This brings us to an important point:   We can acknowledge and look at our fear without fearing our fear .   (Repeat)   Moreover, in looking, we learn to stop fearing. If we will not allow ourselves to think about our fear, we cannot look at it. If we cannot look at it, we cannot understand it. If we cannot understand it, we cannot find solutions.  Fear is so powerful in our lives that we often obey our fear rather than fearing and obeying God. We worship fear more than we worship God, for worship is really about allegiance and obedience. This brings us back to   Nancy’s   original point:   If we want to stop obeying our fears, we must first be willing to look at them .  When we are misoriented, we are in a constant state of fear, whether we recognize it or not. Our fears began with the basic anxiety of living in a world without the skills or support that we needed to survive. We tried to save ourselves from the tyranny of our fears by designing an Idol Self and adhering to its dictates. Our imagined ability to live up to the standard of these dictates then became a source of pride, but this only served to increase our fears because our pride was now invested in our achievements. Shame and inadequacy, our inglorious past, and our failure to fulfill our claims and shoulds hurt our bloated pride. We became afraid of our own self-condemnation; we became afraid of our own self-hate.  We will be able to manage our self-hate more easily if we can first calm our fear. So, during this coming week, try to identify the events that seem to trigger your fears. Make a list of these events and fears on your   Meeting Preparation Guide   under question two, the question about being messed-up. In KF training, we will apply the idea from First John of the   day of judgment , which can be likened to a courtroom. 5   In this courtroom of examination, it is your reactions to particular events that are sifted and weighed. Here, the truth about the quality of your faith and where you have placed your trust is revealed. This is a gift. You get to discover the level of your trustworthiness and the truth about your confidence in God. Like a scientific researcher, just step back and observe your reactions. Put on your white lab coat and capture the evidence of what is there. Pop a cork into the test tube of your fear and hold it up to the light.  As you begin this investigation, remember that fear reactions may not feel like fear. For your first research project, begin comparing your behavior and choices with those on the list   Love or Pride?   At the end of the day, look over the list and identify any situations in your day where love has not been your primary motivator. Jot down those events on your   Meeting Preparation Guide . At this point in your training, think about this:   If it   isn’t love, it is fear.   If what you are doing is not love, it is fear.  Next week, we will learn how to tap. Tapping calms your body down when you are afraid. With a calmer body, you can mindfully observe your fears and make efforts not to obey them. You will choose an event that has revealed one of your fears, and you will learn how to deal with the fear by using the   Tapping Protocol . 6   To help yourself prepare for next week, you might watch   Alison’s tapping   and TAT videos   on YouTube. Alison is the co-founder of Karis Fellowships. She is also the creator of the KF website, which makes the gift of Karis Fellowships accessible to you.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, I am ready to face my fears. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF3-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  In this lesson, we will begin looking at a familiar passage in the letter from James, which you can find toward the end of the New Testament, just after Hebrews. This is   Nancy’s   translation of   James 1:1 – 4 , with a little paraphrase for clarity.  1 James, a bondservant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes who are dispersed abroad: Greetings.   2 Guide yourselves into all joy, my siblings, when you fall into and are surrounded by all kinds of experiments,   3 knowing that these experiments examine what you trust and act upon. They also grow your ability to remain under examination in future   experiments that will further explore your ever-expanding potential.   4 Give this growing ability of endurance a chance to accomplish its purpose, which is to make you a mature and complete person, lacking nothing, fully equipped for your joy and mission.  Take a deep breath.  James, or Jacob in Hebrew, is writing to the Jewish Christians who were forced by persecution to scatter throughout the Roman Empire. These people knew suffering and fear, and yet James tells them this:  “Guide yourselves into all joy when you fall into all kinds of experiments.” 7  When interpreting this passage, some translators use the words   consider it all joy , but the Greek word for  consider   can also mean to   lead   or   guide oneself . You can guide yourself into all joy when you fall into various tests. These various tests, or experiments, are your days of judgment; they are showing you what you are made of.   What’s   more, this passage teaches that you have an active choice in your experiments. You can choose to be joyful and bold as you discover what is real about yourself and about your world.  Look at your KF Confessions again. We hope that you will post them somewhere to help you keep them in mind. Notice that through the Confessions you are regularly committing yourself to an authentic, real, true, and honest life. If you are in Karis Fellowships ,   you are working toward knowing the truth about yourself, doing true things, and speaking the truth. You will also be learning to step out of the misorientation that hinders you and harms your life. Exploring your misorientation may feel like a depressing task, but take heart!   You won’t   just be knowing, you will also be growing. Guide yourself into that joy.  Now what are these experiments that James is talking about? The Greek word that is often translated as  trial   has to do with tests or experiments that reveal what is real, what is there. When we are interested in the True Self, which Karen Horney calls the real self, we are interested in what is real about ourselves right now. 8   We are like researchers. We are not judging an outcome as good or bad; we are eagerly seeking what is real and true. We also want to know what is possible. When we approach a scientific experiment   without   preconceived ideas about the outcome, we are excited about what we are going to discover. The same principle applies when we examine our lives. Conversely, if we approach an experiment   with   preconceived ideas about what we want to see, what would be good or bad, and what would support our pride, we come to the experiment with apprehension. We are fixated on an outcome

5  karisfellowships.com   KF3-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  that our pride feels it must have. We are focusing on the future, and that takes us out of the real present. We are not joyful or creative about the process. Rather, we are anxious, and our observation is distorted by our efforts to save   the Idol’s life . We may even avoid acknowledging what we see, even if   it’s   beneficial, becaus e it doesn’t fit our   preconceived illusions.  Our True Self, however, is eager for truth to be revealed in our lives because it is motivated by love — and love, as Paul teaches us, rejoices in the truth.   9   Here is an interesting observation about the word  experience . The spelling of the words   experience   and   experiment   is almost the same. That ’s   because they are derived from the same root word. 10   All of your experiences are experiments with reality and can be interpreted as opportunities, or days of judgment, that show you the truth about who you are right now; they reveal your actual self. Experiences measure your progress as you develop the potential of your real glory. Free from the judgments that support your pride, you can rejoice in what you learn. You can rejoice because these discoveries are essential for your growth.   In order to get where you want to go, you have to know where you are right now. (Repeat)  Our prayer might go something like this:  Loving Father, teach me to rejoice in my experiments. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  During the integration, you might jot down some notes on the back of your   Meeting Preparation Guide  or in your KF journal. Sip some purified water and assume a mindfulness posture. Breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider a fear that reveals the truth about your faith.   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider a fear that reveals the truth about your faith , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.  (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Observe with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Graciously allow whatever you are experiencing to just be. As you breathe, hold your experience up to the light. Observe whatever tension might be there as you   consider a fear that reveals the truth about your faith .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider this fear that reveals the truth about your faith .   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you.

6  karisfellowships.com   KF3-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what panic or judgment feels like in your body. You might feel relief or curiosity. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider this fear that reveals the truth about your faith.   Does that feel comfortable, scary, or vague and slippery? Just observe.   (Pause)   Do you judge your fear as good or evil?   (Pause)   What are your reasons? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Is this experience a regular pattern in your life?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you do when they have experienced fears that reveal the truth about their faith. You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   Feelings are just chemical reactions in your body bringing you information. With training, you can choose what you will do with that information.   (Pause)   When a fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting. As you consider this fear, breathe and have compassion for yourself. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I check for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank you for this time together of healing and training. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our glory and to the truth about our faith. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   Zindel Segal, J. Mark G. Williams and John D. Teasdale,   Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy for Depression   (New York: Guilford Press, 2013), 208. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  2   Dr. Roger Callahan, “TFT Stress Buster Tapping Class - Learn to Use TFT Tapping,” Callahan Techniques, accessed  April 24, 2016,   www.rogercallahan.com/learn-to-tap.php . Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  3   Exod. 20:3.  4   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).  5   1 John 4:17.

7  karisfellowships.com   KF3-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  6   Dr. Roger Callahan, “TFT Stress Buster Tapping Class - Learn to Use TFT Tapping,” Callahan Techniques, accessed  April 24, 2016,   www.rogercallahan.com/learn-to-tap.php . Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  7   James 1:2.  8   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).  9   1 Cor. 13:6.  10   www.sloww.co/experience-experiment-etymology/ .

title: KF4 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF4-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF4 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in   the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  Let’s look   at the first KF guideline:   “We cooperate for the security and efficiency of the group.”  Participating members cooperate to ensure a secure environment and an efficient experience for everyone by making a trustworthy effort to attend the entire meeting. By walking together through all the steps of the training, we lay the necessary foundation for the integration process and approach our healing as one entity.  (Optional)   Our souls need congruence; therefore, we cannot say one thing and do another without harming ourselves. In order to maintain this inner balance and integrity, we have to do what we say. We will now do our best to begin our meetings on time. This may seem rigid to some, but our meeting guidelines remind us that, as creatures living in time, we choose to honor time limitations. Our Idol Self will rebel against limitations, and some of us are not yet strong enough to defy the Idol Self. We can easily lose track of time during our sharing, so set a timer or alarm before you share to help you stay within the time restraints.  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Through mindfulness training, you learn that you   don’t   have to judge or even speak when situations arise. During the next few minutes, you can quiet your mind and stop the chatter of the Idol Self.  You are training to be still in your spirit and to observe without judgment while you learn to allow whatever is happening to just   be . During this mindfulness exercise, refuse to evaluate the performance of anyone, including yourself. Observe where your thoughts want to scatter and then gently draw them back to the breath. Take it easy and be kind to yourself in this learning process.  The 3-Minute Breathing Space 1  AWARENESS  Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.   (Pause)   Get to know yourself in   this   moment, in   this   space. Explore your current experience.   (Pause)   You might notice sensations in your body, or you might be aware of passing thoughts and feelings. You may find these comfortable, or you may not. Experiment with simply observing and acknowledging what is there. Just allow it to be, and observe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF4-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  GATHERING  Gently bring your full attention to your breath, watching each in-breath and each out-breath as you breathe naturally. Where do you notice your breathing?   (Pause)   Feel your body move as it breathes. When your mind wanders, gently guide it back to your breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  EXPANDING  Expand your awareness now to include a sense of yourself as a whole person. As you breathe, feel your whole body respond to the inhale and the exhale. Observe your thoughts and feelings. Within your mind, connect your breath to your body, and connect your body to your breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Close this time by gradually re-engaging with the world around you. Open your eyes. You may want to stretch, breathe deeply, or even yawn. Experiment with allowing this connection with yourself to be your companion throughout the rest of the meeting.  During the week, you might notice how the breath is used in the Bible and in our culture.  Listen now to the first verse of the hymn   Breathe on Me, Breath of God .  Breathe on me, Breath of God.  Fill me with life anew,  That I may love what Thou dost love,  And do what Thou wouldst do. 2  Take a deep breath.  (Go straight to the Karis Confession to allow more time for the Toolbox)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  Our Toolbox will be longer in this lesson to give us time to practice a powerful tool called tapping.  This month we are focusing on KF Confession 1:  We confess that we have worshipped and served an Idol Self that we have created.  Wouldn’t it be absolutely glorious to live a fear -free life? In KF, we are working toward freeing ourselves from misoriented fear. That is the direction in which you are headed. Observe how fear interferes with your whole life. Now, if you can,   think about a place in your life where there is no fear. (Repeat)   (Pause)  Isn’t that a wonderful place? It is usually a place of play and fun, of exploration and gratitude; it is often a  place where there are people you trust. You really can learn to live, most of the time, in a place like that —  free from fear.  Your connection to the Holy Spirit, to the Bible, and to a trustworthy community of believers is essential for living fear-free.   Let’s review the KF tools that you now have available to support you.  1.   KF weekly meetings and the Meeting Preparation Guide  Your first tool is your weekly Karis Fellowships meeting, along with the   Meeting Preparation Guide .

3  karisfellowships.com   KF4-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  2.   Our manuals: the Bible and the book   Neurosis and Human Growth 3  To help you stay on track, review your   NHG Reading Guides   and finish reading chapters 12 – 16 of Dr.  Horney’s book.   Add a few minutes of Bible reading to your time of meditation or, perhaps, before or after a meal.  Here is a quote from Robert Louis Stevenson:  You cannot run away from weakness; you must at some time fight it out or perish; and if that be so, why not now, and where you stand? 4  The book study helps you identify areas of weakness where you need to stand against your fears and fight it out.  3.   Mindfulness and meditation practice  Mindfulness training teaches you to observe reality with your mind, to calm your body, and to exercise endurance, all of which strengthens your True Self.  4.   Worksheets and guides — homework for lasting recovery  As the weeks go by, you will have access to a variety of worksheets that support your efforts to rescue and repair your True Self. You will need to keep these documents in a place where they are easily accessible.  5.   Tapping — when the going gets rough  Tapping is one of the tools that we use in KF to train hard so that we can fight easy when dealing with our weaknesses and fears. Stored information in our bodies drives us to react before we can think, so we work with our bodies first. With calmer bodies, we have more freedom to choose healthier outcomes.  I hope that you were able to download the   Tapping Protocol   from the Karis Fellowships website. You can also watch   Alison’s tapping and TAT videos   which demonstrate this tool. While I read, follow along in your notes and participate as best you can.  The Tapping Protocol 5  Before you begin tapping, you need to formulate your healing statement and write it down. This statement describes the problem that triggered your stress reaction and, also, identifies a few of the emotions that you are experiencing. Allow yourself to play with this a little. The statement does not have to be perfectly crafted. Here is an example of a healing statement:   My problem is that I am experiencing a life change, and when I think of that, I feel lonely, distressed, anxious, and vulnerable .  Now let’s go step by step through the process of creating   a personal healing statement.  1.   Determine the focus  What is the problem or issue that you want to address? You might consider one of the fears that you noticed this week. Your problem would be whatever triggered the fear. Begin with the phrase   “ My problem is that . . . ”   and then state the problem in simple terms.   (Pause for 15 seconds)

4  karisfellowships.com   KF4-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  2.   Identify your emotions  What do you feel when you think about your problem?   (Pause)   Add to your healing statement   “ and when I think of that, I feel . . . ”   Now list a few of the emotions that you have identified.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  3.   Write down your complete healing statement  Here is our example again:   My problem is that I am experiencing a life change, and when I think of that, I feel lonely, distressed, anxious, and vulnerable.   Be sure to write down your healing statement and keep it in a place where you can easily find it again for your KF work.  4.   Assess the level of fear or stress  On a scale of one to ten, with ten being the most stressful for you, how stressful is your problem? Make a note of that.   (Pause)  Let’s   practice the first series of the   Tapping Protocol   together.  Sip some purified water and assume a mindfulness posture. Be sure to breathe deeply while you tap.  Opening  With the palm of each hand flat on your chest, rub in a circular motion crossing over the sternum. While rubbing, breathe deeply and repeat this statement after me:  I fully and completely accept myself as I am today. (Read 3 times, pausing for 3 seconds after each reading)  Now pause.  First Series  Continue to breathe deeply as you follow my guidance.  •   Using the three middle fingers of each hand, tap gently on the orbital bones under your eyes. (Repeat)   Read your healing statement out loud and then breathe deeply as you tap:   “My problem  is . . ., and when I think of that ,   I feel . . . ”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  •   Now, under your dominant arm, which is most often the right arm, find a point about four inches below the armpit. Massage this rather tender spot as you repeat your healing statement. Try not to worry about finding the exact location.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  •   Pause. With the palm of each hand facing you, push your little fingers away from you and bring your two ring fingers together so that they touch each other.   Bring all the middle fingers together to form a kind of picket fence and tap on your brow, above your nose, with all six fingertips.  (Repeat)   Breathe, and repeat your healing statement.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  •   Locate your collarbone and follow it out to your shoulder joints. Drop down about two inches into the crevice between your shoulders and chest muscles. Massage these two points and repeat your statement. Breathe.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  •   Now, follow your collarbone back to the sternum. Drop down about two inches on each side of

5  karisfellowships.com   KF4-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  the sternum and tap or massage   the space between your ribs. Repeat your statement, and breathe.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  •   Move to the little finger of your left hand.   With the three middle fingers of your right hand, tap on the inside edge of the left little finger, incorporating the edge of the fingernail. (Repeat)   Repeat your statement, and breathe.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  •   Pause. Take a deep breath and sip some water. On a scale of one to ten, how distressing is the problem or trigger event now? Jot down the number for your reference.   (Pause)  This is the first series of the   Tapping Protocol . In the next lesson we will learn the second series. For a much more effective tap, spend twenty seconds on each step.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, remind me to tap. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  We will be spending some weeks in the letter from James, so you might want to print out the first chapter of James from one of the many Bible websites. Double or triple space the text to give yourself room for taking notes, and keep a copy in your ring binder with your other KF materials.  Let’s look at   James 1:2 .  The NASB translation reads:   “ Consider it all joy, my brethren, when you encounter various trials .” 6   Last week, we learned that the Greek word for   consider   can be translated as   guide yourself . We can guide ourselves into all joy in any situation.   Isn’t that amazing ? However, you might wonder where this joy is that we are guiding ourselves into. Most of us have no idea where to find joy, but fortunately we do not have to know where we are going before we begin the journey. Like all journeys, we must simply begin. Jesus really is   The Way , and on this journey toward reclaiming the True Self, we discover more and more about who He is and who we are becoming. 7   This is the source of all joy.  What are these   various trials   that James talks about? We have learned during these last weeks that trials or experiences are opportunities to discover the truth about who we are and where our real strengths and weaknesses lie. In our passage from First John, we learned that these trials are days of judgment. 8  They show us the truth about our beliefs and our fearful misorientation. Just as a courtroom will explore what is true, so this day of judgment will explore our hearts and reveal the true quality of our faith and love. Although this experience might sound intimidating, John says that we can be bold in this day of judgment. We get to see how much fear we are carrying in our souls. We also get to see how far we have travelled toward our goal of reorienting to God and living in harmony with His Creation. We no longer shrink back through fear of self-hate. 9   All of this knowing leads to our growing, and growing leads to more

6  karisfellowships.com   KF4-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  knowing. Through knowing and growing we gain real self-confidence. Just as the lilies grow without fear, so can you. 10  This is what Nancy wrote about her own journey toward orientation:  In the early days of Karis Fellowships, I thought about how difficult these new ideas might be for some of you, especially if you have been trained to think in a certain way. Our KF work reminds me of how difficult it must have been for those listening to Jesus for the first time. Jesus invited them to rethink their whole culture and upbringing. They naturally felt intimidated and resistant. I thought about a time, years ago, long before we ever thought of Karis Fellowships, when I was agonizing about where   Neurosis and Human Growth   and   my study of Paul’s letter to the Romans   would take me. 11   I was afraid of my own journey toward orientation; I was afraid of going into the not-knowing. I think fear confuses all of us. When we are in fear, we feel abandoned, and in those moments, we need to be reminded that Jesus is with us.  Several years ago, while in prayer, the Lord plainly spoke to me. He said,   “ You must be willing to go into the not-knowing. ”   (Repeat)   At that time, I really did not know what He meant, but all the same His words encouraged me to let go of needing to know where this journey would take me. Let me point out something. Letting go of anything is a day of judgment — and it is probably one of our more severe trials or experiments. We find out where our treasure is when we cannot let go, and that can be extremely painful. Some of us have a compulsive need to be   right . I have always felt that I needed to know the  right   theology, the   right   way to do something, what is   right   about myself, about society, about the choices of others, and what is   wrong   about all of those things. I had to know what was right in order to support my pride and relieve my anxiety. During that year, God encouraged me to give up needing to know what was right. He encouraged me to just keep growing — or, shall I say, to keep going forward on the journey, producing more of the Fruit of the Spirit in my life. I knew in my heart that if I allowed the fear of being wrong to hold me back, I would be obeying my fears. I would be teaching my heart to love fear rather than to love God. What a loss that would have been! If I had followed my fears, I would not have these healing gifts to offer to my community, nor would we have Karis Fellowships.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Jesus, help me go into the not-knowing with You. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes, perhaps in a KF journal. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider going on this journey with Jesus, not knowing where you are going. (Repeat)   (Pause for 30 seconds)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF4-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider going on this journey with Jesus, not knowing where you are going , how does it feel?  (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   Acknowledge your experience with compassion, whatever it may be, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Gently allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. As you breathe, hold your thoughts and feelings up to the light. Observe whatever you may be experiencing as you   consider going on this journey with Jesus, not knowing where you are going .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider going on this journey with Jesus, not knowing where you are going.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. For example, you might recognize what anxiety or resistance feels like in your body. You might feel curiosity or courage.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider going on this journey with Him, not knowing where you are going . Do you feel comfortable with that, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe.   (Pause)   Do you judge this journey as good or evil?  (Pause)   What are your reasons? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something — of loss, of others, or of yourself? Observe your responses as just information and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created you to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you do when they have gone into the not-knowing. You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   With training, you can choose what you will do with those feelings.   (Pause)   When a fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting. Breathe, and allow yourself to feel compassion for all human creatures who are driven by fear. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER

8  karisfellowships.com   KF4-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our glory and to the truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  If you would like more support for your training, you might consider KF mini-meetings. title: KF5 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF5-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF5 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.”   (Psalm 139:23 – 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  Let’s look at the first KF guideline, “We cooperate for the security and efficiency of the group.”  Participating members cooperate to ensure a secure environment and an efficient experience for everyone by making a trustworthy effort to attend the entire meeting. By walking together through all the steps of the training, we lay the necessary foundation for the integration process and approach our healing as one entity.  I would like to remind you that we are a confidential fellowship. This means that we do not share what other members say in the meetings, nor do we share the playback numbers, the recordings, the meeting notes, or the KF self-help guides with people outside Karis Fellowships. If you leave the Fellowships, please let us know your decision and remember that   “ we respect the group by always announcing our presence. ”  It is not respectful or trustworthy to eavesdrop on meetings or listen to recordings if you are no longer participating in Karis Fellowships.  Only those who are in the Fellowships and have done the work to get this far, who have shown themselves to be people of intention and courage, are able to understand and use KF tools effectively. Sharing these tools with those outside the Fellowships will not substantially help them in the long run because they do not have KF support and training. Instead, let them see the development that is happening in you. Tell them what you are learning about yourself. If they show interest, invite them to join you on the journey, beginning with the NHG book study.  0:09   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Over the months, you will learn different forms of mindfulness that will help you reorient to God and to His Creation — a creation that includes your community and your True Self. Mindfulness techniques teach us moment-by-moment awareness, posture, breathing, and non-judgment. We begin by simply noticing our bodies, and then we observe our emotions and thoughts. By being mindful, we can learn to stop manufacturing the feelings and experiences that we use to protect our pride. From a platform of non- judgment, we can observe what is actually there, within us and without. Only then are we able to change the direction of our lives.  You cannot authentically present yourself to the Great Physician to be healed until you acknowledge that

2  karisfellowships.com   KF5-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  you are sick . 1   Mindfulness helps you recognize the subtle changes in your body that indicate soul sickness, or misorientation. If you learn to listen to your body, you will be able to recognize when you are heating up or melting down. You can then use your tools while you still have some self-control. When you are mindful, you are awake. You pay attention to what   is , not to how it should be. Mindfulness tools help you recognize what is real; you find out who you are right now. You can then enter the ring of reality and courageously come to grips with your self-hate. In the ring of reality, your eyes are opened to the real growth that is taking place within you — growth that produces lasting joy and self- confidence in all of life’s  circumstances.  Let’s continue with the   3-Minute Breathing Space . 2   I will give you minimal guidance and let you explore your own experience. Take a mindfulness posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The 3-Minute Breathing Space  AWARENESS  Take one minute to explore your present experience in this present moment.   (Pause for 1 minute)  GATHERING  Gather yourself around your breathing for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  EXPANDING  Take one minute to expand, noticing your entire body as it breathes.   (Pause for 1 minute)  And pause. Remain in mindful awareness while I read another verse of our hymn,   Breathe on Me, Breath of God .  Breathe on me, Breath of God,  Blend all my soul with Thine,  Until this earthly part of me  Glows with Thy fire divine. 3  Take a deep breath.  This hymn was written in 1878 by Edwin Hatch, who served his community as a well-known scholar and Anglican priest.  (Go straight to the Karis Confession to allow time for a longer Toolbox)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  You may wonder why Nancy wrote these notes for you instead of teaching you in a spontaneous manner. The KF team is compiling a written guide for those who are on this journey. Nancy will not always be with us, and by writing these notes she intends to leave a legacy that will guide you and others when she is gone.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF5-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF Confession 1 goes like this:  We confess that we have worshipped and served an Idol Self that we have created.  In this Toolbox lesson, we will practice the second series of the   Tapping Protocol . 4   This entire intervention will then be available to help you stand and fight it out when you step into the ring with your fears. Before  we begin tapping, however, let’s look at a few points that will help you train to be a creature no longer  driven by fear but able to respond in the moment with grace and truth.  1.   Our only hope of recovery is in Jesus, who gives us the alternative to worshipping our fears  When we are born again, we are born as our True Self, and it is our business, in partnership with the Holy Spirit and other believers, to develop our True Self into its glorious potential in Christ. Consider this: if you are not producing the Fruit of the Spirit in your life on a regular and ongoing basis, your connection to the Spirit is faulty. 5   Once you admit that your connection to the Spirit is faulty, you can start the process of rediscovering your True Self and glory.  2.   Events reveal fear that is already there   (Repeat)  During these last weeks, we have observed our fears and the events or trials that stir up those fears. Remember that when you feel like you need to force, rescue, or avoid something or someone, you are probably in fear. Last week, we began learning the   Tapping Protocol   to help us calm our bodies when we fall into various trials. Tap regularly, even when you are not aware of tension building up. Start with smaller, daily issues and then work up to the bigger, compelling, addictive issues. Whenever you feel strain and are not in peace, tap.  3.   Pray ahead and avoid the rush  When we pray ahead about our fears, we are preparing for the experiments, or various trials, that inevitably come into our lives. If you are praying our opening prayer from KF3 — "Examine me, O God, and reveal my motivations ”— you can face your fear with courage and be confident that God is answering your prayer. 6   He is giving you opportunities that will help you recognize the areas of your life where you need training, and, like a great coach, He is there with you to help you succeed. So, you can step boldly into the ring of reality, knowing that He wants you to succeed and that your trial is essential for your training. The Idol Self uses your personal power to fuel the fear that drives its search for glory, but when you choose to co-labor with God in your training, you can harness that power to produce the Fruit of the Spirit in your life and to   access the many benefits of God’s gifts .  Any athlete or musician knows that if you haven’t practiced, you will not be able to perform.   In the same way, if you have not been training hard, the fight will be beyond your range of skills, and you will find it impossible to fulfill your good intentions. When you fail to express the Fruit of the Spirit, you might recognize that you have not trained well enough or are simply not ready for that fight. Rather than judging yourself, consider the quality of your training and the timing of the trial. Do you need more tools? Is there someone who can help you? Do you simply need more time to grow? Other battles will surely come, so do yourself a favor — prepare now for your next battle.  Listen again to our quote from Robert Louis Stevenson:  You cannot run away from weakness; you must at some time fight it out or perish; and if that be so, why not now, and where you stand? 7

4  karisfellowships.com   KF5-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  If you are in KF, you are learning to stop running away from your weaknesses. You are learning how to fight it out, where you stand. Yo ur fight is not with others; it is with the Idol’s pride and its efforts to save  its own life. You   can’t   take on every battle right now, but you can take on the battle that has been revealed to you today. Tapping   is one way to fight it out.  Let’s continue with the second series of the   Tapping Protocol . Recall your healing statement from the last lesson.   (Pause)  Second Series  Continue to breathe deeply as you follow my guidance.  •   To begin, say your healing statement out loud.   (Pause for 5 seconds)  •   Now,   using the three middle fingers of your right hand, gently tap on the back of your left hand between the tendons of your little finger and your ring finger.   (Repeat)   While you are tapping, breathe deeply and say your healing statement out loud one more time.   (Pause for 5 seconds)  We are now going to do an eye movement exercise. Keep your head still and move only your eyes. Breathe deeply and continue to tap the back of your hand while you follow these directions:  •   Focus your eyes straight ahead . (Pause for 3 seconds)  •   Now close your eyes while you continue to tap and breathe.   (Pause for 3 seconds)  •   Open your eyes again and, without moving your head, look sharply down toward your right hip or elbow for a few seconds.   (Pause for 3 seconds)  •   Now look sharply down toward your left side, again without moving your head.   (Pause for 3 seconds)  •   Repeat this right and left eye movement two more times while you tap and breathe.   (Pause for 5 seconds)  •   Now roll your eyes in a circle, three times in one direction and then three times in the opposite direction. You might look to one side and then direct your eyes up the wall to the ceiling, across the ceiling, down the opposite wall, and across the floor.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  •   Continue to tap while you hum the tune   “Happy Birthday” .   (Pause for 5 seconds)  •   Now quickly count out loud to fifteen.   (Pause for 5 seconds)  •   Hum the tune again while you continue to tap.   (Pause for 5 seconds)  Pause. Take a sip of purified water and relax. After the meeting, you can finish up your tap by repeating the first series, which we learned in the last lesson. Use the   Tapping Protocol   to take on your battle for today. To prepare for our next lesson, print out the   Two Paths Flowchart   and add it to your KF ring binder.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF5-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Our prayer might go something like this:  Coach and Father, help me stop running away from my weaknesses. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s go back to   our beautiful passage in the first chapter of James. This is   Nancy’s   translation of   James 1:2 – 4 , with a little paraphrase.  2 Guide yourselves into all joy, my siblings, when you fall into and are surrounded by all kinds of experiments,   3 knowing that these experiments examine what you trust and act upon. They also grow your ability to remain under examination in future experiments, experiments that will further explore your ever-expanding potential.   4 Give this growing ability of endurance a chance to accomplish its purpose, which is to make you a mature and complete person, lacking nothing, fully equipped for your joy and mission.  Take a deep breath.  Nancy’s   first point is often the most difficult to remember.  1.   The struggle is the valuable part   (Repeat)  If you learn one thing from this meeting, learn this: the struggle is the most important part of your process. Do not hesitate to get into the struggle because it is through well-managed struggling that you become strong. If you exercise at the gym or are learning a new skill, you already know this.  In his groundbreaking book,   The Road Less Traveled , Scott Peck begins with a troubling but very true statement:   Life is difficult . 8   (Repeat)   In other words, life is a struggle. Our problem is that we do not know how to struggle productively. We can only think of struggle as an unfair or purposeless kind of suffering. One of our most discouraging struggles comes when we try to live loving lives but find ourselves driven by our compelling needs. In that struggle, we fear that our neurotic needs will go unmet. We also fear living with failure. Failure afflicts our pride system, and hurt pride adds to the burden of our struggle.  When the Idol anticipates failure, our neurotic pride system is threatened, and we find that the terror of our self-hate is stronger and much more compelling than our commitment to love. If you have not been training, your love will be too weak to stand against the compulsive need to protect your pride. Instead, you will sacrifice your True Self and others in order to meet that need, and this will create a further burden of self-hate and fear in your soul. You might think that the way to overcome the unloving reactions of your pride and self-hate is to simply exercise more self-control, but you already know from experience that your self-control is too weak and inconsistent to be reliable. The first step toward building a consistent, loving life is to get rid of your pride and, at the same time, learn to practice a gritty faith that stands against the Idol, fights it out, and trusts our Savior. As self-hate and

6  karisfellowships.com   KF5-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  the fear of hurt pride lose their grip, your struggles will become manageable and productive, and the love that God has already deposited in you will start to emerge.  2.   The discovery and the fostering of our True Self require a lot of endurance  The ongoing discovery of your True Self begins with months of effort, but learning to dwell consistently in your True Self will take years of maintenance and care — in fact, it will take the rest of your life. Just like maintaining your physical health, maintaining your True Self requires commitment, courage, and a sustained effort in an oriented direction. To build anything worthwhile, you need to learn the art of endurance. When you practice endurance, you grow in courage, and with more courage you can endure tension longer and with more productive results. You are an eternally developing creature designed to keep growing, and growth happens when you endure.  3.   Let endurance do its work  What is endurance? The Greek word translated as   endurance   means to   remain under . When you fall into an experiment, it is, as James says, an opportunity to see what skills you have, which areas of your life need work, and how your character is developing. If you can manage your self-hate, you get to see the truth about yourself, and if you can remain under the tension of your opportunity, you become creative — you explore, get help, and work on your connection to the Spirit. You discover how to live with less suffering, and you cause less suffering for others. Your compassion grows, and you experience more gratitude. You learn to lean more on God and less on your Idol Self.  4.   Endurance trains us to be trustworthy  Finally, what is the goal of your endurance through all of these experiments? The goal is to grow you up — to unify and fully equip you so that you have everything you need to accomplish your mission. You have a vital mission;   God’s   reputation and the reputation of the believing community are in your hands. God cannot afford to entrust His redemptive purposes to untrustworthy people, so if you want to co-labor with Him to accomplish your mission, you must endure training to become trustworthy.  You may have been taught that the purpose of endurance and suffering is to fulfill some abstract and mysterious plan, but James teaches that endurance is designed to help YOU fulfill YOUR mission and design. Endurance helps YOU become whole, complete, integrated, and true, so that YOU who are alive in Christ are no longer forced to live in fear, subject to addictive and compulsive reactions to life events. You may think that you lack this or that resource to help you accomplish your mission, but what do you really lack? You lack the health and orientation of the True Self — the self that circulates with God and with His Creation. If you focus your efforts on the restoration of your True Self and your orientation to God and His Creation, you will flourish and grow into your full potential, and you most certainly will lack nothing.  Our prayer might go something like this:  I need endurance training, Coach! (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. In this lesson I will give you minimal guidance. We will spend one minute on each step of the   FAITH Process . Assume your mindfulness posture, and

7  karisfellowships.com   KF5-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider what happens when you are faced with an opportunity to endure. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH   Process  Feelings  Recognize any feelings or numbness that you experience when you   consider what happens when you are faced with an opportunity to endure . Observe and breathe . (Pause for 1 minute)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to rest in your awareness as you   consider what happens when you are faced with an opportunity to endure.   Notice any conflicts or resistance. Give yourself permission to explore without judgment whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice if it is reacting to your opportunity to endure.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Talk to Jesus  Imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider this experience of   endurance .   (Pause)   Are you learning something about hurt pride or self-hate? We often experience hurt pride and self-hate when an aspect of our   Idol’s search for glory   is threatened or lost. Observe and breathe.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Heal  For thousands of years, human beings have felt strong feelings when they have had to endure a trial or difficulty. You are not alone in your experience. When your feelings signal you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than reacting and getting caught up in stories and judgments. Breathe, and help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 1 minute)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time together to train and to heal. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our glory and to the truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)

8  karisfellowships.com   KF5-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  Remember to finish off your tap by repeating the first series of the   Tapping Protocol . Williams, and John D. Teasdale,   Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy for Depression   (New York: Guilford Press, 2013), 208. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  3   Breathe on Me, Breath of God   by Edwin Hatch   (1835 – 1889),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=M5keJHZdWYM .  4   Dr. Roger Callahan, “TFT Stress Buster Tapping Class - Learn to Use TFT Tapping,” Callahan Techniques, accessed  April 24, 2016,   www.rogercallahan.com/learn-to-tap.php .
