title: KF6 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF6-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF6 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.”   (Psalm 139:23 – 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  I am going to read our opening prayer using Karis Fellowships vocabulary:   “Examine me, O God, and reveal  my motivations. Run experiments on me and expose my misoriented thinking. See if there is any hurtful or idolatrous way in me, and lead me in ways that will last forever .”  Take a deep a breath.  Oriented thinking is essential for personal growth and physical well-being. Our minds and bodies are designed to function together in harmony, but we are rarely taught how to create that harmony. Although we may not be aware of it, our bodies inform our thinking, and our thinking is often related to trauma stored in our bodies. The physiological reality is that distressed bodies result in distressed minds. When the body is distressed, it sends chemical signals to the brain that cause our minds to react, and often overreact, in a simple and primitive attempt to survive.  You can calm your mind by first calming your body.   That’s   why, in KF, we start with mindfulness training. Daily mindfulness practice trains our bodies to calm down in those moments when we find ourselves in stressful situations that invite compulsive and addictive choices. These are the emergencies, the times when you are heating up or melting down. In these experiments, choose mindfulness, even for a few seconds, to help calm your body, open your mind to truth, and free your creativity.  We will now learn a new meditation practice taught by John Main, OSB. This Roman Catholic monk noticed that a Buddhist priest had more peace than he did, and he learned that the   priest’s secret   was meditation.  You can read about John Main’s work and history on the web. He writes :  The all- important aim in Christian meditation is to allow God’s mysterious and silent  presence within us to become more and more not only   a   reality, but   the   reality which gives meaning, shape and purpose to everything we do, to everything we are. 1  It may take years of practice for you to experience all that he describes, but that is the nature of meditation . Meditation is “dose dependent” . The more you practice, the more you benefit.

2  karisfellowships.com   KF6-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  We always begin our meditation practice by sitting upright and as still as possible. If you are ill or fatigued, you can sit propped up with pillows. Try sitting up as if you were waiting for someone or something that is just around the corner.   (Pause)   Breathe as you lightly close your eyes.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  The Maranatha Meditation 2  Silently, within your own mind, begin to slowly say the word MAA-RAA-NAA-THAA.   Maranatha   is an Aramaic word that is used as a prayer in the Bible. 3   You can let it roll on the breath like the swell of the sea, or you can simply focus on each syllable for a second or two.   Remember to breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  As you say the word within yourself, attend to the word. Listen to it within your mind throughout the meditation time.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   If your mind wanders, gently draw it back to the word. We will focus on MAA-RAA-NAA-THAA for one minute. Try to let go of the sense of passing time and just relax into the word. Begin.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Now pause and take a few deep breaths as you open your eyes. Gently draw your mind back to the meeting.   (Pause)   Through meditation, we train our mind, body, will, and heart to be still and to wait upon the Lord in any situation, no matter what is happening in us or around us.  Our hymn and prayer is   Breathe on Me, Breath of God.  Breathe on me, Breath of God,  Until my heart is pure,  Until with Thee I will one will,  To do and to endure. 4  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits,   ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  During these past weeks, we have been exploring KF Confession 1:  We confess that we have worshipped and served an Idol Self that we have created.  We will now move on to KF Confession 2:  We abandoned the glory that was ours, designed for us by our Creator.  In this Confession we admit that when our Idol Self is in charge, we readily abandon the glory that God designed for us.  Hopefully, you have a copy of the   Two Paths Flowchart   in front of you.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF6-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Training ourselves takes time, and so does healing. In this fast-paced world, we often cannot accept the limitation of time. It takes time to learn how to use KF tools, so you must think about adjusting your schedule to create space for practice and soul care. If you do not schedule time to care for yourself, you will wear yourself out in this training process. Like any craftsman who regularly uses his tools, you will learn to work faster, more efficiently, and more effectively toward your healing if you practice — and, also, if you rest .  Let’s revie w the KF tools that we are learning to use. These tools help us continue to make progress even when we feel discouraged, frustrated, or stuck.  1.   KF weekly meetings and the Meeting Preparation Guide  In the Karis Fellowships meetings you are trained, healed, and reminded of your disciplines. These meetings guide your training efforts and give you a chance to share the progress and challenges that you have recorded on your   Meeting Preparation Guide . Sharing your battles and discoveries with others is essential for your healing.  2.   Our manuals — the Bible and the book   Neurosis and Human Growth 5  You may be starting to see how these two resources work together to guide you back to your design and mission.  3.   Mindfulness and meditation practice  Mindfulness training teaches you to observe with your mind, calm your body, and exercise endurance, all of which strengthens your True Self.  4.   Worksheets and guides — homework for lasting recovery  These worksheets and guides can be found on the KF website under   Toolbox . You can start exploring them at any time. Ask your Karis Link to help you choose a worksheet or guide that might be useful in your situation. You might also attend additional training groups where you can practice using KF worksheets.  5.   The Tapping Protocol 6  Here is our   quote from Robert Louis Stevenson: “You cannot run away from weakness; you must   at  some time fight it out or perish; and if that be so, why not now, and where you stand?” 7   Tapping is one way to fight it out against the weakness of your fear. After a few months of training, you will be able to quickly detect the fear, feel the strain within you, and tap.  6.   The Two Paths Flowchart  This valuable tool reveals the path you have taken in a situation — the path of judgment or the path of agape love. If you want the Fruit of the Spirit to shine through your life, you will have to give up the judgments that fuel your Idol Self, and learn to dwell in real love.  Hopefully, you have been able to look at the   Two Paths Flowchart . In our KF training, we have begun to identify our fears and the events that trigger those fears. In addition to fearful reactions, reactions of euphoria also send us down a dangerous path. Mindless euphoria is the result of judging that something is extraordinarily good. This strong emotion puts us in   the Idol’s hand s because we become forgetful. We lose touch with our limitations and weaknesses as creatures. We forget that we need maintenance and soul care. We forget what has happened in the past. We think that the euphoria indicates new potential,

4  karisfellowships.com   KF6-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  and we mindlessly take on challenges that are beyond our abilities. Then, when reality catches up with us, we are completely blindsided and fall.  The two paths of the flowchart represent the dualities that we see in the Bible — spirit and flesh, life and death, and many more. The upper path is the path of the True Self and the lower path is the path of the Idol Self. In the next few weeks, you will be introduced to a worksheet that will help you to understand and use this chart.  Look at the flowchart this week and try to notice when you are taking the lower path as you go through your day. What is the event?   What assault on your Idol’s search for glory   has disconnected you from God and thrown you into fear? It may help to remember that if your reaction is extreme, it is probably fear- driven. Did you judge the event as good or evil? What story are you telling about yourself, about others, or about life? What emotions are then justified by that story? What choices are you making based on those emotions? What is the outcome of your choices? Play with the flowchart this week and see what you can discover about yourself.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Guide and Friend, reveal to me the path that I have taken. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox? ” )  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s return to the first chapter of James.   Hopefully, you have printed out this chapter and have the text in front of you. We will review what we have learned in the last few meetings and then consider what agape love looks like for Christians.  Our text for this lesson is   James 1:2 – 4 . These verses have been translated by Nancy.  2 Guide yourselves into all joy, my siblings, when you fall into and are surrounded by all kinds of experiments,   3 knowing that these experiments examine what you trust and act upon. They also grow your ability to remain under examination in future experiments, experiments that will further explore your ever-expanding potential.   4 Give this growing ability of endurance a chance to accomplish its purpose, which is to make you a mature and complete person, lacking nothing, fully equipped for your joy and mission.  Take a deep breath.  1.   The struggle is the valuable part of our process  It is only in the struggle that we develop endurance and courage. Endurance without judgment gives us the creative space that allows us to learn how to build a glorious life and a karis relationship with God. Keep in mind that our most productive struggle is against our Idol Self — not against others or  against the Creation. Our pride wants to “get it right” the first time, but we learn humility when we  have to   struggle to “get it right”. The humbling process of struggle disables our pride system and

5  karisfellowships.com   KF6-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  invites God to be our ally, whereas the easy achievement of goals often feeds our pride. Only when we have effectively dealt with our pride can we successfully handle the rewards of our achievements. Immanuel Kant, who is considered to be the father of modern philosophy, 8   taught that   struggle is the indispensable accompaniment of progress . 9   (Repeat) . Our popular culture has certainly strayed from that belief! Christians, however, are not bound by that culture and are invited by God to learn to  struggle well. So, let’s learn how to struggle well.  2.   The discovery and fostering of our True Self requires a lot of endurance  Any kind of growth requires a sustained effort in a consistent direction. That takes courage. For example, Karis Fellowships itself is the result of courageous, sustained effort over decades. Without the courage and endurance of several people, we would not be here. As you begin to discover your True Self, you will feel fear because you are going into the not-knowing and abandoning your search for glory. If something goes wrong, if the   path isn’t easy,   or if you are uncomfortable and feel that fear again, you will need courage to withstand the temptation to run back to old patterns of reacting. You will also need courage to endure your self-hate long enough to manage it productively, first by recognizing that you are in self-hate and then by using your KF tools. Your tools will help you hold an oriented course instead of escaping into compulsive addictive behaviors or imposing frantic claims on others and on life.  3.   Let endurance have its perfect result  What is endurance? The Greek word translated as   endurance   means to   remain under . It means to resist running away. Running away looks different for different Idol types. A mastery type runs away by self-assertion or grabbing control. A self-effacing type runs away by appeasing and complying. A resigned type just runs. It takes faith, or trust, to stand and resist running away. We learn that productive endurance is   for   us; it plays a crucial role in developing our True Self and revealing our real glory. Most of us were not trained to endure productively. We endured only to support the agenda of the people around us or to indulge their comfort — in other words, to pacify their Idol Self. This kind of endurance was not about developing our potential but about satisfying so meone else’s compulsive  needs. We suffered without any benefit to ourselves. Now, however, we have tools that make endurance beneficial and even profitable, not only for ourselves but also for this world.  Let’s switch   gears a little and look at an aspect of agape   love that is similar to endurance. The passage that describes Christian agape is found in First Corinthians, chapter 13. First of all, love is   makrothumos . 10   That is the Greek word for this quality. Makrothumos is listed first because without it we cannot develop the other qualities of love. Makrothumos means   long-tempered   as opposed to   short-tempered.   It is sometimes translated as   long-suffering . When you choose long-suffering, however, you are not choosing to just suffer for a long time. Makrothumos is strategic. It has a purpose in view and uses your discomfort to achieve that purpose.  You are learning to welcome the way that life runs all kinds of experiments on you. God uses these trials as opportunities to reveal where your trust lies, where your heart is. Ultimately, your goal is to learn to be long-tempered no matter how you feel — to refuse the easy path of giving in to your tensions; to resist running away; and, instead, to be strategic in thought, word, and action. When your True Self is connected to the Holy Spirit, you can trust God when others are panicking, snatching, controlling, or hysterical. You know what that looks like — going out of control to get control. It is fear, once again, paralyzing people and driving them to mindlessly resist, manipulate, or attack.

6  karisfellowships.com   KF6-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Do you want to live without fear? The Apostle John tells us that only love can cast out fear. 11   In Karis Fellowships, we are learning to be people of no fear who are becoming the love of God in this sorry world.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, help me allow Your love to cast out my fear. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Bible teaching? ” )  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider a situation in which you cannot love yourself or someone else.  (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider a situation in which you cannot love yourself or someone else , how does it feel?   (Pause)  Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable. Recognize with compassion whatever you may be experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. We often flush thoughts and feelings from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us. Breathe, and hold your thoughts and feelings up to the light as you   consider a situation in which you cannot love yourself or someone else .   (Pause)   Give yourself permission now to explore your thoughts and feelings without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider this situation in which you cannot love yourself or someone else.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might recognize what frustration or hatred feels like in your body. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider this situation in which you cannot love yourself or someone else .   (Pause)   Have you judged yourself or this situation as good or evil?   What are your reasons? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Is your experience a regular pattern in your life?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something — of loss, of deprivation, of others, or of yourself? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling

7  karisfellowships.com   KF6-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  like you feel when   you cannot love. You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)  You can observe and learn something from what you have just experienced. When a fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause and take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the integration? ” )  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank you for this time together of healing and training. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our glory and to the truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?” )  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  The KF book study of   Honor, Patronage, Kinship, and Purity   (HPKP) by Dr. David deSilva is in progress. This study has helped many KF members explore the integrity of their own Christian beliefs in the context of first century values and culture.  1   John Main,   Silence and Stillness in Every Season: Daily Readings with John Main , ed. Paul Harris (New York: Continuum International Publishing Group, 1997), 2.  2   John Main,   Monastery without Walls: The Spiritual Letters of John Main , ed. Laurence Freeman (London: Canterbury Press Norwich, 2006), 32.  3   1 Cor. 16:22; Rev. 22:20.  4   Breathe on Me, Breath of God   by Edwin Hatch   (1835-1889),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=M5keJHZdWYM .  5   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).  6   Dr. Roger Callahan, “TFT Stress Buster Tapping Class - Learn to Use TFT Tapping,” Callahan Techniques, accessed  April 24, 2016,   www.rogercallahan.com/learn-to-tap.php . Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  7   "Robert Louis Stevenson Quotes, ”   Goodreads , accessed April 24, 2016,  www.goodreads.com/author/quotes/854076.Robert_Louis_Stevenson .  8   Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy , s.v."Immanuel Kant," last modified January 25, 2016,  plato.stanford.edu/entries/kant .  9   Will Durant,   The Story of Philosophy: The Lives and Opinions of the W orld’s   Greatest Philosophers from Plato to John Dewey   (New York: Pocket Books, 2006), 366.  10   1 Cor. 13:4.  11   1 John 4:18.

title: KF7 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF7-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF7 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.”   (Psalm 139:23 – 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  We are exploring the   Maranatha Meditation   taught by John Main, OSB. 1   You can search the web for his work and history. He writes:  The all- important aim in Christian meditation is to allow God’s mysterious and silent  presence within us to become more and more not only   a   reality, but   the   reality which gives meaning, shape and purpose to everything we do, to everything we are. 2  We begin this meditation by sitting upright and as still as we can. If you are ill, fatigued, or holding a baby, sit propped up with pillows. Breathe as you lightly close your eyes.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Continue to breathe while I offer a little clarification.   Maranatha   is an Aramaic prayer from the Bible. 3   It can be translated three ways:   Our Lord is coming! . . . Our Lord has come. . . . Come, O Lord!   Silently, within your own mind, slowly say the word MAA-RAA-NAA-THAA during the meditation time. Some members find it helpful to move their lips as they attend to the word. If your mind wanders, gently draw it back to the word. We will focus on   maranatha   for three minutes, and I will remind you of this word at the start of each minute.   Let’s b egin. MAA-RAA-NAA-THAA.   (Pause for 3 minutes, restating the word at the beginning of each minute)  Now pause. Take a few deep breaths and open your eyes. Gently bring your mind back to the meeting. John Main recommends that we meditate for twenty to thirty minutes twice each day.  Our hymn and prayer is   Teach Me Thy Way , by Benjamin R. Ramsey.  Teach me Thy way, O Lord, teach me Thy way!  Thy guiding grace afford, teach me Thy way!  Help me to walk aright, more by faith, less by sight;  Lead me with heavenly light, teach me Thy way!   4  Take a deep breath.

2  karisfellowships.com   KF7-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we are considering KF Confession 2:  We abandoned the glory that was ours, designed for us by our Creator.  For this meeting, you might want to have your   Two Paths Flowchart   handy.  Our only hope of recovery is in Jesus. He gives us an alternative to worshipping our fears and obeying our compulsions. It is His resurrection, His example, and His love that empower us to courageously learn to be people of no fear.   To follow Christ’s example , we must courageously learn to love. There is no other way to follow Him. Thankfully, we have the Bible, the Holy Spirit, and a community of fellow believers to help us heal and teach us how to love.  Let’s review some   of our KF tools.  1.   The Meeting Preparation Guide  Someone pointed out that the   Meeting Preparation Guide   is like a progress chart that measures how  far we have come and how much we still need to grow. That’s one reason why the guide is so valuable.  As you fill out the guide, you learn to tell your real story, and you may experience more peace because you are getting in touch with reality. The guide helps you celebrate your progress and admit where you need more training. Sharing what you learn about yourself is a confession to God and to the group. Genuine confession strengthens the True Self. Be sure to keep your finished guides so that one day you can look back and see how far you have come.  2.   Our manuals  The Bible and the book   Neurosis and Human Growth   are our manuals in KF. 5   When you read your Bible, consider how what you are reading brings into spiritual perspective Dr. Horney's description of our battle with neurosis.  3.   Mindfulness and meditation practice  We are now learning the   Maranatha Meditation , but you also have the   3-Minute Breathing Space   in your toolbox. 6  4.   Worksheets and guides  Tools like the list   Love or Pride?   help you untangle your reactions and recognize the underlying fear.  5.   The Tapping Protocol 7  We introduced tapping a couple of weeks ago. If you would like to see a video demonstration, go to  Alison’s tapping and TAT videos   on YouTube. The   Tapping Protocol   script can be found on the KF  website under the   Toolbox   tab.  6.   The Two Paths Flowchart

3  karisfellowships.com   KF7-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  This tool helps you confront the secret life of your Idol — a secret life of continual anxiety, judgments, hurt, and storytelling, all of which lead to chaotic outcomes. You can use the flowchart to trace these outcomes back to their beginnings and then to explore how you might redirect your precious energy toward healthier outcomes.  Take out your   Two Paths Flowchart . I hope that you have added a printed copy to your KF ring binder.  This flowchart starts with an event. Events happen to everyone all the time. Events are those experiments that we have been talking about. Some events feel good, and some feel bad, but that   doesn’t mean tha t the events   are   good or bad. It only means that we have feelings about them. Perhaps you have now learned that your feelings are untrustworthy guides for judging good and evil.  The Idol Self is driven by fear, and it reacts with judgment. When we are surrounded by various experiences and common life events that threaten our search for glory, our Idol Self reacts by blaming our circumstances or other people; it is unwilling to give up its illusions about what it deserves or how life should be. The True Self, on the other hand, recognizes that life is full of all kinds of events; it knows that, with training and with God, it is fully capable of successfully handling whatever comes. It is only through our cooperation with the love of God   residing in the True Self that we can successfully navigate life’s  events.  Try not to be discouraged at this point if you find yourself living on the lower path of judgment. Nancy has not met a single person who, seeing this flowchart for the first time,   has said, “Isn’t it marvelous? I am consistently living on the upper path!”   We live on the lower path for understandable reasons. In the coming weeks, you will learn how to begin moving from the lower path, which is the path of constant judgments and fear, to the upper path, which is the path of mindful observation and love. You will learn how to move from your sinking ship to a ship that floats.  Remember that you cannot use all of the KF tools all of the time. Schedule your own KF training time this week and take one of the following small steps toward your liberty and potential:  1.   Read again or listen to the introduction and first chapter of   Neurosis and Human Growth . 8   Listening to a book can expand our understanding of the material, and you might explore that option using a program like   Audible . 9  2.   Review the chapters in the book that describe your neurotic solution, and you might read chapters 12 – 16. Begin making a short list of the kinds of events that are likely to send you down the judgment path.  3.   Use your   Meeting Preparation Guide   to record events and your reactions to those events. You might review what you have written on your earlier guides and see how far you have already come.  4.   Schedule time to read the   Expanded Version   of the teaching notes or email KF admin and ask for the  KF Compass , which regularly delivers portions of the   Expanded Version   to your email.  5.   Practice one of your tools. You might tap or, perhaps, review an event using the flowchart.  Remember, any effort toward investing in your True Self is success. Let me say that again: any effort is success. Just showing up for your meeting is success. You are not looking for perfection. You are looking

4  karisfellowships.com   KF7-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  for slow, small, but steady progress.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, show me where to take time to practice my KF training. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox? ” )  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s continue to explore   KF Confession 2:  We abandoned the glory that was ours, designed for us by our Creator.  When you find yourself in a time of endurance, you often feel fear, which can present itself as frustration or anger. Courage is the ability to endure that fear while you make oriented choices. Your times of mindful endurance then become productive because whenever you endure your fear, you grow your courage, and this leads to more oriented outcomes. Courage is like a muscle; it is strengthened through exercising endurance in challenging situations. Developed courage is essential if you are to become a person of no fear. Here are two points that we might keep in mind.  1.   Endurance requires long-tempered love  Endurance is not forever even though it may feel like it at times. We need endurance when we are in situations that examine our commitment, our trust, and our trustworthiness. Last week we learned about love being long-tempered rather than short-tempered. We are growing into long-tempered endurance that can resist compulsive reactions to uncomfortable and revealing events — those life experiments, those days of judgment or examination. Your KF training empowers you; you no longer find yourself without choices. Instead of giving in to the dictates of your fear, you can choose to endure your discomforts productively and respond with love and orientation.  2.   People differ in what they must learn to endure  Always remember with compassion that people differ in what they find hard to endure. What requires dogged endurance for one Idol type may be easy for another. Our job is to help each other, but we are not called to help each other indefinitely. Some people need to find themselves without help in order to feel desperate enough to give up their idolatry and get into training. Not even God will continue to support us if we persistently hesitate and waver in our obedience to Him and consistently choose the path of our Idol Self.  Let’s   return to our study of the letter from James. This is Nancy ’s   translation of   James 1:5 – 8 .  5 But if anyone should find themselves lacking practical skill in situations, let them ask God about it. God generously gives practical help to everyone, and He gives without throwing their dysfunction back in their faces to shame and belittle them. God will give wisdom to the one who asks for skill to deal with situations,   6 but that person must ask in faith. In other words, they must be ready to act upon what God shows them, without any

5  karisfellowships.com   KF7-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  hesitancy or wavering; for the one who wavers is like the surf of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.   7 Such persons ought not to imagine that they will receive anything from the Lord,   8 being double-minded, or of two spirits, and, therefore, unstable in all their ways.  Take a deep breath.  1.   Double-minded people cannot receive guidance from God  We see in this passage that God is willing to give to everyone the wisdom they need to become accomplished, integrated, and fully equipped. Each time you fall into a trial or an experiment, you discover areas where you need wisdom. Discovering these areas is essential for your growth. God is always willing to teach you, but you can forfeit the benefit of His guidance by being double-minded and holding open the option to judge according to your own understanding. If you find yourself continually changing your mind or choosing misorientation, it means that you are still, as yet, without conviction. Either you need more training and healing, or you need a more thorough commitment.  Every kingdom divided against itself will fall. 10   When you are acting out of neurosis, you are a divided kingdom. You vacillate between your allegiance to the Idol and your allegiance to love. You are not yet willing to take responsibility for how you perpetuate your suffering through your own choices and reactions. When your commitment wavers and is unstable, the Lord really cannot guide you to wisdom. Your house is built on sand. 11   God would love to help you, but your pride stands in His way.  2.   We have a choice as to how we will live  When we commit to learning how to live on the upper path of the Two Paths Flowchart, our lives really do become more peaceful, more loving, and more authentic. We also discover that we have more self-control. Just as we have been trained to default to the path of judgment, we can retrain ourselves, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, to choose the path of love. You really can do it. The Bible says you can, and empirical research says you can.  Our second Bible reading for this lesson is   Proverbs 3:5 – 7 . You might look at this passage in the context of the whole chapter, which offers encouragement and all kinds of promises to those who choose to become single-minded and learn wisdom. Here   is Nancy’s version of   this text:  5 Make sure that all your motivation begins with trust in God. Do not lean on your own understanding.   6 In all your choices be mindful of Him and He will straighten your path toward oriented outcomes.   7 Do not be wise in your own estimation; fear God and turn away from doing damage.  Take a deep breath.  The quality of your relationship with God is the result of your choices. If you choose to lean on your own understanding, being wise in your own estimation and doing things your own way, you will stay on the lower path of the flowchart and disconnect yourself from God. But if you are mindful of what God values and honor His way of doing things, you will remain on the upper path and will learn to trust God with all your heart.   Your greatest experiment in this world is to choose to live your life God’s way and see what  happens. Fear God by obeying Him as the Boss. Let Him make your path straight. Choose today whom you will serve. 12   You really do have a choice. Trusting in   God’s   way of doing things is how godly choices are made.

6  karisfellowships.com   KF7-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, in one area of my life this week, remind me to acknowledge You as the Boss and trust Your way of doing things. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Bible teaching? ” )  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider a situation in which you want, so badly, to lean on your own understanding. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider a situation in which you want, so badly, to lean on your own understanding , how does it feel?   (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to rest in your awareness. Breathe, and hold your experience up to the light. Observe whatever you may be experiencing as you   consider a situation in which you want, so badly, to lean on your own understanding .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider this situation in which you want, so badly, to lean on your own understanding.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what craving, anger, or anxiety feels like in your body. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider this situation in which you want, so badly, to lean on your own understanding .   (Pause)   Do you tend to judge this situation as good or evil?   (Pause)   Is this judgment a regular pattern in your life? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something — of loss, of hurt, of others, or of yourself? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you do when they have wanted, so badly, to lean on their own understanding. You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   You might remember that feelings are just chemical reactions in your body bringing you information. With training, you can choose what you will do with that

7  karisfellowships.com   KF7-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  information.   (Pause)   Breathe with compassion for yourself and for all those who long to lean on their own understanding. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the integration? ” )  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are so grateful for this time together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to the truth about our faith in You. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath. title: KF8 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF8-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF8 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.”   (Psalm 139:23 – 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  If you are benefiting from this ministry, we invite you to return a financial gift in proportion to your financial resources. This is   karis , the Greek word for grace, which we now understand as a relationship with others based on mutual generosity. In KF,   we learn to respond to God’s gifts by returning a gift that  represents our gratitude. We also learn to respond to one another with karis generosity. Find   Give a Gift  at the top right of the KF website home page. You can offer a one-time gift to Karis Fellowships, or you can select the option to make an automated donation.  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  We might thank Alison, who created the original Karis Fellowships website as a gift to the KF community. Alison has donated much of her time and skill to the organization and design of this ministry. She and her husband explored the mindfulness training that was offered in their community and then brought to KF some of the practices that they had learned, including the   3-Minute Breathing Space   and a prototype of the   FAITH Process . We are grateful for their contribution. We recommend that you seek extra mindfulness training in your own community and online. Websites like   meditationoasis.com   and   headspace.com   may  help you develop a practice that works for you. You can also look for guided meditations on YouTube.  The Maranatha Meditation 1  Begin by sitting still and as upright as you can.   Breathe as you lightly close your eyes.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Silently, within your own mind, begin to slowly say the word   MAA-RAA-NAA-THAA .   Maranatha   is Aramaic for   Come, Lord . Pay attention to the word as you explore what works for you. You might try saying two syllables on the inhale and two on the exhale. Or, if you wish, you can pace your breath and attend to all four syllables on the inhale and to all four syllables on the exhale. You can explore that now.   (Pause for 30 seconds)   To help you endure, I will remind you of the word   maranatha   once during our three-minute meditation. Relax into the word as you continue to observe your breath, and begin.   (Pause for 3 minutes with a reminder of the word at 1.5 minutes)  Pause. Take a deep breath and open your eyes. Gently draw your mind back to the meeting. You might begin practicing this meditation for twenty minutes in the morning and then again later in the day.

2  karisfellowships.com   KF8-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Remember that the struggle to focus strengthens your ability to be mindful, just as the struggle to lift a weight makes you strong.  Our hymn,   Teach Me Thy Way, O Lord   describes normal life events that happen to everyone. Mindfulness training helps us endure productively   so that in all of life’s events we can respond by doing things God’s  way.  When I am sad at heart, teach me Thy way!  When earthly joys depart, teach me Thy way!  In hours of loneliness, in times of dire distress,  In failure or success, teach me Thy way! 2  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  (Optional)   When we find ourselves in experiments and events, the key to our healing is to observe, confess, and work on our own misorientation. We cannot heal ourselves if we are focused on the misorientation of others.  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we are exploring KF Confession 2:  We abandoned the glory that was ours, designed for us by our Creator.  Pull out your   Two Paths Flowchart   once again. We would like to remind you to keep practicing the tools that you have learned so far. You now have several tools to help you maintain your orientation to God and to your True Self.   It’s   not enough to have the tools in your toolbox, however. You must develop the skill to use those tools, and that takes time and practice.  Let’s review some   points that will help clarify our mission in Karis Fellowships.  1.   Our purpose in KF  You are working to reclaim the glory that your Creator intended for you. You are His child, an heir of  your Father’s house , but the world, the flesh, and the devil still hold you captive. 3   In order to reveal His glory, you will need to co-labor with God to ransom the creature that He created, which is your True Self. Co-laboring with God in that process may require much of your resources right now. The ransom of your True Self cost Jesus a great deal, but Jesus thought you were worth it. Do you? Our book,   Neurosis and Human Growth ,   tells us why we often do not think we are worth it. 4   So, part of our work in Karis Fellowships is to develop a new vision of ourselves as individuals who are of inestimable value to God and have an essential mission in this material world.  2.   The Two Paths Flowchart — living in love or judgment  Over the next few weeks, we will be looking closely at how to use this flowchart.  3.   The event or the day of judgment

3  karisfellowships.com   KF8-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  James refers to events as   experiments ,   and we can also apply John’s phrase,   the   day of judgment . The purpose of these pesky life experiments is not to condemn or shame us; the purpose of these experiments is revelation. Life events examine and reveal the quality of our trust and our trustworthiness. We can welcome these experiments because   God must   reveal the problem before He can heal the problem .   (Repeat)   And we want to heal.  4.   Feelings are not meant to be our primary motivators  Feelings are just feelings. They are untrustworthy guides for knowing what is good and evil. We know this because the same event can affect people in different ways. Some will judge an event as good, and others will judge the same event as evil. Nancy has seen people completely change their own evaluation of an event after a brief discussion or after doing some healing work. It seems like a miracle. What twenty minutes ago felt so evil now feels good to that same person.  5.   The fear of death is the source of all unhealthy fear  All living things react to the environment. If your environment presents a threat, you will react. These reactions often spring from the fear of losing your idealized life. This fear is the fear of death. The author of Hebrews writes that, without Jesus, all human creatures are enslaved to the fear of death throughout their lives. The fear of death, and the compelling need to escape that fear, is like a black hole that sucks all the energy and delight from our lives.   Let’s look at   Hebrews 2:14 – 15   in   Nancy’s  translation.  14 Therefore, since the children share in flesh and blood, Jesus Himself likewise also shared the same limitations so that through death He might render powerless the one who had the power of death, that is, the devil or accuser,   15 and might liberate those who have been enslaved all of their lives because of their fear of death.  Take a deep breath.  When our search for glory is endangered, we experience intense feelings of frustration and threat; when we imagine that we have escaped our fear and are on our way to an idealized glory, we feel euphoric. Both of these reactions, however, are rooted in fear. Whether we are afraid or euphoric, the deep fear of death keeps our beautiful energy focused on saving our lives and our pride. We then unconsciously force that focus onto those around us. We try to conscript them into supporting us in our efforts to save the life of our Idol Self. Unfortunately, by conscripting others, we sometimes succeed in getting our own way, and this encourages us to believe that we have saved ourselves and escaped from death. As long as we are able to maintain this illusion, we are content. What a poor vision of happiness! Life is full of difficulties and mishaps. Happiness is not found in avoiding such things, but rather in knowing how to handle them.  Nancy’s   email address is   nancy@karisfellowships.com . This week, you are invited to send her a list of your  three greatest fears. She will send you an email to remind you. We will look at these fears anonymously in the weeks ahead and see what we can learn. How exciting!  Our prayer might go something like this:  Great Counselor, show me my real fears. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF8-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s continue with   James 1:5 – 8 . This is   Nancy’s   translation.  5 But if anyone should find themselves lacking practical skill in situations, let them ask God about it. God generously gives practical help to everyone, and He gives without throwing their dysfunction back in their faces to shame and belittle them. God will give wisdom to the one who asks for skill to deal with situations,   6 but that person must ask in faith. In other words, he or she must be ready to act upon what God shows them without any hesitancy or wavering; for the one who wavers is like the surf of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.   7 Such persons ought not to imagine that they will receive anything from the Lord,   8 being double-minded, or of two spirits, and therefore, unstable in all their ways.  Take a deep breath.  1.   Success is often more spiritually unstable than distress  Remember that in order to develop the True Self we need a long-tempered endurance. No matter what happens around you, your real goal is to develop the long-tempered endurance that will equip you to live your life gloriously. We often think that we need endurance most in times of fear or loss, but   that’s   not always the case. God usually has our attention in times of failure and during what our hymn calls   “times of dire distress” . 5   It is in times of success that the quality of our training is revealed, and when we experience success — when we get what we want, when we feel euphoric — we need to be especially mindful and aware. How often have we seen so-called successful people fail to build trustworthy, fulfilled lives?  You might imagine that you will naturally learn to handle success productively and find peace with the new status quo, but this also requires training. Success brings unprecedented experiences and changes that create tension, and this tension causes our Idol Self to react. Your ability to handle  success with success is directly proportional to your ability to endure that tension. Let’s take as an  example the tension that we experience when we are successful in our personal development. For mastery type Christians, to show heartfelt kindness or mercy is success, but in order to maintain this positive direction they must endure the tension that comes from forfeiting an opportunity to conquer and punish. When self-effacing types successfully stand up for themselves or assert their preferences, they must endure the tension of feeling selfish; they must resist the compulsion to give in, please, or apologize. When resigned types dare to touch an area of self-awareness and make some progress toward feeling their real feelings, they must endure the craving to escape into stagnation and numbness. God is regularly seeking to stretch your ability to live gloriously, but He can only do this if you are able to productively endure the tension created by change. God wants to explore with you as, together, you discover your potential. You are an eternally developing creature who is learning the ways of eternity.  2.   The basic problem is our commitment — are we committed to our Idol or to God?  Trusting G od’s wisdom   requires training — training that prepares you to courageously act on the wisdom He offers. God cannot train you, however, if you are still committed to the judgment path;

5  karisfellowships.com   KF8-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  you will refuse to follow through on His way of doing things. But remember this: if you continue to harbor divided loyalties, you are not simply choosing between judgment and love; at the heart of your choice is this question — Who is your God?  When we are committed to our Idol Self, we are committed to another god, and if we obey the fear and compulsive demands of the Idol, we are obeying another god.   It’s   not hard to see that the Idol Self is just another god, so whenever you follow its guidance, you   are breaking God’s first  commandment:   “ Thou shalt have no other gods before Me. ” 6   When God confronts that problem in you, He is doing you a huge favor.  3.   Two spirits are two masters  When we are torn between two masters, our instability becomes readily apparent, even to ourselves. We are not to be trusted. We talk about being a Christian, but neither the quality of our words nor our lives reflect that glorious new birth. We have not yet agreed within ourselves that God is who He says He is — the Creator and the only Lawgiver and Judge. We are not convinced that opposing Him has real consequences. We would rather gratify our pride than access and enjoy God as our ally.  4.   Karis Fellowships gives us tools that help us become single-spirit people  Here is another way of describing our goal in KF: we are working toward becoming   single-spirit   people. No one can serve two masters. 7   If you find that your life is full of unstable habits and relationships, if you make decisions but are regularly unable to follow them through, if you commit to training and then refuse to train, or if you have taken the name of Christian but choose to do your own thing, then you are like the surf of the sea, tossed back and forth by the winds of circumstances and feelings. 8  Would you put your trust in that kind of sea? Would you trust that kind of person?  Hopefully, you are now willing to admit that you are tempted to serve two masters. You might tell God this week that you are ready to give up trying to be God and are willing to train your woefully underdeveloped True Self. When you give up the life of trying to be your own god and doing your own thing, you will be free to pursue your real potential as a glorious creature in karis relationship with the real God, who is love. This love is beyond all that you can ask or think, but it is not beyond what you can experience.  Our prayer might go something like this:  God and Creator, I am ready to be Your creature in karis relationship. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your stillness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider living as a glorious creature serving the real God in a created world.  (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process

6  karisfellowships.com   KF8-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Feelings  As you   consider living as a glorious creature serving the real God in a created world , how does it feel?  (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you may be experiencing, and breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush real feelings or thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us.   (Pause)   Breathe, and hold your experience up to the light as you   consider living as a glorious creature serving the real God in a created world . Give yourself permission now to explore without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Lovingly notice what it is doing as   you consider living as a glorious creature serving the real God . What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might notice what disbelief or potential feels like in your body. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  living as a glorious creature serving the real God in a created world . Does that feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe.   (Pause)   Do you judge the idea of glorious living as good or bad? What are your reasons? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have   considered   living as a glorious creature serving the real God in a created world.   You are a human creature, and you are not alone in your feelings.   (Pause)   When a fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting. Breathe and allow yourself to feel some compassion for everyone who embraces the possibility of real glory. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are so grateful for this time together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our glory and to the truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF8-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  There is a lot to learn and relearn as we renew our minds and thinking. You may wish to download and print out these teachings so that you can review them during your quiet moments, or you might ask admin to email you the   KF Compass . You may also find it helpful to play back the recordings of these meetings and capture a few ideas to carry with you during the week.  1   John Main,   Monastery without Walls: The Spiritual Letters of John Main ,   ed. Laurence Freeman (London: Canterbury Press Norwich, 2006), 32.  2   Teach Me Thy Way, O Lord   by   Benjamin Mansell Ramsey (1849 – 1923),   youtu.be/FmY6848ZQeo .  3   James 3:15.  4   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).  5   Teach Me Thy Way, O Lord   by   Benjamin Mansell Ramsey (1849 – 1923),   youtu.be/FmY6848ZQeo .  6   Exod. 20:3.  7   Matt.6:24.  8   James 1:6.

title: KF9 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF9-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF9 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.”   (Psalm 139:23 – 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  After you have practiced the   Maranatha Meditation   for a while, you will find it a helpful tool when your Idol employs its tactics to derail your mind. For example, when self-hate torments you with anxiety or condemning thoughts, when your mind is wasting energy on vain imaginations or obsessive thinking, when you feel a craving to default to old unhealthy patterns, or when you are too excited or euphoric —  in all these situations,   Maranatha (O   Lord, come!)   can   give you some peace from the stories and thoughts that lead to more suffering.  The Maranatha Meditation 1  Begin by sitting still and as upright as you can. Prop yourself up with pillows if you cannot sit up comfortably. Breathe as you lightly close your eyes.   (Pause)   Your mind may not be focused right now, but  don’t let that   discourage you. One of the benefits of meditation is that it provides a safe opportunity to practice endurance. So, if you feel frustrated, congratulate yourself for exercising endurance. Try not to judge the level of your meditation skills. Meditation is a discipline that requires training and patient effort. Be kind to yourself as a learner.  Now, silently, within your own mind, begin to slowly say the word MAA-RAA-NAA-THAA. If your mind wanders, gently draw it back to the word, without judgment. To help you endure, I will remind you of the word once during our three-minute meditation. Relax into the word as you breathe, and begin. MAA-RAA- NAA-THAA.   (Pause for 3 minutes with a reminder of the word after 1.5 minutes)  Pause, and listen to our hymn and prayer,   Teach Me Thy Way, O Lord .  When doubts and fears arise, teach me Thy way!  When storms o’erspread   the skies, teach me Thy way!  Shine through the cloud and rain, through sorrow, toil and pain;  Make Thou my pathway plain, teach me Thy way!   2  Take a deep breath and open your eyes. You might begin practicing this meditation for twenty minutes

2  karisfellowships.com   KF9-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  each morning and then again later in the day. If you have little ones who need you, practice for five minutes several times a day. Use a timer or a meditation app to help you relax and disengage from a sense of passing time.  In a more precise and elegant form of English than we now speak, to address someone using the word  thou   indicated intimacy and a close family relationship. To address someone as   you   was considered formal and polite.   Isn’t it strange that   today   thou   sounds so formal and so religious, when in reality it describes a very close human relationship?  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits,   ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   this training ?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month our focus is on KF Confession 2:  We abandoned the glory that was ours, designed for us by our Creator.  Over the last few weeks we have been looking at the   Two Paths Flowchart . This tool helps us recognize the sequence of choices that lead from an event to an outcome. Using the same amount of energy, we  can choose the path toward God’s glory or the path toward the Idol’s glory. The lower path charts the  mechanical,   programmed reactions that we depend upon for saving our Idol’s life. However, we can train  ourselves to take the upper path of love, even when we feel the fear of death. Here are some points to consider as you explore this flowchart.  1.   Judging good or evil  If an event supports our search for idealized glory, we will automatically judge it as good; if an event threatens our idealized glory, we will automatically judge it as evil. When the Idol is threatened, we feel the fear of death. We then react like terrified wild animals, and we react in predictable ways. Our reactions feel rational and authentic, but in reality, we are simply defending our Idol Self.  2.   Train hard, fight easy  The   Two Paths Flowchart   helps us explore step by step the path that we have taken. With diligent training, we can change our path.  3.   Our emotional reactions are not trustworthy guides for making decisions  Our feelings often distort our perception of reality, and it might be distressing to learn that we cannot depend on our emotional reactions to help us make healthy decisions. At this stage in our training, all immediate and extreme reactions are suspect. If an event frightens us into reacting with rage, hurt, or stagnation, we have already told a story about why that event is evil. If an event relieves us from the fear of death, we feel euphoric and have a story in place about why the event is good. In euphoria, we become mindless and forget that we have limitations. We forget that in every situation we have a Lord to serve.  4.   Judgments are based on our own legal systems, or law  The more we derive our sense of self-confidence from fulfilling our shoulds, taboos, and claims, the

3  karisfellowships.com   KF9-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  more we are compelled to mindlessly react to adverse events, and the force of our emotions reveals how badly we need to protect our sense of security, self-value, and pride. The more committed we are to the Idol, the less flexible we are when we fall into various experiments. So, you can pretty well determine the level of your commitment to the Idol Self by how rigidly you react to   life’s events . Do you find yourself reacting in the same way over and over again? Are you, as James says, unstable in your ways and easily unbalanced by events?   3   The inability to control your reactions tells you  something about the Idol’s grip on your life.  The Idol pursues its imagined glory with secret strategies, and like any secret system, it keeps its members in the fog about what is really going on. The book study invites you to come out of the fog of neurosis with its deceit and illusions. Coming out of the fog is a difficult process, but with humility and training you can learn to watch for signs of idolatry, such as compulsive and habitual reactions, inflexibility, and extreme emotions. It is in your best interest to be on the watch. You are in a position of strength when you know your enemy.  5.   There is no condemnation in Jesus 4  There are lots of reasons why you have learned to react as you do, but knowing those reasons is not as helpful to you   as finding the solutions. That’s why you are in Karis Fellowships— to find solutions. Remember that you are not designed to motivate yourself with judgments and self-condemnation. By doing so, you just set up the judgment path again. Accept that you are dealing with a combination of healthy and unhealthy forces; you are both growing and resisting growth. Be patient with yourself. Work on your weaknesses and acknowledge your strengths. Take time to work, and take time to rest.  6.   Your fears correlate to your Idol type  Perhaps you can already see the correlation between your fears and your Idol type. Self-effacing types fear taking charge of their own life and feel safer as victims. Mastery types fear vulnerability and loss of control. Resigned types fear restriction, imposition, and any change, even in themselves.  7.   The fight with the Idol Self is the right fight  Paul felt so much self-confidence at the end of his life that he could say,   “ I have fought the good fight. ” 5   (Repeat)   The good fight is the right fight, and   defending your Idol’s pride system is not   the right fight. The right fight is against your Idol Self. Through your work in KF, you are fighting on the side of truth and the True Self — and the God of truth is fighting for you. You are probing the secret strategies of the real enemy, your Idol Self.   Learn to look for progress, not perfection.   (Repeat)   Be patient with your own process.  Thanks to everyone who sent Nancy a list of their three greatest   fears, but if you haven’t   done so yet, there is still time to send them. Email Nancy at   nancy@karisfellowships.com . We will take a look at our  fears in the next few weeks.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, reveal the fears that harm me. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING

4  karisfellowships.com   KF9-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s look again at KF Confession 2:  We abandoned the glory that was ours, designed for us by our Creator.  We will move away from James for a while and talk about the glory that we have abandoned. You were designed to express the glory of God through manifesting the truth of who He created you to be — and that truth is your glory in Christ. Through your KF training, you will begin to reveal this glory that is uniquely yours.  1.   Learn to live joyfully in the material world as a spiritual creature  Whether you are consciously aware of it or not, your True Self desires to live in continual communion and correspondence, or co-respondence, with its Creator. It was designed for that relationship, with no confusion about who the Creator is — you or God. The True Self wants to live out its life joyfully and in constant gratitude, submitting to all the limitations of being a creature while discovering the glory of what is possible.  2.   Your True Self is an eternally creative creature  You are created in the image of the Creator who creates. The person that you build and the contributions of your creative nature are gifts to heaven and to earth. When you live out of the True Self, you are undivided. From that single spirit, you will develop a deep security and peace, which will be expressed in power, a contributing livelihood, generous gratitude, and vitally connected relationships. The whole New Testament declares this potential that is yours.  3.   Our personal glory expresses the love of God in this world in a unique way  Your potential is   “ love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith ” . This pithy statement is found in First Timothy 1:5. Translation is a difficult business, but through the following paraphrase Nancy hopes to convey a fuller understanding of what Paul is saying here.  Agape love flows from a healthy mental and emotional function, from a co- understanding with God that generates goodness, and from all of the powerful reorienting influence that naturally springs out of the authority of our trustworthiness before God and our trust in Him.  In KF, we do not compare our potential with that of other people. Your potential is built on the reality of your physical body, your genetics, your energetic patterns, and your antecedents, all of which are unique and all of which carry their own limitations. Comparing yourself to others reveals your ignorance about the unique potential that each of us has.  Let’s look at a few of the qualities of love that indicate a healthy True Self. You will find a description of  these qualities on the KF handout   Love or Pride? , which you can find on the website under   Toolbox   and  Worksheets .  We learned in   chapter 13 of First Corinthians   that love is long-tempered. It is able to maintain orientation for a long period of time under adverse circumstances, but this is more than simple endurance or patience. A long temper is the fruit of having allowed endurance to accomplish its designed purpose, which is to

5  karisfellowships.com   KF9-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  make you whole, fully equipped, and lacking nothing so that you can explore your true glory. Long temper is the ability to draw on all that you have gained through productive endurance.  We also see in verse 4 that love   does kindnesses . We can choose to act kindly out of the strength of a whole, mature, and fully equipped long temper. Kindness is active goodness toward ourselves and others regardless of our feelings and regardless of the failings of others. Even when we fail in our own search for an idealized glory and then experience self-hate, we can choose to be kind.  Next,   let’s look at verse 7, which tells us that   love   covers all things . Your translation might say that love  bears all things , but we can understand this verb to mean covering, just as a roof covers a house. In other words, love covers us and love covers others. So, when we cover for each other, we show love. Out of our growing magnanimity, we can proactively choose to extend generosity. When we or someone else is misoriented, we do not judge or condemn — we cover. We do not rejoice in mistakes and foolish choices to justify our vindictive triumph or appease our self-hate. For example, when someone loses something or acts out of mindlessness, we do not grab the opportunity to act superior, to punish, or to take on a victim role; instead, we step up and minimize the damage with kindness. We gently cover for each other until we can grow.  Our prayer to God might go something like this:  You who covered for me, help me cover all things, both for myself and for others. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider how you might cover and care for yourself or for another person. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider how you might cover and care for yourself or for another person , how does it feel?   (Pause)  Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. You can honor your feelings without allowing them to master you.   (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. We often flush feelings or thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us.   (Pause)   Give yourself permission now to explore, without judgment, your real thoughts and feelings about covering. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing as you   consider how you might

6  karisfellowships.com   KF9-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  cover and care . What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you, even when you are faced with the challenge of covering. You might recognize what frustration or the long temper of mindful endurance feels like in your body. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider how you might cover and care. (Pause)   Do you judge that effort as good or evil, as a possibility or a bother?  (Pause)   What are your reasons? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   If you were to cover, are you afraid of deprivation, hurt pride, losing control, or of what you might discover about yourself? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have   considered how to cover and care for themselves or for another person.   You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   You can observe and learn something from what you have just experienced. Rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting, breathe with compassion for yourself and for others who find it difficult to authentically   cover for another person or for themselves.   Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our glory and to the truth about Your love. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   John Main,   Monastery without Walls: The Spiritual Letters of John Main ,   ed. Laurence Freeman (London: Canterbury Press Norwich, 2006), 32.  2   Teach Me Thy Way, O Lord   by Benjamin Mansell Ramsey (1849 – 1923),   youtu.be/FmY6848ZQeo .  3   James 1:8.  4   Rom. 8:1.  5   2 Tim. 4:7.

title: KF10 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF10-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF10 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.”   (Psalm 139:23 – 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Dr. Thorndyke, a character in detective fiction created about a hundred years ago, defined mindfulness as  the capacity for continuous observation   and   a habit of allowing nothing to pass without a certain amount of conscious attention . 1   In KF, we begin our mindfulness training by observing our breath. Then, as we continue to train, we learn to expand our capacity for continuous observation to include everything, both within and without, as we go through our day.  Centuries ago, some jealous teachers questioned a great teacher about the difference between his disciples and theirs. They said,   “Our disciples walk, and so do yours. They   eat, as yours do. What is the  difference?” The   great   teacher answered, “Th is is the difference. My disciples   know   that they are walking and they   know   that they are eating .” 2   By this he meant that his disciples were consciously aware of their movements and choices. They had learned to stop damaging things, forgetting things, going on autopilot, and messing things up, because they had learned the habit of allowing nothing to pass without a certain amount of conscious attention. We can learn to live like that, too.  Let’s practice the   Maranatha   Meditation . 3  Begin by sitting still and as upright as you can. Breathe as you lightly close your eyes.   (Pause)   Your mind may not be focused right now, but   don’t worry about that. It’ s better to try to meditate and to do it imperfectly than to   give up meditation because you can’t do it without some frustration. Meditation is a  discipline that requires training and practice. Be kind to yourself as a learner.  Continue your mindful observation of the breath as within yourself you begin to say the word MAA-RAA- NAA-THAA. If your mind wanders, gently draw it back to the word and the breath.   (Pause)   To help you endure, I will remind you of the word once during our three-minute meditation. Begin, and relax into the word as you breathe.   (Pause for 3 minutes with a reminder of the word after 1.5 minutes)  And pause. Your breath can function as an anchor to bring you into a present state of awareness without judgment. The   Maranatha Meditation   trains your mind to stop dashing around out of fear or euphoria.

2  karisfellowships.com   KF10-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  You learn to take charge of your body and your mind when your Idol Self feels the compelling need to fulfill its search for glory.  Our hymn and prayer is   Teach Me Thy Way, O Lord .  Long as my life shall last, teach me Thy way!  Where’er my lot be cast, teach me Thy way!  Until the race is run, until the journey’s done,  Until the crown is won, teach me Thy way!   4  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we are exploring KF Confession 2:  We abandoned the glory that was ours, designed for us by our Creator.  Over the past few weeks, we have been looking at the   Two Paths Flowchart . This tool helps us think through how we, or others, are handling an event. If we have taken the judgment path, we have reacted with fear, but it might not feel like fear at the time. Fear might feel like fatigue, rage, or an addictive compulsion. When examining your experiences and reactions, it is important to remember that the event itself is not causing the fear. The event is only revealing the fear that is already there, the fear that you already carry. Nancy has designed a guide called the   Two Paths Worksheet   to help you apply the flowchart to an event. You might like to print it out and explore it this week.  As we learn to recognize and unload our fears, we become more and more aware of the areas where we cannot trust ourselves. You might review the chapter   on your Idol type in Dr. Horney’s book , as well as chapters 12 – 16, to help you identify the situations that tempt you to react with fear, making you untrustworthy.
