Your fear reactions are based on your personal law, your   “ Ten Commandments ” . They are the shoulds, taboos, and claims that enslave you to the fear of death.   God’s co mmandments are healthy and support our true glory, but our personal commandments compel us to save   our Idol’s life   and, with it, our pride. We need to reclaim the treasure of   the glory that has been stolen from us by our Idol’s fear.  Our fears fall into three general categories — the fear of self, the fear of others, and the fear of loss, including the loss of control.  First, we fear ourselves. We fear that something is wrong with us and that this fundamental wrongness will inexorably ruin our lives. Deep down, we know that we can destroy our lives, but the fatal flaw is to believe that we cannot help it. The truth is that we actually can make choices that will produce positive outcomes.  Second, we fear people, God, or institutions. Some of us fear that others will outshine us, obstruct us, or shame us. We are afraid that they will not support us in our efforts to fulfill our imagined glory. Some of us fear that others will abandon us, reject us, or judge us. Their opinion of us is critical to our well-being.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF10-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  When others are stronger or quicker than we are, we may fear that they will impose on us and make us do things we   don’t want to do.  The last general category of fear is the fear of loss .   We may fear the loss of a loving relationship, a life- style, freedom, control, wealth of any kind, or even the loss of a sense of superiority. We are terrified of losing whatever our Idol Self values, whether mastery, love, or freedom. We are afraid that time and resources will be stolen from us. We fear the loss of our true potential.  Most of the fears that KF members identified were fears of self. This is typical of KF members and is actually quite positive. It means that you have a reasonable fear of how powerful your choices can be. You may not know how to manage those choices right now, but you are in KF because you have hope that you can learn. You are willing to be trained and are making the effort to learn courage and endurance. You are far, far above the average person in your efforts to change your life.  The Idol Self conscripts our natural fears, which are designed to promote survival, and uses those fears to defend itself when threatened. Fear is an extremely powerful motivator, and it is the only motivator that the Idol Self knows how to use. Over the years, your body has adapted to using fear as its primary motivator in all kinds of situations. You are now so accustomed to living in fear that you may be afraid to give it up; the idea of a life free from fear may actually frighten you. What will help you make choices if not fear? What will you use to justify your compulsive need to attack, appease, medicate, or withdraw? You may tell yourself the story that your misoriented choices are motivated by common sense, justice, a real need, or Christian obedience, but, in reality, they are motivated by fear. For all of us, fear is difficult both to acknowledge and to give up.  Continue to use the   Tapping Protocol   when you recognize that fear is motivating you. Through tapping you can relieve the aching need to fight or control, lie or apologize, escape or block. Calm your distress as you would calm a distressed child.  In our next lesson, we will learn how to use the   Two Paths Worksheet , which helps us analyze our reactions to people and events, and guides us to creatively consider our options. You might wish to explore this worksheet with your Karis Link.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Loving Lord, help me in the moment to recognize the fear. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  If you have your Bible with you, turn to the second chapter   of Paul’s letter to the   Philippians.  In this letter, Paul wants to remind us of the glory that we abandon when we choose the Idol Self over the real God. The Bible tells us what our glory looks like and feels like, and it describes the results of living in that glory , but we don’t believe   what the Bible says. We have not been encouraged or trained to

4  karisfellowships.com   KF10-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  understand that our true glory can be experienced now, today, here on earth. The problem is a little more sinister than that, however. We have imagined a glory that we think is better than the one designed for us by our Creator. It takes humility and courage to give up the pursuit of fulfilling our imagined glory and, like Jesus, to take up the form of a servant and pursue our real glory.  This is Nancy ’s   translation with paraphrase of   Philippians 2:5 – 11 .  5 Think within yourselves as Christ Jesus did, 6 who, though in the form of God from the beginning, led the way in not grasping for that prize of equal footing with God.   7 Instead, He stripped and emptied Himself of the form of God and took the form of a slave, becoming just like other people with creaturely limitations, and was discovered by everyone to look just like a human being.   8 He humbled Himself, becoming obedient right up to His death, the death of the cross, perhaps the humblest death of all.   9 Therefore, God super-exalted Him, much more than Jesus could have exalted Himself, and God  karissed   to Jesus the Name above all names — that is, His own reputation and authority,  perhaps God’s greatest gift— 10 in order that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, the knees of every heavenly and earthly being and of those in the underworld,   11 and every tongue should make grateful acknowledgements, with the giving of thanks, that the Lord, the Name above all names, is Jesus Christ; and all of this adds to the glory of God the Father.  Take a deep breath.  If we will choose to cultivate the same attitude of humility that Jesus had, we can follow Him to real glory. Jesus really was God, but unlike our Idol, He did not snatch at being God. Instead, He chose to be a bondservant and allowed others to experience Him as a simple human being. If we want to follow Him, we will have to come down from the lofty illusions of our imagined glory and become obedient to God to the point of what often feels like death — for that is what it takes. Obedience will feel very much like the death of our idealized dreams of personal fulfillment, but when our training in humility is complete, we will experience a resurrection just as Jesus did. God will take over the exalting part and will help you, even you, to become more than you ever dreamed possible. This is not just storytelling. We see it happening in Karis Fellowships every week.  In our last lesson, we learned that when we live out of the True Self, several things happen:  1.   We live in continual correspondence, or circulation, with the created world and the Creator.  2.   We become truly creative creatures who are bringing the glory of God into the material and spiritual world.  3.   We explore what Paul meant   when he wrote to Timothy: “The mature outcome of our message is love  from a clean heart and mind, from a good moral co-understanding with God, and an authentic, active  trust.” 5  Through the Holy Spirit living in us, the True Self has been birthed by God, our true Father; and when we produce the Fruit of the Spirit in our lives, we reveal our new family heritage. We can learn to nurture the production of this Fruit, just as we can learn to nurture the produce of a garden.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF10-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  When fruit is ripe, the harvest feeds us and everyone around us. 6   However, producing fruit, whether in a garden or in our lives, does not happen overnight. A harvest of fruit requires the intentional and consistent investment of preparation, training, time, and resources. The real business of the True Self is to provide an environment that eventually produces the Fruit of the Spirit in every situation. You are a new creation in Christ. You are no longer compelled to conform to the world with all of its conflicts, fears, and cravings, nor are you obligated to adhere to old family systems that promote and maintain futile ways of life. You  don’t have   to perpetuate the fears, misoriented choices, and secrets of your forefathers.   7   Nothing changed until Jesus came to do something new. Now, you are doing something new.   It’s   not easy to do new things, but nothing will change unless you do.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord and Creator, help me become something new. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider choosing to become something new .   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider choosing to become something new , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)  Recognize with compassion whatever you are feeling, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness, without judgment. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush feelings or thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us. Breathe, and hold your experience up to the light as you   consider becoming something new .   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider becoming something new . What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what hopelessness, terror, or inspiration feels like in your body. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider becoming something new . Does that feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe.   (Pause)   Do you judge becoming something new as good or evil, as liberty or threat?   (Pause)   What

6  karisfellowships.com   KF10-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  are your reasons? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something — of loss, of others, or of yourself?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have   considered   becoming something new.   You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   Breathe with compassion for yourself and for others who are making an effort to become something new. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time to heal and train together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our real glory and to the truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   R. Austin Freeman,   The Red Thumb Mark   (London: Collingwood Brothers, 1907), chapter XIII. Accessed 18 June, 2016,   gutenberg.net.au/ebooks/c00002.html .  2   Nhat Hanh, Thich.   The Long Road Turns to Joy: A Guide to Walking Meditation   (Berkeley: Parallax Press, 1996), 4.  3   John Main,   Monastery without Walls: The Spiritual Letters of John Main ,   ed. Laurence Freeman (London: Canterbury Press Norwich, 2006), 32.  4   Teach Me Thy Way, O Lord   by Benjamin Mansell Ramsey (1849 – 1923) ,   youtu.be/FmY6848ZQeo .  5   1 Tim. 1:5 (translated with paraphrase by Nancy Diven).  6   Gal. 5:22 – 23.  7   2 Cor. 5:17;   1 Peter 1:18.

title: KF11 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF11-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF11 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lea d me in the ways of eternity.”   (Psalm 139:23 – 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  During the past few weeks, we have been learning the   Maranatha Meditation . 1   Try to practice this meditation in the morning and again later in the day; then , when faced with life’s problems, you will  already be trained to step back and find your center. You will have the skill to be able to collect yourself and connect to God. Put a memo on your phone or on your daily schedule as a reminder to practice.  This month we will learn a new meditation practice called the   SALT Process . Nancy designed this tool to help members explore stressful events. You cannot cast your real fears onto God if you avoid knowing what those fears are. The   SALT   Process   will help you examine your fears and cast your cares onto Him. 2  The SALT Process  1.   S   is for   Skin  Let’s begin with the mindfulness   posture. Lift the top of your head toward the heavens and plant your feet or tailbone on the earth. Let your shoulders hang from that upright structure. Breathe.   (Pause)  Focus your mind on your body as the breath moves in and out.   (Pause for 20 seconds)   Notice where your skin is. Simply notice it.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Now, gather your attention to observe only what is within your own skin. If your mind wanders outside your skin — into the future, the past, a problem, or toward someone else — gently guide your mind back to what is happening in   your   body within   your  skin. Observe your experience without judgment, and breathe for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   A   is for   Assess  Bring to mind an event or an outcome that you have judged as evil. If you   can’t recall anything, think  of something good and try to imagine what the lack of that thing would be like.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  As you consider this bad or evil situation, assess on a scale of one to ten how uncomfortable you are about it. An assessment of ten would mean that you feel very distressed and have judged the situation as very bad. Observe how your body feels. Is there fatigue, tension, or restlessness?   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Where in your body do you feel these things?   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Continue to breathe and observe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF11-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  If you find that the tension or discomfort in your body is too uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting. After taking a breath or two, respectfully return to the area that is reacting. Try using a long exhaling breath or a sigh to help your body process what you are feeling.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  3.   L   is for   Look  Look for the fear behind the judgment. What makes the situation so uncomfortable? You might explore the sensations in your body and ask yourself:   What frightens me about this situation?   (Pause) Is my freedom threatened? (Pause) Will this situation cause suffering for myself or for others? (Pause) Does this situation interfere with my pride system or my search for glory? (Pause) How might this situation stir up self-hate?   Ask God to help you identify your fear.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Step back from your assessment of the event as good or evil and just look at the fear that drives that assessment. Part of your training is to learn to simply observe your fear. Fear brings you valuable information.  (Pause)   You might try welcoming the fear. Thank the fear for what it tells you about your Idol Self and for how it motivates you to train toward freedom from fear. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  4.   T   is for   Tell  Tell God about your   fear. Tell Him about your Idol’s terror and how enslaved you are   to fear. Ask Him to help you learn how to overcome your fear by directing your energy toward love. Fear is often based on lies and illusions, so you might ask God to tell you the truth about what you fear. Then, explore your fear with His guidance, and continue to breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  And now, bring yourself back into co-respondence with your environment, that which is outside your skin. Allow what is within you to calmly observe and respond to what is without. Rest, and take a few deep breaths.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  We won’t read   a hymn or prayer right now.   Let’s spend a moment   just appreciating the effort we have made to learn a new practice.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits,   ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we will begin exploring KF Confession 3:  We constructed   legal systems based on our own assessment of good and evil.  I hope that you have the   Two Paths Worksheet   in front of you. This worksheet helps you see how powerful you are.  How do we create a glorious life? Unfortunately, painful mistakes are part of that process. We cannot possibly know it all, be prepared for it all, foresee it all, and always protect our pride. In KF, we are learning to respond to our mistakes like little children. Little children   don’t   react to their mistakes with hurt pride, judgment, and self-hate. Instead, they take responsibility for their mistakes by trying something new and finding out what works.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF11-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  We know that we are in pride and self-hate when we avoid taking responsibility for our mistakes by blaming, escaping, or making up virtue stories. When pride and self-hate are driving you toward misoriented reactions and destructive outcomes, the   Two Paths Worksheet   can help guide you into the path of love. You really can learn to build new outcomes in your life.  L et’s look   together at steps 1 – 6 in the right-hand column of the worksheet under Judgment. We will use the example of   Nancy’s   own experience to help us learn how to use this worksheet.  1.   Outcome  You can begin your journey through this worksheet at any point, but often when trying to untangle a process that has resulted in anxiety, misery, or a mess, you have to begin with the outcome. You know that an outcome is misoriented when it does not reflect the Fruit of the Spirit. 3   Nancy found herself making chaotic decisions based on fear, and as James puts it, she was tossed around like the surf of the sea. 4   The quality of this outcome told her that quite recently she had taken the Judgment Path.  2.   Action  Ask yourself the question:   What did I do or avoid that produced this outcome?   As a self-effacing neurotic, Nancy acted by instantly following the advice of someone who had just given her distressing information. She started making decisions before breathing, praying, meditating, or getting counsel. Self-effacing types need to affirm their inferiority by pleasing others, seeking validation from others, and even inviting others to punish them.  3.   Rejoicing in the misorientation  This step invites you to explore the emotions that may have compelled you to act. Nancy was feeling intimidated. Self-effacing types need to imagine and focus on evidence that proves how weak and helpless they are. Mastery types need to imagine evidence that supports the illusion that they are blameless, right, in control, and have it all figured out. When that illusion is threatened, they feel rage, revenge, acute anxiety, and contempt. Resigned types try to maintain the illusion that they are free to do as they please, without any adverse consequences. When they feel disappointed, restricted, resentful, fatigued, or locked-down, they use these emotions to justify their dash for freedom. All Idol types, however, can feel defensive, irritable, and unfairly treated, or they may simply go cold when their pride system is threatened.  4.   Story  What story have you invented to explain why the situation is good or bad? Self-effacing types will tell the story that other people have more to offer than they do. They believe that they are inferior to others and that they always need support. Mastery types tell stories that demonstrate their own superiority. They must imagine that others are competitive, offensive, or stupid in order to justify their overweening ambition to win or beat others down. When resigned types feel that their freedom is threatened by events, by others, or even by their own feelings, they will tell the story that something or someone is manipulating, coercing, or imposing on them. Their story helps them rationalize their choice to stonewall, push back, or escape. Nancy calls these imagined stories   virtue stories . We invent virtue stories to justify the emotions that compel us to act. These stories make our misoriented emotions, judgments, and choices seem virtuous, realistic, and of moral value.  5.   Judging as good or evil  You are now ready to look at the judgment that you have made. Is this event good or evil? Has it supported or threatened your search for glory?

4  karisfellowships.com   KF11-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  6.   The fear of death and euphoria  Judgments are fueled by the fear of death, especially the death of our pride and dreams. This fear is experienced differently by each Idol type. The chapters in the book   Neurosis and Human Growth   that illustrate your Idol type will help you identify your particular fear of death. 5   Remember that euphoria, or the escape from the fear of death, also sets us on the Judgment Path. When an event relieves us from the fear of death, we judge it as good and our pride is restored. Euphoria is what you feel when you have been released from your fear.  Once you have worked through steps 1 – 6, you can use the   FAITH Process   to help you unload your fear of death. In the months to come, you will learn more ways to unload the burden of your fear. No one else can do that for you, and yet we often want others to take responsibility for our fear and unload the burden for us. We want to remind you again that Karis Fellowships is not a need-based ministry. It is an effort- based ministry. Changing your   life is no one’s responsibility but yours . Unloading my fear is my business, and unloading your fear is your business.  After you have made an effort to unload your fear, you might use your glorious imagination to take the Believe It Path of the left-hand column. Rather than judging something as good or bad, just believe what has happened. State what   is . Imagine what the story might be if you could lay your judgments aside. What have you learned about yourself, others, or life? What action might you take based on what you have learned? Talk with your Karis Link and enlist the imagination of others to help you. When you learn to take the Believe It Path, God will finally have the chance to show you what marvelous things He can do.  This week, you might try exploring one of your misoriented outcomes using the   Two Paths Worksheet . Recall your three greatest fears. Could one of them be driving your judgment?  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, teach me to take responsibility for my own fears. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s   dig a little deeper into KF Confession 3:  We constructed   legal systems based on our own assessment of good and evil.  We will now return to the letter from James and look at chapter 1 again. We learned that having our faith or trust tested is essential for our growth. If   we want to grow, we will welcome life’s events because they  show us where we have put our trust — whether in God or in our Idol Self.  God brings into our lives people and situations that stir up areas that need examination and healing. One of these areas is the area of wealth. We can be rich in money, skill, time, health, relationships, antecedents, and natural gifts. We can also be poor in any of those areas. Our tendency is to judge wealth or poverty as good or evil.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF11-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  This is Nancy ’s   paraphrase of   James 1:9 – 12 .  9 To the siblings of small resources, rather than feeling shame, let them proclaim their trust from their high place of living within limitations.   10 The wealthy can proclaim their trust by refusing to use their resources to circumvent their limitations; they can choose to live as lowly creatures, because the reality is that the wealthy are subject to decay, just like a flower of the grassland.   11 For we know that the sun rises with burning heat that withers the grass; its flower falls, and its attractive façade is utterly destroyed. Even so, while going along in his or her way, the person of large resources will also fade away, just like all creatures.   12 Favored   is the one who endures life’s experiments, whatever their  circumstances may be, so that being approved as genuine and trustworthy that one will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who are loving Him.  Take a deep breath.  God has told us that this world is passing away, and when we judge wealth or poverty as good or evil, we  are not seeing things from God’s perspective. 6   We often judge wealth as good because we perceive wealth as the absence of limitations. What bliss for the Idol Self to be free from limitations! Our Idol then develops an attachment to wealth as a desirable and even a necessary thing. Poverty might be defined as an extremely limited lifestyle. That makes poverty particularly evil for the Idol. The limitations imposed by poverty or loss of wealth do not allow our Idol to feel superior or free.  Perhaps we find ourselves stuck in poverty in some area of our lives. We may even choose not to access real resources because having resources is taboo and we need to feel poor. We then use our perceived poverty to justify the demands we make on ourselves and on others.  When our identity is wrapped up in wealth or poverty rather than in the love of God, we believe that we deserve accommodation from others and from life. This attachment to accommodation creates anxiety and makes us vulnerable to disappointment and resentment. When we are not accommodated, our sense of significance and self-worth is threatened, and our pride is hurt. In our search to fulfill our imagined glory, we have put our trust in some kind of wealth or in the superiority of entitlement, and when those things elude us, we feel cheated.  James warns us that when we attach to something as vulnerable as the grass, which is passing away, we set ourselves up for all kinds of disappointments. Fear of loss stagnates our lives and numbs our creativity, driving us into all kinds of misorientation and resulting in more disappointment and loss. We live in a world that is passing away, but we are depending on it for our joy. How crazy is that? As eternal creatures, we  just weren’t designed to attach to this material world.  Humble circumstances, or poverty in some area, can be glorious because people with fewer resources are invited to develop more trust in God. These people learn to be grateful for everything. They learn to live within limitations and are highly motivated to change their lives. Their hunger is stronger than their fear.  James teaches us quite a bit about wealth in his letter. He’s not against wealth, but he is against how we  use wealth to support the Idol Self. The wealthy — those who are rich in money, abilities, possessions, family background, or experiences — are to glory in humiliation by choosing to participate in the limitations experienced by the rest of the world. They can take part in activities that put them in the place of a learner, and they can acknowledge their position as fellow creatures by demonstrating trustworthiness and active

6  karisfellowships.com   KF11-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  kindness. They must circulate gifts   in proportion to their resources , or else their souls will stagnate into fear and self-hate.  In both poverty and wealth, persevering in the development of the True Self is the key to success. Through persevering in this process, we gain practical experience both in the world and in our relationship with God. This practical experience grows our self-confidence and gives us greater authority in whatever socio- economic mission field we are designed to serve. Who gives us the stamp of approval when we persevere in the development of the True Self? Certainly God, but we too can approve the outcomes of an oriented life.  Hopefully, you will experience both poverty and wealth in many areas of your life, and at different times. Poverty can cleanse and prune the soul, while wealth can support more opportunities for exploration and service. Your goal is to be complete and lack nothing. By running your race with endurance, whether in poverty or in wealth, you are learning to wear your crown of life, in this life, with authority and love.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, teach me to glory in both poverty and wealth. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider an area of poverty or wealth in your life.   (Repeat)   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider an area of poverty or wealth in your life , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)  Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush feelings or thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us. Breathe, and hold your experience up to the light as you   consider this area of poverty or wealth in your life .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider poverty or wealth in your life.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not

7  karisfellowships.com   KF11-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what deprivation and envy or security and abundance feel like in your body. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   conside r  this area of poverty or wealth in your life . Does that feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe.   (Pause)   Do you judge poverty or wealth as good or evil, as a liberty or a threat? What are your reasons? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Is this judgment a regular pattern in your life? Does your family culture or early training influence your judgments?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something — of the not-knowing, of responsibility, or of someone taking advantage of you? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have   considered   poverty or wealth.   You are a human creature and are not alone in your feelings.   (Pause)   When a fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting. Breathe with compassion for yourself and for anyone who mindfully encounters the challenges of poverty and wealth.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time together to train and heal. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You continue to guide us to our real glory and to the truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and design. Help us to circulate with our community, with the rest of the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   John Main,   Monastery without Walls: The Spiritual Letters of John Main , ed. Laurence Freeman (London: Canterbury Press Norwich, 2006), 32.  2   1 Pet. 5:7.  3   Gal. 5:22 – 23.  4   James 1:6.  5   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).  6   1 John 2:7.

title: KF12 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF12-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF12 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  If you can, make it a habit to have some purified water with you during the meeting. Sipping water helps your body process what you are experiencing.  Mindfulness training strengthens our ability to focus with endurance. We are then able to learn the skills we need to deconstruct our judgmental reactions. If you find that you struggle with the mindfulness training, allow yourself to struggle without judging the struggle. Observe any frustration or despair that you might feel and remember that enduring those feelings is also part of your training. Give yourself the gift of compassion while you practice endurance.  Le t’s continue to practice the   SALT Process .  1.   S   is for   Skin  Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.   (Pause)   Notice where your skin is and what is beyond your skin. Perhaps your skin is sensing the air around you or the fabric of your clothing.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Now, guide your attention to observe only what is within your skin — your sensations, your thoughts, and your feelings. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   A   is for   Assess  Allow an event or an outcome to come to mind, one that you have judged as evil or as a threat. Observe how your body feels when you think about that event or situation.   (Pause)   Assess on a scale of one to ten how uncomfortable those sensations are.   (Pause)   If you feel distress or are distracted during your mindfulness practice, you might try using the Dragon Breath. The Dragon Breath is a forced exhaling breath that comes from your diaphragm, loud and strong — the sort of breath that would fog a mirror. I will demonstrate it for you.   (Demonstrate the Dragon Breath)   Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  3.   L   is for   Look  Now we can look for the fear behind the assessment. Usually, the nature and extent of our fear is irrational. We might ask ourselves:   Of whom or of what am I afraid? What threatens my Idol Self or

2  karisfellowships.com   KF12-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  my pride system? Am I experiencing self-hate or the dread of self-hate?   Ask God to help you identify your fear. Remember that your conscious fears are mostly of self, of others, or of loss and will have characteristics particular to your Idol type.   (Pause)   Observe your fear without judgment. It is bringing you information about the grip that the Idol has on your life.   (Pause)   You might try welcoming the fear and thanking it for what it is telling you about the quality of your trust, or faith. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  4.   T   is for   Tell  Tell God about your fear and, if you can, tell Him why you feel afraid.   (Pause 10 seconds)   Now, ask God to tell you the truth about what you fear and to fill this misoriented place of fear with the positive motivations of trust, hope, and love. You might wish to use a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now bring yourself back into correspondence with your environment, that which is outside your skin. While you breathe, allow what is within you to calmly observe and respond to what is without. Breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Our hymn for this confession is   All the Way My Savior Leads Me,   by Fanny J. Crosby. This hymn is especially meaningful because Fanny became blind shortly after her birth. She wrote over 8,000 hymns.  All the way my Savior leads me. What have I to ask beside?  Can I doubt His tender mercy, who through life has been my Guide?  Heav’nly peace, divinest comfort, here by faith in Him to dwell!  For I know, whate’er befall me, Jesus doeth all things well;  For I know, whate’er befall m e, Jesus doeth all things well. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we are focusing on KF Confession 3:  We constructed   legal systems based on our own assessment of good and evil.  Let’s look at the   Two Paths Worksheet   again.  When we are afraid of something or feel threatened, we are tricked into thinking that the threat is our business. Without any consideration, we go straight into judging as bad or evil whatever has threatened us. We do this because we have already allowed our hearts to attach to a certain outcome — an outcome that we have judged as good. When we experience events or when people make choices that threaten our desired outcome, we feel fear, and our fear compels us to judge. We then try to control the situation, hoping to force an outcome that will deliver us from fear and save our pride.  If we are suffering, it is natural to want to change our circumstances. However, if we try to force change that supports our Idol Self and its judgments, our efforts are egocentric, compulsive, focused on the quick

3  karisfellowships.com   KF12-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  fix, and ultimately destructive. The   Two Paths Worksheet   can help us learn how to respond to suffering in a healthy way that will lead to positive outcomes.  Let’s look at steps 7– 10 of the   Two Paths Worksheet .  7.   Event  It is our business to build new outcomes in our lives. At the bottom left of the worksheet, we can record the event that scared or delighted our Idol Self. Remember that euphoria is the ecstatic release from fear; it is the illusion of success. Whether we react with fear or euphoria, the situation is not necessarily our business — but we know through our KF training that   our fear   is certainly   our business . When we accept that our fear is our responsibility, we can observe it with compassion and then invest our beautiful energy in the kind of training that helps us make oriented choices, leading to glorious outcomes.  8.   Love believes  Next, we can access our creative mind and record under step 8 what a   long-tempered   response to our fear might be. When you have a fear reaction to an event, you might ask yourself:   Is this situation my business?   Asking yourself that question lengthens your temper, and your answer will weed out a lot of unnecessary and wasteful effort.  9.   Story  Now move up to the story. Try to list, without judgment, the simple facts that led to the event. This is objective evidence. The Idol loves its illusions and drama, but the True Self thrives on facts.  10.   Rejoicing in the truth  What have you learned about yourself, others, or life from this event? If you can lay aside your pride and the misoriented illusions that force compulsive reactions, you can look for the training opportunity in the situation. This is   rejoicing in the truth . Your feelings, too, are facts that tell you something about who you are, but you now understand that feelings are rarely reliable guides for evaluating an event. Your feelings and your choices are your business. You can honor your feelings but make choices based on objective evidence.  When we talk about business, we really mean responsibilitie s . We live in a real world that generates real business that must be attended to. All this business falls into three categories:  •   My business — which is about me, my contribution, and my role in the community.  •   Other people’s   business — which is about them, their contribution, and their role.  •   God’s   business — which is everything else.  When you are experiencing an event, observe what your mind is doing and consider this question:   Is this event   my business, other people’s business, or God’s business ?   Tell God about it. Then use the   Two Paths Worksheet   and your mindfulness training to bring yourself back to your business.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, help me stick to my business. (Repeat)

4  karisfellowships.com   KF12-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  If you start thinking about your business, you are more likely to make choices that create stable and oriented outcomes. Of course, your Idol Self does not want you to think about your business. To keep you enslaved to your search for idealized glory, the pride system of your Idol will oppose your healthy choices and manipulate you with fear. Once you have experienced real peace and joy, however, you will not be so easily manipulated. You will start fighting for your liberty.  Think about how much a hunter relies on fear or euphoria to capture his prey. He frightens it out into the open where he can shoot it, or he uses bait to lure it into a snare. His prey will be either terrified by the fear of death or feel euphoric about finding a convenient tasty morsel. Both the fear of death and the release from the fear of death are used by the hunter to dominate his prey.  As human creatures, we can be like wild animals that react to threat in mindless and preprogrammed ways. We are so habituated to reacting with fear that we rarely make healthy choices when we feel threatened. We are addicts who use fear as a drug to help us avoid facing up to the reality of our situation. If we want to recover from our addiction, we will need to identify ourselves as addicts and work to change our habits.  Let’s return to James, chapter 1.   In this passage, James combines the metaphor of hunting with the  metaphor of breeding livestock, but you won’t notice these images in English translations.   The Bible is really quite unabashed about sex. The writers are not ashamed that we, as male and female creatures, engage in procreation. They respect the power of sex by teaching us to use it gloriously.  This is Nancy’s version of   James 1:13 – 20 .  13 Let no one say when   tempted into misorientation, “I am   being   examined by God.”  Consider this: God is incapable of being tempted with evil and does not tempt anyone with evil.   14 Here is the truth: each one of us is tempted when he or she is lured away by the craving to relieve fear, just as   the hunter’s prey is lured   with bait into a snare.   15 Then when that craving has been captured and taken prisoner (or we can use the metaphor of one of our prize cows getting together with the undesirable bull next door), that craving, coupled with fear, gives birth to misorientation; and when misorientation reaches full term, it produces death as its offspring.   16 My beloved siblings, do not be led astray like unwitting prey by the bait of the hunter, or by the craving of a prize heifer.   17 The hunter’s  bait seems like a gift, and you might feel euphoria; but every gift that God gives and every benefit that promotes our true potential comes from above, coming down from the Father of Lights, with whom there is no variation or shifting shadow where a hunter could hide . You can trust the Father’s gifts.   18 Know this, my beloved siblings: the Father never intended death to be the harvest of these times of trial; rather, it is His intention to produce our True Selves by the creative process and the first principle of truth so that we would be a kind of first fruits among His creatures.   19 Now let everyone be quick to hear, like wary prey; slow to speak ( don’t make noise! ); and slow to wrath, which causes us to

5  karisfellowships.com   KF12-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  act recklessly.   20 For human wrath and judgment do not do the work necessary to achieve orientation to God.  Take a deep breath.  In this passage, we can see how our attachments, fears, and cravings trick us into taking the Judgment Path. Our fears trigger the compulsion to snatch, escape, and defend our pride. When an event feels threatening, we run out into the open like startled rabbits; and when an event presents to us an opportunity for easy gratification, we cannot resist our craving to take the bait. Whenever we act out of fear or euphoria, we are seeking to save our idealized life. The hunter is your Idol Self, full of pride, judgments, stories, fears, and self-hate, taking you prisoner and planting in your precious soul the seeds of misorientation. Those seeds flourish like weeds in your weakened soul and choke out your true life. That is the outcome of the Judgment Path.  You, however, are a child of the Father of Lights, whose intention is not to hunt you down and hurt you but to give you gifts of truth that promote your potential and glory. The Father knows your longings, and rather than using those longings to deceive you, He wants to lead you into the right pasture where the Spirit can plant within your soul the good gifts that lead to a fulfilled and glorious life.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father of Lights, train me with Your gifts   to give up my addiction to the Idol’s fears. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and, if you wish, prepare to take some notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider a situation that tempts you to take the bait. (Repeat)   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider a situation that tempts you to take the bait , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.  (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Acknowledge with compassion whatever you may be experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush our feelings or thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us. Breathe, and hold your experience up to the light as you   consider a situation that tempts you to take the bait .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not

(Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider taking the bait.  What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what craving or panic feels like, or perhaps euphoria or disgust.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to respectfully observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe. What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Is this situation a regular pattern in your life? Are you afraid of something — of being wrong, of missing out, of exertion? karisfellowships.com   KF13-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF13 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lea d me in the ways of eternity.”   (Psalm 139:23 – 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  This month we are looking at KF Confession 3:  We constructed   legal systems based on our own assessment of good and evil.  In recent lessons we have been using mindfulness training to explore our legal systems. We create legal systems because we are afraid of something. We think that these laws will help us feel safe in a chaotic world. Through the   SALT Process , you are learning to examine your legal systems by identifying an area of your life that you have judged as evil. You are also learning to look at the fear behind your judgment.  Training is always somewhat difficult because you have to tear down what you have previously built so that you can build something new. If you struggle with the mindfulness training, observe the struggle without judgment and simply allow it to be. You are building new brain pathways, and that is hard work. Your endurance gives those new brain paths time to grow. It takes a great deal of effort to forge a new path through the jungle of your mind, so think of yourself as an explorer carving out a new path toward mindfulness. Later in your training, you might increase your meditation time to twenty minutes, twice each day. You are creating a new habitat where you will be able to remain peaceful, observe without judgment, know what is   your business , and have a real choice as to how you will speak and act.  Let’s continue   practicing the   SALT Process .  1.   S   is for   Skin  Assume a mindfulness posture.   (Pause)   Focus your mind on your body, and breathe. Feel the air move in and out.   (Pause)   Notice where your skin is. Perhaps you can feel the air or clothing on your skin. Notice how your skin provides a delineation between what is outside and what is inside. Your skin is a physical boundary.   (Pause)   Now, guide your attention to observe only what is within your skin, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   A   is for   Assess  Allow an event or situation to come to mind, one that you have judged as evil. Observe how your body

2  karisfellowships.com   KF13-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  feels when you think of that event or situation.   (Pause)   Is there tension, fatigue, restlessness, or something you cannot describe? Where in your body do you feel those sensations?   (Pause)   On a scale of one to ten, assess the intensity of what you are feeling.   (Pause)   If you feel discomfort that is too distracting for you, use the Dragon Breath to dissipate the tension, breathing loudly and powerfully from your diaphragm. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  3.   L   is for   Look  Look for the fear. Ask yourself and ask God:   What frightens my Idol Self about this event or situation? What seems to undermine my search for glory? (Pause)   Step back from judging the event and simply look at the fear behind the judgment. Observing the fear brings you valuable information about yourself and is part of your healing process.   (Pause)   You might try welcoming the fear and thanking it for what it is telling you about the quality of your faith, or your trust in God. Thank the fear for its part in motivating you to grow. As you thank the fear, use a long exhaling breath, like a sigh.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  4.   T   is for   Tell  Tell God about the fear. Talk to Him about what frightens you and about the stories that you use to justify your fear.   (Pause)   Are your stories about the past or the future, about others, or about yourself?  (Pause)   Ask God to tell you the truth about this situation that frightens you and to replace the fear with the positive motivations of hope, trust, and love. Offer Him gratitude. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause, and take a few relaxing breaths. You may wish to take a sip of water and jot down a few notes about what you have learned, or you might simply rest in the stillness for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  As you rest, listen to our hymn for this confession,   All the Way my Savior Leads Me .  All the way my Savior leads me, cheers each winding path I tread,  Gives me grace for every trial, feeds me with the living Bread.  Though my weary steps may falter, and my soul athirst may be,  Gushing from the Rock before me — Lo! A spring of joy I see;  Gushing from the Rock before me — Lo! A spring of joy I see. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time   permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we are exploring KF Confession 3:  We constructed   legal systems based on our own assessment of good and evil.  The   Two Paths Flowchart   begins with an event. Right now we are concerned with events that trigger a  fear reaction. If we perceive the event as a danger or a threat to our Idol Self, we judge it as evil. If the event seems to deliver us from danger, we judge it as good.   The judgment, however, more than the event, is what hurts us. (Repeat)

3  karisfellowships.com   KF13-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  We are so afraid of messing up, of others messing up, or of life messing up according to our ideas of good  or evil, and yet these feelings of fear are not evil in themselves — the fear of lost opportunity and potential may actually motivate us to do the work of recovery. You can learn to recognize fear in your body whenever you feel strain, the need to force your reality, the craving to run away, the urge to appease, or the need to control, undermine, attack, or play the victim. Even if you   can’t   name your fear, you can take the Believe It Path instead of reacting on autopilot like a silly rabbit that runs   into the hunter’s snare. As  you work through the   Two Paths Worksheet , you are training yourself to ask:   Do I want to take the Judgment Path or the Believe It Path?   Just by asking yourself that question, you choose to disengage from autopilot and refuse to be unwittingly driven into slavery by your fear; you pause and consciously choose to endure the tension of saying no   to fear while you train to achieve a healthier outcome.  Unexamined fear tricks you into taking the Judgment Path over and over again. In KF, you are learning to  recognize misoriented fear for what it is — simply a habitual physical reaction triggered by unprocessed trauma. Exchange your fear for wonder. Practice using the energy devoted to your fear to develop your faith, or your trust, in God and in His design. As you develop your trust, you will become less and less fearful and spend less of your life on autopilot.  Your faith or trust is your business, and learning to trust is your responsibility. You cannot depend on  anyone else to learn and exercise faith for you. However, you will need training. Training means that you submit to a program for a time until you can learn to productively direct yourself. Training gives you vision for what is possible, and it helps you develop the skills and resources required to achieve that vision.  The Idol Self would have you believe that you can tackle all kinds of situations, relationships, or work,  without any training or effort. It even tells you that God makes things happen for you without your participation. Like magic, you should be able to manage every situation heroically . It’s crazy!   The Idol cannot tolerate being a mere mortal in need of training. Everyone needs training in everything, and Karis Fellowships is one of the many programs available to help you train.  Your business is to get training, but the Idol Self is against you doing your business, so you may actively  distract yourself from that pursuit. Working on your business may feel loathsome for a little while, and  that’s   why the effort you make to deal with your business is another way of losing y our life for Christ’s  sake. 2   You can learn to submit to the limitation that your business has to be done in this world and can only be done by you. That worthwhile and rewarding process requires endurance and cooperation with  God’s   training as He works to bring you into your real glory and potential.  The   Two Paths Worksheet   trains you to take the path of love, which leads to oriented outcomes. It  teaches you how to untangle the jumble of judgments, thoughts, and feelings that are often triggered by  life’s events   and people’s choices . When you practice the Believe it Path, you learn not only to recognize your business but to manage your business and to stop wasting your energy on unproductive judging.  Next week, we will look at the   Shoulds Worksheet .   Print out a copy for your KF ring binder and explore it  this week, perhaps with your Karis Link.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, help me take up the work of my business. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF13-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?” )  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s look   again at the first chapter of James.  In our last lesson, we learned from James that the deceitful gifts of the hunter   harm us, while God’s gifts rebirth us into our design and potential. If we are to courageously reject the hunter’s gifts, we must have vision for what God’s gifts can do.   Hopefully, through KF, you are catching a glimpse of that vision.  Let’s read Nancy’s   translation of James 1:18.  18 God never intended death to be the harvest of these times of trial; rather, it is His intention to produce our True Selves by the creative process and the first principle of truth so that we would be a kind of firstfruits among His creatures.  What does it mean to be firstfruits? It means that we, in Christ, have become something completely new. We are a new family expressing the Person and character of God, our Father, in a way that the world has not yet experienced. 3   Later in this chapter, James teaches us that in order to become those firstfruits, we have to take responsibility for our business.   Let’s   take a minute to expand our understanding of the Greek word   logos , which we touched on in the   KF Introductory Meeting . Logos can be translated as   word , but it can also be accurately understood as   God’s way of doing things . Jesus was the Logos; He showed us how  to do things God’s way. It is our business to get rid of   all those things that interfere with our ability both to receive and to bind ourselves to the logos.  Here is Nancy ’s   paraphrase of   James 1:21 – 25 .  21 Therefore, wiping away all filthiness and all that remains of cowardice, in humility receive the logos implanted, which is able to rescue your True Self.   22 Become doers of the logos and not just hearers who will not evaluate themselves accurately;   23 because if anyone is a hearer of the logos and not a doer, that person is only an image, an illusion, and is revealed to be the kind of person who only glances at the logos as they would glance into a mirror simply to see their natural face.   24 How do we know that? Because once that illusion-person has compared themselves to the logos and gone away, they immediately forget what kind of person they actually are.   25 But the one who makes an effort to lean on the logos, which is the fulfilling law of real freedom, and works to remain near it — not having become a forgetful hearer, but an effortful doer — that person will be happy and favored in all of their doing.  Take a deep breath.  Earlier in this chapter, James taught us that we are lured by the hunter, or get into the wrong pasture, because of our cravings and greed. We learned that the outcome of those cravings is death. James contrasts   the outcome of death with the creative principle of God’s way of doing things— the logos —  which leads to life. One of the many things we can see in this passage is the need to get rid of all the stuff that is clouding, muddying, and interfering with an honest self-evaluation. We need to clean the mirror.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF13-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  By doing so, we get into the right pasture and are then able to humbly   accept the logos, God’s way of  doing things.   When we embrace God’s way, our True Self is   rescued, and we are granted a place of favor in our karis relationship with Him.  Our business is to practice what we learn and become doers of the logos, but, like all learners, we will make mistakes and be inconsistent.   We can’t do it all, all of the time, and right now.   So, as you explore your KF tools, find the ones that work for you. You are presently collecting tools and exploring how helpful they might be. Choose a tool and use it for a few weeks, and then set it aside while you practice another one. Return to the tools that work for you.  What is this law of freedom? How does James describe it? The law of freedom is the logos, and the logos is described as   telos , which is often translated as   perfect . Telos   is the fulfillment of a designed purpose. Your designed purpose is to grow in the logos and learn to live in this law of real freedom. If you are in that process, you are fulfilling the logos and are, therefore, perfect or telos. Thomas Sterner in his book  The Practicing Mind   offers a metaphor that describes the perfection of a growing thing that fulfills its created design at every stage of its development. He writes:  As we attempt to understand ourselves and our struggles with life's endeavors, we may find peace in the observation of a flower. Ask yourself:   At what point in a flower's life, from seed to full bloom, does it reach perfection? 4   (Repeat) (Pause)  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord of the law of freedom, help me be a perfect doer of the logos at whatever stage I am. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Bible teaching ?” )  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. Breathe, and hold your experience up to the light as you   consider an area of your life where you might choose to do things   God’ s way .   (Pause)   Feelings

(Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing as you   consider this area of your life where you might choose to do things   God’s way .   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might recognize what resistance or the fear of losing control feels like in your body, or perhaps what courage or trustworthiness feels like. Breathe. You are a human creature and are not alone in your feelings.
