Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.”   (Psalm 139:23 – 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  As part of a research project, a group of children were placed in a situation of great temptation and then secretly observed. 1   They were told that they would receive a very desirable reward if they would wait for the facilitator to come back into the room before eating the treat in front of them. Some of the children did not have the skills to endure their craving for the treat; they could not bear the tension of waiting. As a result, those children chose the immediate gratification of their desires. Their inability to courageously wait prevented the possibility of a greater reward.  Other children, however, had endurance skills and were able to manage their tension. They were able to resist immediate gratification in order to discover what their desirable reward might be. They avoided looking at the treat, pulled on their hair, or wiggled out their tension until they reached their goal. They had learned methods of coping with their immediate cravings. Although they did not know if the promised reward would be worth it, they at least gave themselves the opportunity to find out. They practiced a kind of mindfulness that helped them stay the course no matter how they felt.  Your KF work requires lots of courageous endurance. When we change life patterns, there will be tension, but just like the children who endured, you can use your mindfulness training and tapping to manage that tension. By constructively enduring, you can give yourself a chance to discover the rewards that are possible for you in Christ.  Let’s continue   practicing the   SALT   Process .  1.   S   is for   Skin  Take a mindfulness posture and breathe.   (Pause)   Focus your mind on your body. As you breathe, feel the air move in and out.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Your skin is a physical boundary. Notice how it provides a delineation between what is within and what is without.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Now, guide your attention to observe only what is within your skin, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   A   is for   Assess  Allow an event or situation to come to mind, one that you judge as evil. Observe how your body feels

2  karisfellowships.com   KF14-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  when you think about that situation or event.   (Pause)   Is there tension, fatigue, restlessness, or something that you cannot describe?   (Pause)   Where in your body do you feel those sensations?  (Pause)   On a scale of one to ten, assess the intensity of what you are feeling, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  3.   L   is for   Look  Look for the fear. Ask yourself and then ask God:   What threatens my Idol Self about this event or situation? What am I afraid of? Of loss . . . of others . . . or of myself? (Pause)   Step back from judging the event and just look at the fear behind the judgment. Observing the fear brings you valuable information about yourself and is part of the healing process.   (Pause)   You might try welcoming the fear and thanking it for what it is telling you about the quality of your faith, or trust in God. Thank the fear for its part in motivating you to grow. As you thank your fear, use a long exhaling breath, like a sigh.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  4.   T   is for   Tell  Tell God about your fear. Talk to Him about what threatens you and about the stories that you attach to the fear.   (Pause)   Are your stories linked to the past or the future? Are they about what is fair or unfair, right or wrong?   (Pause)   Ask God to show you the truth about this situation and to replace your fear with the positive motivations of trust, hope, and love. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take a few relaxing breaths and rest in the stillness for one minute. You may wish to take a sip of water and jot down a few notes about what you have learned.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Pause. Use the   SALT Process   this week, spending a minute or two on each step, and see what you can learn.  Our hymn and affirmation is   All the Way My Savior Leads Me.  All the way my Savior leads me. Oh, the fullness of His love!  Perfect rest to me is promised in my Father’s house above.  When my spirit, clothed immortal, wings its flight to realms of day,  This my song through endless ages: Jesus led me all the way;  This my song through endless ages: Jesus led me all the way. 2  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  During this Toolbox training,   you might want to have a   Shoulds Worksheet   available.  This month we are exploring KF Confession 3:  We constructed   legal systems based on our own assessment of good and evil.  Our Idol’s   laws dictate how we should think and how we should act, and this list of laws, or legal standards,

3  karisfellowships.com   KF14-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  supports our pride system. When we adhere to these standards, we feel superior and secure, but when we fail to achieve them, our pride is hurt, and we severely judge ourselves for whatever limitation is hindering us. These perceived failures and judgments are the source of our self-hate.  Rather than using your precious energy to reassert and strengthen your pride system, why not use that same energy to disarm your shoulds and taboos? That would make the experience of your real limitations much less painful. After all, your legal systems simply foster judgment and self-hate and block your creativity. Is that really what you want?  The   Shoulds Worksheet   is designed to help you dismantle your legal systems and escape the tyranny of the shoulds. Make a few copies of this worksheet and keep them handy in your KF ring binder. When you are in the middle of wrestling and wrath and looking down the back of the accusing, craving bull that has  just claimed you for the next dance, you won’t   have the presence of mind to print out worksheets. You will be too busy dancing! So, do yourself a favor and have a few worksheets ready to help you throw off the bull ’ s control.  We recently learned to use the   Two Paths Flowchart   to help us understand how we create outcomes through our choices. The flowchart begins with an event, and here is something you may not realize: even self-hate is an event. Self-hate scares us, and when something scares us, we tend to judge it as evil. Many people get to this stage in their KF training and quit. The unconscious self-hate that they have been suppressing all of their lives begins to surface, and they start to feel strong emotions toward themselves and toward others. These emotions feel dangerous, and it seems safest just to quit this work. When members tell themselves that they have simply lost interest in their KF training, they may actually be avoiding the next challenge in their personal development and the inevitable self-hate. Self-hate is an event that powerfully generates the fear of death. However, even in the midst of self-hate, judgment, stories, and feelings, we can realign ourselves with love.  Please take out your   Shoulds Worksheet .  We will only explore Part One in this lesson. Part One helps us define what is real about ourselves at this moment.  1.   Indicators and reactions  What have you done, thought, or felt that lets you know that you are no longer in peace? You may find yourself in chaotic outcomes, having anxious nightmares, battling obsessive thoughts and hurt feelings, or simply experiencing strain or tension. You might recognize compulsive cravings or  behaviors, or perhaps you are trying to manage God’s or someone else’s business.  2.   Identify your emotions  Use the list of feelings to help you map your emotional reactions. Circle or highlight the feelings that describe your experience. Write down any others that you may be experiencing. Notice your body. Is it reacting to the situation? If so, how and where?  3.   When and what?  Ask yourself:   When did I start feeling this way? Was there a specific event that I judged as bad or not good enough? What was that event?  4.   Restoring comfort or pride

4  karisfellowships.com   KF14-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Most of us have learned what emotions and behaviors will immediately appease our Idol and indulge our cravings to return to old misoriented patterns that offer effortless gratification and release from the tension of endurance. These default patterns restore our pride but undermine our true potential and that of others.  Whenever we try to avoid discomfort and appease our Idol by giving into its demands, our real motive is to restore neurotic pride. Mastery types tend to grab control, create conflict, or conscript slaves. Self-effacing types suffer, lie, and accuse others while exaggerating their own helplessness. Resigned types can neglect responsibilities and resist change; they retreat to their stronghold of self- complacency and addictive escape.  In our next lesson, we will look at Part Two of the   Shoulds Worksheet . Take time to explore it further and bring your questions to the KF meeting. You might also talk to your Karis Link. We hope that you will be able to offer some of your experiences during the sharing time.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord Jesus, show me my shoulds. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?” )  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s look at Paul’s letter to the Galatians, which you will find   in the Bible right after Corinthians. You might read the full chapter or the entire letter and see how the alternative understanding from this meeting  helps clarify Paul’s teaching about legal systems.   The Bible is one of your manuals for healing. You really do need to know what the Bible says if you hope to recover your True Self.  This month we are focusing on KF Confession 3:  We constructed   legal systems based on our own assessment of good and evil.  Here is some information that you might find useful. The Greek word for   faith   can also be translated as  trust   and   trustworthiness . Additionally, in the first verse of Hebrews chapter 11, we are taught that faith, or trustworthiness, is the evidence of an unseen reality.   Faith is living the kind of life that is trustworthy evidence of the reality and character of the unseen God.   (Repeat)   This definition helps us understand what Paul means by faith in his letter to the Galatians.  Now   let’s   read Nancy’s paraphrase of   Galatians 2:16 – 21 .  16 You know that no one orients by trying to fulfill legal systems of shoulds, taboos, and claims, judging good and evil. Instead, we orient through becoming the evidence of the unseen truth of Jesus Christ. And we have confidence in this truth, which gives us the courage to make life choices that reveal who He is. This confidence does not spring from

5  karisfellowships.com   KF14-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  fulfilling our legal systems for no one will ever be oriented through trying to fulfill legal systems.  17 But if while seeking to be oriented in Christ, we discover also that we are terribly misoriented, does it mean that Christ is a servant of misorientation? Absolutely not!   18 Let me explain. If I build again a legal system that I once destroyed, I re-partner with those who have missed the path.   19 Think of it this way: through trying to have a relationship with my own legal system, I died to that system so that I might live in a trust relationship with God. I have been crucified with Christ on the cross of all legal systems.   20 And I, as the Idol Self, no longer live, but Christ lives in my True Self. And my real qualities, which were usurped by the Idol, have now become the evidence of the unseen character of the Son of God, who out of His great goodness loved me and took tremendous risks on my behalf.  21 By living this new life, I do not dismiss or discount the value of   God’s karis gift , which invited me into relationship with Him. Think about this: if we are oriented through the efforts we make to fulfill our legal systems — by our shoulds, taboos, and claims — would Christ have died for us as a karis gift?  Take a deep breath.  So, what is this passage saying? As much as we wish it were possible, no one orients to God through the legal systems of shoulds, taboos, and claims. We orient to God by becoming the evidence of Jesus Christ in this world. This difficult process requires a lot of trust in Jesus, but our confidence in the process grows as our life reveals more and more of the truth about Him.  Now that we are in training, we may be struggling with our legal systems in a new way. In fact, trying to become more like Jesus can stir up more self- hate, but that isn’t the fault of Jesus. It   happens because we are trying to construct another system of laws for ourselves — based, perhaps, on being a   “ good ”   member of Karis Fellowships. But, as Christians, we can give up being motivated by legal systems altogether and learn how to live as Jesus did, in karis relationship with God. We are   God’s   creatures, and when we humbly give up our legal systems, He can use all of our natural strengths and our training in karis relationship to express who He is. If God had wanted us to live by legal systems, would He have sent Jesus to die for us as a karis gift?  Our prayer might go something like this:  God of giving, teach me about my karis relationship with You. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Bible teaching ?” )  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider letting go of a should — what you should be or what you should do, what others should be or do, or what life should be or do   according to your   Idol’s standards.   (Repeat)

6  karisfellowships.com   KF14-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Choose just one should that causes you to react with judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider letting go of this should , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush feelings and thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us. Breathe, and hold your experience up to the light as you   consider letting go of this should .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider letting go of this should.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what intense frustration or shutting down feels like in your body, or perhaps what hope or trust feels like.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider letting go of this should . Does that feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe.   (Pause)   Do you judge letting go of this should as good or evil?   What are your reasons? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Is this should a regular pattern in your life? Are you afraid of something — of loss, of missing out, of hating yourself, or, perhaps, of discovering your real glory? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  For thousands of years, human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have   considered   letting go of their shoulds.   You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   Feelings are just chemical reactions in your body bringing you information. You can observe and learn something from what you have just experienced. With training, you can choose what you will do with your feelings.   (Pause)  When a fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting. Breathe with compassion for yourself and for all of us who are dealing with shoulds. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the integration ?” )

7  karisfellowships.com   KF14-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time to heal and train together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our real glory and to the truth of who You created us to be. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?” )  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_marshmallow_experiment .  2   All the Way My Savior Leads Me   by Fanny J. Crosby (1820 – 1915),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=ekUELQCnQlM .

title: KF15 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF15-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF15 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  Returning a gift for a gift received is an essential practice that supports our healing. Giving and receiving gifts is healthy karis circulation. Karis Fellowships is a gift from God and from volunteers — a gift to you. These volunteers offer their gifts of service and finances in response to what God has done for them through Karis Fellowships. Please join with us by circulating your gifts. You can make a regular automatic donation to KF through the   Give a Gift   button on the KF website.  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  In this lesson we begin looking at KF Confession 4:  We judged ourselves and others with contempt and felt justified in our wrath.  In KF, we teach mindfulness exercises that we ourselves have found helpful, but there are many other options out there that you might try.   When life’s experiments trigger judgment and wrath, you need to  be skilled in mindfulness, so take time to train, if not every day, then regularly. See if you can work up to spending twenty minutes, twice each day, in mindfulness practice and meditation. If you are raising young children, you might want to take small breaks throughout the day to explore mindfulness together. You can invite your children to join you in short times of practice. Teach them to simply notice their breath for one minute, and then see what happens.  The   Mercy Meditation   supports our efforts to reorient the misdirected energy described in KF Confession 4. 1   With the addition of this meditation, you will have four different practices available to you. Explore the same meditation for a whole month to give you time to discover whether it works for you. Or you might practice each of the four meditations for five minutes, giving you twenty minutes of meditation practice.  By practicing mindfulness, you bring your mind and emotions under the guidance of your own will. You are then free to connect to the Holy Spirit in a moment. Undisciplined minds are like wayward and unruly puppies jumping at every opportunity to impose their own primitive wills. Puppies are big enough to do damage and, like all beginners, are in desperate need of training. Your mind and emotions also need

2  karisfellowships.com   KF15-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  training, just like those puppies. Be kind to yourself during this process, and remember that there are seasons of effort and seasons of rest.  The Mercy Meditation  Assume a meditation posture, and breathe. You might wish to take some notes in your KF journal.   (Pause)  Draw your mind away from the events of the day, from the past or the future, and from others. Focus on what is happening inside your skin. Settle into being present and aware in this moment.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  And now, reflect for thirty seconds on each of the following three questions. Observe your feelings and thoughts without judgment, and n otice your body’s reactions.  1.   In what areas am I most critical of myself?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause, and if you haven’t   already done so, take thirty seconds to jot down your thoughts.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   For what do I need to forgive myself?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. You might make a note of what came to mind.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  3.   How do I treat myself when I make a mistake?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause, and if you wish, write for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now experiment with bringing compassion to yourself in some way. For example, call to mind someone who loves you just as you are. This might be someone divine, like God or Jesus, or perhaps someone  mortal and human. You might call to mind one of God’s other creatures.   (Pause)   Imagine seeing yourself through their eyes. You might give yourself an appreciative hug.   (Pause)   However you choose to bring compassion to yourself, just observe and rest for one minute. Practice letting go of judgment and breathe.  (Pause for 1 minute)  And pause. In this practice, we plant seeds of mercy — not only for ourselves but for others. Mercy is the civil law   of God’s kingdom. 2  Our hymn for this lesson is   When I Survey the Wondrous Cross . This is one of 750 hymns written by Isaac Watts, many of which we still sing today. Isaac Watts was an evangelical non-conformist Christian in seventeenth century England. Both he and his father were excluded from the established church and from any gove rnment position, and Isaac’s father spent years in prison for his Christian convictions.  Let’s listen to our hymn .  When I survey the wondrous cross  On which the Prince of Glory died,  My richest gain I count but loss,  And pour contempt on all my pride. 3  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?” )

3  karisfellowships.com   KF15-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  Hopefully, you have a   Shoulds Worksheet   in front of you as we explore KF Confession 4 together. This Confession reminds us that when we are misoriented, we judge ourselves and others with contempt and feel justified in our wrath. Our judgments are the main obstacles to our growth and development, and those judgments inevitably undermine the growth of others.  Paul’s letter to the   Galatians reminds us that while striving to become like Jesus, we can experience intense self-hate because we have inadvertently adopted an additional set of standards by which we measure and mercilessly judge ourselves. Our KF tools help us to courageously endure moments of self- hate while we grow.  As you give up your search for the   Glory of Me! , you will look back with compassion on your former life of striving, and you will experience increasing gratitude to God for His patience and love in supporting you while you find your way home.  Shoulds and taboos are the artificial internal motivators of the Idol. They are the legal systems, or law, that we use to motivate ourselves and to impose our will on others. Externalized shoulds express themselves in two different ways: we either try to force others to conform to our standards, or we believe that others are forcing their standards on us. These standards that we think others are imposing on us are often standards that we are imposing on ourselves. When others do not fulfill our shoulds, we feel toward them all the fury that we unconsciously feel toward ourselves; and when others appear to impose their shoulds on us, we feel compelled to comply with them, resist them, or fight against them. Externalized shoulds explain why we need to impose our will on others and, also, why we feel so much judgment from others. We assume that others are judging us with the same wrath with which we judge ourselves. God lovingly gave us the Ten Commandments, but we have imposed upon ourselves ten gazillion other commandments in the form of claims and shoulds.  Let’s   look at Part Two of our   Shoulds Worksheet . One KF member observed that we are not looking deeply for spiritual insight here. We are looking deeply at how crazy we are!  Part Two: Looking Deeply  1.   Recognize the   “mistake”  Ask yourself:   What did I do that was   “ wrong ”   or has caused my discomfort?   Here are some examples of how you might answer this question:   I said this thing and another person reacted negatively. I messed up my interview and lost that job opportunity. I allowed that organization to impose their ideas on me.   I wasn’t strong enough to follow   through.   I can’t make any friends.  2.   Write down your shoulds  Should-statements often begin with should-phrases, such as   I should always ,   I should never ,   I should be able to ,   I should feel , or   I should know . On this worksheet Nancy has given you a number of examples of how you might finish these phrases. Here is how a KF member finished one of his should- phrases : “I am committed to the idea that I   should always be able to manage my limitations so that nothing can interfere with any of my plans. ”

4  karisfellowships.com   KF15-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  3.   Define perfection according to your Idol  When you write this statement, you can have a little fun describing the extremes of perfection to which you aspire. Sometimes   it’s   helpful to see how crazy our dreams of glory can be, and smile.  4.   Identify your limitations  In this step, we deal with the real limitations of being material creatures living in a misoriented world. You might also   think about the limitations that God’s logos   imposes on you personally — limitations like honesty, purity, honor, and trustworthiness. You cannot expect outcomes that are productive and healthy if you lie, practice addictive behaviors, dishonor your own   or another’s   body, and live chaotically — disrespecting God, others, and yourself. So, what are your limitations?  Notice when you are using the words   should   and   shouldn’t   in your thinking and conversation. Those words can reveal the   thou shalts   and   thou shalt nots   that you have created to support your Idol Self. You might try this trick:   When you notice that you are using the word   should , try replacing it with the word   could   or  might .   (Repeat)   See what happens. Nancy learned that trick from her husband a long time ago, and it has helped her recognize her shoulds. You might try it for yourself.  Our prayer could go something like this:  Merciful God, help me let go of my shoulds. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?” )  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  This is KF Confession 4:  We judged ourselves and others with contempt and felt justified in our wrath.  Let’s turn to   the Gospel of Luke, chapter 6.  Perhaps by now you have scheduled a regular time to practice your KF tools. During that time, you might explore a   Shoulds Worksheet . To help you identify your own particular shoulds, review chapter 3 of  Neurosis and Human Growth   and the chapters that describe your Idol. 4   You might make a running list of the shoulds that you have discovered in your own life and then see how that list changes during your KF training. Notice that Nancy is not saying that you   should   do any of these things. She is just reminding you of a few things that you   might   do during your KF time to help you achieve the oriented outcomes that you desire. In the months ahead, you can review all of these tools, especially when extra training is offered. We hope that using the tools will become part of your soul-care routine. You are a creature in time and have all the time you need to grow. How does that feel? You have all the time you need to grow. That feels pretty good , doesn’t it?  Here   is Nancy’s translation of   Luke 6:41 – 42 , a passage that is probably quite familiar to many of you:

5  karisfellowships.com   KF15-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  41 Why do you regard the twig that is in your sibling's eye, but do not fully observe the beam that is in your own eye?   42 Or how can you say to your sibling,   “ Sibling, allow me to take out the twig that is in your eye, ”   when you yourself do not see the beam that is in your own eye? You pretender! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see straight in order to take out the twig that is in your sibling's eye.  Take a deep breath.  Whenever we want others to do things our way, we have already judged that their way is wrong based on our righteous and omniscient wisdom. Our judgment is often the externalization of unachieved standards that we have imposed on ourselves. We desperately want others to fulfill those standards for us because we imagine that their compliance will stop our self-hate; we hope that changing them will take us effortlessly into our imagined glory.   That’s how we   end up in other people’s business.  This metaphor of twigs and beams   is about the relative importance of our business and another person’s  business, and it reflects the problem of our misoriented perspective. When we impose our legal systems on other people,   our perspective becomes distorted, and we start focusing on their business rather than taking care of our own. Instead of changing ourselves, we try to fix or change them . In this metaphor, Jesus uses the Greek word for a construction beam — something that we build with. These beams support the temple of our Idol Self, but this temple is so vulnerable that we need others to validate it by accommodating our pride system. If they comply with our shoulds, they must expend on us the resources they have been given for dealing with their own beams. However, most people will not participate in our search for glory. They see things differently. What in our eyes has the importance of a structural beam holding up our temple is a mere twig in someone else ’s eyes . Other people cannot possibly understand how important our beam is to us.  What we don’t understand   and refuse to explore is how our problems with other people are mercifully exposing the tyranny of our shoulds and self-hate. We try to avoid that humbling exposure by employing the same forceful, manipulative tactics that we have always used to make others support our Idol ’s   pride. We might get compliance from others in the moment, but we damage the long-term possibilities for relationship. When we impose our shoulds on someone else, we avoid the painful process of removing  the beam in our own eye, which means actively demolishing our Idol’s temple. Those twigs that we   see in  another’s eye are   often our own beams reflected from afar. It is a problem of perspective and interpretation. We see in another what is actually within ourselves.  Your feelings of discomfort and your fear of self-hate are used by the Idol to justify your clumsy efforts to remove the twig in someone else ’s eye. No wonder people don’t trust you! Have you noticed that   when you try to fix other people, whether actively or in your own mind, the focus goes outside your own skin  and into someone else’s business? This is why getting into other people’s business is so dangerous   and even rather stupid; you are not motivated by the truth about the situation but driven by the compelling need to keep the beams   of your Idol’s temple   securely in place.  If you want to be real and express the love of God, you must give up imposing your shoulds on others and on yourself. Go back to the list   Love or Pride?   Is your attitude and your behavior in line with love?  Once you know your own business , you can ignore everything else. Isn’t that amazing? You don’t even  have to think about it. The problem is that we often want to think about everything else and everyone else in order to avoid our own business. Most of us have spent our whole lives avoiding our business. You

6  karisfellowships.com   KF15-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  may be asking right now:   What is my business? 5   Your trustworthiness and your healing are your business. Your fear is also your business — and so is your true glory.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, help me stick to my business. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Bible teaching ?” )  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds )  Here is our integration focus:   Consider a twig in someone else’s eye, somet hing that you would like to fix. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider a twig in someone else’s eye, something that you would like to fix , how does it feel?   (Pause)  Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Recognize with compassion whatever you may be experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. Breathe, and hold your experience up to the light as you   consider   a twig in someone else’s eye .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider that twig in  someone else’s eye .   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might recognize what frustration or vindictive triumph feels like in your body, or perhaps what anxiety or hurt pride feels like.  (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to respectfully observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider a   twig in someone else’s eye . Isn’t it wonderful that   He will consider that twig with you?   (Pause)   Have you judged the twig as good or evil?   What are your reasons? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Is this judgment a regular pattern in your life?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something — perhaps of others or of the loss of your hope for glory? Are you avoiding your own business or your True Self?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF15-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Heal  God created you to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have   considered fixing someone else.   You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   Feelings are just chemical reactions in your body bringing you information. With training, you can choose what you will do with those feelings.   (Pause)   You can observe and learn something from what you experience. Breathe with compassion for yourself and for others who long to fix another person. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the integration ?” )  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are so grateful that it is Your loving intention to train us for our true glory. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You continue to guide us to the truth of who You created us to be and what You want us to do. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?” )  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   www.livingmindfully.org . The Mercy Meditation has been resourced from Mindful Living and adapted for Karis  Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  2   James 2:12 – 13.  3   When I Survey the Wondrous Cross   by Isaac Watts (1674 – 1748),   youtu.be/U-hz6L6LAug .  4   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).  5   See KF11.

title: KF16 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF16-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF16 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  This is KF Confession 4:  We judged ourselves and others with contempt and felt justified in our wrath.  Here is Nancy’s account of   how she took the Believe It Path when she was tempted to judge herself and others with contempt.  I had gone out of the house in an unfamiliar town without my keys or phone. When I returned, no one was at home and I was locked out. A KF meeting was due to start in thirty minutes, and I really needed to be in the house and at my computer.  I sat on the doorstep lamenting my fate and going into self-hate for forgetting phones and keys, because I should not, according to my Idol Self, forget phones and keys. Then I remembered my KF training. I used my mindfulness skills to manage my self-hate and got busy with WAA! W-A-A: Words, Attitude, Action. I used my words to pray. I changed my attitude to dismiss shame, and then I was able to creatively open my mind. I took action by boldly looking for a key hidden outside even though I knew that my friends did not leave keys outside. My first stop was the traditional front door mat and, very surprisingly, there under the mat was a key. I was able to get into the house and join the Karis Fellowships meeting on time. The mystery of this story is that my friend said that she had not left the key there. The best part of the story is that my paroxysm of self-hate and self- contempt was not allowed to muddy my prayers or my attitude. Having mercy on myself opened my mind to the possibility of taking oriented action. I was able to find the way that God in His mercy had prepared for me.  Let’s continue with   the   Mercy Meditation . 1  Assume a meditation posture and breathe for one minute. Settle into being present and aware.   (Pause for 1 minute)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF16-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Draw your mind away from the events of the day, from the past or the future, and from others. Focus on what is happening inside your own skin.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  In this lesson, we will reflect for thirty seconds on three questions. However, when practicing this exercise on your own, you might reflect for one minute. If it works better for you, jot down your thoughts as soon as they come to mind. Sometimes our thoughts   get lost if we don’t catch them on the spot.  Let’s begin our training.  1.   In what areas am I most critical of myself?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. Take thirty seconds to jot down what came to mind.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   For what do I need to forgive myself?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause,   and if you haven’t   done so already, take thirty seconds to jot down your thoughts.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  3.   How do I treat myself when I make a mistake?   ( Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause, and if you wish, write for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now experiment with bringing compassion to yourself in some way. For example, call to mind someone who loves you just as you are. This might be someone divine, like God or Jesus, or perhaps someone  mortal and human. You might call to mind one of God’s othe r creatures.   (Pause)   Imagine seeing yourself through their eyes. You might give yourself an appreciative hug.   (Pause)   However you choose to bring compassion to yourself, just observe and rest for one minute. Practice letting go of judgment and breathe.  (Pause for 1 minute)  And pause.  Our hymn for this confession is   When I Survey the Wondrous Cross .  Forbid it, Lord, that I should boast,  Save in the death of Christ my God!  All the vain things that charm me most,  I sacrifice them to His love. 2  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  L et’s return to our   Shoulds Worksheet .  We cannot give up our legal systems unless we are willing to give up our search for the   Glory of Me!   or, as Karen Horney puts it, the commitment to actualize the idealized self. This idealized self is an idol that we have manufactured to replace God. When we give up pursuing the Idol ’s dreams , we can give up the legal systems that drive us to actualize our Idol.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF16-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Part 3 of the Shoulds Worksheet: Recovery  This section is divided into eight steps.  1.   Recognize the judgment  Our first step is to look back at the   Two Paths Flowchart.   We have felt fear and have taken the path of judgment. We have decided that a situation is good or bad. Perhaps at this stage you are wondering:  How do I take the path of love?   The   Shoulds Worksheet   helps you learn how to do that, but   don’t  forget that, as a neurotic, you will be tempted to think that knowing something is the same as  practicing. Let’s get real. Knowing is NOT the same as practicing. You might read a book   that teaches the art of skiing, but until you go up the mountain, you will not learn to ski. You cannot learn until you are willing to fall down, get up, fall down, get up, fall down, and get up again.  Remember:   Train hard. Fight easy.   (Repeat)  2.   Identify the fear  If you cannot perform perfectly, what do you fear? Your Idol is supported by your pride system and your search for an idealized glory. What area of your pride would be hurt if you could not perform  perfectly according to your Idol’s standards? What   aspect   of the Idol’s dream of glory would be lost?  It hurts our pride when we cannot control other people or perfectly manage every area of our lives, when our plans   don’t   work out, and when an imagined future that we have judged as good is snatched away from us. Hurt pride can stop you in your tracks; you become frozen and fierce. You are then unable to move forward and be creative because you are afraid of experiencing more hurt pride. This is how pride interferes with your real potential.  3.   Stick to the facts  Now that you have recognized the judgment and identified the fear, describe the situation as a simple sequence of events. This skill is the foundation of the Believe It Path. Here is an example:   I went on a trip. I had plans. Someone got sick. I was not able to follow through with my plans. The End . Oh my! The Believe It Path   doesn’t   sound very dramatic or sensational, does it? It just   is . We can’t write a  soap opera or a country western song about the Believe It Path —it’s too boring!   The Believe It Path gives us nothing to whisper about or to yell at others about. The Judgment Path, on the other hand, leads to conflict, and conflict is the essence of drama. Drama makes our Idol Self feel alive. Feeling alive is very important when you are not alive.  4.   Make a decision: Are you willing to let go of the judgment?  When Nancy is coaching someone, she will eventually get to the question:   Are you done with that ?  (Repeat)   You have a choice. You have the power to say yes or no. When you choose to be done with your judgments, you finally give yourself permission to change.  5.   Consider your progress: What have you learned?  Try to write a few sentences about what you have learned by doing this worksheet.  6.   Take action: Talk to God  You have been using words to describe what the Believe It Path looks like for you. You are now in touch with the reality of your own business and can make different choices. Perhaps your attitude has changed. Now is the time to take positive action, and your first positive action is a prayer of confession.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF16-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  7.   Integrate  Your body may need some help orienting to the work you have done, so in this section Nancy suggests a number of different ways to help your body process your work. You can find instructions for using these methods under   Toolbox   on the KF website and, also, at   Alison’s tapping and TAT videos .  8.   Celebrate  We are all learning from each other in this training process, so we hope that you will share what you have learned with your KF community.  You don’t have to wait until after an event to do a   Shoulds Worksheet . This is quite important. You can do a worksheet before you are in a situation that you know will trigger your   Idol’s   shoulds and self-hate. A preemptive worksheet can help you calm your body and forestall judgments and reactions. Also, by working through an upcoming situation on a worksheet, you might find it easier to stand in that situation, oriented in peace.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord of healing, encourage me to do the work of my own healing. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Toolbox?” )  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  If you have your Bible with you, turn to the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 7.  As we have said before, legal systems do not foster gratitude. When we expect people to act in a certain way, they can do no more than meet our expectations. When they do manage to comply, we feel no real gratitude for their efforts. We only experience a brief respite from our fear of not being in control. If people only approximate our expectations, there are no points in their favor. They have failed to fulfill all the requirements of our imagined standards and, therefore, deserve our wrath. If, on the other hand, they do meet our expectations, they are not allowed to feel that they have given us a gift of any kind. They are only allowed to feel that they have escaped our wrath for a moment. Laws of shoulds and claims perpetuate contempt, ingratitude, fear, wrath, and resentment, not only toward others but toward ourselves.  Nancy studied First Corinthians 13 for many years without really understanding what Paul meant when he   said, “Love does not insist on its own way, nor does it seek its own.” 3   One day, the meaning became clear to her —and it felt terrifying. She realized that if she wanted to express God’s love through her life,  she would have to give up her own ideas about how things should be. She would have   to submit to God’s  way of doing things. Jesus taught us that if we insist on our own way, seeking the fulfillment of our shoulds, we will never experience our true glory. 4   After several years of exploration, Nancy began to learn how to exchange her personal law of shoulds and claims for oriented, healthy desires. She learned not to insist on her own way, but to meet her needs and attain her wants by asking, seeking, and knocking. This is what Jesus Himself taught us to do in   Matthew 7:7 – 8 . Let’s listen to these verses in Nancy’s translation:

5  karisfellowships.com   KF16-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  7 Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.   8 This is how it works: the asking one receives, the seeking one finds, and to the one who is knocking, it will be opened.  Take a deep breath.  You might like to read the whole chapter and notice how the Bible supports what we teach in Karis Fellowships. In the passage for this lesson, Jesus encourages us to stop wasting energy trying to impose our shoulds and claims; instead, He invites us to learn the process of asking, seeking, and knocking. Asking, seeking, and knocking are all qualities of a person. If you are the kind of person who keeps asking, the kind of person who keeps seeking, and the kind of person who keeps knocking on a regular basis, then Jesus is talking about you.  Asking is Words  Ask for help. Start by learning to ask questions so that you can understand the situation. Tell God and others what is going on inside your skin. Do you know that other people   can’t   read your mind? It is an infantile claim to expect them to do so. Toddlers learn to use their words, and so can you. Telling others what is going on inside you is not a license to impose your demands on others and on the world, nor is it an opportunity to voice your opinions about what they should or should not do to accommodate you. When you ask, you have an opportunity to practice expressing your own reality in a moderate way. Moderate expression and the ability to communicate what you would prefer is evidence that you have been doing your own work and attending to your own business.  Seeking is   Attitude  When our seeking is motivated by the True Self, we are open to what we can learn about ourselves, about others, about God, and about our environment. We are not attached to an outcome that we, in our omniscient and self-righteous judgment, have deemed to be right or good. Seeking is a journey, and it opens up the possibilities of unforeseen discoveries and delightful surprises.  You might ask:   If I am to seek, how do I know what to seek?   You are seeking to produce the Fruit of the Spirit, which manifests through your life the attributes of love — and if you make love your destination, you will discover other very valuable things along the way, like your True Self. 5  Knocking is Action  Explore an oriented action and see what happens. When you find a possible path, use your courage and endurance to keep knocking on the door of the not-knowing or, as Nancy did, to keep looking for the key. You really have to give up the idea that you already know what should be behind that door. With oriented effort and an open mind, you can go into the not-knowing and knock in the face of your fears. A door in your mind may open, or a door to your future may open —it’s   really the same thing.  We often forget that the solutions to our problems are not a matter of just asking. We are so familiar with the acronym A-S-K for Ask, Seek, and Knock that we forget that oriented results come from a three-step process. Our Idol remembers only the easy part — “ Ask and you shall receive ” — so when we have asked, we think our work is done and expect God to do the rest. But   remember that there’s   another way to think about this three-step process: W-A-A or   Words-Attitude-Action. (Repeat)  This is the time to exercise the kind of self-discipline that an excellent father would teach you.   Don’t   just cry   “ Waa! ”   like an immature child or act like a victim whining to the universe and blaming self,

6  karisfellowships.com   KF16-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  circumstances, God, and others. Instead, you can think: WAA! — Words, Attitude, Action. This process does not lead to effortless superiority. You have to work to get what you want. Use moderate words to ask so that you and others can understand what you want. Seek with an open attitude, without judgment, looking for something real that will be revealed. Knock because only action produces re-action — and if you want to make something oriented happen, you have to take oriented action.   You don’t just sit around,  indulge your feelings, or follow distracting rabbit trails; nor do you hold others, including God, responsible for your business. Instead, you actively look for a key under the doormat.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Holy Spirit, remind me to use Words, Attitude, Action. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Bible teaching ?” )  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider an area of your life where you could be asking, seeking, and knocking — where you could use Words, Attitude, Action. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider an area of your life where you could use your words, seek with an open attitude ,   and take oriented action , how does it feel?   (Pause)   With compassion, recognize whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to rest in your awareness. Observe whatever tension you might be feeling as you  consider this area of your life where you could use your words, seek with an open attitude ,   and take oriented action.   (Pause)   Give yourself permission now to explore your thoughts and feelings without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider   this area of your life where you might use Words, Attitude, Action.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   You might notice how your body responds to the fear of hurt pride or to feelings of anxiety or resistance.   (Pause)   Breathe, and help your body process with a long exhaling breath or with the Dragon Breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  this area of your life where you might use Words, Attitude, Action.   Do you feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe.   (Pause)   Are you afraid of what others might do or think, or are you afraid of something in yourself? Perhaps you fear losing your idealized dreams. Observe your responses as just information, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF16-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Heal  As you breathe, repeat to yourself the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore an area that might hurt your neurotic pride.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit of truth, who is eager to train you to use Words, Attitude, Action.  •   Welcome your present reality and all the progress you have made so far.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 6  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I use Words, Attitude, Action, I let go of the longing for power and control.  •   As I use Words, Attitude, Action, I let go of the longing for affection and self-admiration.  •   As I use Words, Attitude, Action, I let go of the longing for comfort and security.  •   As I use Words, Attitude, Action, I let go of the longing for perfection.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the integration ?” )  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time to heal and train together. Hold us in the power of this redirected energy as You guide us to our real glory and mission. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?” )  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   www.livingmindfully.org/ . Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  2   When I Survey the Wondrous Cross   by Isaac Watts (1674 – 1748),   youtu.be/U-hz6L6LAug .  3   1 Cor. 13:5.  4   Matt. 10:38 – 40.  5   Gal. 5:16 – 26.  6   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html .
