content:
karisfellowships.com   KF17-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF17 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  Let’s briefly look at our definition of karis : karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity. What does that mean? The word   karis   is used in Greek to say   thank you . When a person gives you a gift, you must decide whether you want to return a gift to show your gratitude. If you do not offer a gift in return — not even the simple gift of saying thank you — you are letting others know that you are not interested in their gift nor in the benefits of a relationship with them. When Jesus came into our lives, He came as a karis gift from God. Are you returning any gifts to God as evidence of your gratitude and your desire for more relationship?  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  A productive goal is to spend twenty to thirty minutes, twice a day, in prayer and meditation. The benefits  of meditation practice are “dose dependent” . That means you will benefit in proportion to the amount of effort you invest. However, any effort to meditate and practice mindfulness is success.  Have you had a chance or felt a need to practice the   Mercy Meditation   this week? 1   Whenever you rebel against your shoulds and taboos, the Idol Self will have no mercy on you and will punish you with self- hate. When that happens, you will need to show mercy to yourself. Self-promotion or increased self-care will throw self-effacing types into self-hate. For a mastery type,   letting something slide or extending mercy invites self-hate and is often followed by aggression or self-sabotage. Resigned people might feel vaguely uncomfortable after a moment of self-revelation or strong emotion. They might then be irritable or seek numbness again. The   Mercy Meditation   helps us show mercy to ourselves despite our shoulds and the judgments we make about our behaviors and feelings. When our judgmental attitude has calmed down, we can see our value and appreciate the efforts we are making today toward wholeness; and once we know our own value, we can extend value to others as a gift.  The Mercy Meditation  Sit quietly for a few moments. Notice your breath and settle into your environment.   (Pause)   As you breathe, sense the air moving in and out.   (Pause for 10   seconds)   Scan your body for tension.   On the exhale, allow your body to soften.   (Pause)   Give any tense areas permission to relax, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF17-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Draw your mind away from the events of the day, from the past or the future, and from others. Focus on what is happening inside your skin, right now.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  And now, reflect for thirty seconds on each of the following three questions. Feel free to jot down your thoughts as they knock on the door of your mind. Observe your feelings and any physical sensations.  1.   In what areas am I most critical of myself?   ( Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. If you haven’t   done so already, take thirty seconds to jot down what came to mind.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   For what do I need to forgive myself?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause, and if you wish, jot down your thoughts.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  3.   How do I treat myself when I make a mistake?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause, and write for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now experiment with bringing compassion to yourself in some way. For example, call to mind someone who loves you just as you are. This might be someone divine, like God or Jesus, or perhaps someone mortal and human. You might call to mind   one of God’s other creatures .   (Pause)   Imagine seeing yourself through their eyes. You might give yourself an appreciative hug.   (Pause)   However you choose to bring compassion to yourself, just observe and rest for one minute.   Practice letting go of judgment and breathe.  (Pause for 1 minute)  And pause. Sometime this week, try reflecting for one minute on each of those questions and then practice bringing compassion to yourself.  Our hymn for this confession is   When I Survey the Wondrous Cross .  See, from His head, His hands, His feet,  Sorrow and love flow mingled down.  Did ever such love and sorrow meet,  Or thorns compose so rich a crown? 2  Take a deep breath.  Next week we will practice the   Mercy Meditation   and apply it to others.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we are exploring KF Confession 4:  We judged ourselves and others with contempt and felt justified in our wrath.  During the past three lessons, we have been looking at the   Shoulds Worksheet . We are learning to untangle the stories that we fabricate about our disappointments, fears, and judgments. Perhaps we can

3  karisfellowships.com   KF17-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  see how we punish ourselves for not being perfect. We also looked at what we expect from others and what we imagine others expect from us. These are externalized shoulds. When we are unable to actualize our idealized glory, we try to make others do it for us.  Let’s turn our attention   now to another compon ent of the Idol’s legal system : the claim. According to Dr. Horney, a claim is applied in two ways. 3   First, we make the claim that we are entitled to privileges and are exempt from common limitations, suffering, and struggles. We believe that we should receive special care, consideration, and deference. We think that we have a right to get away with our misoriented choices. The more misoriented we are, the stronger our opinions will be about what is right and fair, and the more claims we will impose on others and on life. Perhaps the most prevalent claim of this type is that we do not need to struggle and endure to become mature and complete, lacking in nothing; for us, growth and healing should happen quickly and effortlessly. 4   We might claim that we can be well after attending a few KF meetings because we are just smarter than other people.  In our pride, we believe that we are so special that we should be able to ignore common rules of engagement. For example, we might claim that we are exempt from maintaining the speed limit or from showing up on time. Intense feelings then result from a traffic ticket or from a missed flight. We might feel extreme frustration when others do things differently or do not go out of their way to make us feel comfortable. We might even claim the right to live in a God-fearing country! Perhaps   we are disrespectful to others but require that others treat us with respect. One of our most damaging claims, however, is the story that, even though we call ourselves Christians, we are exempt from following Jesus, doing what He says, and living as He lived in this world. We excuse ourselves from going through what He went through; we imagine that we are above our Master. 5   These are just a few examples of the entitlements and exemptions that we claim to be our right.  Second, we make a claim when we believe something about ourselves that is not supported by evidence. Without that evidence, we will need to lie to ourselves about our assets, such as our intelligence, our abilities, or our spiritual maturity. These lies help us weave the fabric of our virtue stories, those pride- supporting narratives about who we are and why we do what we do. When Nancy was a young Christian, she attributed to herself the qualities of peace and love because her Idol Self required her to appear peaceful and loving, both to herself and to others. However, the evidence of her life revealed a person who was easily frustrated, extremely anxious, and constantly compelled to control others. She did not want to look at the evidence of her actual life because she had no means of dealing with the self-hate   that would follow the exposure of her illusions. She could not rejoice in the truth. Truth was terrifying to her, and to psychically survive, she had to claim to have certain attributes that she did not actually possess.  Sometimes   our reactions to life’s events help us   catch a glimpse of our claims. In KF, however, we learn to do more than just catch a glimpse. We acknowledge and identify our claims and use our tools to deal with them. The   Claim and Blame Worksheet   helps us untangle our neurotic stories so that we can see what is really going on. It helps us deal with ourselves before we deal with our situation. If we can let go of our judgments, we will have the courage and freedom to seek with an open attitude and to mindfully observe what   is — what is real, what is actual evidence. With mindful courage, we are able to be creative and follow the Holy Spirit. You might begin this week to explore   the   Claim and Blame Worksheet .   You can find it on the KF website, under   Toolbox   and   Worksheets .  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, I am now ready to work on my claims. (Repeat)

4  karisfellowships.com   KF17-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Prayer is courageously and consistently asking, seeking, and knocking. Here is another way to think about prayer: when we ask God for something, we are also inviting Him to reveal the pride tangled up in our request. Honest prayer gives God permission to reveal our pride so that He can safely provide for us. If He provided for us without first dealing with our pride, He would be jeopardizing our personal development and the potential of our relationship with Him. As we continue to humbly knock on doors seeking His provision, we can be confident that God is dealing with any hidden pride as He skillfully guides us.  Tackling our problems can feel like death, especially when our pride is threatened.   It’s   so painful! But by going through the valley of the shadow of death with God, we learn to trust Him, and we discover through experience how trustworthy He is. Without your pride, the valley will be much more manageable and productive. Helen Keller, a woman with great limitations who lost both her sight and her hearing as an infant, said this:   The best way out is always through . 6   (Repeat)   She may have been quoting the American poet Robert Frost, who said:   The only way out is through . 7   The only way out of your problem is to go through it. The only way to the banquet is through the valley of the shadow of death.   8   You can learn to rejoice in your valley because it is there that you are trained and cleansed for your provision and for your mission.  Our text for this lesson is   James 4:1 – 6 . Nancy has incorporated our KF understanding of the Idol and the True Self into her paraphrase of this passage.  1 What   is the cause of warfare and fighting among you and within you? Don’t these causes  come out of your malicious desires that advance like an army against your True Self and God, stirring up conflict within your own physical body and with other people?   2 You set  your heart upon some outcome and then it doesn’t happen. So, you feel murderous and  envious because you do not have the power to get your own way. You fight others and are at war within yourself, but you cannot have what you want because you do not speak your reality moderately and ask for what you want.  3 When you do ask for what you want, you cannot attain it because you ask for things that support the Idol Self in order to expend your real gifts on your malicious desires.  4 Adulterers, do you not see that cozying up with the Idol’s system of values and strategies  makes you an enemy of God? Therefore, whoever is willing to be on the side of the Idol takes the position of enmity toward God.   5 Do you suppose that the Scripture does not mean it when it says that the spirit that dwells in us wastes away through cravings?  6 Scripture offers us a great gift when it shows us that God marshals Himself like an army against those who believe that they and their desires are superior to His purposes. Scripture also encourages us that God offers gifts of relationship to those who actively choose to take a low place, ready to please Him and to learn.  Take a deep breath.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF17-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  In its unrelenting search for an imagined glory, our Idol Self makes unreasonable demands. Our covetous desires support the claim that we are special and entitled and, therefore, deserve to have everything go our way. We claim to always be right because being right strokes our pride. We believe that we should always be able to do, or not do, whatever we want, without any adverse consequences.   No wonder there is so much strife and discontent! We are all imposing our craving desires on others and fighting to have things go our own way.   We obsess about what we don’t have . We obsess about forcing our   “ right ”  judgments on life — the rabid froth of our compulsive needs and our pride system. And when our pride is threatened, our self-hate   is so terrifying that we have to lie to ourselves in order to survive; we must make ourselves believe that we are other than we are — and we must force others to support that belief. We imagine that if we could make the world and others be what we want them to be, we would be able to rest for a moment. Count Leo Tolstoy, the acclaimed Russian novelist, put it this way:   In our world everybody thinks of changing humanity, and nobody thinks of changing himself.   9   (Repeat)  The antidote to claims is this: choose to stop setting yourself up as the righteous judge of all the earth, full of extraordinary knowledge and wisdom. God is ready to offer you the gifts of karis relationship if you choose to take the low place, seeking to please Him and learning how to do things His way. The   Claim and Blame Worksheet   helps you recognize your misorientation and observe what is going on around you from a more empowering perspective. It helps you see how your pride is creating more pain. Joy   doesn’t   come from having your compulsive needs met by others or by God. Joy is the Fruit of the Spirit, produced by a True Self that is deeply connected to its Creator.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Be the source of true pleasure in my soul, O God. (Repeat )  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider how your beliefs about a particular situation prevent or shut down an open, courageous attitude.   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider   how your beliefs about a situation prevent or shut down an open, courageous attitude , how does it feel?   (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to rest in your awareness. Observe whatever tension you may be feeling as you  consider how your beliefs about a situation prevent or shut down an open, courageous attitude .   (Pause)  Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to

6  karisfellowships.com   KF17-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider   how   your beliefs about a situation prevent or shut down an open,   courageous attitude. (Pause)   You might recognize what resistance or the fear of losing your   Idol’s   life feels like in your body. You might recognize the fear of others or the fear of hurt pride. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  how   your beliefs about a situation prevent or shut down an open, courageous   attitude .   (Pause)   According  to your Idol’s standards, do   you feel compelled to judge your beliefs or the situation as good or evil?  (Pause)   Is there a story that you might explore, perhaps from your past?   (Pause)   How might your Idol’s  pride be hurt if you were to examine the evidence behind your story?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  We will continue to use the idea of welcome. You might imagine a door of opportunity opening before you. As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore an area of humble learning.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit, who is eager to teach you new things.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 10  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I go forward with courage, I let go of the longing for, or the fear of, power and control.  •   As I go forward with courage, I let go of the longing for, or the fear of, esteem and affection.  •   As I go forward with courage, I let go of the longing for, or the fear of, comfort and peace.  •   As I go forward with courage, I let go of the longing for, or the fear of, change in my situation .  (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time together of healing and training. Hold us in the power of this new direction as You guide us to our real glory and to truth. Reveal the evidence of who we are as You lead us to the next step in our healing this week. Encourage us to co-labor with You to reorient our own lives for a more effective

7  karisfellowships.com   KF17-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and design, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1 www.livingmindfully.org . Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  2   When I Survey the Wondrous Cross   by Isaac Watts (1674 – 1748),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=U-hz6L6LAug .  3   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (W. W. Norton & Company, 1991), chapter 3.  4   James 1:4.  5   Luke 6:40.  6   www.quotesigma.com/45-famous-quotes-helen-keller .  7   Frost, Robert. North of Boston:   A Servant to Servants . (New York: Henry Holt and Company, 1915), lines 56 and 58. Available online at   www.bartleby.com/118/9.html .  8   Psalm 23:4 – 5.  9   Tolstoy, Leo.   Letters to Friends on the Personal Christian Life . (Christchurch, Hants: The Free Age Press, 1900), 71,  www.azquotes.com/author/14706-Leo_Tolstoy .  10   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html . Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.

title: KF18 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF18-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF18 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me   in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  This month we are focusing on KF Confession 4:  We judged   ourselves and others with contempt and felt justified in our wrath.  Any effort we make to train in meditation and mindfulness is worthwhile. We learn to endure the discomforts and struggle of learning a new skill. Through practice, we develop the courage to maintain a consistent direction, and we strengthen our ability to focus. Meditation supports our overall health by training our minds to abide in the present moment with the balanced and creative perspective of non- judgment. We learn to stop wasting our energy on illusions and limitless possibilities; instead, we invest our gifts in the immediate and the real.  At this point in your training, you may wish to print off the four exercises that you have been learning and practice each one for five minutes. You might adopt this as a daily plan, giving you twenty minutes of mindfulness and meditation practice. If you have little ones to care for, take short breaks throughout the day to meditate.  •   For five minutes, make a list of what bothers you today and tell God about it. Then, practice the  3-Minute Breathing Space . 1  •   For five minutes, practice the   Maranatha Meditation . 2  •   For   five minutes, practice the   SALT   Process . You might choose to work on an item from the list of what is bothering you today.  •   For five minutes, practice the   Mercy Meditation   focusing on either yourself or others. 3  Just explore. Your purpose is to find a meditation practice that works for you. In this lesson, we will use the   Mercy Meditation   to extend mercy to another person.   Let’s begin.  Settle into your environment and observe your breathing.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Notice how your body softens on the exhale.   (Pause)   Scan your body for tension and give any tense areas permission to relax. Notice especially your face. Is there tension there? Relax.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF18-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Draw your mind away from the events of the day, from the past or the future, and from others, and focus on what is happening inside your own skin right now.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Allow a person to come to mind to whom you wish to extend mercy, or you might wish to consider a situation in which you find it difficult to extend mercy to someone.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  And now, as you think about that person, reflect for thirty seconds on each of the following three questions. You might jot down the thoughts you wish to remember.  1.   In what areas am I most critical of this person?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. If you haven’t   done so already, take thirty seconds to jot down what came to mind. You might write in your KF journal or on your   Meeting Preparation Guide .   (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   For what do I need to forgive this person?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. Take a moment to jot down what came to mind.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  3.   How do I treat this person when they make a mistake or do not live up to my standards?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause, and write for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now, use your imagination in a healthy way to experiment with bringing compassion to this person. You might call to mind someone who loves this person as they are. This might be someone divine, like God or  Jesus, or perhaps someone mortal and human. You might call to mind one of God’s other creatures.  (Pause)   As you breathe for one minute, observe whatever comes to mind and practice letting go of judgment.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Pause, take a deep breath, and re-engage with the meeting.  You will learn more about mercy in later lessons, but right now you are learning to let go of fear and judgment. This is a way of planting seeds of mercy, not only for others but also for yourself.  Our hymn of mercy is   When I Survey the Wondrous Cross .  Were the whole realm of nature mine,  That were an offering far too small;  Love so amazing, so divine,  Demands my soul, my life, my all . 4  Actually, there is no demand in karis; there is simply an invitation to generously respond   to God’s   gift of salvation so that we may experience more and more of His amazing love.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  In this lesson we will explore the   Claim and Blame Worksheet . This worksheet is designed to help you

3  karisfellowships.com   KF18-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  identify and untangle your claims about what you think you deserve from others and from life. You might ask your Karis Link to explore it with you, and you might also sign up for other KF training opportunities.  Let’s look   briefly at the   Claim and Blame Worksheet   now.  Part One: You Are Here  1.   Indicators and reactions  What feelings or reactions have let you know that you are misoriented? Your KF training begins with mindfulness because without this skill you cannot be aware of how you are feeling or notice how you are reacting, nor can you spot the events that trigger your feelings and reactions.  2.   Identify your emotions  The   Claim and Blame Worksheet   deals with feelings that arise when an event seems unfair, when you  can’t get away with something, and when you are envious of what others do or have.   Nancy has included a list of feelings that may be associated with your claim. However, you might recognize other feelings that are not on the list. Feel free to jot those down, too.  3.   When and what?  Try to determine the event that invited you to take the Judgment Path. You can ask yourself:   When did I start feeling this way? Was there an event that I judged as bad or not good enough? What was that event?  4.   Restoring pride  Your sense of fairness or justice is often related to hurt pride. What do you imagine would fix your feelings and soothe your hurt pride?  Part Two: Looking Deeply  1.   It’s not fair!  Now you can use your imagination to go to an extreme of what you think would be fair. Why is this situation unfair and how does it threaten the   Glory of Me! ?  2.   I deserve  You learned   from Dr. Horney’s book   that you are averse to recognizing your own claims because you need these illusions to maintain your pride system. You may, therefore, find it difficult to identify your claims unless you feel frustrated, cheated, hurt, or compelled to retaliate. Keep in mind that judging as unfair what happens to others may also reveal a claim that you have for yourself. Write down what you believe you deserve in the situation — that is, in your situation, to what do you feel entitled?  3.   My right to react  Now that you have defined what you think you deserve in the situation, you can identify the behaviors and choices that you use to redress the violation of your claim. When your claims are not met, what reactions do you feel you have a right to indulge? These reactions often seem rational, just, or understandable to us in the moment, but they are actually powered by judgment, hurt pride, and fear.  4.   My perfect life  This question helps you define your claim. You get to laugh at yourself a little and explore the imagined

4  karisfellowships.com   KF18-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  superiority of your wisdom and judgments. You also have the chance to be extravagantly and ludicrously honest with yourself.  Part 3: Recovery  1.   Assess the judgment  Recall the   Two Paths Flowchart . If you have judged an event as evil, you have probably felt fear. This is where you explore the fear and the evils that you imagined when your claim was not met. If your claim was met, you may have felt euphoria and judged the event as good. Perhaps by now you can see how your judgments are very partial, unrealistic, and unjust when they are based on a claim.  2.   Identify the fear of loss  You have reacted because something has made mincemeat of your search for the   Glory of Me! , and, as a result, you are gripped by fear, grief, and rage.  3.   Stick to the facts  You can now take the Believe it Path and simply list the sequence of events. This is where you get real. You give up your judgments, detach from your feelings, and just look at the facts. As your True Self grows, you will become more interested in the truth than in your neurotic entitlements and compelling illusions which help you feel superior and protect your pride.  4.   Make a decision  Perhaps at this point you are ready to let go of your judgments and are willing to deal with how things actually are.  5.   Rejoice in the truth  As long as you continue to play with the pretend toys of your illusions, you will not learn the mature skills that you need for handling reality and building healthy relationships. Only the truth can set you free to live in humility and access the gifts of   God’s   grace.  6.   Take action: talk to God  God gives grace only to the humble; He extends an invitation of fellowship to the one who confesses the truth and is ready to make the effort to grow out of egocentric cravings. Pride is so destructive. It is the toxin that stunts your growth and hinders the lives of those around you. God must oppose your pride. He cannot support illusions and fantasies. He is true, and He is working to bring you into truth.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, loosen the grip of pride on my soul.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  KF Confession 4 reminds us of how we waste our energy in the service of the Idol.   Let’s   hear it again:

5  karisfellowships.com   KF18-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  We judged ourselves and others with contempt and felt justified in our wrath.  Jesus often encourages us to think through what we want, and in the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 5, He teaches us to be motivated by our wants rather than driven by the law of our shoulds. 5   We can stop wasting our energy   thinking, “I should do that,” and, instead, use our energy to ask, “What outcome do I want, and how do I get it?”  The text for our lesson is   Matthew 5:3 – 10 . We will be reading this well- known passage in Nancy’s  translation.  3 Happy are beggars in spirit who are continually pleading and crying out for spiritual connection, because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.  4 Happy are those who truly mourn, because they are the ones who shall be comforted by someone who is called alongside to help.  5 Happy are the mild and gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.  6 Happy are those who hunger and thirst for orientation, because they are the ones that shall be satisfied like grazing herds in a spring meadow.  7 Happy are the compassionate and merciful, for they are the ones who shall receive help, compassion, and mercy.  8 Happy are the single-minded, pruned, purified by fire, and free from their guilty, craving hearts, because they are the ones who shall see God.  9 Happy are those who generate peace, for they shall be called the sons of God and carry the authority of His name.  10 Happy are those who have been persecuted for the sake of orientation, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.  Take a deep breath.  Jesus tells us how to be happy, blessed, and favored. He also exposes the lies we tell ourselves about what would make us happy. He invites us to build a happy life by developing oriented qualities and choosing oriented behaviors. Unfortunately, oriented behaviors are difficult to learn when we are caught in the grip  of the Idol’s pride system . It is much easier to claim to possess Christian qualities than it is to grow them in our lives.  Jesus says that if we want to know real, abiding happiness and experience the karis favor of God, we must  recognize the poverty of our Idol’s   pride system and choose another kind of poverty — we must become beggars in the spirit.   Beggars learn quickly what works and what doesn’t   work. They are highly motivated to get their needs met and   don’t   waste their energy gratifying their pride. No beggar comes to a time when he can stop begging. The hunger and thirst that he feels today he will feel tomorrow. The beggar keeps begging until he dies. In KF, we learn to keep begging every day for the needs of our soul to be met and for an ever-expanding spiritual connection with God — and as long as we are training here in this material world, we will need to keep begging.  Look at the list of beatitudes in Matthew 5. Each line begins with the word   happy . Do you want to be happy, or favored? Perhaps you have a claim that you deserve happiness because you have certain beliefs. You might envy the apparent happiness of others and yet ignore the ways in which you are making yourself unhappy. Do you know that it is within your power to be happy, favored, and blessed? Look at the causes of happiness at the end of the sentences in our text. We are happy because we have spiritual

6  karisfellowships.com   KF18-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  authority, because we are comforted, because we are satisfied, because we can see God. In order to produce the effect of being happy, Jesus says that you must develop certain qualities and make certain choices. These qualities and choices are the cause that produces the effect of your happiness. For example, if you want spiritual authority, you must choose to be a beggar in the spirit; if you want to see God working in your life, you must become single-minded. The unwillingness to develop these qualities and make these choices is what interferes with your happiness and well-being.  What do you really want?  Trying to motivate yourself by what you think you should do will not help you productively endure in every situation or in the long run. If you want to achieve your desired outcomes, you will need to learn to motivate yourself by what you really want. Rather than thinking , “I   should hunger and thirst for spiritual connection, ”   you might realize that what you really want is to be satisfied. On the other hand, you might claim that you do hunger and thirst for spiritual connection, or orientation, but your lack of satisfaction is evidence that your claim has no substance. How do you become satisfied? Jesus tells you how. Refuse to prop up your pride system. Learn to keep asking, seeking, and knocking for orientation — just as a hungry person asks, seeks, and knocks for food — and you will become satisfied.  We might compare the motivation of shoulds with the motivation of real wanting. Listen to the following statements and use your mindfulness training to observe your emotional reactions:  •   I should be a beggar in the spirit.  •   I should hunger and thirst for orientation.  •   I should be mild and gentle.  •   I should be a peacemaker.  How does that feel?   (Pause for 5 seconds)  Now, observe your emotions when you hear the following statements:  •   I want spiritual authority.  •   I want to be satisfied and fulfilled.  •   I want to inherit the earth.  •   I want peace within and around me.  (Pause for 5 seconds)  Does this second list of statements feel less tense, more single-minded, and more congruent — more like the voice of your True Self? Does your body feel less strain?   (Pause for 5 seconds)  So, what is   preventing you from accessing God’s   provision of happiness or well-being? This might seem a little crazy, but there are days and even years when we do not want to have spiritual authority, receive mercy, be at peace, or be satisfied. The problem is that a big part of us does not want to be well. Our pride stands in the way. But the good news is that we can allow ourselves to be messed up in our feelings and still choose life. No matter what you feel, choose life. 6   As you taste real life and its outcomes, you will discover how worthwhile it is to keep choosing life.

7  karisfellowships.com   KF18-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, I am willing to be happy. Show me how to get there.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider the power to choose the outcomes of your own life.   (Repeat)   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider the power to choose the outcomes of your own life , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to rest in your awareness as you   consider the power to choose the outcomes of your own life . You might notice a compulsion to argue with yourself or with God, to judge yourself and others, or to make up stories. Give yourself permission now to explore your experience, without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing as you   consider the power to choose the outcomes of your own life.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might recognize what doubt, panic, or hope feels like in your body.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider your power to choose the outcomes of your own life . What do you believe about your power?   (Pause)   How  might your Idol’s pride be hurt if yo u accepted this power to choose?   (Pause)   It’s OK if you don’t know.  Just observe how you respond, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  You might imagine a door of opportunity opening before you. As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome .  (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore your power to choose.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit of truth as He teaches you about your design and authority.  •   Welcome the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)

8  karisfellowships.com   KF18-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 7  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I develop my power to choose, I let go of the longing for, or the fear of, responsibility and self- determination.  •   As I develop my power to choose, I let go of the longing for, or the fear of, appreciation and affection.  •   As I develop my power to choose, I let go of the longing for, or the fear of, security and comfort.  •   As I develop my power to choose, I let go of the fear of changing my outcomes and becoming happy.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are grateful for this time together to heal and to train. Hold us in the power of this redirected energy as You guide us to our real glory. Show us the next step in our healing this week. We want to co-labor with You so that we can access all of Your karis gifts in this life and the next, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   Zindel Segal, J. Mark G Williams and John D Teasdale,   Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy for Depression   (New York: The Guilford Press, 2013), 208. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  2   Laurence Freeman, Editor,   Monastery without Walls: The Spiritual Letters of John Main   (London: Canterbury Press Norwich, 2006), 32.  3   www.livingmindfully.org/ . Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  4   When I Survey the Wondrous Cross   by Isaac Watts (1674 – 1748),   youtu.be/U-hz6L6LAug .  5   Mark 10:51.  6   Deut. 30:19.  7   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html . title: KF19 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF19-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF19 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  In our last lesson, Nancy suggested a plan for a twenty-minute meditation spending five minutes on each of the following four exercises:  1.   Write down what is bothering you today or what you are thankful for and tell God about it. Then practice the   3-Minute Breathing Space . 1  2.   Practice the   Maranatha Meditation . 2  3.   Practice the   SALT   Process . 3   This is where you explore your business.  4.   Practice the   Mercy Meditation   focusing on   either yourself or another person. 4  Print out the mindfulness and meditation exercises that you have learned and keep copies handy for easy review. If it works better for you, practice in five-minute segments at different times during the day. You might set up a reminder on your phone. Your goal is to meditate for twenty minutes twice a day, once in the morning and then again later in the day. Take small steps and see what happens.  You might also revisit the   FAITH Process   integration that you practiced in the last meeting. Review the KF teaching notes and choose an area of your life that you would like to explore. You could also sign up for the   KF Compass   to help   you review the week’s teachings.  Let’s   continue to practice the   Mercy Meditation   and apply it to another person, or you might imagine a situation in which you often find it difficult to offer mercy.  Sit quietly for a few moments. Notice your environment as you breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Draw your  mind away from the events of the day, from other people’s business,   and from the past or the future, and just focus on what is happening inside your own skin right now. Breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   How do you feel? Do you notice your thoughts wandering? Where do they go? Just notice and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now, engage your mind to respond to each of the following three questions for thirty seconds:

2  karisfellowships.com   KF19-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1.   In what areas am I most critical of another person?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause, and if you haven’t   already done so, take a moment to jot down what came to mind.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   For what do I need to forgive this person?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. Write down what came to mind.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  3.   How do I treat this person when he or she violates my claims and shoulds?   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. What came to mind? You might write that down.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now experiment with bringing compassion to this person. Use your imagination in a healthy way to call to mind someone who loves that person as he or she is today. Imagine seeing your chosen person through the eyes of that love. Observe whatever comes to mind, and breathe. As you exhale, practice letting go of your claims and shoulds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. When you practice this meditation, you are planting seeds of mercy, not only for others but also for yourself.  Our hymn for our next KF Confession is   My Faith Looks Up to Thee . Ray Palmer wrote these words in 1830 after seeing Jesus in a vision. You might wish to read the story surrounding this hymn at   cyberhymnal.org .  My faith looks up to Thee,  Thou Lamb of Calvary,  Savior divine!  Now hear me while I pray,  Take all my guilt away,  Oh, let me from this day  Be wholly Thine! 5  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask,   “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  Our claims and shoulds form a kind of psychic structure — a legal system that provides a framework for making decisions. This framework supports the Idol Self and creates an artificial sense of self-confidence and congruence. Living by the legal system of our shoulds and claims is a way of escaping the laborious effort required to build a skilled, mindful, and meaningful life.  Don’t   rely on your feelings while you do your KF work. KF training is exactly like a workout at the gym. You do the work regularly in the hope that you will see results over time. In any workout, you move against resistance in order to get strong. This is true in the gym, and   it’s   also true in KF. If you do not exercise, you will not get strong. Remember our motto:   Train hard. Fight easy .   (Repeat)  When we exercise at the gym, we   don’t   do all the possible exercises at once. We do a few here and there

3  karisfellowships.com   KF19-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  according to what we need. You can use the same strategy for your work in Karis Fellowships. As you learn different KF tools, use the ones that seem to fit your present need. Ask your Karis Link to help you.  Replace the thought,   “ I should do my KF work, ”   with the question,   “ What outcome do I want ? ”   (Repeat)  Look at the list of Beatitudes that Jesus has given you. 6   Do you want the outcomes that He tells you will make you favored and happy? What outcomes in your life do you really want?   Let’s get real.   Your choices tell you what you really want.  If you are willing to work toward the outcomes that Jesus describes, you will experience all kinds of rewards along the way, like increasing trust, joy, and the pleasures of gratitude. Each step forward is success. Remind yourself that perfection is not your goal. Instead, teach yourself this affirmation:   Every effort is success. (Repeat)   You are successful whenever you attend a meeting, do a worksheet, read Dr.  Horney’s   book, practice meditation, review the teaching notes, or fill out your   Meeting Preparation Guide . Tell God and others what you want. Seek, using all the support and tools offered to you. Knock when the opportunity to explore presents itself.  When you unload your shoulds and claims, you are investing in your True Self, and you become authentic enough to explore what you really want. Untrammeled by compelling needs, you are able to access and explore your free will, perhaps for the first time in your life. You can learn to distinguish between the compelling needs of the Idol and your real wants, and you can grow into the kind of person who is able to freely enjoy the fulfillment of those wants. Personal development takes time and training, and when you pursue your real wants out of your True Self, you will have the endurance to go through the process.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord Jesus, help me develop healthy free will so that I can explore my real wants. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  This month we are learning about KF Confession 4:  We judged ourselves and others with contempt and felt justified in our wrath.  In our last Bible lesson, we looked at the Beatitudes in the Gospel of Matthew, chapter 5. We learned that it is much healthier to be motivated by the desire for real happiness than to be driven by the taskmasters of our legal systems. Do you believe what Jesus says about happiness? Do you want the outcomes that Jesus promises you, or do you really want something else? Your choices will reveal the truth about what you want. For example, your choice to do your KF work reveals your intention to grow and your desire to cooperate with God. Your efforts show Him that you mean business about being happy and gaining His promised rewards.  Let’s look at another passage that   encourages us to make choices about what we want. This is Nancy ’s  paraphrase of   First Peter 3:8 – 12 .

4  karisfellowships.com   KF19-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  8 My purpose in teaching you about husbands and wives is to train the whole community to be harmonious and compassionate, having the same mutual commitment toward one another, to be like loving siblings, to have healthy bowels and the ability to stay inside your own skin;   9 not returning hurt for hurt, or insult for insult, but doing just the opposite. Bless each other by speaking well and resist any vindictive triumph for this reason: you were called into blessing and praise so that you might inherit blessing and praise.   10 Let me quote this proverb:   “ Those who desire to live well — to love and experience good days — reveal that intention by refusing to give voice to the pride system of the Idol Self and speak the harm on the tip of their tongues.   11 They must turn away   from misorientation and do good. They must seek peace and pursue it. ”   12 Why is this proverb famous? Because the eyes of the Lord are upon oriented people and His ears hear them express their needs and wants, but the face of the Lord is against those who choose misorientation and do harm.  Take a deep breath.  Just before this passage, Peter has been teaching about the relationship of marriage. Did you know that even though marriage is a legal contract, it is also a karis relationship? In his book   Getting the Love You Want , Dr. Hendrix explains why marriages built on legal systems are full of conflict, while marriages based on positive mutual exchange grow in love. The purpose of   Peter’ s teaching is to guide us in all our relationships, both in the intense laboratory of marriage and in our interactions with our community.  The success of a relationship is directly related to the number of positive interactions between the people involved. 7   Both giving and expressing gratitude are positive interactions. This is why cultures develop systems of etiquette and good manners. No matter how you feel, you can choose to act and react with good manners. Good manners provide beneficial limitations or boundaries that maintain a positive quality of engagement and protect the trust necessary for healthy growing relationships. These manners rein us in when we feel compelled by volatile moods or egocentric pride to choose misorientation. Just like every other system in this material world, relationships are subject to real cause and effect. Misoriented behavior pushes all relationships into further distrust and fear. When you react with the bad manners of imposing, manipulating, or withholding, you block a future inheritance of blessing for yourself and for others.  In our passage from First Peter, we see some very clear   do ’ s   and   don’ts .   Do ’ s   and   don’ts   are necessary. They show us how to get what we want. Peter teaches that if we desire life , love, and the Lord’s favor,   we must first pay attention to our words. Do your words offer grace, or do they impose your claims and shoulds? 8   Our words tell us a lot about who we are, and who we are produces the outcomes of our lives. Next, we must identify our misoriented behavior. Are you aware of unproductive patterns that you repeat over and over again? Unhealthy repetitive patterns are probably compulsive. Have some compassion on yourself, but get real! If you want the kind of life and love that Peter is talking about, you will have to loosen the deadly grip that the Idol has on you — and to do that,   you will need God’s help.   Do you want  God’s help? If you do, you can prove   it to Him by your choices. Train hard with your KF tools. Refuse to do damage. Choose good and avoid harm. Do whatever it takes to learn to live in peace with others and  within yourself. You cannot get God’s   substantial help in any other way.  By offering positive interactions in any situation, you give a karis gift — a gift that invites communion in a  safe environment. Every positive effort you make to build human relationships fulfills the logos, God’s  way of doing things, and strengthens your personal relationship with God.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF19-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  You will always get what you’ve always got if you always think   what you’ve always thought. Let me repeat  that:   You will always get what you’ve always got if you always think what you’ve always thought.   Our job in Karis Fellowships is to change our thinking. Changing our thinking changes our choices, and changing our choices changes our outcomes. You are here to change what you think in order to get something new. Paul teaches in Second Corinthians that, in Christ, you are a new creation. Old things and old thinking have passed away; and look! — all things are becoming new. 9  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, help me change my choices and create new outcomes. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider telling God what you really want. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider telling God what you really want,   how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)  Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow what you are experiencing to rest in your awareness .   Observe whatever tension you may be feeling as you   consider telling God what you really want .   (Pause)   Your wants at this time are probably  misoriented, but that doesn’t matter. Give yours elf permission now to explore your wants without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing as you   consider telling God what you really want.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what futility, shame, or perhaps wonder feels like in your body. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider what you really want   today .   Does that feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe.   (Pause)   What do you believe about your wants?   (Pause)   Are your desires based on past experiences or family systems? Do your desires support your real, designed glory or do they support your pride system?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

6  karisfellowships.com   KF19-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Heal  As you inhale, think:   Welcome .   (Pause)   Invite your desire into your space, not to be judged as either good or bad but to be blessed as simply your want.   It doesn’t matter whether the want   is oriented or misoriented right now. Welcome your want in for a chat and a cup of tea. Breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, welcome the Holy Spirit into the conversation and give Him permission to explore your desire.  (Pause for 10 seconds)   If you learn something, welcome what you learn. You might wish to jot it down.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  As you breathe, hold your desire in a tender place of compassion and listen to the following statements. On the exhale, let go of any compulsive need that may surround this desire.  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   Although I want this thing, I let go of my longing for power and control.  •   Although I want this thing, I let go of my longing for esteem and affection.  •   Although I want this thing, I let go of my longing for security and comfort.  •   Although I want this thing, I let go of my longing for perfection.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time together of healing and training. Hold us in the power of this new direction as You guide us to our real glory and to living a life of truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and mission, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   Zindel Segal, J. Mark G. Williams, and John D. Laurence Freeman (London: Canterbury Press Norwich, 2006), 32.  3 See KF11.  4   www.livingmindfully.org . title: KF20 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF20-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF20 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of etern ity.” (Psalm 139:23– 2)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  This month we will be learning about the self-hate experience. You might think that your enemy is self- hate, but that is not true. Your real enemy is the Idol Self. Self-hate is simply the result of living in the  Idol’s system.   When you fail to meet your idealized standards, the Idol uses self-hate to drive you into compulsive choices and then punishes you with more self-hate for having made those choices. Over the last few weeks, we have been retraining our minds and learning to value our real or imagined failures as opportunities for growth. We have also been exploring tools that help us deal with the associated feelings, motivations, and behaviors of self-hate.   The training isn’t easy, but we are training hard   so that we can fight easy for the life of our True Self. Even in the midst of self-hate we can connect to God and make oriented choices.  Research has proven the many positive benefits of meditation and mindfulness practice. 1   One of those benefits is the ability to recognize self-hate. Mindfulness training helps us pause, step back, and observe rather than react. The ability to step back gives us the breathing space that we often need to make a healthier choice.  The Self-Hate Massage  Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Bring to mind an area of your life that chronically stirs up self-hate for you. Perhaps you have made some mistakes, or perhaps your limitations have prevented you from achieving something. You might dislike your physical body, or you might wish  that you were someone else. Let’s   connect that hurt to our breathing and get acquainted with it using our new tools.  CONSIDER  Take a moment to collect yourself within your present space. Feel the air or the clothing on your skin. Notice any noises.   (Pause for 30 seconds)   Now consider this area of self-hate. Notice the discomfort you feel when you think of it. Even though you hate this thing, gently and without judgment allow it to rest inside your skin for one minute. Breathe.   (Pause for 1 minute)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF20-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  COMPASSION  As you breathe, experience yourself as a creature with limitations breathing in a material world.   (Pause)  You are not a god.   (Pause)   As you breathe in and out, imagine your area of self-hate moving in and out with the breath, massaging this place in your soul that is stuck or cramped. For one minute, help that area of self-hate circulate in and out with the breath. Give it and receive it with compassion.   (Pause for 1 minute)  CLEANSE  Notice your entire body as it breathes.   (Pause)   Breathe with your mind, body, and soul as you open the doors of doors of the prison cells of your shame, regrets, pain, and guilt.   (Pause)   Allow the clean air to sweep through those dark, stagnant places for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  And pause.  Our hymn for this confession is   My Faith Looks Up to Thee .  May Thy rich grace impart  Strength to my fainting heart,  My zeal inspire;  As Thou hast died for me,  Oh, may my love to Thee  Pure, warm, and changeless be,  A living fire. 2  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   this   training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we are exploring KF Confession 5:  We attacked and cruelly suppressed our True Self and lost our true life.  Let’s consider these five points about self -hate:  1.   Our job is to grow out of our self-hate  This month we will begin looking at how self-hate operates in our lives. We have two choices when dealing with self-hate: we can either appease it by sacrificing our True Self and submitting to the demands of the Idol, or we can grow out of it.  2.   Train hard – fight easy  When we experience self-hate, we often   don’t   know what we are experiencing. We just suddenly feel the need to run back to old feelings, stories, and behaviors that have made us feel safe or comfortable in the past. We   can’t   deal with self-hate without training. This is why it is imperative that we train hard.   It’s   not our goal as God’s people to repeatedly cause harm and create chaos . Our goal is to

3  karisfellowships.com   KF20-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  produce the Fruit of the Spirit in every situation. 3   To do that, we need to train hard so that we can fight self-hate easy.  3.   Calm the fear through mindfulness training  Over the years we have learned to fear self-hate and the ravaging chaos it creates.   What’s more, we  have developed automatic and habitual patterns of thought and behavior that we hope will enable us to avoid our self-hate. Rather than reverting to these habitual patterns, we can use mindfulness to calm our minds and bodies. We are then free to choose healthy patterns of thought and behavior that help us grow out of our self-hate.  Just as mindfulness training helps us refocus our wandering minds during meditation, it empowers us to redirect our thinking when the Idol has us by the throat and is lashing us with self-hate. When we recognize the symptoms of self-hate, we can choose to simply wait and mindfully endure our chaotic feelings until we are able to figure out   what’s   going on. We learn that we do not have to react. Instead, we can compassionately observe, listen, and learn.  Writing the lessons for this confession was very difficult for Nancy because for most of her life she had been paralyzed by self-hate. She felt terrified and wanted to go into paralysis and procrastination to affirm her compulsive need to feel inadequate and a disappointment both to herself and to others. She wrote for a whole week and was unable to find her path.  4.   Self-hate can actually strengthen our endurance  Self-hate has the power to stop us in our tracks, so how was Nancy able to write this lesson? She had been in training through the book study and through meditation practice. She persevered in her work despite her discomfort, working against the resistance of her fear. This work-out strengthened her courage and trained her to endure skillfully. She was able to choose healthy and productive behaviors no matter how she felt. The week of writing and getting nowhere actually led her somewhere. She learned how to be productive in the midst of her self-hate, knowing that God would support her if she humbly endured her discomforts.  5.   The unlived life is not worth examining  Socrates, the ancient Greek philosopher, said that   the   unexamined life is not worth living , 4   but some writers turn that quotation around and assert that   the   unlived life is not worth examining .   (Repeat)  We have lived in a state of perpetual flight from self-hate for so long that flight feels natural to us. Running away may help us feel less tension in the moment, but that choice is compulsive rather than free and does not express the glory of God. Running away results in an unlived life. The examination of such a life might awaken a little pity, but it will also be extremely boring.  Flight from self-hate looks different for different Idol types. Some will run away by controlling or abusing themselves or others; some fly by appeasing and pleasing; and then there are those who flee by taking refuge in their fortress of non-engagement. All neurotic flight is self-sabotage. Think of any  good story. It’s the discovery of the hero’s character , how he or she grows and responds to life, that grips our interest and helps us relate to the hero.   But what if the story was a constant series of “Thi s scary thing happened, and he ran away. And then this other painful thing happened, and she ran away. And   then there was this incredible opportunity and . . .”?   By now we can finish the story for ourselves — we ran away.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF20-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  With training, you can learn to stand without running away. You can mindfully stay inside your skin as the wave of self-hate rushes over you and eventually exhausts itself on the shore.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Captain of the hosts, train me to stand.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about th e Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  KF Confession 5 describes the path of wasted energy and lost potential:  We attacked and cruelly suppressed our True Self and lost our true life.  Let’s look at   Psalm 23:1 – 4 . Nancy offers here a valid alternative translation using familiar KF vocabulary.  1 The Lord is my Shepherd ,  I have everything that I need today.  2 He makes me lie down satisfied in green pastures;  He leads me beside quiet waters.  3 For His own reputation and for my reputation as His creature,  He restores and repairs my True Self.  4 He guides me in the tracks of orientation even though  I walk through the valley of the shadow of death.  I fear no harm, for You are with me.  The guidance and training of Your rod and staff comfort me.  Take a deep breath.  1.   Our Shepherd is the Lord, not our Idol Self  Our relationship with the Shepherd is not a legal contract based on shoulds, claims, and punishments. It is based on the trust and the trustworthiness that is developed in a karis relationship. The Shepherd takes into consideration your unique personhood as He guides you; He responds to what you reveal about yourself. He is the one who trains you for your joy and for your mission.  2.   I have everything that I need for today  With Jesus as our Shepherd, and not the Idol Self, we can gradually let go of fighting for our idealized life, fleeing self-hate, and trying to get our compulsive needs met. As we spend time doing things His way, we begin to experience satisfaction and contentment.  One of the things that we need when we are in self-hate is a quiet, safe place. When you are with someone who is suffering from self-hate,   Nancy’s   advice is this:   No sudden movements. No loud noises.   (Repeat)   In other words, be compassionate around those in self-hate, including yourself — and be very careful.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF20-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  3.   He restores my True Self, not my Idol Self  In order to restore our lost True Self, we need to calm down, follow   the Shepherd’s   leading, and find rest. The Hebrew word for   restore   can be translated as   turning back . It also carries the meaning of  repair . Does your soul need repair? The soul that Jesus died for and repairs is our True Self, not the Idol Self. Sometimes we feel very disappointed about that.  4.   He guides me in the tracks of ori entation for His name’s sake  If we call ourselves Christians, we bear the name of Jesus and are responsible for His reputation. As oriented people, we are the representatives of His name and character in this messed-up world. Sometimes we get caught up in representing a way of thinking or an organization. That is not our real business. Our business is to be oriented to God and represent His kingdom.  5.   The tracks of orientation lead into the valley of the shadow of death  To our dismay, the tracks of orientation always lead into the valley of the shadow of death. It will feel like death to give up old patterns and behaviors that you have habitually   used to save your Idol’s life. 5  We are in Karis Fellowships because we want a different life, but in order to gain that different life, we have to l ose the Idol’s life . The fear of death is only a shadow for Christians. It is the darkness that we enter when we dare to resist the Idol Self and its pride system. The fear of death is real, but it moves on like a cloud passing over the sun. It only has the power of a shadow.  6.   His rod and staff comfort me  The rod and staff are instruments of training — the   do ’ s   and   don’ts   of the Bible. They replace the shoulds and claims of your own legal systems. When you commit   to doing things God’s way , you have to stop doing things your way. That feels like losing your life. But when you want to abandon the path toward orientation and avoid this difficult process of training,   the promise of God’s presenc e and His faithful provision can help you keep going.   You can trust the rod and staff in the Shepherd’s hands as  He trains you for your potential.  Psalm 23 encourages us to grow in our courage while we confront the problem of our pride, self-hate, and judgments.   With God’s support , we can journey productively through any problem.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Shepherd, strengthen my courage and endurance for the valley. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have   comments or questions about the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider something in your life that feels like the valley of the shadow of death.   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process

6  karisfellowships.com   KF20-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Feelings  How does it feel to stand on the edge of the valley of the shadow of death?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to rest in your awareness as you   consider this situation that feels like the valley of the shadow of death . Observe whatever tension you may be feeling.   (Pause)   Give yourself permission now to explore your feelings and thoughts without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you consider this situation. What sensations are there?   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to respectfully observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider this situation that feels like the valley of the shadow of death . Do you feel compelled to judge that valley as good or evil?   (Pause)   What do you believe about this valley? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)  How m ight your Idol’s pride be hurt if you   were to step into the valley?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have   considered a   valley that feels like death . You are not alone in your experience. In the Bible we read of many people who have walked through dark valleys.   (Pause)   Feelings are just chemical reactions in your body, and that chemistry is often created by your past experiences. 6   Just acknowledging your feelings can help you understand yourself. When feelings bring you information, you can choose what you will do with that information.   (Pause)   We must each contend with our own valleys, so breathe and allow some compassion to flow toward yourself and toward others. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Allow your feelings to inform you but not motivate you. Apply your training, consider what is your business, and make oriented choices as you enter your valley.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about th e   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for the gift of healing and training together. Help us find courage in Your promises as You guide us to access Your provision. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to pass through the valley of the shadow of death so that we can flourish in our connection with our True

7  karisfellowships.com   KF20-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Self and design, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   www.healthline.com/nutrition/12-benefits-of-meditation#section13 .  2   My Faith Looks Up to Thee   by Ray Palmer (1808 – 1887),   youtu.be/X5g-Att0bmE .  3   Gal. 5:22 – 23.  4   en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The unexamined life is not worth living .  5   Matt. 10:39.  6   en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candace Pert .
