karisfellowships.com   KF21-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF21 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  This month we are learning about the self-hate experience. Self-hate is the product of the condemning judgments that we make when we fail to achieve our idealized standards. It brings to consciousness the deep judgments that we carry with us all the time. However, regardless of the pain that self-hate causes, self-hate is not our enemy. The real enemy is the Idol Self. This Idol depends on the fear of scathing judgment to lash us into submission and to maintain its pride system. But if you walk courageously through the valley of the shadow of death, working with your tools, you will drain the stagnant storage tank of self-condemnation and judgment that fuels your self-hate. The awareness of self-hate will become an invitation for exploration rather than the paralyzing, excruciating torment that you have experienced in the past.  For the last few months, we have been training our minds to observe what is within us, bubbling up from the depths of our souls. This month we will practice observing those bubbles, the evidence of our weaknesses and strengths, without getting caught up in the feelings, motivations, and behaviors of self- hate. With training, we learn to step back from self-hate, choose life, give a blessing, fortify our True Self, and strengthen our connection with God.  The Self-Hate Massage  Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Bring to mind an area of your life that chronically stirs up self-hate for you. Perhaps you have made a mistake, or perhaps your limitations are preventing you from achieving your dreams and goals. Something in your life may be imperfect, or you might fear that you are not good enough. Perhaps you have challenged your Idol Self in some way. We will connect that hurt to our breathing and get acquainted with it using our KF tools.  CONSIDER  Take a moment to collect yourself within your present space. Feel the air or the clothing on your skin. Notice any noises.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Now consider this area of self-hate. Notice the discomfort you feel when you think of it. Even though you hate this thing, allow it to rest inside your skin for one minute, without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 1 minute)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF21-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  COMPASSION  As you breathe, experience yourself as a creature with limitations breathing in a material world.   (Pause)  You are not a god.   (Pause)   As you breathe in and out, imagine your area of self-hate moving in and out with the breath, massaging the place in your soul that is stuck or cramped. For one minute, give it and receive it with compassion.   (Pause for 1 minute)  CLEANSE  Notice your entire body as it breathes.   (Pause)   Breathe with your mind, body, and soul as you open the doors of the prison cells of your shame, rage, disappointments, and guilt.   (Pause)   Allow the clean air to sweep through those dark, stagnant places for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  And pause.  Our hymn for this confession is   My Faith Looks Up to Thee .  While life’s dark maze I tread,  And griefs around me spread,  Be Thou my guide;  Bid darkness turn to day,  Wipe sorrow’s tears away,  Nor let me ever stray  From Thee aside. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  KF Confession 5 reminds us that our self-hate is a tragic and colossal waste of glory and potential:  We attacked and cruelly suppressed our True Self and lost our true life.  The Idol ’s   system is like a fascist regime that suppresses the real power of the people. The word  suppressed   reminds us that beneath   the Idol’s system   there is another power at work — a power that we can access to free ourselves from the Idol and actualize our potential.  All tyrants use fear to control others and our inner tyrant, the Idol, is no different. It uses the fear of hurt pride and self-condemnation to control us. Fear is the strongest motivator that most of us know, and we have learned to turn it to a dubious advantage. Fear keeps us moving. It forces us to take action, and depending on our neurotic development, we habitually fight or flee when events trigger our fear. Through fight or flight, we create the illusion that we are doing something about our fear.  A mastery person was proud of his imagined sense of justice. He hated himself whenever he showed mercy to someone, so he would regularly flee from opportunities to be merciful and retreat into his habitual patterns of aggression. He was more terrified of his self-hate than he was of the damage that he caused by attacking.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF21-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  A resigned person felt the terror of self-hate whenever an event revealed her inner conflicts and her need for self-development. She had a taboo against making changes in her life and was proud of her imagined ability to detach from her feelings. Whenever she was presented with an invitation to grow, she would flee by shutting down.  The strange thing about our relationship with self-hate is that we fear it and need it at the same time. So, although we fear the damaging effects of self-hate, we often actively do things to keep our self-hate alive. We need self-hate to keep us moving toward our imagined glory; we cannot afford to let something die that spurs us on. To keep our self-hate alive, we hurt others and ourselves, neglect our training and our rest, fumble our jobs and our relationships, and revert to addictive, compulsive behaviors. We then concoct a story that focuses on our misoriented choices, but this story is actually a smokescreen that obscures our understanding of the real problem, which is our   Idol’s   hurt pride.  When we make the judgment that our choices   and “mistakes”   fall short of our imagined standards of perfection, our pride is wounded, and we then hate ourselves and often despise anything or anyone connected to us. Our self-hate invites self-torment and we punish ourselves with degrading and destructive thoughts, feelings, and actions. The fear of self-torment becomes a powerful motivator that relentlessly drives us to work harder to achieve   our Idol’s   impossible and ever-shifting standards. Unfortunately, and inevitably, we   meet with more “failure” and   end up crippled with more self-hate as we try to force ourselves beyond our limitations and created design.  Here are some suggestions that might help you compassionately manage your self-hate:  1.   Review   Dr. Horney’s   book  Continue to explore   Neurosis and Human Growth   looking for insights into self-hate. 2   Make a list of areas that could be self-hate hotspots for you.  2.   Write a letter of compassion to yourself  What would you say to encourage a friend who is in self-hate? What would encourage you? Write down your thoughts in a letter of encouragement to yourself and keep this letter in your KF notebook. When you begin to break free, your Idol will invariably use self-hate as a whip to force you back into line and suppress any efforts you might make toward your healing. So, in this letter, remind yourself that we often experience self-hate when we refuse to comply with our Idol.  3.   Talk to your   Karis Link  Hopefully, your Karis Link has learned some tips for managing self-hate. You might ask them to do a KF worksheet with you. Together, consider and appreciate the progress you have made since joining Karis Fellowships.  4.   Talk to someone who can help you reconnect to reality  This person can be anyone, a professional or just someone wise, who can give you a   “ reality check ”  and point you back to the Believe It Path. Self-hate is largely the product of illusions. A reality check reminds you of what is true, what is real, and what is your business.  5.   In the midst of your misery, remember to pray  If you are training hard, ask God to give you an encouraging present or gift. Watch for His care and  then return to Him a gift of gratitude. God’s mercy is greater than your self -hate.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF21-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  6.   Make a gratitude list  Write down the things for which you are thankful. Gratitude creates soothing endorphin chemistry that helps your mind and body return to the Christian reality of positive hope. 3  7.   Mindfully breathe  Learn to respond to self-hate with mindful breathing, connecting to your body and to God.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Shepherd, what does my self-hate reveal to You about me? What can it reveal to me about You? (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  We are our own worst enemy . Let’s stop   blaming others or our circumstances and acknowledge that our real enemy is ourselves.  Last week we began looking at Psalm 23 from a KF perspective. Here is a summary of what we learned:  1.   The Lord our Shepherd meets our real needs  Jesus said, “I am the good Shepherd.” 4   He provides the security and support that we need as we give up   our Idol’s law and pride system.  2.   It is Jesus who restores, or repairs, our soul  Our redeemed and alive soul is our True Self. Jesus created our soul and He knows how to repair it. He wants to help us become the people He created us to be.  3.   The Idol Self will not support the restoration of our soul  In order to survive and maintain its power, the Idol Self will resist any effort you make to restore your True Self. If you choose humility and freedom, the Idol will fiercely oppose your efforts using fear and self-hate as its weapons. You will enter the valley of the shadow of death.  4.   The Shepherd’s rod and staff   guide and help us  Secure in   the Shepherd’s care, we can refuse to be guided by our shoulds, taboos, and claims and , instead, learn to respond to His guidance. With skillful hands, the Shepherd uses His rod and staff to train, direct, and protect us, meeting our needs and responding to our choices. The Shepherd knows what particular training and provision each person requires to help them maintain an oriented path.  Now let’s   look at the last two verses of   Psalm 23 , which   Nancy has translated using some alternative vocabulary to help expand our understanding.  5 You set in order before me a table with my particular limitations.  You have enriched my head with oil;

5  karisfellowships.com   KF21-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  My cup overflows with abundance.  6 Good things and kindnesses will follow after me all the days of my life,  And throughout my life I will return to the house of the Lord.  Take a deep breath.  Most of us have heard that the Lord prepares a table before us   in the presence of enemies . According to  Strong’s   Concordance, the Hebrew word for enemies also means a narrow place, or a binding, as in being tied up. There is a sense of distress and limitation as in a besieged city. To give us a more thorough understanding of this psalm, Nancy has conveyed this idea of restriction by using the word   limitations . When we meet with limitations, we often feel distressed, or under siege, because we perceive these limitations as obstacles to our happiness and satisfaction.   Let’s listen   again to verse 5   in Nancy’s  translation:   You set in order before me a table with my particular limitations. (Repea t) Your table is set with limitations that are uniquely yours. They are part of the abundance that is promised to you through the picture of anointing oil and a cup that overflows. How can that be?  Real limitations protect us. The Shepherd knows what we can handle at our present stage of development, and He uses real limitations to help protect us from what we cannot handle. When we mindfully accept what   is,   and courageously sit at the table ordered for   us , our limitations become part of our strategy rather than the focus of our judgments. This oriented submission to reality invites us to work creatively within our limitations and discover our great potential. 5  In misorientation, however, we can rarely imagine this potential. We are fixated on what   should   be, so rather than exploring our real potential in a particular situation, we feel discontented and resentful. We look around at   other people’s tables and feel the unfairness of   not having what others have. This is neurotic envy.  The promise that goodness and kindnesses will follow us and that our home is with the Lord our Shepherd inspires us to courageously sit at our own table and stop looking around at other tables.  At this point, we might ask ourselves:   Do I want to leave a trail of goodness, health, and compassionate mercy behind me, or would I rather continue to work hard at actualizing my Idol Self? Do I want to face the realities of my present situation and discover the potential of my particular challenges and strengths, or am I only interested in my judgment of how things should be? What do I want?  What do you want?  Our prayer might go something like this:  Shepherd, I want to leave behind me a trail of goodness and kindnesses. Help me make that happen.  (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water, and prepare to take a few notes. Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.

6  karisfellowships.com   KF21-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (Pause for 10 seconds )  Here is our integration focus:   Consider one of your present limitations. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  How does it feel when you   consider one of your present limitations? (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Gently hold in awareness your experience with this limitation. Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider this limitation.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might recognize what frustration, unfairness, or self- condemnation feels like in your body. You might feel relief. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider one of your present limitations.   Do you feel compelled to judge this limitation as good or evil?   (Pause)  What do you believe when you make this judgment? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   How might  your Idol’s pride be hurt if you were   to submit to this limitation? How might your True Self be liberated?  (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  As you breathe, repeat to yourself the word   Welcome .  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore your limitations.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit, who wants to lead you to abundance.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 6  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I observe this limitation, I let go of the craving for power and control.  •   As I observe this limitation, I let go of the craving for self-esteem and affection.  •   As I observe this limitation, I let go of the craving for security and comfort.  •   As I observe this limitation, I let go of the craving to escape my situation.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.

7  karisfellowships.com   KF21-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time of healing and training. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You continue to guide us to our real glory and to the truth of who you created us to be. With Your rod and staff, train us for the next step as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and design, with the Creation and the community, and with You, for the honor and glory of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   My Faith Looks Up to Thee   by Ray Palmer (1808 – 1887).  2   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).  3   simplyfit4life.com/releasing-endorphins-no-its-not-a-disease .  4   John 10:11 – 16.  5   en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Obstacle_Is_the_Way .  6   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html . title: KF22 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF22-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF22 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways o f eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Many of us are just now realizing the truth of KF Confession 5:  We attacked and cruelly suppressed our True Self and lost our true life.  When we notice that we are attacking and suppressing ourselves, or attacking and suppressing others, we can exercise our mindfulness muscles to help us recognize and disengage from the feelings, motivations, and behaviors of our self-hate. We can then use our KF tools to explore and reorient what we are experiencing. Both mindfulness training and KF tools help us reconnect with our True Self.  The   Self-Hate Massage  Assume a mindfulness posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   Bring to mind an area of your life that consistently stirs up self-hate for you. Perhaps you have made some mistakes, or perhaps your limitations have prevented you from achieving something. You might dislike your physical body, or you might wish  that you were someone else. Let’s connect that hurt   to our breathing and get acquainted with it using our new tools . (Pause for 10 seconds)  CONSIDER  Take a moment to collect yourself within your present space. Sense the air or the clothing on your skin. Notice any noises.   (Pause for 30 seconds)   Now consider this area of self-hate. Notice the discomfort you feel when you think of it. Even though you hate this thing, allow it to rest without judgment inside your skin for one minute, and breathe.   (Pause for 1 minute)  COMPASSION  As you breathe, experience yourself as a creature with limitations breathing in a material world.   (Pause)  You are not a god.   (Pause)   As you breathe in and out, imagine your area of self-hate moving in and out with the breath, massaging this place in your soul that is stuck or cramped. For one minute, give it and receive it with compassion.   (Pause for 1 minute)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF22-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  CLEANSE  Notice your entire body as it breathes.   (Pause)   Breathe with your mind, body, and soul as you open the doors of the prison cells of your shame, rage, regrets, and guilt.   (Pause)   Allow the clean air to sweep through those dark, stagnant places for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  And pause.  Our prayer is based on Revelation 3:20.  Lord Jesus, You stand at the door of my life and knock. I am learning to hear Your voice and open the door. Come, Lord Jesus! (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time   permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  Our misoriented development often determines how we attack and suppress our True Self. If you are living with other misoriented people, you might try to identify their self-hate hotspots so that you can quickly recognize when they are in self-hate and gain a better understanding of why they do what they do, think what they think, and feel what they feel. Understanding helps you lovingly   stand   rather than react when the behaviors or choices of others feel so personal. Whenever you or another person turns  away from the Idol’s compulsive need to react, self -hate will inevitably follow. In order to maintain an oriented direction, you must be able to step back from the invitation to engage with that self-hate —  whether your own self- hate or another’s— and then endure the tension of refusing to repeat old patterns  of behavior. That’s why , in our KF training, we learn to endure before we learn to deal with self-hate. Self- hate will accompany every training opportunity in your process of redemption, so if you do not have the strength to endure the discomforts of self-hate, you will not be able to grow out of the pride system that drives your self-hate and determines your choices.  Every neurotic is vulnerable to self-hate. Self-effacing types are thrown into turmoil when they lose  someone’s support   or take the biggest cookie. Mastery types hate themselves when they feel manipulated or helpless, when   things don’t go their way , or when they feel confused. Resigned types feel acute anxiety and withdraw support from others when they begin to feel their feelings, take charge of their own development, or sense that the community requires something from them.  All of us are vulnerable to feelings of self-hate when we compare our present condition to our expectations of what we   should be   by now. Whenever we measure our present condition against these expectations, our real progress is judged as paltry or meaningless and therefore ignored, or even abhorred. Learn to recognize and hold in your mind the real progress you have made. The record of your  Meeting Preparation Guides   and spontaneous positive observations offered by trustworthy people are clear evidence of that progress.  The Internal Parents  When you are in self-hate, your internal parents, father and mother, are your two greatest allies. These two archetypes can teach you self-discipline and self-nurture.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF22-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  The father archetype stands up to protect and defend the True Self. He knows that training in self- management feels just as uncomfortable as any other kind of training, so he helps us endure our feelings while he directs our intellect toward training hard and taking action. He defends our minds and bodies from chaotic emotions, and when we are faced with the challenge of learning self-management, he encourages us to endure the inevitable sense of self-deprivation.  Building up the True Self is similar to building up our physical bodies. In our misoriented condition, we have allowed the muscles of maturity to atrophy, and now they are sluggish and whiny when we ask them to perform. When you begin working on any kind of development, you feel uncomfortable and may even suffer, but after the workout you have the satisfaction of having made a good effort toward your goal. If you are suffering or stuck, rather than looking for immediate release from the tension of your discomfort take some time to observe your condition as you endure. Then, you might ask yourself, or you might even ask a father that you admire,   “How would a n excellent coach or   father direct me now?”   (Repeat)  Self-nurture is the internal mother. While the father keeps us on track in the midst of our suffering, the mother is caring for our needs. She tucks us into bed early. She gives us nourishing and even delightful food. She takes us for a walk and encourages us to breathe fresh air, and, like a gentle mother, she lets us cry our hearts out for a time or mope and fuss like an infant. Our internal mother allows us to have our feelings, but she does not allow us to abuse ourselves or others with those feelings. Our feelings are our feelings, and they are our responsibility.  This week explore your internal parenting. Observe how you interact with yourself within your own mind and observe your interactions with others. Consider how you were parented. That might give you some clues as to why you treat yourself and others the way that you do. When you are in self-hate, you might imagine what advice and encouragement an excellent father or mother would offer.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Loving Shepherd, be for me the voice of excellent parents.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  KF Confession 5 reminds us that when we attack and cruelly suppress our True Self, we create destructive consequences; we end up losing our true life. What would our lives be like if we accepted and cared for ourselves as God accepts and cares for us?  Let’s look at   Psalm 103 , which describes   God as a loving father. Nancy has expanded the meaning of this psalm by contrasting the demands and unmerciful retribution of the Idol Self with the kind intention and mercy of God. This psalm is a little long, so relax and consider just one or two ideas that resonate with you.  A psalm   of David in praise of the Lord’s mercies:

4  karisfellowships.com   KF22-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1 Tell of the goodness of the Lord, my True Self,  And all that is within me reveal His exceptional character.  2 Tell of the goodness of the Lord, my True Self,  And forget none of His benefits (especially when I am in self-hate);  3 The Lord, who pardons all of my iniquities (even when I can’t forgive myself),  The Lord, who heals all of my diseases (even when I can’t figure out how to stop being  neurotic),  4 The Lord, who redeems my life from the pit (even when I’ve dug that pit for myself),  The Lord, who endows me with lovingkindness and compassion (even when I can’t  experience it),  5 Who satisfies my desires with good things (even when I can’t recognize what is good).  His goal is to renew my original, created design so that I can soar like an eagle rising on its wings.  6 The Lord performs oriented deeds (and hopes that I will do the same),  And He gives justice to all who are oppressed (crushed   by the Idol’s legal systems, pride,  and self-hate).  7 He revealed His good and beneficial support to Moses, His ability to guide and to help the sons of Israel.  8 The Lord is compassionate and gracious (unlike the Idol, which is vindictive and demanding).  The Lord is slow to anger and abounding in lovingkindness (unlike the Idol Self, which is quick to wrath and abounds in compulsive egocentric reactions).  9 The Lord will not always strive with our Idol Self,  Nor will He keep His anger forever (unlike the Idol, which must reserve a store of wrath and keep accounts of wrongs suffered).  10 The Lord has not dealt with us according to our misorientation (unlike the Idol, which deals with us severely   when we don’t perform to   its standards).  Nor has the Lord rewarded us according to our iniquities (unlike the Idol, which rewards us with self-hate when we fail to live up to its pride system).  11 For as high as the heavens are above the earth,  So great is the Lord’s lovingkindness toward those who fear Him (who are more  responsive to Him than to their Idol Self).  12 As far as the east is from the west,  So far has the Lord removed our transgressions from us (unlike the Idol, which keeps those past failures ever-present and full of shame).  13 Just as a father has compassion on his children,  So the Lord has compassion on those who fear Him (on those who want to do things His way).  14 For He Himself knows our frame and its limitations;  He is mindful that we are only dust (whereas our Idol is only mindful that we should be God).  15   As with all creatures, our days are like grass;  As a flower of the field, so we flourish,  16 But when the wind has passed over it, it is no more,  And its place acknowledges it no longer (but the Idol is screaming,   “ Wait! What about the  Glory of Me! ? I am forever! ” ).  17 Though we are just dust, the lovingkindness of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting toward those who fear Him,

5  karisfellowships.com   KF22-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  And His orientation is passed from His children to their children,  18 To those who are trustworthy and keep His covenant,  Who remember His do’s and don’ts and are guided by them .  Take a deep breath.  The last part of this psalm reminds us of our creatureliness and vulnerability and, also, of the lovingkindness of the Lord, which never changes toward those who fear Him. The Lord wants to be on our side. He wants to support us in our true development, but as long as we are serving the interests of the Idol, He is forced to compassionately oppose us and wait.  In this material world that is passing away, it is so easy to forget that we are by birth eternal beings, the children of a heavenly Father. We were created for happiness, and we can experience happiness at any moment in time, as well as in eternity.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Help me see things like You do, Father. Help me see myself like You do.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider what it means to be an eternal being, the child of an eternal Father.  (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you consider   what it means to be an eternal being ,   the child of an eternal Father,   how does it feel?  (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Gently hold your experience in your awareness as you   consider   what it means to be an eternal being . You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush feelings and thoughts from our consciousness before they have a chance to teach us.   (Pause)   Give yourself permission now to explore your thoughts and feelings without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Breathe, and bring your attention to your body. Notice what it is doing when you   consider what it means to be eternal.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might recognize what liberty or

6  karisfellowships.com   KF22-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  anxiety feels like in your body.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to respectfully observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider what   it means to be an eternal being .   (Pause)   Do you judge eternity as good or evil? ( Pause)   What do you believe when you consider eternity? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something, or do you hope for something?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have had very strong feelings about eternity. We know this through archaeology and ancient texts. You are also a human creature and are not alone in your feelings.   (Pause)   When your feelings bring you information, you can choose what you will do with that information.   (Pause)   Breathe, and allow some compassion to flow for yourself and for others who, as eternal creatures, are learning to manage this material experience. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I check for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are so grateful for this time of healing and training together. Help us explore our eternal nature as You guide us to our glory and to the truth about who we are. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our own lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and all of its limitations, with the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  If you would like more support for your KF training, you might consider mini-meetings. Ask your Karis Link about this tool or email admin.

content:
karisfellowships.com   KF23-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF23 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:02   OPENING  0:03   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  We sometimes want to avoid the sad truth of KF Confession 5:  We attacked and cruelly suppressed our True Self and lost our true life.  The Self-Hate Massage  Assume a mindfulness posture,   and breathe.   (Pause)   Bring to mind an area of your life that stirs up chronic self-hate for you. Perhaps you cannot please others,   or perhaps you cannot please yourself. Perhaps your limitations are interfering with the achievement of your dreams. You may be experiencing self -hate  because you have begun to break out of your Idol’s pride system or, perhaps, because you are still stuck  in it. If you cannot identify the cause of your self-hate, you might be able to focus on the symptoms. We will bring our hurt and fear into this meditation and get acquainted with it using our KF tools.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  CONSIDER  Take a moment to collect yourself within this present space. Feel the air and the clothing on your body. Notice any noises. What is going on inside your skin?   (Pause for 30 seconds)   Now, consider this area of self-hate. Notice the discomfort you feel when you think of it. Even though you hate this thing, allow it to rest inside your skin for one minute, without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 1 minute)  COMPASSION  As you breathe, experience yourself as a creature with limitations breathing in a material world.   (Pause)  You are not a god.   (Pause)   As you breathe in and out, imagine your area of self-hate moving in and out with the breath, massaging this place in your soul that is stuck or cramped. For one minute, give it and receive it with compassion.   (Pause for 1 minute)  CLEANSE  Notice your entire body as it breathes.   (Pause)   Breathe with your mind, body, and soul as you open the doors of the prison cells of your shame, regrets, hurt, and guilt.   (Pause)   Allow the clean air to sweep

2  karisfellowships.com   KF23-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  through those dark, stagnant places for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  And pause.  Jesus sees our efforts and offers us the gift of an open door to more training and opportunities. He invites us to respond with the karis gift of allowing Him to train and purify us so that we can enter into the joy of fulfilling our potential in karis relationship with Him.  Continue to breathe while I read Nancy’s translation   of Revelation 3:8.  8 Jesus says, “ I know your efforts. Look at what is in front of you! I grant to you this open door, a door that no one is able to shut — not even you. There is evidence that you do have a little strength, for you have guarded My way of doing things and have not rejected My character and authority in your life .”  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  All Idol types feel a compulsive need to terminate the tension that comes with making changes in their lives, and they terminate that tension by returning to old habitual patterns. Although each type experiences and releases their tension in different ways, the driving forces are the same. All types are driven by the fear of self-hate and the fear of their inability to fulfill their idealized dreams.   Nancy’s   son once told her about a French novelist who described this compulsive need to silence these fears as the  rage to conclude . 1   The rage to conclude is the discomfort we feel when we are enduring our craving to return to old habitual patterns. We want to conclude the tension of going into the not knowing, of changing course, and of taking responsibility for the quality of our own lives, so we give in to the compelling needs of our fear and pride.  As you begin to turn toward your True Self, you will regularly feel uneasy and confused about what you should do . That’s because   you are disengaging from   your Idol’s   autopilot, and your claims and shoulds are no longer in charge.   The Idol Self won’t give up easily, so you may have chaotic feelings   and strong compulsions   that you can’t explain . Things may feel worse before they get better even though you are experiencing more stability in your life.  If you are a mastery type and seeking to recover your True Self, you will practice letting go of control and begin resisting the temptation to assert yourself; you will let go of forcing others to comply, to admire, or to meet your standards. You will learn to value understanding others more than being understood. You will come to recognize your own limitations. Even though you may long to be the hero, the punisher, or the Standards and Evaluations Officer, you will start admitting that you are often helpless and vulnerable. Of course, your Idol Self is not interested in becoming a humble beginner who needs to learn new skills, so every time you practice these skills, you will feel quite uncomfortable.  Mastery types have a difficult time attending Karis Fellowships. Showing up regularly means that they need help, have messed up, and   can’t   figure it all out in a week. Oh, the multitude of horrors they endure!

3  karisfellowships.com   KF23-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  They are even asked to reveal to others their weaknesses and failures! Mastery   types crave opportunities to display their superiority; KF, however, invites them to practice humility. Rather than examine the quality of their choices and behavior, they prefer to spend their time asserting themselves in activities that satisfy their pride system. They want to believe   that knowing is the same as being and that the illusion of effortless superiority, based on their own evaluation of themselves, is enough to achieve orientation. Mastery types seek to gloriously commandeer the powerful life that is the goal of our KF training. They cannot understand that such a life cannot be gained through willpower or by accumulating information. This higher quality of life is achieved gradually and organically as we continue to develop our True Self —  and mastery types find the process exasperating.  Self-effacing people love KF when they first join, but eventually they are confronted with the reality that they must give up their dreams of finding fulfillment through others and take up the very frightening work of investing in their own True Self. If their mission involves anything but self-sacrifice and connecting to others, they feel terrified. Investing in others gives them a sense of value . They need to find their value through others   because they   don’t value themselves. Whenever they invest in themselves, they suffer the  painf ul backlash of the Idol’s vicious judgment. They often externalize this inner experience and believe  that the judgment is coming from other people or organizations — even from Karis Fellowships. They unconsciously goad others into attacking or despising them in order to maintain their role as martyrs and victims. Giving up their role as a self-sacrificing victim would mean giving up their identity.  Resigned people feel uneasy or even anxious about any situation that might reveal their need to change, cooperate, or contribute. They conclude their tension and calm their anxiety by restricting their thinking, feelings, and experiences. They are very adept at stonewalling or excusing themselves with stories that confuse, fatigue, or irritate both themselves and others. It is a huge accomplishment for a resigned person to endure the effort and bother of change and suffer the pain of the associated and unpredictable struggles. Resigned people sometimes leave the Fellowships when they begin to thaw out and start experiencing uncomfortable emotions. They feel anxiety when they realize that they cannot continue to drift but need to grow up and take responsibility for the quality of their lives; they need to circulate and offer something in this world. If they become aware that they need to change, or if they see evidence of real change, they often stop filling out and sharing their   Meeting Preparation Guides .   They don’t want to  deal with real evidence or have any record of beneficial change in their lives. It is inexpressibly difficult for resigned types to work on themselves because they find change terrifying; even the thought of a worksheet or a tap is excruciating. The obvious way to conclude this tension is to quit.  When we are in self-hate, the rage to conclude is compelling, but with the help of KF training, we can just stand and observe. We can also rejoice, knowing that our discomfort is an indication that we are strong enough to engage in battle with the Idol.  In KF lesson 25, we will learn another powerful tool for calming the rage to conclude. It is called the   T-A-T , or the   Tapas Acupressure Technique . 2   If you want to start exploring the   T-A-T , you can find instructions on the Karis Fellowships website under the   Toolbox   tab, or you can search for TAT at   Alison’s tapping and  TAT videos .  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, in my rage to conclude, remind me to hold my course toward You.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF23-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  In this lesson, we will look at some familiar verses from the Gospel of John that give us insight into the mechanism of self-hate. These verses also encourage us to continually present ourselves to the light of examination so that we can learn how to cooperate with God and fulfill our business. Our business is to deal with our fear, reorient to our true glory, and reveal the divine nature that God has given to us, His creatures.  Let’s   now read   John 3:16 – 21   in Nancy’s paraphrase. In the   preceding verses, Jesus has been talking to Nicodemus about being born again. Poor Nicodemus seems to be feeling some self-hate, and Jesus addresses those feelings.  16 God loved this sick world so much that He gave to the world the only child of His nature, His Son, so that everyone who trusts Him with their lives shall not be ruined or destroyed but live an eternal life.   17 Let me explain. God did not send His Son into this sick world to decide against the world; God sent His Son so that the world might be rescued through Him.   18 There is no judgment against a person who trusts the Son, but those who do not trust Him are already decided against. They are becoming ruined and destroyed because they have not trusted in the character and authority of the only Son of God.   19 And   this is that judgment: the light has come into this sick world, and people, out of their own character and choice, loved the darkness rather than the light because their beliefs and actions were misoriented, causing pain and trouble for everyone.   20 For those who do worthless things hate the light and do not come to the light because they fear that their deeds will be shown to be what they actually are — worthless and producing nothing of real value.   21 But the one who is a doer of the truth comes to more and more light so that his or her deeds may be revealed for what they are — the result of hard work and the fulfillment of their own business in God.  Take a deep breath.  Although John often uses the word judgment in this passage, it is evident that God isn’t judging anyone.  Quite the contrary! It is we who are judging ourselves. When we studied   Neurosis and Human Growth  together, we felt exposed. The book shone a light on our illusions and pride, and we may have experienced some symptoms of self-hate, like feeling bored or overwhelmed, or perhaps angry or dismayed. In the same way, when we read about the life of Jesus or compare our choices to those of an oriented person, we judge ourselves   and may feel some shame.   In the light of oriented understanding, this reaction is quite natural, but we take it a step further — we condemn ourselves. We compare our own misoriented choices to what we now recognize as oriented and healthy, and we find ourselves wanting, or falling short. We might then judge self-examination as bad, reject it, and even hate it. Or we might run away because we simply prefer to go on as we are. So, we see in this passage that self-judgment is really the result of a kind of exposure; we are exposed to light that shows us who we actually are   —and we don’t like it.  So, what is John saying here about judgment?   Let’s look at this passage in terms of our KF purpose, which  is to restore the True Self. As you learn to trust Jesus, you experience His gracious character and stop

5  karisfellowships.com   KF23-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  judging yourself. You are able to rest in His authority as the only Righteous Judge because you know that He is not judging you. You acknowledge that you are His creature, and you understand that your business is to allow yourself to be rescued and to cooperate with Him as, together, you restore your True Self. God has declared you to be safe from condemnation, so it is not your business to heap self -hate on yourself. 3  The more that you understand His authority and your business, the more vision and courage you have to take the Believe It Path instead of judging yourself or others. Jesus is the Great Shepherd, and as you cooperate with Him, He will guide you back to your True Self.  If you do not believe or trust Jesus, you cannot cooperate with Him because, frankly, you are too afraid to do so. You yourself are the only god that you recognize. In your mind, you alone have the authority to judge, and you judge everything, including yourself, according to the standards imposed by your Idol. As a result, you live in a state of constant self-judgment and self-hate. When you are not trusting Jesus, you are trapped in the black box of your pride system. Your mind is attached to what is illusion and what  should   be rather than open to what is real and what   could   be. You prefer the darkness of your cherished illusions and rebelliously choose to avoid the light because you do not want the truth about your misorientation to be exposed.  With Jesus as our Advocate in the courtroom of our soul, we have the courage to step into the light and allow our misorientation to be revealed and healed — and as we dare to reveal more and more of who we are, we discover more and more of who He is. 4  In Karis Fellowships, we have chosen to come to the light in order to have the truth about our deeds revealed. Those deeds may be far from oriented, but what we do with our deeds is quite remarkable and unique: we bring our deeds to the light so that, together with Jesus, we can examine them and find healing. We are no longer living on autopilot, compulsively running away from the light and seeking the comfort and oblivion of darkness. This is a gigantic step forward. In the light, we examine our choices and desires and   ask ourselves, “Is this the outcome I want?”   If the outcome is not what we want, we set about exploring our healing and begin training hard. We learn to stop repeating the misoriented patterns of the past, and we build new patterns of thought and action that will produce oriented outcomes for our future.  When you are in self-hate about some deed, choice, or some kind of limitation, remember to appreciate the efforts you have made to grow and to change. Your efforts are of extraordinary value for they declare to the whole world the hope of the Gospel — the hope   that we can grow and change, that we are not stuck, that we are not slaves. Growth means that we are alive, and anything that is truly alive reveals and declares the glory of God.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, kindly lead me to the light so that I might be truly alive. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some clean water and prepare to take some notes.   (Pause)   Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)

6  karisfellowships.com   KF23-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Here is our integration focus:   Consider allowing Jesus to reveal your deeds for what they truly are.   (Repeat)  Keep in mind that Jesus does not seek to judge you but to rescue and commend you.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider   allowing Jesus to reveal your deeds for what they truly are , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   Just observe your feelings, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Hold your experience in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush feelings or thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us and stretch us. Gently observe whatever you may be experiencing as you  consider allowing Jesus to reveal your deeds for what they truly are .   (Pause)   Give yourself permission to explore your thoughts and feelings without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider   allowing Jesus to reveal your deeds for what they truly are.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Your body is always talking to you. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe. For example, you might recognize what relief or dismay, or perhaps anxiety or curiosity, feels like in your body. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  allowing Him to reveal your deeds for what they truly are . Are you comfortable, uncomfortable, or do you feel numb? Just observe.   (Pause)   Do you judge the exposure of your deeds as good or evil?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something? Do you hope for something?   (Pause)   Observe   your responses   as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  As you breathe, repeat to yourself the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity of an open door inviting you to explore your deeds.  •   Welcome the light of the Holy Spirit, who leads you into all truth. 5  •   Welcome the reality of where you are right now and how far you have come.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 6  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As my deeds are revealed, I let go of the craving for power and control.  •   As my deeds are revealed, I let go of the craving for esteem and affection.

7  karisfellowships.com   KF23-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  •   As my deeds are revealed, I let go of the craving for survival and comfort.  •   As my deeds are revealed, I let go of the craving to change my situation.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time of training and healing together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to the light and to the truth about who You created us to be. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and design, with our community and the rest of Creation, with our mission, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   Gustave Flaubert, Correspondence (Paris 1929), volume 5, 111:   “The rage for wanting to conclude is one of the most deadly and most fruitless manias to befall humanity.”   Taken from   Beautiful Evidence , Edward Tufte, Graphics Press LLC, 2006.  2   en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas_Acupressure_Technique .  3   Rom. 8:1.  4   1 John 2:1.  5   John 16:13.  6   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html .
