title: KF24 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF24-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF24 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  Please join with us by circulating your gifts. You can make a regular automatic donation through the KF website.  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  This week we will start learning another meditation practice. Our goal in this part of the meeting is simply to introduce different mindfulness and meditation techniques. During your meditation time, you can use a variety of practices, or you can choose one practice to suit your present need and state of mind. The meditation masters encourage us to stick with one method for a few years, and we can understand their reasons, but for the rest of this year, you might just practice the meditation of the month and explore what works for you. In this lesson we will look at a meditation practice called   Centering Prayer ,  popularized by Father Thomas Keating. 1  In the   Centering Prayer   pamphlet, we read:  Centering Prayer is a method of silent prayer that prepares us to receive the gift of contemplative prayer, prayer in which we experience God's presence within us, closer than breathing, closer than thinking, closer than consciousness itself. This method of prayer is both a relationship with God and a discipline to foster that relationship. 2  Centering Prayer  Begin with stillness, resting in your spirit and your natural breath. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.   (Pause)   To straighten your neck, lift the back of your head and lower your chin a little. Reach the crown of your head toward the heavens and your tailbone toward the earth. You might try standing during this meditation time, which may help focus a wandering mind. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now, try asking God for a word, a phrase, or an image.   (Pause for 10 seconds)   We will use the simple term  word   to refer to these words, phrases, and images. Some people identify a word like   love ,   mercy ,   or   Jesus  or a meaningful image — for example, a waterfall or a bird in flight. You might choose a word of guidance like   let go   or   connect . Allow your word to float to the surface of your consciousness and stick to it during

2  karisfellowships.com   KF24-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  the meditation time. When other thoughts intrude into your consciousness, gently return to your word. Breathe, and allow your mind to rest in stillness as you continue to recall the word.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  When you are comfortable with your word, try allowing it to float away from your mind. Dwell in the silence and rest in the stillness as you simply observe your breathing. You might attend to the word for one breath and then allow your mind to repose silently for two breaths. We will practice for one minute. Remember to consciously breathe.   (Pause for 1 minute)  During this last minute of meditation, we will let go of the word completely and allow our minds to rest in stillness as we observe the breath.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Take a fresh, deep breath as if you were stretching your insides. Gently open your eyes and re-engage with your environment.  (If time permits,   ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we will turn our attention to KF Confession 6:  We chose to foster illusions to save the life of our Idol Self.  Before we get started with our Toolbox training, you might want to take out a   Two Paths Worksheet . You will also need this worksheet for the Bible Teaching.  When you look at the   Two Paths Worksheet: Believing v. Judging , perhaps you can see how far you have come in your training. This worksheet reminds us of how we used to live, with all of our stories, reactions, and mindlessness.  If we choose to live in the pride system, we are driven to maintain an artificial and legalistic state of being. Maintaining our pride system takes a lot of work and uses up tons of our precious energy, but it is work that we are used to . Powerful fear drives us, and we are lured into the hunter’s snare by the illusion that  adhering to our pride system will save our lives. When we become aware of our fear and realize that we cannot use our pride system to escape the grip of fear, we can use W-A-A! (Words, Attitude, Action) and other KF tools to defuse the chaotic feelings of self-hate. 3   Simply recognizing our fear can give us a moment to breathe instead of immediately reacting to an event. Use the   Two Paths Flowchart   regularly to look at what is happening in your life and allow yourself a moment to breathe before you act.  Now let’s   review the   Two Paths Worksheet: Believing v. Judging . You can actually start anywhere on this worksheet, but in this lesson we will begin with step 1, the outcome.  1.   OUTCOME:   What am I experiencing?  You will find this step under the Judgment Path. It’s often helpful to begin by exploring your outcome because most of the time you don’t know what led to that outcome.   What are you experiencing right now? You might ask yourself:   Is my outcome demonstrating the love of God and supporting His purposes in this world?   If not, you are probably on the Judgment Path.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF24-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  2.   ACTION:   What did I do or avoid that invited this outcome?  When you have observed the outcome, you can use the worksheet to trace your outcome back to its source. What choice did you make or what action did you take that led to the outcome? Or did you avoid a courageous choice or action?  3.   REJOICING IN THE MISORIENTATION:   What emotions did I experience that drove me to act?  The idea that you have rejoiced in misorientation can be difficult to understand at first. Misoriented emotions drive misoriented choices, so you might ask yourself:   Did I indulge in some kind of vindictive triumph? Did I delight in euphoria through self-indulgence or recklessness? Did I get caught up in illusions about myself or others? Did I relieve my tension in a rage to conclude?   Did I act out of self- hate or the fear of hurt prid e?  4.   THE STORY: What story did I tell that generated emotions?  Human beings are creative; we are designed to tell stories. The Idol Self hijacks that natural ability and uses storytelling to create an alternate reality. We all have a story about why we are the way we are, why we do what we do, and why we feel what we feel. Our stories justify our judgments, fuel our misoriented emotions, and support our pride system.  5.   JUDGING AS GOOD OR EVIL:   What was my short-tempered judgment?  What was your automatic reaction to the event or situation? Did you judge it as good or bad?  6.   FEAR OF DEATH OR EUPHORIA:   What standard of my Idol Self was threatened or fulfilled?  You might ask yourself:   What was dangerous or delirious about this event? How did it threaten or fulfill my search for an imagined glory?   You may now recognize what scared you or what, perhaps, relieved you of your fear of death.  After you have worked through steps 1 – 6, choose an intervention to help you gain more clarity about your reactions. You might wish to use the   Tapping Protocol , mindfulness practices, or our next tool, the  T-A-T ,   which we will explore in our next lesson. 4   Then, use your creative imagination in an oriented way as you work up the left side of the worksheet taking the Believe It Path.  7.   EVENT:   What triggered the fear or the euphoria?  Perhaps at this stage you are able to identify what ignited the fuel in the cylinders of your self-hate engine or what temporarily fulfilled your idealized dreams of glory. What happened that sent you down the Judgment Path? Try to describe the event simply.  As you work through steps 8 – 12, use the beautiful gift of your imagination in a healthy way to help you take the Believe It Path and plan a course that could create an opportunity for oriented, productive outcomes. The KF Compass and the   Expanded Version   of this Toolbox contain   Nancy’s instructions for  navigating these steps.  You already know that extreme outbursts, irritations, anxieties, self-sabotage, hurts, depression, forcing things, and shutting down are all symptoms of the self-hate that drives each of us back into slavery to the Idol. But you really can look at self-hate with compassion even when you are feeling its compelling invitations. You can courageously observe what is going on, learn to manage yourself, and, eventually, grow out of self-hate.  Our prayer might go something like this:

4  karisfellowships.com   KF24-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Holy Spirit, guide me to defuse the power of my self-hate.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s   listen once again to KF Confession 6:  We chose to foster illusions to save the life of our Idol Self.  This month we will look at our illusions about life, others, and ourselves — illusions that we ferociously defend in order to protect our pride. In the midst of our anxiety and chaotic choices, we have learned to depend on our pride as a substitute for real self-confidence. When things fall apart, we get a marvelous chance to examine our pride and our attachments.  Let’s look at an event in the lives of John the Baptist’s disciples and examine it through the lens of the   Two Paths Worksheet . Here is Nancy’s paraphrase of   John 3:22 – 30 .  22 After these things Jesus and his disciples went into the land of Judea, and He was spending time with them and baptizing (which is symbolic of purification).   23 John was also baptizing in Aenon near Salim since there was lots of water there, and people were coming to be baptized.   24 This was before John had been thrown into prison.   25 In the midst  of this baptizing, John’s disciples initiated a discussion with a Jew about purification.  26 Then they came to John and said to him, “Rabbi,   He who was with you on the other side of the Jordan, the one that you endorsed — just look at Him! He is baptizing and all are coming to Him .”   27 John answered and said, “No one is capable of receiving anything like purification unless it is granted to them from heaven. So, it really doesn’t matter who they  go to for purification.   28 By the way, you yourselves can endorse me — I have already told you that I, myself, am not the Christ, but that I have been sent ahead of Him.   29 The same principle of purification   applies to marriage rites. It’s not about the one who does the  purifying but about the one who has the bride — that is, the bridegroom. The friend of the  bridegroom who stands by and hears him greatly rejoices in the bridegroom’s voice  because he is not envious or desiring his place. Therefore, my mission as friend is completed, and this makes me full of joy.   30 The bridegroom is the one who must be  brought to manhood, and I, myself, must recede from the scene.”  Take a deep breath.  To give us a deeper understanding of this story, we will now use the   Two Paths Worksheet . We can start with step 7 because this passage describes the event. We will follow   John’s   disciples as they take the Judgment Path, and we will see that at step 2, the point of action, these well-trained disciples apply what they have learned: they switch paths, get creative, and make an oriented choice.  7.   EVENT: What triggered the fear or the euphoria?  Jesus is becoming more popular than John, and in this passage we see two very different reactions to

5  karisfellowships.com   KF24-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  that same event. How is it that John takes the Believe It Path, but his disciples take the Judgment Path?  6.   FEAR OF DEATH OR EUPHORIA: What standard of my Idol Self was threatened or fulfilled?  What do the disciples fear? They are obviously in a rage to conclude the tension created by their  leader’s   declining influence. They want John to do something about their tension.   We don’t know  exactly what they fear, but   John’s disciples   suddenly see their search for glory disappearing into the mist, and they feel anxious.  5.   JUDGING AS GOOD OR EVIL: What was my short-tempered judgment?  We have been conditioned to judge as evil any event that triggers our fear. In this passage, we see that the disciples judge as bad the decline of their ministry.  4.   STORY: What story did I tell that generated emotions?  John’s disciples   seem to be judging Jesus and blaming John. Perhaps they hate themselves because they think that they should be able to know it all, convince others effortlessly, and attract the crowds by their spiritual superiority. Their pride is invested in their own way of doing and understanding things, and their investment is now threatened.  3.   REJOICING IN THE MISORIENTATION: What emotions did I experience that drove me to act?  The story that we tell ourselves can generate a whole range of emotions. The disciples may be feeling anxiety over their limitations, frustration because they   should   be able to change the situation, dismay  or embarrassment about their leader’s   decreasing popularity, or wrath and indignation because the situation is   unfair . They are rejoicing in misoriented emotions that support their wobbling pride.  11. ACTION: What choices can I make based on the truth?  At this point, John’s disciples switch from   step 2 on the Judgment Path to step 11 on the Believe It Path. The emotions generated by their story invited them to take misoriented action, but now the quality of their training becomes evident. These disciples respond to their self-hate in a healthy way. They are willing to explore the Believe It Path, and they take action by talking to their teacher. Even though they may appear to be whining, they are at least engaging their teacher in a conversation which may reveal to them another perspective.  In this material world, we live on a timeline, so when we take a misoriented action, we cannot go back and undo the damage we have done; we have passed the point of no return. Misoriented actions always produce misoriented outcomes, and misoriented actions are the result of misoriented emotions. However, if we can recognize and humbly admit that our emotions are misoriented, we can choose to take oriented action instead of continuing down the Judgment Path and creating a mess. We can redirect our misoriented trail of cause and effect toward orientation.  Now loo k at John’s response   to his declining popularity. John takes the Believe It Path; he is a person of no fear. He has trained hard, so his fight is easy. Without the emotional turmoil generated by judgment, he simply believes the fact that the crowds are going to Jesus. Rather than trying to defend hurt pride, he rejoices in the truth of who God designed him to be. He experiences the secure confidence of having faithfully completed his mission. He feels joy over the rise of Jesus and embraces his own decline in popularity because he is not attached to an idealized outcome based on the illusion of personal superiority.

6  karisfellowships.com   KF24-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, when things fall apart, guide me into believing it and trusting You.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some clean water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider a time when you were not or were no longer valued.   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider   a time when you were not or were no longer valued , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.  (Pause)   You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Gently hold this experience in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. We often flush real feelings or thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us and stretch us. Observe your thoughts and feelings without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider   this time of not being valued.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   You might recognize what rage or abandonment feels like in your body.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to respectfully observe those uncomfortable sensations. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  not being valued . Jesus knows what that feels like.   (Pause)   Do you judge not being valued by others as good or evil?   (Pause)   What do you believe when you see or feel that you are not valued? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created all of us to have these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have had very strong feelings when they were not or were no longer valued. We all know what that feels like.   (Pause)   When these feelings are triggered, you can breathe rather than reacting and allowing yourself to get caught up in stories. You can let go of managing   God’s business. Breathe , and extend compassion to yourself and

7  karisfellowships.com   KF24-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  others in this situation. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time together to train and to heal. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our real glory and to the truth about who we are and what You would have us do. Lead us to the next step in our own healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and mission, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   www.centeringprayer.com .  2   Ibid.  3   See KF16.  4   Dr. Roger Callahan, “TFT Stress Buster Tapping Class - Learn to Use TFT Tapping,” Callahan Techniques, accessed  April 24, 2016,   www.rogercallahan.com/learn-to-tap.php . Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven;  en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas Acupressure Technique .

title: KF25 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF25-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF25 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  When dogs learn to live and work in a human community, they develop acute abilities to gauge every expression and sound that humans make. Nancy tells this story:  “ Several years ago, we lived in the north of England near a sheep farm. From our kitchen window we could watch the sheepdogs moving out into the field and then waiting, simply waiting, for a signal from the shepherd. The dogs were in a state of relaxed attention —  relaxed, but all eyes and ears alert, each dog eagerly watching the shepherd for its particular signal.   These dogs were not anxious to take on another dog’s business, nor  were they impatient with their work of shepherding sheep. They understood that in the natural order of things there are dogs and there are masters, and there is a job to be done. They had no fear and no opposing pride. They knew without any doubt that their business was to follow their particular signal from the shepherd. Together, the dogs and the shepherd accomplished the mission. ”  These dogs were designed and trained for their work, and they seemed to rejoice in their work as they fulfilled their design. We, too, are creatures designed to joyfully accomplish a particular work, and we also need training.  Meditation trains us to patiently and purposefully wait on the Lord with our mental and energetic eyes and ears alert. When we have learned to mindfully wait, our Shepherd can trust us to watch for His signals and skillfully complete our mission. It is in carrying out our mission skillfully that we find the joy.  Let’s continue practicing   Centering Prayer . 1   Assume a meditation posture and breathe.   (Pause)   Begin with silent prayer, resting in the spirit and in the breath. You might try standing up during this practice while maintaining a sense of connection between heaven and earth.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  And now, ask God for a   word . Remember that this can be an image, a word, or a phrase. Allow the word to surface in your consciousness. If nothing surfaces, just relax into the breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF25-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Use the word to focus your mind on stillness and on the breath. Stick to this word during your meditation time. When other thoughts intrude, gently return to your word.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  When you are ready, allow the word to float away, and then rest in the stillness of your mind. You might attend to the word for one breath and then rest in the stillness for two breaths. To balance your breathing, try inhaling and exhaling for equal amounts of time. Practice for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  And now, if you can, let go of the word entirely. You might continue with the balanced breath, inhaling and exhaling for equal amounts of time. Practice resting in the stillness, the quiet mind, for one minute. If your mind starts to wander, use the word to draw your mind back to the breath.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Take a deep fresh breath as if you were stretching your insides. Gently open your eyes and re-engage with your environment.  Try to find a regular time in your day for meditation. In the evening, you may be too busy or too fatigued to meditate, so you might try scheduling an afternoon meditation. Take a break at work and find a quiet conference room where you can spend a few minutes in meditation, perhaps before you leave the office. Use your meditation practice to refresh your mind. Your cue to watch TV or to surf on the web might be converted into a cue to meditate first. Tell those living with you what you are doing and ask for their support.  Our scripture for this meditation is Isaiah 40:31, reading from the King James Version.  But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run and not be weary; and they shall walk and not faint.  Let’s learn to wait on the Lord.   Take a deep breath.  (Go straight to the Karis Confession to allow time for the longer Toolbox)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  In this lesson, we will learn the   T-A-T   integration method. 2   T-A-T   is the acronym for   Tapas Acupressure Technique . The   T-A-T   can help you find clarity when you are caught in a story that is fostering illusions. It can also help you get back into reality when you find yourself going down the Judgment Path. In this lesson, we will move quickly through the steps of the   T-A-T ,   but you can find a more detailed presentation of this technique at   Alison’s tapping and TAT videos .  Each Idol type has its own characteristic hotspots, and we can predict the types of situations that will trigger them. When these hotspots are triggered, they drive us into habitual reactions and feelings. If you have reviewed the chapters in   Neurosis and Human Growth   that apply to your Idol type, you are now armed with a list of your hotspots and can boldly confront them with new understanding. 3   Mindfulness training helps you notice when the fumes of hurt pride are building up in the cylinders of your self-hate engine, ready to be ignited by your hotspots. Simply noticing that these fumes are building up can help you take a step toward redirecting the outcome of those situations.  Expansive types hit hotspots when they feel helpless and vulnerable, sense disrespect from others, or feel

3  karisfellowships.com   KF25-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  they have lost control. Self-effacing types ignite their self-hate when they stick up for themselves or invest in their own potential. Resigned types flare up against imposition, especially the imposition of their own internal conflicts and feelings. All types will hate themselves for having the   wrong   kind of feelings — that is, feelings that seem wrong to them.  We will now practice the   T-A-T   tool to help us process a hotspot. You might use your   Meeting Preparation Guide   or your KF journal to jot down a few notes about what you experience during this training. Take this training gently, and breathe.  The T-A-T  Begin by identifying the ring finger and thumb on one of your hands. With those two fingers gently grasp the bridge of your nose, between your eyes.   (Pause)   When you are comfortable with that position, adjust your arm and wrist so that you can place the middle finger of the same hand on your lower middle forehead, about half an inch higher than the area between your eyebrows.   (Pause)   You are now lightly touching three facial points with your fingertips. This is called the   pose.   Hold that pose during each of the  T-A-T   steps. While you hold the pose, breathe deeply and follow the instructions. Remember to breathe deeply throughout the exercise.  1.   Choose an issue or problem.   (Pause)   (Repeat the instruction)  You might want to choose one of your hotspots as your problem. Observe yourself enduring the experience of that hotspot. What are you thinking and feeling? Are you feeling hurt, defensive, enraged, or scared? Hold the pose, and breathe for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now pause. Take thirty seconds to jot down a few words that will help you remember what you thought and felt about the problem.   (Pause for 30 seconds)   On a scale of one to ten, with ten being the most intense, rate the intensity of your discomfort about the problem or the amount of resistance that you feel while exploring this issue. Make a note of that.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Take the pose again, and breathe.  2.   Imagine how you would think and feel, and what your life might be like, if you did not have this problem.   (Pause for 15 seconds) (Repeat the instruction) (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause and jot down a few descriptive words.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now take the pose again, and breathe.  3.   Listen to this clearing statement:   “God, thank You for healing the origins of this problem.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “ The origins of this problem are healing now . ”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. Jot down a few notes. How are you feeling?   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again and keep breathing.  4.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “God, thank You for healing all the areas of my life, mind, and body that are misoriented by this problem.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “All the areas of my life, mind, and body that are misoriented by this problem are healing now.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)

4  karisfellowships.com   KF25-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Pause. If you have any thoughts about that, write them down now.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose, and breathe.  5.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “God, thank You for healing all the places in me that get something out of holding on to this problem.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “All the places in me that get something  out of holding on to this problem are healing now .”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. If you have any thoughts, jot a few of them down.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The next step leads us into forgiveness.   We will learn more about forgiveness later in KF training, but for right now, think of it as simply letting go of something that you are holding on to.  Take the pose, and breathe.  6.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “ I forgive everyone and everything that I have blamed for this problem, including God and myself. ”   Breathe, and on the exhale, let go.   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “ I forgive everyone and everything that I have held responsible for this problem, including God and myself. ”   Breathe, and on the exhale, let go.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. Jot down any thoughts you might have.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose and breathe deeply one more time.  7.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “ I ask forgiveness from everyone and everything that I have harmed by holding on to this problem, including God ’s   purposes and my True Self. ”   Breathe.   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “ I ask forgiveness from everyone and everything that I have harmed by holding on to   this problem, including God’s purposes and my True Self.”   Breathe.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. Make a note of any thoughts you might have.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Write down how you now feel about the problem. On a scale of one to ten, how would you rate the intensity of your discomfort or resistance when you think about this problem? Compare this number with your assessment in step 1.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. The original   T-A-T   protocol suggests a two-minute focus on each step. You might follow the instructions in the   Expanded Version   of this meeting and try the two-minute series during this coming week. The   T-A-T   can help you honor your emotions without allowing them to enslave you and drive you to conclude your tension. When you honor and then disarm your emotions, you can wait more patiently  and purposefully for the Shepherd’s signal .  Our prayer might go something like this:  Holy Spirit, remind me to practice my KF tools so that I might use them skillfully.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  0:30   SHARING

5  karisfellowships.com   KF25-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (If the meeting is running behind, divide the group into small subgroups so that you can move through the Sharing quickly and get back in sync with the Meeting Schedule)  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  This month our focus is on KF Confession 6:  We chose to foster illusions to save the life of our Idol Self.  During this lesson, we will spend a little time talking about the   hope of the glory of God.   We were given an imagination for a reason; imagination is the instrument of hope. By using our imagination, we can envision an oriented, glorious life — a life that co-relates or correlates with the reality of the Person of God, a life that demonstrates and displays the character of God so that as He is, so are we in this world. 4   We can also imagine the real destructive consequences of refusing to develop that glorious life. Those consequences are briefly summarized in the first chapter of   Paul’s letter to the   Romans. Our desire to avoid such consequences can be a powerful incentive to choose orientation when events trigger our hotspots. The vision of real glory is like a beacon that guides the lifeboat of our True Self out of chaos and into the light of our potential in Christ.  Let’s look at   Romans 5:2   in Nancy ’s   translation.  2 Through Jesus we have patronage and access to this karis relationship in which we stand; and we exult in hope of the glory of God.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  Do you wonder what   exult   means? It means   to show or feel a lively or triumphant joy; to be highly elated or jubilant . 5   That is how Christians are supposed to feel about the hope of the glory of God.   Isn’t that  interesting?  What is glory? Glory is the expression of the true character of something wonderful, authentic, and real. That expression is then observed by others who add to the glory by appreciating and praising what they see. A good reputation is glorious. In the Bible, glory is often described as light and can be understood as energy that is radiant, unfettered, and unpolluted by misorientation. We may not be aware of our own glory, but as children of light we shine with a radiant energy and express a unique quality that can be seen by others. 6  When we do the   T-A-T   intervention, we are asked to imagine what life would be like without our problem. We recall the Believe It Path and imagine how we might have acted in a healthier manner or how we might have allowed another person space to grow. We might also imagine what it is like to live in another  person’s shoes .   That’s   called   empathy.   When we use our imagination as God intended, we are living in the hope that as we continue our work, we will be able to increasingly express the character of God and the quality of our design. This is the hope of the glory of God, and it is the glory that God intends for each one of us. This glory is not legalistic perfection; it is active, productive, vital growth.  The Idol has a hope, too. It hopes to actualize its illusions. We were designed to be glorious, but the Idol switches the track of that glorious design and shunts our God-given express train onto a rail siding of imagined glory leading nowhere. God intended our imagination to be harnessed for exploration and

6  karisfellowships.com   KF25-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  development and for contributing to our community, but the Idol hijacks and enslaves that beautiful imagination and uses it to foster illusions about ourselves, others, and the future — and even to rewrite the past. Our amazing, God-designed imagination is also mercilessly employed by the Idol to punish us with anxieties about the past, the future, and life, and to lash us with self-torment. By abusing the power of this great gift, the Idol distorts reality, discounts or ignores real evidence, and transports us into a fantasy world where we can escape what is true. Our imagination then serves the   “ Hope of the Glory of  Me!” , and we use it to manufacture a spurious confidence in our own prideful judgments and to glorify our paltry, egocentric achievements. Our misoriented hope is that our Idol Self will be glorified, perfected, and actualized in the material world.  Whenever you   start a thought with “if only,” you are living in the “ Hope of the Glory of Me! ”   For example, you might think:   If only I had other parents, genetics, other bosses, a different home, or another spouse or body . . . if   only I hadn’t done that   . . . if only they would do this . . . if only I was gifted with his looks, her talent, his brains, her opportunities —then wouldn’t   I   be glorious?   But   God’s hope   for you is that you develop the core strength of love which casts out all fear wherever you are and in whatever situation you find yourself. God has a thousand ideas for your future, all of which will delight and stretch you at the same time, but   He’s   not just looking to please you. His great hope is that you will fulfill your glorious potential and co-labor with Him to rescue this sorry, messed-up world.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, show me Your vision for me today.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some clean water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider expressing the glory of God through your life.   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you   consider   expressing the glory of God through your life , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.  (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Gently hold whatever you are experiencing in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them. Observe whatever you may be experiencing as you   consider   expressing the glory of God through your life .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF25-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider   expressing the glory of God through your life.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Perhaps you don’t believe that you can express  the glory of God, or you might feel resistant to the idea.   You might be confusing God’s glory with   your  culture’s ideas of glory or those of your Idol . Perhaps you are intrigued and see glimpses of potential glory. How does that feel in your body? Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider expressing the glory of God through your life .   (Pause)   Do you judge expressing that glory as good or as undesirable?   (Pause)   What do you believe when you consider declaring   God’s glory ? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something, or do you hope for something?   (Pause)   Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  For thousands of years, human beings have had very strong feelings and have been quite confused when they have   considered expressing the glory of God through their lives . You are also a human creature and know what those strong feelings are like.   (Pause)   Breathe rather than reacting and getting caught up in stories about what your glory might look like or what it should look like. Let go of managing   God’s business.  Breathe with compassion for everyone facing the challenge of expressing the glory of God through their lives. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time to heal and train together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our real glory and to the truth about what that glory looks like. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with our community, with the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   www.centeringprayer.com .  2   en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas_Acupressure_Technique .  3   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).  4   1 John 4:17.  5   www.dictionary.com/browse/exult .  6 Matt. 5:14 – 16.

title: KF26 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF26-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF26 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me   in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  A well-known body bio-mechanics expert said that   the most important piece of restoring function starts with creating space in your day to heal . 1   (Repeat ) Karis Fellowships meetings are a healing space, and so is your meditation practice.  A KF member wrote about the stages on his journey as he worked toward a satisfying meditation practice. This is what he said:  “ My first thought was —I should meditate, but I can’t do it.   After a while I learned that it is a challenge to meditate — I will try to do it. I did that for a few weeks, and I realized that meditation helps me — I see value in doing it. Then, with amazement, I was able to see that I need to meditate — I am changed by doing it. After several months I thought I want to meditate — I like to do it. Near the end of the KF training, I understood that meditation is an adventure and wondered what is possible if I continue to do this? ”  Let’s continue to practice   Centering Prayer . 2  Take a meditation posture. You might try standing during this exercise and see if that works for you. Begin with silent prayer, resting in the spirit and the breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Ask God for a   word , and allow that word, phrase, or image to rest in your mind . (Pause for 30 seconds)  Stick to this word during your meditation time. When other thoughts intrude, gently return to your word. Try practicing the balanced breath, using equal amounts of time to inhale and exhale.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  When you are ready, allow the word to float away, and then rest in the stillness of your mind. You might try saying or attending to the word for one breath and then resting in the stillness for two breaths. Breathe.   (Pause for 1 minute)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF26-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  And now, practice resting only in the stillness, the quiet mind, for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Pause. Take a full deep breath, as if you were stretching your insides. Gently re-engage with the meeting.  Our scripture for this meditation is Psalm 27:14.  Wait on the Lord;  Be of good courage,  And allow your heart to be strengthened.  Yes, wait on the Lord.  Take a deep breath.  (Go immediately to the Confession to allow time for the Toolbox)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  The world is mesmerized by appearance, talent, and money. In KF, we call these attributes the   ATM . With the same effortless ease that cash can be withdrawn from a machine, people draw on their assets of  appearance, talent, and money to create an illusion of superiority and to feed the Idol’s search for glory.  We are all encouraged by our culture to buy into the illusions of the ATM and may therefore feel fear or show deference when a person with a big ATM balance comes into the room. This is called   partiality .  It is not only the appearance of wealth that clouds our ability to make principled decisions. The appearance of poverty can also interfere with our ability to maintain orientation. Our culture often pressures us to show partiality toward people who appear to be in need. However, these people may be projecting a small ATM to create the illusion of helplessness.  Like someone who has a stash of money but acts as if they have none, a person can give the appearance of being more disadvantaged and less capable than they actually are. These people use the illusion of their poverty to steal from the community. 3   Others use their real poverty to manipulate the community into taking care of them and to avoid taking responsibility for their own lives. Their poverty then supports their pride system and gives them an illusion of power.  The ethos of Karis Fellowships is very different from the culture of our market economy, which is based on contracts and the ATM. Our ministry simply aspires to empower all Christians who want to recover their True Self for the glory of God. KF is not a need-based ministry; it is   effort-based . This is extremely important. It is the effort you make to recover your True Self and build karis relationships that reveals your true intention. Your ATM balance is not important in the karis economy; it is your effort, not your need or your wealth, that invites support and care from other KF members. We gain strength through fellowship with others as together we stagger toward the goal of developing a strong and resilient True Self. We invest in effort-based people so that when our True Self starts to run, we can run with those who are also running. This is a new kind of race in which we all start weak but end strong.  We will now use the   T-A-T   to explore the issue of money. 4   In this training session we will spend one minute on each step. Feel free to continue holding the pose rather than writing down your thoughts. Just do whatever is most helpful for you.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF26-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  The   T-A-T  Let’s begin. Take the pose , and breathe.  1.   Choose an issue or problem.   (Pause)   (Repeat the instruction)  During this first step, imagine a problem, a craving, or any illusion you might have about money. If you can, experience in your body the sensations associated with money, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause. On a scale of one to ten, rate the intensity of the craving, discomfort, or resistance you might feel about confronting this problem. Very uncomfortable feelings would rate as a ten. Jot down a few words that will help you remember what you thought and felt about the problem.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again, and breathe.  2.   Imagine how you would think and feel, and what your life would be like, if you did not have this problem or illusion about money.   (Pause for 15 seconds) (Repeat the instruction) (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. You might wish to jot down a few notes.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again, and breathe.  3.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “God, thank You for healing the origins of this problem.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “ The origins of this problem are healing now . ”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause, and if you wish, jot down your feelings or thoughts.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again, and breathe deeply.  4.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “God, thank You for healing all the areas of my life, mind, and body that are misoriented by this problem.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “All the areas of my life, mind, and body that are misoriented by this problem are healing now.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. If you have any thoughts or feelings about that, write them down now.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again, and breathe.  5.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “God, thank You for healing all the places in me that get something out of holding on to this problem.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “All the places in me that get something  out of holding on to this problem are healing now .”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. If you have any thoughts or feelings, you might write them down now.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose, and breathe deeply.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF26-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  The next step leads us into forgiveness. The Greek word often translated as   forgive   means to   release from debt .  6.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “ I forgive everyone and everything, including God and myself, that I have blamed for this problem. ”   Breathe, and on the exhale, let go.   (Pause for 15 seconds )   “ I release everyone and everything that I have held responsible for this problem. ”   Breathe, and on the exhale, let go.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. Write down your thoughts.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  And now, for the final step, take the pose and breathe.  7.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “ I ask forgiveness from everyone and everything that I have damaged by holding on to this problem , including God’s purposes and my True Self . ”   Breathe.  (Pause for 15 seconds)   “ I accept responsibility for the damage that I have caused to anyone or anything by holding on to this problem. ”   Breathe.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. Make a note of any thoughts you might have.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Write down how you now feel about the problem. On a scale of one to ten, how would you rate the intensity of your discomfort?   (Pause for 30 seconds)  And pause. As homework, you might practice using this tool again, focusing on the same problem while holding the pose and breathing for two minutes at each step. Evaluate the difference between using the shorter and the longer   T-A-T .  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father of Lights, help me be responsible with the good gift of money. 5   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  (If the meeting is running behind, divide the group into small subgroups so that you can move through the Sharing quickly and get back in sync with the Meeting Schedule)  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  KF Confession 6 reminds us of how much energy we have wasted in misoriented living.  We chose to foster   illusions to save the life of our Idol Self.  In the last lesson, we talked about how to use our very human gift of imagination in a healthy way. When we have a misoriented response to the ATM, a well-trained imagination can help set us on the Believe It Path. We can learn to appreciate the ATM without judging ourselves or others. Once we are free from the constraining preoccupation with appearances, talent, and money, we can make choices that create oriented outcomes that declare the glory of God.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF26-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  How people feel about money and how they handle money is often a real puzzle. Just like energy, the flow of money becomes distorted and is aimlessly dissipated   when it passes through misoriented hands. Let’s  see what James says about the ATM. This is   Nancy’s   paraphrase of   James 2:1 – 17 .  1 My siblings, do not abuse the trust of our Lord Jesus Christ — who is committed to real glory — by   showing   favoritism   to   others   because   of   the   false   glory   of   material appearances.   2 Here is an example: If a gold-ringed man comes into your synagogue in splendid, bright clothing and, also, a beggar enters in filthy clothing,   3 and you gaze upon the one wearing the radiant clothes and say,   “ You sit here in the good place, a good place that carries with it the symbol of achieved virtue ,”   and then you say to the beggar,   “ You stand over there away from me because to be associated with you is social suicide, ”   or, perhaps,   “S it below my footstool to show that I am superior to you,"   4 are you not distinguishing the rich man from the beggar by your choices and becoming judges using worthless and malicious calculations?   5 Listen, my beloved siblings. Did not God choose the beggars of the world to be rich in trusting God and to be heirs of the kingdom which He promised to anyone who loves Him?   6 But you have judged the beggar to be unworthy based solely on his poverty. Are not the rich gaining control over you and dragging you into court where people are judged by man- made laws, not by God’s laws?   7 You put the rich in a seat of virtue, yet do they not vilify and defame the virtuous name of Jesus for which you all have been summoned as witnesses?   8 If, however, you are fulfilling the kingdom law according to the Scripture   “ Love your neighbor as yourself ” , you are a doer of virtue. Doing virtue looks like this: If you are giving up the good place to a rich person of real virtue because he is your neighbor in a karis relationship, you are creating more virtue and orientation.   9 But if you are simply showing partiality based on outward appearances, you are working at misorientation and are in error, and under the kingdom law of God your choices are evidence that you have missed your way.  Take a deep breath.  In this passage, James compares real glory with appearances. Real glory is virtuous action, whereas false glory can be cheaply attributed to others based on no action at all. That is called   partiality : offering honor to someone who has done nothing to deserve it. We see how the ATM — appearance, talent, and money —  can make us partial to those whose actions reveal no evidence of real virtue.  Let’s skip down a bit   in this same chapter to where James talks about faith, or trust, and real virtue.  14 What use is it, my siblings, if someone says that he trusts God but makes no effort to contribute to the community? Can that trust save him?   15 If a brother or sister is without clothing and in need of daily food,   16 and one of you says to them, “Go in peace, be warmed and be filled,” and yet you do not give them what is necessary for their body, what use is  that?   17 Even so, faith or trust, if we make no effort to help, is dead, being only words and illusions.  Take a deep breath.  If we are deluded enough to trust money more than we trust God, we will feel insecure whether we have money or not. We will therefore create virtue stories that justify our hoarding and will reckon as virtue

6  karisfellowships.com   KF26-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  generous intentions that never translate into substantial action. Every kind of hoarding and greed stifles the karis   economy within our community.  When we claim to trust God but refuse to act on that trust, we are living in an illusion. James is telling us a simple truth:   Only action is action (Repeat),   and our action reveals the quality of our faith, or trust. God is not telling us to give to every poor person or to every cause. He is telling us to support the community of spiritually committed brothers and sisters with whom we experience various levels of karis relationship. These are the people who show by their choices that they trust God and are making real efforts to grow into the possibilities of that trust.  Our prayer might go something like this.  Lord, teach me to take real action that reveals the quality of my trust in You .   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider revealing what you believe through your actions.   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider revealing what you believe through your actions , breathe and recognize any feelings or any resistance that may be present.   (Pause)   Just observe your experience with compassion, and breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. Simply observe your experience as you  consider   revealing what you believe through your actions. (Pause)   Give yourself permission to explore without judgment your feelings and thoughts, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider revealing what you believe through your actions .   (Pause)   Acknowledge any sensations you may feel. Observe and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider revealing what you believe through your actions . Do you feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or do you feel nothing at all? Just observe.   (Pause)   Do you feel compelled to judge this revelation as good or bad?   (Pause)  Are you afraid of something? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Observe your experience as just information. You might process with a long exhaling breath or the Dragon Breath. 6   (Pause for 30 seconds)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF26-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Heal  God created human beings to have feelings about everything. You can choose to honor and observe your feelings without reacting to them. We all have to learn to experience our feelings and, at the same time, choose to live oriented lives.   (Pause)   The fact that you can step back and observe your experience lets you know that your experience does not define you; you are separate from your experience.   (Pause)   Breathe with compassion for everyone who is learning to deal with what is revealed by their actions. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Optional:   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are grateful for this time to heal and train together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You continue to show us the truth about ourselves. Help us learn to trust You as we use our real resources to serve. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and mission, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  *This is the time in our KF training cycle to consider whether we, as KF members, have the MATH to offer the next NHG book study to our wider community. All current members are invited to participate in offering this gift by signing up on the spreadsheet in the recent email sent from admin.  (*Except when preparing for the Jubilee year)  1   nutritiousmovement.com .  2   www.centeringprayer.com .  3   Eph. 4:28.  4   en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas_Acupressure_Technique .  5   James 1:17.  6   See KF12.

title: KF27 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF27-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF27 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Let’s continue our practice of   Centering Prayer . 1  Assume a meditation posture and breathe.   (Pause)   Now, in silent prayer, rest in the spirit and the breath. You might practice the balanced breath using the same amount of time for your inhale as for your exhale.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Ask God for a   word , and allow that word to surface in your consciousness.   (Pause for 30   seconds)   Stick to this word during the meditation time. When other thoughts hijack your consciousness, gently return to your word.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  For one minute, try recalling the word for one breath and then rest in the stillness for two breaths.   (Pause for 1 minute)  And now, as you are able, practice resting in only the stillness, the quiet mind, for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Pause, and take a full deep breath, as if you were stretching your insides.   (Pause)   Gently open your eyes and re-engage with the meeting.  You may already know this hymn by the American composer Clara H. Scott. Pray these words with me as I read.  Open my eyes, that I may see  Glimpses of truth Thou hast for me;  Place in my hands the wonderful key  That shall unclasp and set me free.  Silently now I wait for Thee,  Ready my God, Thy will to see,

2  karisfellowships.com   KF27-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Open my eyes, illumine me,  Spirit divine! 2  Take a deep breath.  (Move immediately to the Karis Confession to allow time for the Toolbox)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we are focusing our attention on KF Confession 6:  We chose to foster illusions to save the life of our Idol Self.  When we are living out of misorientation, we foster illusions that fall into two categories: the illusion of our perfections and the illusion of our limitations.  In this world, there is real perfection and there is also the illusion of perfection. Real perfection is a quality that cannot be improved or changed. It is finite and not part of our design or purpose. Rather, it is the perfect arrangement of form, like in mathematics or architecture. In contrast to real perfection, imagined perfection is infinite and continually uses the language of   always ,   never ,   more , and   better.   Imagined perfection is never satisfied; it chronically requires more and more effort to achieve its illusions. Imagined perfection is the engine of our discontent. 3  KF members who have seen tremendous improvement in their lives through using the KF tools will sometimes become disenchanted with KF because   their accomplishments are not what they imagine they should be. Perhaps they unconsciously imagined an improvement that would support the glory of their Idol Self and became disappointed because they did not achieve it.   It’s   easy to forget that the Idol will always move the target of our expectations and present new perfections to be discontented about. When you seem to be making no progress through your KF work, you might consider whether you are actively, or unconsciously, discouraging yourself by forgetting what you have already accomplished or by judging any achievement as insignificant and petty. By allowing yourself to dismiss what you have gained, you are inviting the jackals of self-hate to take you down.  Just as there is real perfection and the illusion of perfection, there   are also real limitations and the illusion of limitations. Real limitations are set by physical laws like gravity and thermodynamics and by physical resources like time, money, health, or mental and emotional strength. These real limitations are all part of the simple restrictions of living in a material world. There are, of course, other real limitations that have to be honored if we are to care for ourselves, build healthy relationships, and develop a supportive community.  Although our Idol Self refuses to acknowledge real limitations, it carefully fosters imagined limitations   —  the electric fences and the   No Trespassing   signs of the Idol’s taboos.   If you are a mastery type, you will have taboos about giving up or giving in. You will feel strain when you experience the appearance or the actuality of failure, or when you allow someone else to have the attention or the control. If you are resigned, you will feel the punishing shock of the electric fence when you see yourself changing, feel your real feelings, or engage with real life. It is important to realize that we all have taboos. The taboos of

3  karisfellowships.com   KF27-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  others may differ from ours, and we may not understand them, but taboos have just as much power in  other people’s   lives as they do in our own.  Think about an area of imagined limitation in your life, a taboo .   (Pause for 5 seconds)   Your taboo is not a real limitation; it is an area of your life where your reactions, feelings, and thoughts hinder your progress and stifle your ability to appreciate your achievement. Perhaps this taboo prevents you from maintaining your new level of freedom.  We will now use the   T-A-T   to explore the taboo that you have identified. 4   During the pauses, you might like to jot down a few notes. We will spend one minute on each step, but in your personal work, follow the instructions in the   Expanded Version   and spend two minutes on each step. You will find the experience to be more thorough and helpful.  The T-A-T  Take the pose by placing your fingers on the three facial points. You might also place the palm of your other hand over the occiput, where your spine meets your skull. Breathe deeply.   (Pause)  1.   Experience this imagined and self-imposed taboo or limitation. Breathe.   (Pause for 15 seconds) (Repeat the instruction) (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. Jot down some thoughts and rate how uncomfortable or resistant you feel about violating this taboo.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again and breathe deeply.  2.   Imagine what you would think and feel, and what your life would be like, if you did not have this imagined limitation or taboo.   (Pause for 15 seconds) (Repeat the instruction) (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause and jot down a few notes.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again and breathe deeply.  3.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “God, thank You for healing the origins of this taboo.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “ The   origins of this imagined limitation are healing now.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause, and if you wish, write.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again, and breathe.  4.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “God, thank You for healing all the areas of my life, mind, and body that are misoriented by this imagined limitation.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “All the areas of my life, mind, and body that are misoriented by this taboo are healing now.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause, and write if you wish.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again, and breathe.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF27-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  5.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “God, thank You for healing all the areas of my life that get something out of holding on to this taboo.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “All the areas of my life that get something out of holding on to this imagined limitation are healing now.”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. If you wish, jot down a few thoughts.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again and breathe deeply.  6.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “ I forgive everyone and everything that I have blamed for creating this taboo, including God   and myself. ”   Breathe and let go.   (Pause for 15   seconds)   “ I release everyone and everything that I have held responsible for creating this imagined limitation. ”   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause, and write if you wish.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take the pose again, and breathe deeply.  7.   Listen to the clearing statement:   “ I ask forgiveness from everyone and everything that I have harmed by holding on to this imagined limitation , including God’s purposes   and my True Self. ”  Breathe.   (Pause for 15 seconds)   “ I accept responsibility for the damage that I have caused to anyone or anything by holding on to this taboo. ”   Breathe.   (Pause for 15 seconds)  Pause. If you wish, jot down your thoughts . (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now write down how you feel about this taboo or limitation. On a scale of one to ten, rate the intensity of your feelings or resistance.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Pause.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Good Shepherd, cut the electric fence of my taboos.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  In our last lesson we talked about the illusions created by appearance, talent, and money. We saw how distracted we are by the ATM, and we learned from James that the only real asset is faith — that is,   action based on oriented beliefs . 5   We also considered how the ATM can be used to support illusions of effortless superiority and the   if onlys   of limitless possibilities. For example, we might think, “If only I had enough  money, I could stop my body aging. ”   We are often hoodwinked by the   ATM rather than guided   by realities.  Many of our perceived limitations are imagined, and in neurosis we carefully foster them in an effort to save the life of our Idol. In chapter 12 of Second Corinthians, we will see how Paul deals with some of his imagined limitations. This passage has encouraged many Christians to revel in, and even be proud   of, their

5  karisfellowships.com   KF27-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  weaknesses. Others have used this passage to justify their unwillingness to develop their true potential in Christ.   Nancy’s paraphrase of   Second Corinthians 12:7 – 10   is based on her own translation and offers  alternative insights. Let’s listen to it now.  7 In order to keep me from raising my True Self up to actualization, and because of the loftiness of those revelations about my potential in Christ, I was given a thorn of judgment and self-hate which spotlights all of my human limitations, real or imagined; a messenger that Satan (or the adversary) used to slap me down, so that I could not raise myself up to the height of my true potential.   8 Three times I called on the Lord to give me some encouragement about my limitations so that the pain of self-hate and judgment might be sent away from me.   9 And the Lord   said to me, “My gift of karis relationship is s ufficient to reach your goal. Look at it this way. Active energy is matured in frailties. In other words, lack of skill and weaknesses are not to be avoided for fear of self -hate but, rather, to be acknowledged and trained so that your real abilities may have more effect with less ef fort.”   10 With greatest pleasure, therefore, I have confidence in my real weaknesses rather than in my imagined strengths because the strategic can-do power of Christ that dwells in me is waiting to develop real strength from those weaknesses. Because of  Christ’s ability to train me, I have a positive attitude in weakness, in self   -hate, in necessities, in persecution, and whenever I am in a   tight spot on behalf of Christ. It’s like  this: when I feel weak in my Idol Self, at the same time I, in my True Self, am very capable.  Take a deep breath.  Rather than imagining that Satan, the Idol Self, and life events have the power to limit him, Paul takes the position of regarding all life experiments as opportunities to train. He has learned to let go of making his  limitations the excuse for remaining in the dreary pasture of his Idol’s comfort zone. He exults in his weaknesses, trusting in Christ’s ability to   train him in real skills and a growing God-confidence. Rather than going into self-hate each time an area of weakness is exposed, Paul welcomes we akness as an opportunity to explore and grow. Having a need for training is not a limitation — it is a gift. Paul is eager to courageously explore his weaknesses and to give God the opportunity to help him discover the strengths inherent in his design. In the process of becoming strong, Paul breaks through the electric fence of his imagined limitations and discovers his real limitations. This ongoing discovery strengthens his self- confidence in every area of his life.  All real growth is stressful.   Let’s hear   that again. All real growth is stressful. You cannot pick up true glory on the bargain table — there are no shortcuts to developing strength and maturity.   That’s   why very few people are interested in real growth. In order to grow, we must move out of the comfortable land of predictable miseries and unsatisfying pleasures and courageously step into the stresses of wandering into the not-knowing with untried skills, but with hope. Through the experiment of navigating this unfamiliar territory, we gain confidence and our faith is strengthened. All the ground that we cover in our explorations becomes familiar territory. Experiments become experience, and life is no longer scary because we have real, tested skills. The struggle against the internal resistance of imagined limitations can be extremely productive. In that struggle we grow strong; we develop real tested skills that God and everyone else can trust.  Let God, your Trainer, decide when it is time for you to rest and when it is time for you to continue the journey. He will not push you beyond your capabilities, but He is eager to see you grow. As you continually stretch both your internal and external capacities, you grow from strength to strength, from faith to faith,

6  karisfellowships.com   KF27-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  from trust to trust, and from glory to glory. Each time that you are launched into a new challenge, you will begin the journey with more hope and courage than you had in previous challenges. You cannot be perfect and perform perfectly in new challenges because you are an eternally developing creature who is always learning. Perfection is finite, but the karis relationship with God is infinite.  Our prayer might go something like this:  My Divine Trainer, I am more interested in karis with You than in my imagined limitations.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits,   ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Bible teaching ?” )  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and, if you wish, prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider giving God permission to expose a taboo and to train you beyond that imagined limitation. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider   giving God permission to expose a taboo and to train you , breathe and recognize any feelings or resistance that you may be experiencing.   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness as you   consider   giving God permission to expose a taboo and to train you . Observe your experience. Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission to explore   them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider giving God permission to expose a taboo and train you . You might acknowledge to yourself what sensations are in your body right now.   (Pause)   Observe those sensations, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  this taboo and this opportunity to train . Are you comfortable or uncomfortable? Just observe.   (Pause)   Do you feel compelled to judge exposure and the need for training as good or evil?   (Pause)   What story do you want to tell about this limitation or taboo? What story do you want to tell about training?   (Pause)  Observe your responses as just information. You might breathe with a long exhaling breath or with the Dragon Breath. 6   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal

7  karisfellowships.com   KF27-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  As you breathe, repeat to yourself the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore your taboos.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit who stands ready with His spiritual snippers to cut your electric fence.  •   Welcome where you are today and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 7  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   In the face of this taboo, I let go of my longing for power and control.  •   In the face of this taboo, I let go of my longing for esteem and affection.  •   In the face of this taboo, I let go of my longing for security and comfort.  •   In the face of this taboo, I let go of my longing for perfection.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are grateful for this opportunity to train and heal. Redirect the flow of our energy toward   our potential and toward an authentic life that declares the glory of who You created us to be. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  *This is the time in our KF training cycle to consider whether we, as KF members, want to offer the next NHG book study to our wider community. All current members are invited to participate in offering this gift by signing up on the spreadsheet sent with the recent email from admin.  The Romans study begins in mid-October. If you are interested in participating, please register on the website.  (*Except when preparing for the Jubilee year)  1   www.centeringprayer.com .  2   Open My Eyes That I May See   by Clara H. Scott (1841 – 1897),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZJnGxPEv1vU .

8  karisfellowships.com   KF27-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  3   William Shakespeare,   Richard III (Act 1, Scene 1) .  4   en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas_Acupressure_Technique .  5   James 2:14 – 28.  6   See KF12.  7   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html .
