If we are suffering because of hurt pride, God has to oppose us, and our suffering becomes torment. But if we choose humility, God is ready to give us gifts of grace. So, when you are suffering, give up your pride and humbly ask God for a gift that will encourage you on your way. Then watch for the gift. These special and personal gifts from God encourage you to endure   the difficult process of becoming fully equipped for your joy and mission.  Think about how you might recognize healthy, productive seeds of change in your own life. These seeds will all have CORE — C-O-R-E — characteristics. C is for Courage; O is for Orientation; R is for Reality; E is for Endurance. To make the most of any challenge, you must be courageous, oriented, engaged with reality, and you must endure. You have probably heard about core muscles and the need for core strength. Without core strength, you are substantially weak; you   can’t   even stand up. Similarly, without CORE strength, your soul is weak and will be unable to stand in the midst of your suffering. How are you managing your challenges and your suffering? Are you acting courageously? Are you asking, seeking, and knocking for oriented solutions? Are you practicing mindful awareness with gratitude and staying in touch with what is real, or are you generating more suffering through stories, hurt pride, and self-hate? Can you endure uprightly until your oriented path is revealed? Remember CORE — Courage, Orientation, Reality, Endurance — and consider Jesus, who possessed all these core qualities and taught us how to access the redemptive potential of suffering. He exchanged His cross for joy. 2  When we have CORE muscles, we are no longer helpless victims suffering from illusions about who we  should   be and the kind of life we   should   be living. Rather, we are explorers of what is real. We explore what God is presenting to us now for our training and development. CORE muscles give us the freedom

3  karisfellowships.com   KF32-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  to make oriented choices. We become the cause that sets in motion a redemptive cycle of cause and effect. Sometimes our choice results in a predictable outcome. At other times, the outcome cannot be predicted, and our motivation to make an oriented choice is based solely on our karis relationship with God. We need developed courage to go with God into the not-knowing without attaching to a particular outcome, proving to God both our trustworthiness and our trust in Him. When we choose to do things  God’s   way, we affirm our loyalty to Him, and we demonstrate our determination to let go of our prideful judgments about how things should be.  In your prayers this week, ask God to show you how He wants to use your present circumstances for your training. Ask Him to guide you as you make the oriented choice to keep training in those circumstances, however difficult they may be. Try working through the worksheet   Suffering: An Opportunity to See Yourself .   You might offer your discoveries in the sharing time next week.  KF training teaches us to calm ourselves, choose positive action, and remember how far we have come. This changes our nervous system and our emotions, which in turn changes our experience.  Here is our quote again:  Research has shown that repeated action, learning, and memory can actually change the nervous system physically, altering both synaptic strength and connections. Such changes may be brought about by cultivated change in emotion and action; they will, in turn, change subsequent experience. 3  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, train my CORE muscles for courage, orientation, reality, and endurance. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the   Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  In the third chapter of his letter, James teaches us to observe our words. Your words tell you a lot about the health of your soul. What comes out of your mouth — not just your words but also your tone and delivery — is a kind of fruit, and that fruit reveals what you carry in your heart all the time. In unguarded moments or in moments of distress, self-hate, or euphoria, your words can tell you and others how your soul is really doing. However, we often do not pay attention to what comes out of our mouths. So, ask trustworthy people to reflect back to you what they notice; this is a time for humility, not self-defense. Remember to celebrate when your spontaneous words reveal the growing health of your soul and when your verbal interchanges with others indicate encouraging progress toward orientation.  In the Toolbox we talked about the CORE muscles of the soul — Courage, Orientation, Reality, Endurance. When your CORE is weak, you cannot stand in the face of compulsive behaviors, destructive habits, or sudden provocations; every part of you is vulnerable to weakness and injury. Unless you train your CORE muscles to be strong, you will be weak just when you need your strength the most.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF32-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  In his letter to the Ephesians, Paul teaches us to perpetually keep our enemy in mind. If we choose to live in the lazy illusion that there is no enemy and make little or no effort to train, we will be vulnerable to enemy attack.  Let’s look at Nancy’s paraphrase of   Ephesians 6:10 – 18   in which   Paul teaches us how to prepare for the good fight against our real enemy. 4  10 And one more thing, learn to take up your abilities in the Lord and take them up in the strength that comes from doing things His way.   11 Put on the complete armor of God, as when one warrior gifts his armor to another, and move toward the goal of having the ability to stand against the schemes of the slanderer and the Idol Self.   12 We need this divine armor from God because our battle is not against material creatures, but against the things that rule those creatures, against the actual authorities in their lives, against the governors of their world-system that create this present darkness, and against spiritual things that cause injury in the world beyond this world.   13 God has passed this battle on to you, but you cannot fight the battle for your own soul without the proper equipment. Therefore, take up the complete armor of God that He has gifted to you so that when those days of injury threaten you, you can stand against the onslaught — and doing all that you can, keep standing.  14 In case you have not understood, you must stand! Wrap your core muscles with truth and cover your vital organs with orientation.   15 Keep your shoes on, prepared to deliver the good news of peace at every moment.   16 And in all that you do, take up the shield of trust — of believing it — with which you can extinguish all the incoming missiles that are thrown at you by those who seek to inflame you and provoke you to imagine and judge that you have been injured.   17 And solemnly receive the helmet of wholeness, which protects your thoughts, declares your loyalty, and identifies you as one who has been rescued from the power of the enemy.   Receive   also the sword of   the Spirit and the breath, which is all that God has spoken about who you are.   18   With a cultivated attitude of sacred prayer, make requests in every moment and with every breath; pray with your spirit. Always keep awake and stay alert with obstinate persistence. Keep making requests concerning the saints — I mean those who are your fellow soldiers and who, like you, have set themselves apart to serve the purposes of God.  Take a deep breath .  If you want to live an oriented life, you must accept the reality that you have an enemy. Your enemy is determined to undermine any effort you make toward restoring your True Self. When you waste your energy searching for a counterfeit glory, you are pridefully opposing God and cooperating with the enemy that   seeks to sabotage God’s plan for your life, your mission, and your   designed glory. Healthy fear of a real enemy motivates us to secure our boundaries and guard the   ground that we have   gained.   It may seem like a paradox, but fear can be your friend. Fear can motivate you to undergo the difficult but necessary training that prepares you to face the enemy and gives you real self-confidence in the fight.  Paul is not saying in this passage that you can never rest. In fact, he is teaching you how to maintain a state of alert relaxation, trusting in the quality of your armor and your training.   If you put on God’s armor,  which is a metaphor for all the oriented qualities that you need for the fight, your enemies both within and without will no longer have power over you. Whether the enemy is Satan, your Idol Self, or the Idol

5  karisfellowships.com   KF32-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Self of others is immaterial. What is important is that you acknowledge the reality that you have   an enemy. Keep learning to stand when things get rough. If you rely on the armor of orientation, you will no longer need to run back to your old habits of relieving tension and restoring pride. You can just stand using your CORE muscles.  In the past, you may have judged people who are compelled by neurotic needs   and self-hate,   but now you are able to peacefully believe it and offer the good news of peace by being at peace.   With God’s armor , you can protect yourself from the fiery missiles of others that seek to pierce your soul and ignite mindless reactions. Just stand, believing rather than judging what people   choose and what people do, knowing that you do not have to participate. Spot the fools quickly and circumvent them. Recognize the wise. Walk with them and cling to them. The safest place for you to be is by their side.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord of the armies of God, teach me to stand.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  You might sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider a distressing situation that you just   can’t stand . (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider   a distr essing situation that you can’t   stand , recognize any emotional feelings that are present.   (Pause)   Our feelings are ours to teach us about ourselves, to guide us, to show us our limitations, and to train us. They can often be uncomfortable. We are learning to honor our feelings without allowing them to master us. Observe and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Graciously allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. Notice any struggle you may have with this experience. Do you want to escape, attack, or perhaps drift into self-pity?   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are part of the struggle. They are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission to explore whatever you are experiencing without judgment   and use a long exhaling breath to quiet your feelings.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body. What is it doing when you   consider a situation in which you cannot stand ? For example, you might notice what shutting down, craving, or, perhaps, unfairness and rage feel like in your body.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus

6  karisfellowships.com   KF32-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  thi s situation that you can’t   stand . What do you believe when you consider this situation? Do you feel compelled to judge as good or evil this   “reality check”   about your ability to stand?   (Pause)   What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Observe your experience   as just information,   and breathe.   (Pause for 30   seconds)  Heal  As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore this present distress.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit of truth as He uses your suffering to heal you.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 5  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I train to stand, I let go of my longing for power and control.  •   As I train to stand, I let go of my longing for admiration and affection.  •   As I train to stand, I let go of my longing for security and comfort.  •   As I train to stand, I let go of my longing for perfection.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I check for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time of healing and training together. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You continue to teach us how to stand. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and mission, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   Spirit of God, Descend Upon My Heart   by George Croly (1780 – 1860),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=CmWVY4n_-wY .  2   Heb.12:2.  3   Maggie Macnab, Decoding Design:   Understanding and Using Symbols in Visual Communication   (How Books, 2008), 174.

7  karisfellowships.com   KF32-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  4   1 Tim. 6:12.  5   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html .   Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.

title: KF33 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF33-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF33 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in   the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  In this lesson we will introduce the   Lectio Divina   meditation.   Lectio Divina , or   divine reading,   is a traditional Benedictine practice of meditation and prayer. Its purpose is to help us personalize Scripture and deepen our communion with God. There are four steps in the   Lectio Divina . First, we read a passage from the Bible several times. We then meditate, opening our minds to what the Holy Spirit might be saying to us through the passage. Next, we respond to any impression that we receive. Finally, we contemplate, or maintain our awareness, of what we have experienced. There are no right or wrong responses to the passage.   Lectio Divina   is an entirely personal experience.  Lectio Divina  Take a meditation posture, with the crown of your head reaching toward the heavens and your tailbone reaching toward the earth. Allow your body to hang from the central pole of your spine. Scan your body for tension, and relax. Breathe. You might use the word   CALM   to center yourself for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  1.   Read the passage  I will read a short text from the Bible and then pause. You may wish to focus your mind by repeating the Scripture to yourself. Observe as you allow the words to rise and fall with your breath. The text for this meditation is from John 17:1.  Glorify your Son so that your Son may also glorify You .  (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  2.   Receive as you listen  Relax while I read this sentence three times, pausing for thirty seconds between readings. Take the attitude of a listener and observe your experience. In the stillness between the readings, allow a feeling, thought, or image to come to mind that may be related to the words. If nothing comes to mind, notice the absence of thought or just enjoy the stillness. Compassionately notice any other  feelings or thoughts that may intrude, and then return to the text. Let’s begin.

2  karisfellowships.com   KF33-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Glorify Your Son so that Your Son may also glorify You.  (Read 3 times, pausing for 30 seconds after each reading)  3.   Respond  If you were aware of an impression, an understanding, or a feeling as you listened to the words, respond to God with affirmation and gratitude.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  4.   Rest in awareness  Now rest in stillness for one minute as you hold in your awareness whatever has happened during this time. You might allow the Scripture to gently recede, and then focus your mind on your breath.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Pause, and re-engage with your environment. You may wish to take this next minute to record your experience in your KF journal or on your   Meeting Preparation Guide , or you may wish to rest and return to your breathing.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we will begin to explore KF Confession 8:  We co-labor with the Creator to seek and to save that which was lost.  Consider for a moment what people in the ancient world had to do to recover a kidnapped loved one. To achieve their goal, these people needed developed courage, resources, and skills; they needed to face realities; and they needed endurance. You are engaged in the same process, but you are not alone. The God who created you is working with you to seek and to save the person that you have lost. That person is your True Self.  Quiet self-confidence, peaceful self-management, and mindful generosity are trustworthy indicators that you have found your True Self. In KF we are looking to see progress in these areas, not perfection. Once you have experienced living in your True Self, you will want to guard the life of that self and nurture its glorious potential.  In our early KF training, we learned that there are three categories of fear. First, we might fear ourselves. We are afraid that we are crazy, worthless, or vulnerable and will fail to meet our standards, so we are harsh with ourselves and try to force a certain performance. We might also choose inertia to confine our minds and our behavior. Second, we might fear others. What others think and do terrifies us, and in order to feel safe we compulsively avoid them or try to control them. Third, we might fear loss — loss of our self- image or reputation, loss of support from others, loss of money, loss of our time or personal space, and loss of control. We might fear missing out on life.  You can probably sense right now what a huge amount of energy it takes to live in fear — energy that could be used to seek and save your True Self. If you are full of fear, it will take all the energy you have just to

3  karisfellowships.com   KF33-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  manage that fear and keep you functioning. Think about your fear. What are you afraid of losing — your self-value, your reputation, or missing out on the delights of this world?   You may be discovering that you are more motivated by your fear of loss than by your love .   (Repeat)  It takes courage to act in an oriented manner no matter how much fear we feel. You might recall our KF motto:   Train hard. Fight easy. 1   (Repeat)   Just as soldiers are trained to act in a disciplined manner in the face of fear, members of Karis Fellowships are trained to move through the fear into self-disciplined action. We start by training our courage. You may have read and heard that   courage is the foundation of all virtue . Let me repeat that:   courage is the foundation of all virtue . 2   Without courage   in the face of life’s  experiments, you will not take the steps that lead to real virtue, moral integrity, and principled choices. Without courage, you will find yourself retreating into old patterns of behavior, and you will justify your choices with virtue stories that restore your pride and mask your fears; and when you are faced with the challenges and enticements of this material world, the compulsion to save your life will overwhelm your best intentions.  Every time you exercise your courage and make an oriented choice in the face of fear, your courage grows. This is called training. Then, when you have to bear the heavy weight of distress or success, or you need to take the next step in your journey toward healing, you will have the courageous muscle to stand your ground no matter what your Idol Self is screaming at you. When your mission requires you to take risks, to assert your real power and influence, or to let go, you will be able to remain oriented because you have been training hard.  You might consider this:   Your fear of loss may be just a shadow of the horror and grief that you unconsciously feel over a much more profound loss — the loss of your True Self.   (Repeat)  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, for Your sake, I want to give up my search for glory and seek my True Self. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  ( (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  In the second chapter of his letter, James writes about faith. To give us a better understanding of what James is teaching us, Nancy has introduced other accurate and valid translations of the Greek word for faith, including   trust ,   believe , and   a set of beliefs .  Let’s listen now to Nancy’s paraphrase of   James 2:10 – 23 .  10 If you try to use the law of your Idol’s system and then fail in one area of your law, you  will condemn everything about yourself.   11 The same Lawgiver who says, “Do not be sexually untrustworthy,” also says, “Do not be murderous.” In other words, if you choose  to live by law and be chaste, but are still murderous, you make yourself fail the whole law.  12 Instead, speak and also act like citizens who are brought to court by the law of freedom rather than like slaves who are brought to court by the law of the Idol.   13 The resulting

4  karisfellowships.com   KF33-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  verdict of the court according to the Idol’s law will be inexorable for those who are  inexorable for they cannot help but punish themselves and others through self-hate. Mercy, however, exults and is self-confident in trials. Mismanaged self-hate throws us back into slavery, but having mercy on ourselves and on others is the new way to handle mistakes and invite possibilities. Mercy is real self-confidence in action.  14 How does it benefit you, or anyone, if you say that you believe but do not act on what you believe? Your belief will not rescue you or anyone else.   15 And that lack of congruence between your beliefs and actions will be exposed when you encounter a member in the community who is in need.   16 For example, you say to someone in need, “Go away from  me in peace with my blessing of warmth   and food,” but   you do nothing practical about  their need. Their need is stirring up conflicts in you, and since you won’t deal with your  own inner conflict about showing mercy to yourself, you refuse to deal with any conflict about mercy.   17 In this way, relying on a set of beliefs without taking action destroys your  faith’s vitality.   18 Look at it this way. You say that you trust God, or have a set of beliefs that you trust, but I take action. Show me your trust apart from action, and I will show you my trust by my action. Which is more real?   19 You say that you believe that God is undivided in His person and in His activities, and that is admirable, but even demons believe that. Unlike you, however, who separate faith from action, demons are congruently afraid of God.   20 You vain and pretentious people, are you willing to recognize that your faith separated from your action is not doing its job? It is not preparing your soil for seeds of orientation.   21 Abraham, who was our first example of a person living in a relationship with God based on faith, was oriented through his action — the action of taking Isaac, his son, up to the place of sacrifice. In the same way, you are learning to sacrifice your dreams of an idealized glory.   22 You can see that his action was congruent with his faith, and through his action his faith reached its fulfillment. That fulfillment was  orientation to God. Abraham’s gift to God in karis relationship was his effort, not his set  of beliefs.   23 And what is written was fulfilled: “Abraham was trustworthy with God,  responding to God with his karis gift, and this act — this offering — was credited to  Abraham as orientation, and he was called the beloved friend of God.”  Take a deep breath.  Let’s look at   a few points that James presents in this passage.  1.   The law cannot rescue you  You cannot rescue the True Self by imposing legal systems on your life. It is impossible to fulfill all the requirements of a legal system, and if you try, you will always be in danger of self-condemnation.  2.   Freedom is what kidnapped slaves are seeking  Slaves have no power over their own lives, and yet they can envision a life of freedom. In Christ, we are no longer slaves of the Idol but citizens living under the law of liberty, and as citizens we have the freedom, the resources and, also, the responsibility to change our lives.  3.   Mercy is self-confidence in action  Mercy triumphs over judgment. 3   Mercy is the law of Jesus in the court of freedom and is the opposite of self-hate. Under the kingdom law of karis, there is no condemnation, so we are free to make

5  karisfellowships.com   KF33-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  mistakes, find out what works, and then become the cause of our own beneficial outcomes, which builds more self-confidence.  4.   Mercy toward others  The unseen mercy that we show to ourselves is manifested in the material world by the mercy we show to others. Mercy is an active, effortful self-extension that shows God we mean business about His mission, His priorities, and our relationship with Him. Showing mercy to our community is often difficult. It requires courage, and it costs us something —and that’s   why mercy is a karis gift.  5.   God is united in effort and principle  We are called to be imitators of God, acting in congruence with what we know to be good, right, and fair. 4   James reminds us that what God says, He does. He   doesn’t   compartmentalize, believing one thing and yet doing something else.  6.   Abraham gave the karis gift of obedience  In obedient response to God’s request, Abraham relinquished what he loved   most — his son, who was his hope for the fulfillment of his search for glory. Abraham was congruent. He acted on what he believed about God, and through his choices, not through his ideas or good intentions, he became  God’s beloved friend.  Our prayer might go something like this:  God of Abraham, help me become Your trustworthy friend. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider b ecoming God’s   trustworthy friend.   (Repeat)   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider   becoming God’s trustworthy friend , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)  Recognize with compassion whatever you may be experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Graciously allow your experience to rest in your awareness. Notice if there is any tension or resistance as you   consider   becoming God’s trustworthy friend .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)

6  karisfellowships.com   KF33-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing as you   consider   becoming God’s trustworthy  friend.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might notice   what hope, pessimism, or shame feels like in your body. You might feel nothing at all. Gently maintain awareness of whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  the possibility of becoming God’s trustworthy friend . Is your experience right now comfortable, uncomfortable, or vague and slippery? Just observe.   (Pause)   What do you believe when you consider  becoming God’s trustworthy friend? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you, perhaps like Abraham, afraid of loss? Observe your experience as just information, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore friendship with God.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit of truth as He reveals the realities of your faith.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 5  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I learn to be God’s trustworth y friend, I let go of the craving for power and control.  •   As I learn to be God’s trustworth y friend, I let go of the craving for admiration and affection.  •   As I learn to be God’s trustworth y friend, I let go of the craving for security and comfort.  •   As I learn to be God’s trustworth y friend, I let go of the craving for perfection.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I check for further integration.  Pause.   Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  We are so grateful for this time together. Hold us in the power of our growing trustworthiness and lead us to the next step in our healing this week. Help us co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and design, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF33-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  *Pray for those who are organizing the NHG study. Pray that God will fulfill every one of their oriented desires for goodness and for the accomplishment of their work of faith through their can-do energy so that the name of our Lord will be glorified in them, and they will be glorified in Him. 6  (*Except when preparing for the Jubilee Year)  1   en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Alexander_Suvorov .  2   www.brainyquote.com/quotes/quotes/c/cslewis100842.html .  3   James 2:13.  4   Eph. 5:1; Proverbs 2:9.  5   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html .   Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  6   2 Thess. 1:11.

title: KF34 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF34-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF34 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 4)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  In this lesson we will continue with the   Lectio Divina   meditation.  When you practice the Lectio Divina in your own meditation time, try reading a longer passage — perhaps a paragraph or a story from the Gospels. Engage with the passage by following the same steps.  Take the meditation posture by sitting upright. Straighten your neck as you lower your chin a little. Allow your shoulders to relax and fall back.   (Pause)   Scan your body for tension and release it on the exhale. You might use the word   CALM   to center yourself. Breathe and prepare for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  1.   Read the passage  I will read a short text from the Bible and then pause. You might wish to allow the words to rise and fall in your mind with your breath. Our text is from the first chapter of James, verse 4.  Give endurance a chance to accomplish its oriented outcome .  (Repeat)   (Pause for 10 seconds)  2.   Receive as you listen  Relax while I read this sentence three times, pausing between readings. Take the attitude of a listener and attend to your experience with the Scripture. In the stillness between the readings, allow a feeling, thought, or image to come to mind that may be related to the words. If nothing comes, notice the absence or just enjoy the stillness. Observe with compassion any other feelings or thoughts that may intrude, and then return to our text.   Let’s begin .  Give endurance a chance to accomplish its oriented outcome .  (Read 3 times, pausing for 30 seconds after each reading)  3.   Respond  Now, whatever your experience might be, respond to God with affirmation and gratitude.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF34-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  4.   Rest in awareness  Rest in stillness for one minute as you contemplate whatever has happened during this time. You might allow the Scripture to gently recede and then focus your mind on your breath.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Pause and re-engage with your environment. You may wish to take this next minute to rest or to record your experience, perhaps in your KF journal or on your   Meeting Preparation Guide .   (Pause for 1 minute)  And pause.  Our hymn for KF Confession 8 is   And Can It Be?   by Charles Wesley.  He left His Father’s throne above,  So free, so infinite His grace!  Emptied Himself of all but love,  And bled for Adam’s helpless race.  ‘ Tis mercy all, immense and free,  For, O my God, it found out me.  ‘Tis mercy all, immense and free,  For, O my God, it found out me! 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  In KF Confession 8 we commit to partnering with God in the rescue of our True Self:  We co-labor with the Creator to seek and to save that which was lost.  This month we are learning about the CORE muscles of our soul. CORE — C-O-R-E — stands for Courage, Orientation, Reality, Endurance. Last week we looked at how life experiments offer effective training opportunities to grow our courage. When we walk through suffering or success mindfully, we develop the muscle of our courage, which increases our confidence to explore other challenges — challenges that we know will bring more suffering and, also, more success. Challenges stretch our courage, our ability to remain oriented, our engagement with reality, and our endurance.  When you build a muscle at the gym, you work against some kind of resistance, and when you build the muscle of courage, the resistance you work against is fear. Courage is not the absence of fear; it is choosing to act in an oriented manner when fear is goading you to return to habitual and misoriented ways of relieving anxiety. Think of it this way: every real virtue is developed in the face of fear, courage is the soil in which every virtue is planted, and endurance gives every virtue time to grow.  Your Idol likes to say,   “ I did it my way, ”   but actually   doing it my way   only means that you reacted to the fear of death with your habitual patterns — that is, you asserted your claims, met the demands of your shoulds, and maintained your pride system.   My way   is no way at all. It is the hamster wheel that uses up

3  karisfellowships.com   KF34-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  your resources but goes nowhere. We have all seen people who do their own thing, offer only feeble contributions to the community, and never make substantial progress in their lives. These people end up becoming chaotic, demanding, or listless. By contrast, those who have trained to live lives of courageous virtue experience spontaneous love, joy, and peace and have access to all kinds of marvelous gifts.  With growing courage, we can learn to reach for orientation in more areas of our lives. Acting in oriented ways is sometimes called   obedience.   The idea of obedience might be repulsive to you, so you may feel rebellious right now. That is understandable because many of us have experienced abuse in the name of obedience. Authorities in our lives did not consider our needs or desires. They just imposed on us their compulsive need for control. On the other hand, some of us were never taught to obey, and from that neglect we learned that obedience is bad, unnecessary, or too hard — something that demands too much effort and offers no reward. When God tells us to obey, however, He is giving us a gift. He is not impoverishing us or using us. He is training us to be free. To obey God is to recognize that we are creatures who thrive when we live according to our design. God is our Designer, and He knows how we work and what works for us. Trust Him to bring into your life what will train and build your True Self for fulfillment and freedom.  Orientation is living in harmony with God and with the Creation. This Creation includes your body, your personality, your mission, and, also, your community. The Creation flows within the limitations of its design, and as we work within the limitations of our design, our lives line up with the flow of life. Oriented people are ecosystems that are spiritually and energetically cleansing themselves; and by cleansing themselves, they cleanse their environment. We have all been polluted by toxic people. Perhaps you are related to some of them. Cleaning up the ecosystem of your family may be your most important mission in this world.  Just as there are rules in the darkroom for developing film, so there are rules in life for developing your True Self. 2   By choosing to obey these rules, you clean up your life, and you help clean up the energetic path of those who went before you. You also provide a cleaner environment for those who follow you. So, when you read the Bible, look for examples of   do’s and don’ts   and try not to fear this guidance. Telling stories about how restrictive or hard that guidance is   won’t benefit you or anyone else . Instead, recognize the hope that this guidance brings.  Now that you know how to manage your self-hate, you can courageously face whatever reality your choices reveal about your faith, the quality of your orientation, and your commitment to your own growth and mission. You can then valiantly choose to reorient to an authentic life, seeking and saving what has been lost. All that you learn in this process will be woven into the fabric of your real glory. The Father of glory wants to glorify you in your True Self, the self that He designed, so that you might glorify Him. You will discover that the recovery of what you have lost will become part of your message to those in this sick world who have lost the same thing. Give up the Idol and its compulsive illusions about who you should be. No matter what has happened to you, your True Self is still there, waiting to be discovered, nurtured, and supported while you press on to real glory.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord Jesus, support me as I make oriented choices to nurture my True Self and reveal my true glory. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.

4  karisfellowships.com   KF34-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Heaven rejoices when we start to practice KF Confession 8:   3  We co-labor with the Creator to seek and to save that which was lost.  Our Bible passages for this lesson are taken from chapter 15 of the Gospel of John and chapter 3 of First Peter.   Let’s start with   Nancy’s paraphrase of   selected verses from   John 15:1 – 11 . Jesus is teaching about the relationship between the True Vine and its branches.  1 I and no other am the True Vine, and my Father is the vinedresser.   2 All the branches attached to Me that are not bearing fruit He takes away, and all the branches that are bearing fruit He prunes back so that they can carry more fruit . . .   4 In all of your activities, remain in Me, even as I am remaining in you. Just as the branch must remain connected to the vine in order to bear fruit, so you must remain connected to Me . . .   8 When you become My disciples and bear much fruit, others benefit and they honor My Father.   9 Just as the Father is well-pleased with Me, I am well-pleased with you. Live in My love.   10 If you guard My commands, you will remain in My love, just as I have guarded M y Father’s  commands and remain in His love.   11 I have told you these things so that you might experience My joy and that your joy might be complete.  Take a deep breath.  1.   Jesus is the True Vine  Jesus calls Himself the True Vine. This implies that there is a false vine, and Nancy would call this false vine the Idol Self. The True Self is a branch connected to the True Vine, but sometimes that branch  doesn’t seem to be producing much   fruit. Have you ever seen a grapevine that ’s   been pruned for winter? At this dormant stage of its life cycle, the vine is unproductive and unattractive. From a distance the vine looks dead, and you would swear that it could never produce fruit again. You might feel that way about yourself. But if you understand the growth cycle of the vine, you will know that the vine is not dead. It is quietly enduring the winter while it secretly and mysteriously recharges and prepares to produce abundant fruit in the spring.  2.   We glorify the Father by bearing much fruit  The Fruit of the Spirit and our oriented choices can be seen by others. 4   When people see this fruit in us, they recognize the character of Jesus, who is the True Vine and the material expression of the Father. We honor God our Father by remaining connected to the Vine and by bearing fruit in its season.  3.   We abide in the love of Jesus through obedience  The circulating life force of the True Vine is love. If we remain in the Vine, we have access to this love, which, like breath, flows in and through us in harmony with God and the Creation. In this state of harmony, we can do astonishing things. How do we stay attached to Jesus, the True Vine? We stay attached to the True Vine by abiding in His love, and we abide in His love through obedience.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF34-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Now   let’s flip over to   First Peter 3:8 – 12 , which we will read in Nancy’s paraphrase.  8 Here is a summary of what I ’ve   just been saying: All of you, be like loving family —  harmonious, compassionate, tender-hearted, and humble in spirit.   9 Get into a healthy cycle of   blessing others and inheriting a blessing instead of perpetuating the destructive cycle of law-keepers, who return harm for harm and restore their hurt pride by punishing others. Your choice to bless others depends on your karis relationship with God; it does not depend on what others   do or don’t do.   10 Do you remember Psalm 34?   “ Those who desire to live well — to love and to experience good days — reveal that intention by refusing to speak the harm on the tip of their tongues and by refusing to use polite words to cloak resentful wrath. Those who choose life take responsibility for their feelings. They choose to swerve away from harming the Creation, and they do good to themselves and to others. They seek peace and pursue it like a hunter.   12 Why do they choose to live this way? Because the eyes of the Lord are toward the oriented and His ears attend to their prayer, but the face of the Lord is actively against those who perpetuate misorientation. ”  Take a deep breath.  God has invited you into a karis relationship with Him so that you can inherit His blessing. You   can’t inherit  His blessing if you continue to live life your   own way — taking cheap, habitual shortcuts to relieve your anxiety and save your   Idol’s   pride. By consistently   following Peter’s short list of do’s and don’ts , you continue to invest in your stock portfolio of blessing, which in due season will produce abundant and glorious fruit.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord of blessing, whatever it takes, bring me into my inheritance of blessing. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water, and you might prepare to take some notes. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider an area of your life where you might invest to inherit a blessing. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider an area of your life where you might invest to inherit a blessing , how does it feel?   (Pause)  Our feelings are ours to teach us about ourselves, to guide us, and to train us. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

6  karisfellowships.com   KF34-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Awareness without judgment  Allow whatever you are experiencing to rest in your awareness. Observe whatever tension you may be feeling as you   consider where you might invest to inherit a blessing . You might notice a compulsion to push away or excuse thoughts and feelings, or to make up a virtue story.   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider this area of your life where you might invest to inherit a blessing .   (Pause)   You might notice what an old pattern of rationalizing or an old story feels like in your body. You might feel compulsive strain, pushing, and craving or, perhaps, the fear of loss.   Gently keep your attention focused on whatever you might be sensing. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider this area   of your life where you might invest to inherit a blessing.   Does that feel pleasant, unpleasant, or vague and slippery? Just observe.   (Pause)   What do you believe when you consider this investment? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something — of yourself, of others, or of loss? Perhaps you feel hope. Observe your experience as just information, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created all of us to have feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have felt like you feel when they have   considered making an investment to inherit future blessing . You can stop telling stories about this investment by asking yourself , “ Are my present investment choices reflecting who I really am in Christ? How might I invest today in a future of blessing? ”   (Pause)   With compassion for yourself and for others who are making this choice to invest, breathe and help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for this time together of healing and redirection. Hold us in this orientation toward You and toward our inheritance in Christ. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our true design and potential, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS

7  karisfellowships.com   KF34-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1   And Can It Be?   by Charles Wesley (1707 – 1788);   www.youtube.com/watch?v=sQeIGbKqiw8 .  2   See KF6 Expanded.  3   Luke 15:7, 10, 32.  4   Gal. 5:22-23, Matt. 5:16.

title: KF35 Meeting
content:

Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Lectio Divina  Assume your meditation posture and breathe. Straighten your neck as you lower your chin a little. Allow your shoulders to relax and fall back.   (Pause)   You might use the word   CALM   to center yourself. Take the next minute to scan your body for tension and then release it on the exhale. Breathe.   (Pause for 1 minute)  1.   Read the passage  I will read a short sentence from the Bible and then pause. Our text is John 17:17 in which Jesus prays for His people.  Set them apart into the truth .  (Repeat)   (Pause for 10 seconds)  2.   Receive as you listen  Relax while I read this sentence three times, pausing between readings. On the last reading I will use the first-person pronoun. Take the attitude of a listener and gently observe your experience with the words.   Let’s begin.   (Use the singular pronoun for the last reading)  Set them (me) apart into the truth .  (Read 3 times, pausing for 30 seconds after each reading)  3.   Respond  Respond to God with affirmation and gratitude.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  4.   Rest in awareness  Rest in stillness for one minute as you contemplate what you have experienced during this time.  (Pause for 1 minute)  Pause and re-engage with your environment. You may wish to take this next minute to record your

2  karisfellowships.com   KF35-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  experience in your KF journal or on your   Meeting Preparation Guide,   or you might wish to simply wait.  (Pause for 1 minute)  Pause. You can practice the   Lectio Divina   by reading the entire chapter of John 17 and then focusing on a phrase or verse that strikes you, or you might meditate on any other passage or story from the Bible. Take a little time to explore the Scripture through repetition and listening. Breathe, and let God reorient your spirit with the truth of the words.  Our hymn for KF Confession 8 is   And Can It Be?  Long my imprisoned spirit lay,  Fast- bound in sin and nature’s night .  Thine eye diffused a quickening ray —  I woke, the dungeon flamed with light!  My chains fell off, my heart was free;  I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.  My chains fell off, my heart was free;  I rose, went forth, and followed Thee. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  KF Confession 8 reminds us of our real business:  We co-labor with the Creator to seek and to save that which was lost.  This month we ’ve   been talking about our CORE strength — courage, orientation, reality, and endurance. Strong CORE muscles are necessary for tackling the challenges that lie ahead as we seek and save what has been lost. We have already looked at courage and orientation. Courage is feeling the fear and yet choosing orientation anyway. Orientation is a state of flow and harmony with God and the Creation, and we enter into this dynamic state through something called obedience. Obedience demonstrates our choice to live in the reality   of our design. As God’s creatures, we are designed to enjoy a fulfilling  relationship with our Creator, and we can only flourish when that relationship is our goal.  Let’s explore this idea of reality.  1.   What is reality?  Reality is what you have to deal with today. It includes your personal strengths, weaknesses, and antecedents — and those of others. It also includes the prescribed limitations and enforced order of civil law and your community culture. Another reality that cannot be avoided is the universal law of cause and effect.  If we are to dwell in love, our commitment to reality is essential. If we prefer illusions, we cannot love no matter what our imagination tells us.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF35-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  2.   Who are you, really?  God created you to be an eternally unfolding discovery to yourself, to others, and to Him. When you are busy judging yourself, hating yourself, or controlling and suppressing yourself,   it’s   difficult to explore yourself. You will make up all sorts of stories about why you should not use time and resources for exploration and self-discovery. These stories seem credible because in the past you have successfully used them to maintain your pride system. Your stories and excuses are often driven by fear — fear of yourself, fear of what others will think or do, and fear of what you might lose.  3.   It is real that you are a human creature  Every human being is a creature, and since you are human, you are also a creature. Like every other creature, you are finite and impermanent in this material world and subject to the limitations of an animal. You must work, and you must rest. You must make mistakes, and just like any puppy or lion cub, you must be trained to reach your potential. You are not a god. You are a creature with limitations. This is a reality.  4.   You are subject to the limitations of the Creation  There are physical laws, and there are energetic laws. There are civil, social, and financial laws — and there are spiritual laws for healing and growth. These laws apply to everyone, and they function on the principle of cause and effect. So, if you want to achieve a particular outcome, you will have to live within the limitations of cause and effect. For example, if you want to develop trusting relationships, you must become the cause by becoming trustworthy yourself. If you want to heal your soul, you must become the cause by creating the kind of life that allows you the time and resources to heal.  5.   How do you invest in your True Self?  If you want to invest in your True Self, you must learn   to live within the limitations of God’s   design and His rules for physical, mental, and spiritual health. KF training teaches you how to do that. The practice of mindfulness helps you observe and explore your present reality; you learn to recognize your shoulds, your claims, and your pride system, as well as your preferences and delights. You also have your KF toolbox. You can reach in and choose a tool to help you unload the extra baggage of idolatry that cripples your courage and your ability to endure.  There are a number of non-KF tools that have also helped KF members glimpse the pearl of their True Self. 2   One of these tools is the   Myers-Briggs Type Indicator   assessment, which helps you recognize the characteristics associated with your personality type. 3   There are several books available that offer and explain the assessment, and you can go online to find descriptions of the different types. These descriptions may help you recognize aspects of your True Self.  Another tool that some KF members have found helpful often triggers fear and judgment in Christians. This particular tool is a combination of science and art and is as old as the human experience with God. Perhaps you can just observe this suggestion without taking the Judgment Path.  We know that God created cycles and seasons in the material world and, also, in our lives. In Genesis 1:14 – 20, we learn that God designed these cycles and seasons to be governed, or directed, by the sun, the moon, and the stars. We also learn from Psalm 19 that the heavens declare the glory of God. Some Christians believe that it benefits us and   God’s purposes   if we understand what the lights in the heavens reveal about our unique design and its potential. One blog post that you may find interesting is   Astrology from a Christian Perspective . 4

4  karisfellowships.com   KF35-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  There is no need to feel fear right now.   Nancy’s aim   is to give you whatever help she can. She is simply offering a tool that has helped many Christians get a clearer picture of their True Self.  Finally, feedback from others can give you a glimpse of your True Self. If you can be trusted to respond with gratitude and moderation, others can safely reflect back to you areas of your life that need orienting. Their observations are so valuable. Members of a trustworthy community can also help you recognize your natural strengths and unique abilities. They can encourage you to have mercy on your True Self when it shines in all of its underdevelopment and lack of skill.  This week, you might pray this prayer:  Designer of my soul, I want to know my True Self. Show me how to bring it to the light. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s turn   to   Philippians 4:4 – 9   and read these verses together   in Nancy’s translation.  4 Take your pleasure in the Lord at all times. I will say it again, take pleasure in Him.   5 Let your oriented and capable abilities be known to everyone. Let others know that through you the Lord is near.   6 Treat nothing with anxious care, but in everything by prayer and entreaty, mixed with thankfulness, let God know what you want,   7 and the peace of God in Christ Jesus, which exceeds and has a wider extension than all of your limited reasoning, will keep watch over your motivations and perceptions.   8 And beyond that, siblings, in all your dealings take into account what is true, what is divinely noble, what is oriented and just, what is undefiled and pure, what is beloved, what imparts good omen. Notice if anything is excellent and commendable.   9 And make it your business to practice the things that you have learned and taken to yourself, as well as what you have heard and seen in me, and the God of peace will be with you.  Take a deep breath.  Who wants reality? Sometimes reality feels like a grim existence, full of hard slogging, frustrations, and anxiety. These perceptions come from the Idol Self. Like an expert in war propaganda, the Idol uses false reasonings to convince us that reality is our enemy and illusion is our friend. The True Self thrives in reality, so if the Idol can convince us to hate and resist reality, we are only one small step away from hating and resisting the True Self.  God, however, only works in reality. He works with the truth of who we are and the truth about our development. He wants reality to become our natural habitat. If we choose to live in reality rather than illusion and courageously grapple with the challenges, limitations, and possibilities of real life, God can confidently trust us with all the marvelous experiences, fun, and delights that He has in mind.  Here are a few points that Nancy would like you to consider from this passage.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF35-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1.   Take your pleasures with the Lord in mind  The quality of your work toward orientation is often revealed in how you use pleasure. The Idol Self uses pleasure to escape reality and to escape the real God. The True Self experiences pleasure while enjoying God, His creation, and His gifts. As your True Self grows, so does your capacity to enjoy. God is longing to share with you His delights, but if you use your capacity for pleasure to medicate, escape, or stagnate, He cannot trust you with these gifts.  2.   Prayer is real  God listens to oriented people who are guarding the commandments of Jesus in their lives.  3.   God’s peace is real  Real peace is not found in the stories and logic that we use to relieve our anxiety and restore our pride. Unshakable   peace is the fruit of trusting in God’s   desire and ability to be active in our lives as we choose to live in reality and cooperate with Him. We are not alone in our efforts to grow. God is a real player in our lives, and He provides skilled people in the community who can help us learn to live in reality.  4.   Our choices are real  Through Jesus, God has shown us what human glory looks like. However, we are not conformed to this glorious image by magic or without effort on our part. We have to make choices that lead us toward that goal. There are things we must choose to take on, and there are things we must choose to give up.  5.   Our spiritual nature is real  Reality   also   includes   the   marvelous   things   that   stream   from   the   unseen — those   flashes   of understanding that are like beacons guiding us home. Mindfulness training helps us catch these moments of inspiration that remind us of who we are and where we are really going. In all our dealings, mindfulness training helps us stay focused on realities that are divinely noble, oriented and just,   undefiled   and   pure,   excellent   and   commendable,   beloved,   and   imparting   good   omen. Maintaining this focus trains our material existence to cooperate with and express the reality of our spiritual nature.  This is   Nancy’s translation of   First Peter 2:9. In this verse, the apostle describes the real mission of our redeemed True Self and our true identity as the children of God.  You are a select generation, a sovereign priesthood, a company set apart, a people kept safe so that you may proclaim the wonders and goodness of Him who invited you to come out of the darkness and enter into His marvelous light.  Take a deep breath.  Let’s continue   training so that we might become the glorious people God designed us to be.  Our prayer might go something like this:  God and Savior, I want to proclaim Your wonders and Your goodness through my life. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.

6  karisfellowships.com   KF35-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider a situation in which you might choose reality. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider a situation in which you might choose reality , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable. You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you.   (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to rest in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push away the positive evidence, perhaps the evidence of how well you are actually doing or how positive a situation really is. Perhaps you push away positive evidence because   a situation doesn’t meet your   standards. You might find yourself pushing away what you do not wish to recognize or are afraid to acknowledge. Breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice how it signals you when you   consider this situation in which you might choose reality.   Gently focus your attention on those signals.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to respectfully observe those uncomfortable sensations, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider choosing reality.   Is your experience right now pleasant, unpleasant, or vague and slippery? Just observe.  (Pause)   Are you afraid of seeing the real, positive evidence of change in yourself or in others? Are you resisting what the truth is teaching you? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore what is real.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit of truth and His desire to liberate you through the truth.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you and others have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF35-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 5  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I learn to mindfully rejoice in reality, I let go of the craving for power and control.  •   As I learn to mindfully rejoice in reality, I let go of the craving for admiration and affection.  •   As I learn to mindfully rejoice in reality, I let go of the craving for security and comfort.  •   As I learn to mindfully rejoice in reality, I let go of the craving for perfection.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for drawing us together for our healing and training. Hold us in the power of the truth of who we actually are and what we have been created to do. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  *Registration is open for   next year’s   NHG book study. All KF members are welcome to attend and are also invited to sign up on the website to facilitate one or more of the sessions. (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  The process of building strong CORE muscles requires time, and while you are building those muscles, you will have to learn endurance. Most people have not learned the great rewards of endurance because they give up too soon in their training. They are still motivated by instant gratification, snatching at what they hope to gain and losing heart when their goals are not quickly realized. They long for a shortcut that will relieve their tension, even if that shortcut leads them deeper into chaos. They cannot imagine how practicing endurance might benefit them, and their lack of skill prevents them from discovering what marvelous outcomes are possible if they would learn to endure.  1.   Mindfulness and meditation teach us productive endurance  The practice of mindfulness and meditation helps us develop the CORE muscle of endurance. In KF meetings, we learn to take small mindfulness steps, but we hope that each one of you will go on to take bigger steps and increase your meditation time. When you practice mindfulness and meditation, your mind and body must endure the self-criticism, anxiety, frustration, and wiggles of boredom that come with learning any new skill. If you learn to endure these tensions, you will increase your capacity to endure tension in other challenging situations. You are presently learning the skill of mindful endurance by practicing meditation in a quiet environment where there are few distractions. This skill can then be applied in far more distracting and stressful circumstances. You must learn to sail on a sheltered lake before launching out onto the ocean.  During your meditation time, you may have had these thoughts:   I can’t do this. I can’t do it right.   I  don’t want to be doing this.   This isn’t working. I’m   too tired.   I’m   wasting my time.   I’ve g ot a dozen other things to do. Will the timer never ring ? I’m so bored!   It’s quite natural to think and feel   this way.

3  karisfellowships.com   KF36-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Learning to meditate requires endurance —and aren’t these   exactly the kind of thoughts and feelings you have in any place of endurance? The untrained parts of you are being stretched, and they have lots of strong feelings about that! The Idol Self uses these feelings to discourage you from developing the endurance you need to become real and glorious.  2.   Listening to another person teaches us productive endurance  The practice of listening attentively during the sharing and teaching times trains you to endure productively. You learn how to be aware, intentional, and mindful when someone is talking — and that includes God and yourself. God often tells us to listen up.   He isn’t kidding !  3.   Practicing endurance trains us   for life’s difficulties  Without training in productive endurance, you will find it much more difficult to manage your anxiety and respond to   life’s experiments   with orientation. Your business is to practice endurance and give it a chance to accomplish the oriented outcome of developing virtue and a trustworthy character. 2  Whenever you meditate, pray, or listen to others, you strengthen the core muscle of endurance. Life is difficult, and if you   haven’t   learned to endure for even a few minutes, how can you hope to endure for the long run?  If you are suffering and finding it hard to endure, try working through the worksheet   Suffering: An Opportunity to see Yourself ,   and bear in mind that you may be   inflicting suffering on yourself. You are often reluctant to examine your own suffering because that suffering is serving your neurotic goals — your Idol Self is getting something out of it. You might, for example, be using your suffering to punish yourself or others. Suffering can also be a convenient excuse to avoid responsibility or to avoid working on your own healing. Perhaps you use suffering to make yourself and others feel guilty. You can then extort support, sympathy, attention, and even admiration.  When we refuse to honor our limitations and those of others, we often cause our own suffering. We push, shove, and force to the point of exhaustion and to the detriment of our health and are unwilling to learn to be patient in our discomfort. Instead, we cling to the belief that we are like gods and can get what we want if we push hard enough. Then, if our circumstances are not magically transformed, we blame God or others for our suffering. In our karis relationship with God, however, suffering becomes an invitation to acknowledge our limitations and train our ability to live in reality. If you refuse that training, you simply will not have the strength to productively endure adversity. Under stress, you will default to old habits of saving your life and cause more suffering.  Your Idol has loaded you with the baggage of its misorientation, and that heavy weight prevents you from running your race with endurance. In Karis Fellowships, we are working hard to unload this extra weight and strengthen our capacity to endure. We want to run.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord of an easy yoke, I am willing and ready to unload the   Idol’s   weight. 3   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING

4  karisfellowships.com   KF36-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  People in the first century were trained to remember the context of a portion of Scripture. Following that tradition, Nancy has incorporated ideas from chapter 11 in her paraphrase of   Hebrews 12:1 – 17 . As you listen to the text for this lesson, notice how the author uses the words   endurance ,   discipline , and   training .  1 When we consider all those who have gone before us into a better country — those who acted on their beliefs and who already know by experience what we are coming to know — we are encouraged to keep moving toward that country set apart for us by God. Therefore, lay aside the heavy weight of the Idol Self and its misorientation, which so easily entangles us. Let us run with endurance the challenge stretching out before us and  2 fix our sights on the beacon light of Jesus, who by the example of His choices leads us forward. He accomplished the goal of showing us the way home. He endured the cross and exchanged it for joy. He resisted self-hate and took His place of authority next to the throne of God. That is your path, too.   3 You might consider this: Jesus, our Lord and leader, endured the same kinds of misoriented people that you endure — people who resist the person of Jesus in their thoughts and choices. His example encourages us not to abandon our True Self or become weary in our efforts.  4 Let’s get real. You can still do better in your striving against misorientation. Your efforts haven’t killed you yet!   5 You have forgotten the firm guidance that is addressed to you as sons:   “ My son, do not undervalue the discipline of God, believing   that it’s not worthwhile , and do not faint when He corrects you, judging that His correction and discipline are too hard and unfair.   6 Why do we engage with His training? Because God only disciplines those whom He loves, and every son that He receives as a candidate for training He thoroughly corrects .”  7 You endure in order to be trained. In other words, your training requires your endurance. God is dealing with you as He would deal with sons. Think about this: What kind of father would not train his own son?   8 Everyone has received some sort of training, but if you are  not trained by God, then you are not of God’s lineage— you are not His son.   9 Before we were accepted as sons of God, we were trained by fathers of our material lineage, and we turned toward their way of doing things, which did not help us much. We would do better to come under the management of the Father of our spiritual lineage, and live.   10 Let me explain what I mean. Our material fathers trained us for a short time according to what they thought was best, but often not according to what we needed. God, however, trains us according to what would benefit us now and profit us in the better country that He has set apart for us.   11 For all training seems grievous and difficult rather than fun. But if we make our training an exercise in orientation, it will eventually reward us with the fruit of peace.  12 That being the case, restore to action the hands that have given up out of exhaustion and set straight the knees that are wobbling from effort.   13 Stop wasting your energy in bad training that causes exhaustion and wobbling. Get going in the right direction so that you can heal your ability to work and to run.  14 Pursue peace with everyone and work toward achieving a life set apart in orientation

5  karisfellowships.com   KF36-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  and truth. No one will be able to see the Lord in you if you do not achieve that kind of life.  15 Keep a watch on yourselves and see that no one dawdles behind in their karis relationship with God. Make sure that no one allows a root of bitterness to sprout up where karis should be sprouting up; bitter roots cause trouble and defile many.  16 Watch over yourselves and see that no sexually untrustworthy persons dwell among you — people who allow themselves to be trodden on by cravings and defilement. Esau was a person like that. He exchanged his precious firstborn rights for simple food, just because he could not endure a little discomfort.   17 You know how that turned out. Even afterwards, when Esau wished to inherit favor and the blessing, he was rejected as a candidate because he had shown himself unworthy to be a son. As an untrustworthy person, he had refused the karis training. He could not undo the damage he had done even though he sought to do so with tears, because tears are not a substitute for trustworthy action.  Take a deep breath.  This passage is rich in ideas, and you might explore some of them for yourself.   Here’s what Nancy would  like you to remember.  1.   We all have a race to run  Each of us has a different race to run — a contest or challenge that stretches out before us — but the goal is always the same: to develop the character of Jesus in our lives.  2.   We endure tough things because we have a goal  We are in training for our mission and for our joy — and to bring God joy. Our lives are becoming a holy place in a very unholy world. At times,   God’s   training might feel severe, but that is only our perception and not the reality, for we know that the burden Jesus lays upon us is easy, and His yoke is light. 4   One of the benefits of training is the discovery of how weak we actually are; we discover how much our misorientation is interfering with our efforts to run with endurance.  3.   We can choose to strengthen our own souls for the contest  Don’t dawdle   at the starting post out of laziness or the fear of suffering,   and don’t   give up at the first discouraging hurdle. The race set before you is the opportunity that you need to build up your soul. Every hurdle has the potential to increase your joy. Productive suffering turning to joy is one of the cycles of life. 5  Our prayer might go something like this:  Heavenly Parent, teach me to courageously run my own contest with endurance. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.
