Notice what is happening inside your skin as you consider giving God this permission.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to present itself, and welcome that experience into your awareness. You might notice any struggle or tension when you   consider   giving God permission to train you for your contest .  (Pause)   Welcome whatever information that tension brings.   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission to explore, without judgment, whatever you are experiencing.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider   giving God permission to train you for your contest . How does your body respond?   (Pause)   You might notice what fatigue, terror, or even anticipation feels like in your body. You might feel nothing at all. Gently maintain awareness of  your body’s sensations , and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider the possibility of giving God permission to train you for your contest.   Do you feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or numb? Just observe.   (Pause)   Could there be fear or resistance — or, perhaps, joy?  (Pause)   What do you believe when you consider giving God this permission? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Do you fear the loss of some aspect of your   Idol’s search for glory?   Does your need for training hurt your pride?   (Pause)   Observe your experience as just information, and breathe.   (Pause for 30   seconds )  Heal  As you breathe, repeat to yourself the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore the challenge set before you.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit of truth, who finds joy in training you.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 6  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As You train me for my contest, I let go of my longing for power and control.  •   As You train me for my contest, I let go of my longing for esteem and affection.  •   As You train me for my contest, I let go of my longing for security and comfort.  •   As You train me for my contest, I let go of my longing for perfection.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF36-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for drawing us together as we present ourselves to You for training. Hold us in the power of this orientation and continue to guide us to our glory and truth. Prepare the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our true design and mission, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  *If you have the MATH to support the NHG book study, please go to the NHG tab on the KF website and sign up on the NHG Facilitator Signup Spreadsheet. title: KF37 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF37-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF37 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in  me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of   eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  In this lesson we will begin learning the   Three-Part Breath.  Assume a stillness posture, lowering your chin a little as you lift the top of your head. While maintaining that upright posture, allow your shoulders to drop. Close your eyes and observe how your body moves as you breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The three parts of the body that we use in this mindfulness exercise are the abdomen, the lower rib cage, and the upper chest. As you inhale, expand first the abdomen, then the lower rib cage, and lastly expand the upper chest. Feel your shoulders expand at the top of the breath and then exhale. Practice this sequence for one minute, inhaling with the abdomen, then with the lower rib cage, and, finally, with the upper chest.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Now, as you exhale, try to reverse that pattern. Collapse the upper chest under the collar bone first, then the lower rib cage, and lastly the abdomen. Pull your abdomen toward your spine as you exhale, but do n’t  exhale completely. Stop just short of empty, before you feel the need to gasp for air. Inhale again and practice the three-part exhale. Repeat this pattern for one minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  And now, for one minute, practice combining the three-part inhale with the three-part exhale.   (Pause for 1 minute)  You might explore a solid, confident pause just before the top of the inhale and another pause just before the bottom of the exhale. Stop short of a full inhale or exhale. Notice when you feel compelled to take a breath or have any feeling of strain or anxiety. This exercise helps you explore how you breathe. It also trains you to live within your limitations rather than depleting all your resources or indulging in excess. You learn to stop short of either extreme. Practice for another minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  When you inhale, try to smooth out the transitions from the abdomen to the lower rib cage, and from the lower rib cage to the upper chest. When you exhale, practice smoothing out the transitions in the reverse

2  karisfellowships.com   KF37-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  order. You might imagine the breath flowing like a wave through your body. Continue to practice for one more minute.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Now return to relaxed and quiet breathing as you observe what is going on inside your skin.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take a deep breath. Open your eyes and re-engage with the meeting. You might practice the   Three-Part Breath   for a few minutes during your personal meditation time.  Our hymn for this confession was written by George Matheson, a brilliant seminary student who went blind while at university. Blindness ruined his career, and his fiancé abandoned him. His sister cared for him until her marriage, and while everyone was enjoying themselves at her wedding, he wrote this famous hymn,   O Love that Will Not Let Me Go .  O Love that will not let me go,  I rest my weary soul in Thee;  I give Thee back the life I owe,  That in Thine ocean depths  Its flow may richer, fuller be. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  The angels of God rejoice when we practice KF Confession 9: 2  We learn to withdraw from the Idol Self and begin investing in our True Self.  This lesson introduces the practice of   Flow Pages . Writing without evaluating what you write can help you discover what is really going on in your True Self. The purpose of   Flow Pages   is not to fill up a notebook but to record the stream of your consciousness, perhaps in the morning after sleeping when your True Self has enjoyed some freedom from the lash of the Idol.  Like authentic play, writing   Flow Pages   allows your True Self to express its reality. Courageous stream-of- consciousness writing gives you a chance to see what is going on inside your skin. Through writing, you can face what you have been suppressing out of fear and pride. You might discover what is interfering with your growth, or you might unveil some compulsive needs. You learn to just   believe it   and rejoice in the truth of what you learn about yourself. You may also get some clarity about what is causing your suffering or threatening your pride, and that clarity might lead you to do a worksheet, a tap, or a   T-A-T  intervention. 3  While you are writing, you will have lots of opportunity to practice non-judgment. You can even be playful with   Flow Pages . As you write, just watch and see what happens! Most of us are constantly censoring our thoughts and feelings and judging them to be bad or stupid. We avoid   wrong   thoughts and   wrong   feelings because we are afraid of self-hate, and we foster   right   thoughts and   right   feelings because they support

3  karisfellowships.com   KF37-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  our Idol’s   pride and legal systems. Perhaps you believe that writing is only valuable if it is clever, meets your standards of writing well, or expresses deep and original thoughts. You might judge that you should be able to write easily and passionately. You might unconsciously write to impress yourself or to please a teacher, a parent, or a pastor — or even to shock yourself or others. All of this judgment, pride, anxiety, and the desire to impress, control, and perform interferes with the authentic expression of who you are today.  Remember that your True Self is most likely underdeveloped and untrained. In the past, you have been unwilling to invest in your True Self because you have loathed its inability to live up to your imagined glory.  It’s   important to remember that unseen forces that war against the soul have encouraged you to suppress your True Self because they know how powerful that self is —it’s   through the True Self that you become a weapon of orientation in this world. 4  As you write, allow your True Self to speak out of its immaturity and underdevelopment, and be honest about what you feel and think today. No one will read your   Flow Pages   except you and God. Get used to looking at what is real about yourself through your writing. Take credit for what is positive, and compassionately accept what is not. Over the months, you may see your True Self develop and respond to training, just like a beloved child who, having started out as a little savage, can now cheerfully pour the tea — or even change the world. We cannot predict how you will cheerfully pour your unique blend of tea, but we all look forward to finding out! Your particular blend is the contribution of your design, and as you offer that design to your community and to the world, you will glorify your Creator and, also, yourself as His creature.  This week, buy a spiral notebook like the ones you used in school. You might write on the front page in large friendly letters: THIS IS NOT SCHOOL! You might also write a few sentences to remind yourself that the purpose of the notebook is to explore your True Self; it is for your eyes only. Clip a comfortable pen or pencil to your notebook and keep it in a private but easily accessible place. Schedule a regular time for writing. You might set a goal of filling up one to three pages, or you might set a timer and write for fifteen  to thirty minutes. It’s up to you.   Try to keep your pen moving and, without judging, record whatever comes to the surface in your stream of consciousness. Think of it as play. Happy explorations! When you next meet with the group, you might share some of your discoveries.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, will You play with me? (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  The text for this lesson is   Matthew 18:1 – 11 , which we will read in Nancy’s translation.  1 At that time the disciples came to Jesus and said,   “ Who then is greatest in the kingdom of the heavens? ”   2 And Jesus invited a little child to Himself and set the child before them  3 and said, “ What I say to you is real. Unless you turn around and become like children,

4  karisfellowships.com   KF37-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  you will not enter the kingdom of the heavens.   4 Anyone then who gives up their pride like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of the heavens.   5 And whoever, in My name, receives one like this child receives Me;   6 but for the person who trips and entraps one of these little ones who trusts Me, it would be better to have a heavy millstone hung around his or her neck and be drowned in the depth of the sea.   7 Woe to the world because it trips and entraps! What I mean is this: tripping and entrapments are inevitable, but there is further woe to that person through whom the tripping and entrapments come!   8 Consider this: If your hand or your foot trips and entraps you, cut it off and throw it from you. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be cast into the eternal fire.   9 If your eye trips and entraps you, pluck it out and throw it from you. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be cast into the fiery hell.   10 See that you do not disdain and undervalue one of these little ones, for I say to you that their angels in the heavens continually see the face of My Father, who is in the heavens.   11 For the Son of Man has come to rescue that which was lost. ”  Take a deep breath.  When Nancy was very neurotic and compulsive, she understood this passage to mean that in order to experience the life that God intended for her, she would have to practice great self-discipline and self- denial. She was taught to discount and even deny her real abilities and to abhor rather than explore her real assets. Developing real assets was considered dangerous to the soul, and self-loathing was seen as humble. Nancy had no idea that what she thought was humility and self-sacrifice was actually neurotic pride.  Caring for our little ones is, of course, vitally important. In this passage, however, Jesus is also talking about us. The   “ little one ”   is your True Self. Jesus is teaching us that in order to become great in His kingdom, we must give up our pride and judgments and turn back to our original design. Turning back to our original design means giving up the Idol Self that we have created with its legal systems, pride, and fear-driven choices. Turning away from our pride system is going to feel really uncomfortable; if we choose to resist our   Idol’s demands, it will try to drive us back into slavery by punishing us with feelings of guilt,  anxiety, and shame. When we slip out from   under the Idol’s control, we will often find ourselves acting in  ways that are immature and messy because we need training — and that can feel humiliating, too.   God’s  intention is for children to develop the potential of their original design with the support of loving karis relationships, and as adults, we develop the potential of our original design with the help of the karis community.  It is a painful reality that in this life you will trip, make mistakes, and encounter traps. It is even more painful to realize that you often trip and entrap yourself. These traps sabotage your true development. The natural talents and abilities that you are proud of can also trip and entrap you, and it can be painful when you realize that you are using those skills to support your search for glory. Rather than condemning yourself for the misuse of your strengths, you can use your KF tools to unseat the Idol and learn how to employ those natural talents and trained abilities to fulfill your real potential and mission. With the help of your tools, you can let go of feeling entitled to familiar, convenient, and easy resolutions to your problems. You can let go of your slavery to the exalted and unrealistic goals that you impose on yourself and others. Instead, you can choose to become like a healthy, supported little child again. You can explore your design and potential with eager wonder and with a childlike desire and determination to become like the Father who created you.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF37-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Your little child got lost, but Jesus is seeking for you. Why not try seeking Him rather than running, hiding, and fighting the process of being found? What a marvelous reunion that would be!  Our prayer might go something like this:  Savior, come and find me, whatever it takes. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider letting go of pride and becoming like a little child .   (Repeat)   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider   letting go of pride and becoming like a little child again , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself. You can learn to recognize and honor them without allowing them to master you.   (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Gently hold your experience in your awareness. Observe whatever tension you may be feeling as you  consider letting go of your pride and becoming like a little child .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing as you   consider letting go of your pride and becoming like a little child .   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   Try putting your fingertips on your cheeks. Do the tips of your fingers feel hot or cold? Just observe.   (Pause)   Gently maintain your awareness of whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider the possibility   of   letting go of pride like a little child .   Is your experience right now pleasant, unpleasant, or vague? Just observe.   (Pause)   What do you believe about becoming like a little child? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something?   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Consider becoming like a little child again, but with the power and experience of an adult. Can you welcome the little child of your True Self?   (Pause)   Can you welcome the little child of someone else? Imagine welcoming a child who makes mistakes, who is also alive with wonder and joy, who needs comfort and care, and who needs to be protected and trained. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)

6  karisfellowships.com   KF37-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Heal  As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore becoming a healthy, liberated little child.  •   Welcome the gentle Holy Spirit of truth, who in turn welcomes you with truth and tenderness.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 5  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I choose to become like a little child, I let go of the craving to make things go my way.  •   As I choose to become like a little child, I let go of the craving for attention and admiration.  •   As I choose to become like a little child, I let go of the craving to make myself safe and comfortable.  •   As I choose to become like a little child, I let go of the craving to understand and have it all figured out.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for drawing us together to heal. Teach us childlike wonder as You continue to guide us to our glory and our truth. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with You. Help us invest in our true design by shedding old patterns of idolatry, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  1   O Love that Will not Let Me Go   by George Matheson (1842 – 1906),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=sxcnEBn1nA0 ,  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cejtIUBokdo&list=RDcejtIUBokdo&start_radio=1 .  2   Luke 15:10.  3   en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas_Acupressure_Technique .  4   Rom. 6:13.  5   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html . title: KF38 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF38-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF38 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  Let’s look at our prayer again in Nancy’s   alternative translation:  “Examine me, O God, and reveal my motivations. Ru n experiments on me and expose my misoriented thinking. See if there is any hurtful or idolatrous way in me, and lead me in eternal ways .”   (Psalm 139:23 –  24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  In this lesson we will focus on practicing the   Three-Part Breath   while relaxing the perineum and the face muscles. I will read instructions during most of the exercise. By using our breath to engage the body, we practice pure   being — a state in which we no longer need words, thoughts, images, or feelings to calm our anxiety. We allow our minds to cleanse and completely rest.  The Three-Part Breath  Assume a meditation posture and settle into your breathing. Observe how your body moves while it breathes.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The three parts of the body that we use in this meditation are the abdomen, the lower ribs, and the upper chest. As you inhale, first allow the abdomen to expand, then expand the lower ribs all the way round to your back, and lastly expand the upper chest under the collar bone. Take in a consistent amount of air until you are filled to just below capacity. Stop and pause for two seconds, and then exhale. Practice inhaling in this way for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now when you exhale, first collapse the upper chest under the collarbone, then the lower rib cage, and lastly the abdomen. Keep your neck and face relaxed. It might help to maintain a little Mona Lisa smile throughout the exercise. Open the space between your eyebrows by relaxing the muscles on the sides of your face. Release any tension between the eyebrows or in the jaw.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  During your exhale, try to keep the lower rib cage and abdomen expanded while the upper chest relaxes. Then, allow your lower ribs to deflate just before collapsing the abdomen. As you gently pull your abdomen toward your spine on the exhale, keep your perineum relaxed. Do not use your perineum muscles to help squeeze air out; use only your abdomen at the end of the exhale.   (Pause)   Before you reach the end of your breath, stop exhaling and pause for two seconds, then slowly inhale again. Explore

2  karisfellowships.com   KF38-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  for one minute, stopping short of full or empty and pausing for two seconds at the end of each inhale and each exhale.   (Pause for 1 minute)  Notice how you feel during the pauses. What is happening inside your skin? Do you feel anxiety or frustration?   (Pause)   Is there an unwillingness to endure?   (Pause)   Do you need to adjust your breathing to honor your limitations? Just breathe and observe. You may wish to enjoy the pause as a cessation from all effort and a chance to dwell in the stillness of just being.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Take a deep breath and return to relaxed, quiet breathing. Observe what is going on inside your skin.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Open your eyes. Re-engage with your environment and the meeting.   (Pause)  The   Three-Part Breath   massages your internal organs, pumps your lymph system, and mobilizes your cranial bones. Notice how breathing this way also stretches your thoracic spine and rib cage. Under the guidance of your will, you can train yourself to consciously breathe using more of your lung capacity, which allows your body to circulate more oxygen. Practice this breathing method for a few minutes during your regular meditation. As you become more proficient, you might extend your practice.  Our hymn for this confession is   O Love That Will Not Let Me Go .  O Light that follows all my way,  I yield my flickering torch to Thee;  My heart restores its borrowed ray  That in Thy sunshine’s blaze  Its day may brighter, fairer be. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  God’s purposes gain ground through   KF Confession 9:  We learn to withdraw from the Idol Self and begin investing in our True Self.  In Karis Fellowships, we learn a variety of mindfulness and meditation practices and are introduced to tools that help us apply KF principles to our lives. The weekly teachings provide a Biblical basis for understanding the KF Confessions, KF concepts and culture. Our meetings connect us to the KF community and also provide an opportunity for healing. Healing is essential if we want to change our lives. Our choices and behaviors are often the result of hurt and damage, so if we want to live the glorious lives that God intends for us, we need to be healed.  For nearly nine months, you have been investing in your True Self by learning to use KF tools. You have been given a lot of information,   and your toolbox is probably spilling over with tools that you don’t use, don’t know how to use, or don’t work for you right now . We hope that by regularly writing   Flow Pages

3  karisfellowships.com   KF38-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  you will clarify for yourself what is working for you in Karis Fellowships and what is not working — and maybe even why. None of us can use all of the tools all of the time. Perhaps a tool will work for you next year that   isn’t working   for you this year, or perhaps a particular tool works for you in one situation but  doesn’t   meet your need in another. You may use some tools only occasionally, while other tools will become your default choice. When you use your tools to retrain and orient your soul, you invite the Creation to welcome you as   one of God’s creatures   and to support you in your efforts to fulfill your potential. Together, you find out what will work for you today.  The tools of meditation and prayer are essential for maintaining orientation and connection. Choose a meditation practice that works for you and practice it every day for a month or for a year. You can use different practices in different situations, or you can combine practices. Nancy uses the   Lectio   Divina  when a Bible passage strikes her in a meaningful way. She uses the   Maranatha   Meditation   when she needs to rest or focus, and if situations come up that shock or trouble her, she uses the   SALT   Process   or  the   3-Minute Breathing Space . When she experiences self-hate, the   Mercy   Meditation   is her first choice. Sometimes she uses the   FAITH Process   to explore and process an issue throughout the week. To feed her True Self from the Spirit of God, she uses breathing and mental stillness. Nancy keeps her meditation toolbox open. She can always find something there that meets her present need.  When Nancy is in a cycle of   Flow Pages , she carries her notebook with her.   Flow Pages   act like a mental drainage system. Through writing, you   get “stuff”   out of your mind and drain it onto the paper. Getting that stuff out helps stagnant energy start circulating again. You might find it tedious to use   Flow Pages   to explore what you really want, feel, and think. Writing takes effort and time; you have to slow down, and you may experience some self-hate. Your endurance in this process becomes a karis   gift to God.  How would you respond to someone who shoots questions, opinions, and demands at you all day long but never stops to listen, think, or even breathe? Rather than reducing prayer to the mindless and effortless comments that are often thrust at God throughout the day, you might make a conscious effort to record what you are really thinking. The process of writing trains you to focus, to endure, and to think about what you really want. Before making a decision,   it’s a great idea   to stop and pray, but you might also want to stop and write.  You can use your   Flow Pages   as a way of talking to God. You can ask God a question or tell Him what is on your heart. Then you can mindfully write down what you think He might like to say to you. That would tell  you a lot about who you think God is, wouldn’t it? You might also write down what you think someone you trust might say to you. This isn’t inspired Scriptur e.   It’s   just a way of accessing latent wisdom that you may not know you have.  This week, use your   Flow Pages   to ask. Do you remember the lesson on A-S-K or Ask, Seek, Knock? In KF, we also learn to think WAA! — Words, Attitude, Action. Use writing to speak your reality to God. Tell Him how you feel and what you think. Ask God to simplify and focus your life. Co-labor with Him by refusing to overcomplicate your life or get caught up in old habits. Start purging your mind, your body, your relationships, your activities, and your environment. Try to identify anything that is left over from the days of your Idol Self. Use   Flow Pages   to help you figure out what to let go.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, I am ready to clean out my life. (Repeat)

4  karisfellowships.com   KF38-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the Toolbox ?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  When people sign up for an immersion course, they immerse themselves in a language, a culture, and a way of life. Their primary goal is to become comfortable in a new way of living, as quickly as possible. In KF, we are immersing ourselves in the better country of karis. Like immigrants, we are learning a new vocabulary, a new culture, and a new way of life. Learning new ways to live always involves suffering, but it is productive suffering. When, however, we dawdle and resist our training, our suffering is lengthy and fatiguing. We find ourselves in chronic self-hate but without the skills to deal with it, and we are torn by conflicting intentions that create a double mind. Perhaps worst of all, we build neuropathways of habitual resistance to further change or growth. Our pride system calcifies, and we find ourselves opposed by God and at odds with our created design. The Creation cannot support us because we have stepped out of the flow.  This is Nancy ’s   translation of   Romans 6:1 – 11 , with a little paraphrase for clarity.  1 Are we to dawdle in misorientation, hoping to force God into giving us more karis gifts?  2 Absolutely not! How shall we, the same people who are dead to misorientation, find life in misorientation?   3 Don’t you   realize that anyone who has been immersed into Christ Jesus has been immersed into His death?   4 Therefore, we have been buried with Him through immersion into death so that we also might walk around with Him in newness of life, just as   through the splendid revelation of the Father’s ability , Christ was raised up from those that are dead.   5 Let me explain. If, like seeds in the ground, we have been planted together with Christ in the likeness of His death, it follows that like Him we will be raised in resurrection.   6 Knowing this, that our old identity was crucified with Him so that the Idol Self — the whole body of misorientation — might be rendered entirely idle and without influence, and that we, having been liberated by that death, might no longer be  forced to be the Idol’s slaves living misoriented lives.   7 Think of it this way. The one who has died has been set right — or freed from slavery to misorientation.   8 If we have died with Christ, we can confidently trust that we also will live with Him.   9 Christ, having been raised from those that are dead, never dies again. We now understand that death is no longer master over Him, so we need no longer be enslaved by the fear of death.   10 And not only this, the death that He died, He died once for misorientation, but the life that He lives, He lives continually for God.   11 In the same way, take into account that in the register of life you are entered as truly dead to misorientation and, in Christ Jesus, as continually alive to God.  Take a deep breath.  In Romans 6, Paul invalidates all of our excuses for not living in newness of life. If we continue to dawdle in misorientation, enslaved by our pride and the fear of death, it is our own fault if we suffer misoriented outcomes. And the scary thing is this: we can dawdle until we die. God will let us do that.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF38-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  But there is an exciting possibility here. If you are in Christ, no matter how young or old, tall or short, rich or poor, or good or bad you are in this material world, and no matter what your background may be, you have the amazing potential of His resurrection life —   and you are in the process of learning how His life can work through you.  Nancy’s translation of   Second Corinthians 5:17 goes like this:   “If anyone is in C hrist, that person is a new creation. All that has happened before has passed on, and — look! — everything   is new!”   (Repeat)  God invites you to experience the real glory of living in and exploring a whole new world of challenges and delights.   With training, you can patiently cooperate with the Creator’s desire to resurrect your True Self  into newness of life.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Creator and God, lead me into my resurrection. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider walking around in newness of life.   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider walking around in newness of life , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to rest in your awareness as you   consider walking around in newness of life . Observe whatever tension you may be feeling.   (Pause)   You might notice a compulsion to judge yourself, to push away or excuse thoughts or feelings, or to make up a virtue story. Give yourself permission now to explore without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider walking around in newness of life.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   You might notice what hope or lightness feels like in your body. You might feel pessimistic or ashamed. You might feel nothing at all. Gently maintain awareness of whatever your body is experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider the possibility   of   walking around in newness of life . Is your experience right now pleasant, unpleasant, or vague and slippery? Just observe.   (Pause)   What do you believe when you consider walking around in

6  karisfellowships.com   KF38-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  newness of life? What story do you want to tell about that?   (Pause)   Are you afraid of something — of yourself, of loss, or of others? Observe your experience as just information, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  For thousands of years, human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have considered   walking around in newness of life.   You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   You can step back and learn from what you experience.   (Pause)   Breathe with compassion for all who are facing the challenge of a new life. Help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration .  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   the   integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for drawing us together for healing. Hold us in the power of this new direction as You guide us to our glory and to newness of life. Lead us to the next step in letting go of our old ways of living as we cooperate with You to reorient toward Your design for our True Self and to declare the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  For the Christmas and New Year holidays, we will consolidate the regular Karis Fellowships meetings into two mega-meetings. This is a fun and interesting time when all the karis lifeboats link up and we hear voices from other groups. As always, every active KF member is welcome to attend.  *Registration for the spring NHG study is open. You and anyone whom you invite can register on the KF website or through the link on the invitation email sent out by KF admin.  (*Except when preparing for the Jubilee Year)  1   O Love that Will not Let Me Go   by George Matheson (1842 – 1906),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=sxcnEBn1nA0 ,  www.youtube.com/watch?v=cejtIUBokdo&list=RDcejtIUBokdo&start_radio=1 .

title: KF39 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF39-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF39 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23 -24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  In this lesson we will practice pacing the   Three-Part Breath   while relaxing the perineum and the face muscles. This technique strengthens our ability to focus our minds and manage our bodies. It may also generate a little stress, which gives us the opportunity to exercise courage and endurance. Spend a few minutes practicing this breathing method at the start of your own meditation time. Your goal is to maintain a connection between your mind and body while disconnecting from your stories and distractions. When you find your mind wandering, kindly say to yourself , “ Release thoughts ,” and   then gently reconnect to your breath.   Let’s s tart with relaxed, natural breathing. ( Pause for 30 seconds)  The upright meditation posture gives your body more room to expand. Sit up straight with the crown of your head reaching toward the heavens and your tailbone reaching toward the earth. Lower your chin a little as you lengthen the back of your neck. Breathe naturally while maintaining this posture.   (Pause)  Observe how your body moves and how your back expands as you breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Let’s   begin the   Three-Part Breath .   You   don’t   need to work hard at this. Try not to create tension in your body by forcing air either in or out.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Relax your throat and face. It might help to maintain a little Mona Lisa smile throughout the entire breath. Open the space between your eyebrows by allowing the muscles on both sides of your face to relax. Release any tension between your eyebrows and in your jaw.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  When exhaling, focus on the expanded lower ribs and abdomen while the upper chest relaxes. Then allow the lower ribs to deflate just before the abdomen begins collapsing. As you gently pull your abdomen toward your spine on the exhale, keep your perineum and pelvic area relaxed.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now we will try pacing the breath. During the inhale, I will count out six seconds to give you an approximate idea of the pace. At the top of the inhale, I will count to three while you pause or cease breathing. We will then exhale for a count of six, and at the bottom we will pause for a count of three before beginning the next inhale. You will want to stop exhaling before you run out of air so that you are not gasping for breath when you begin the inhale. If you find that you cannot follow the count, go ahead

2  karisfellowships.com   KF39-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  and grab a little air here and there. Are you ready?   Let’s practice.   Inhale 2-3-4-5-6, pause 2-3, exhale 2-3- 4-5-6, pause 2-3.   (Repeat two more times and use a timer or clock to count each second)  Now return to relaxed, quiet breathing as you observe what is going on inside your skin.   (Pause for 30 seconds)   How did you feel when you paused at the end of the breath?   (Pause)   Did you feel any anxiety? Was there an unwillingness to endure?   (Pause)   With practice, you might begin to enjoy the pause between breaths as a cessation from all effort and a chance to dwell in the stillness of just being.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Pause. Open your eyes and re-engage with your environment. Notice how breathing in this way massages your internal organs, flexes your thoracic structure, and cleanses your mind. The   Three-Part Breath  oxygenates your body and trains you to confidently direct your body, even when it is reacting to stress.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits,   ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about   this training ?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  We are exploring KF Confession 9:  We learn to withdraw from the Idol Self and begin investing in our True Self.  Last week we talked about using   Flow Pages   to ask God.   It’s   so important to ask God about everything.   In the past you have practiced the mindless habit of asking your Idol Self about everything.   (Repeat)   Just as a soldier ’s training develops the ability   to react automatically in surprising situations, your KF training develops your ability to automatically ask God. Asking God instantly takes your mind away from judgment and virtue stories and helps prevent choices based on compelling needs. Rather than habitually or compulsively reacting out of fear, self-hate, and pride, you can stop and ask God. When you have learned to ask God first, you are on your way to becoming His trustworthy friend.  You have been training hard, learning to automatically react in an oriented way to surprising situations, and you may have had some   success in resisting the Idol’s attempts to hijack your life. You   might be experiencing a newfound sense of freedom and power. This can feel euphoric, but   it’s   important to remember this: if the Idol cannot directly derail you, it will find subtle ways to distract you by creating the illusion that you can do more, get away with more, and, perhaps, even fulfill that illusive, idealized glory. When you are running strong, keep in mind that you are still a creature — a very powerful creature, but a creature all the same — living within a certain set of limitations.  While we are asking God to teach us about our real unavoidable limitations, we can also productively choose limitations by simplifying our lives. At first, streamlining our lives within those limitations can require a lot of effort. That extra work often discourages us, so we continue to dissipate our resources in cluttered living. Interior designers understand that simplicity is one of the keys to creating a beautiful space. This kind of simple beauty is harmonious and balanced. Like these interior designers, we can build harmony and balance into our lives by cultivating simplicity. As a result, our lives will be much easier —  and more fun. Ask God to show you what is cluttering your life and interfering with the harmony and balance of your True Self. When you get rid of things, activities, and relationships, you create space that

3  karisfellowships.com   KF39-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  draws into your life what is compatible with the person you are becoming. Live in the cycles of life. Trust the process, and let the ebb tide go out, taking with it everything that does not complement the new life that is growing within you. Then allow the tide to return, carrying with it gifts from God and from the Creation.  God is freer to work in you through a simple life. Try withdrawing from an activity or stepping back from relationships that no longer fit your goals. The time, attention, and energy that you give to unnecessary pursuits and unproductive relationships cannot be available for God, His purposes, and for the care of your True Self.   There are, of course, some relationships that you can’t let go, but you can let go of your  old patterns of handling those relationships. Try fasting from an activity for a week or a month, and then assess its value in your life. Whether you are a mother of small children or the leader of an enterprise, you will be more effective if you simplify.   Everyone’s resources are limited , and those resources are there to serve a purpose. You must make choices about which purposes you want them to serve.  Developing a KF routine of self-care requires effort. You have to be intentional about scheduling your  training, but don’t try to do everything all at once. Just   focus on practicing the KF tools that are working for you. You may find it helpful to schedule your KF work around other established routines. For example, you might meditate for five minutes in the parking lot before you go into work. As with any good investment, if you are diligent and committed, both to your training and to the KF community, you will eventually accrue great returns. In your   Flow Pages , explore simplicity. What might a simple life look like for you? What changes could you make? Ask God to teach you to live simply — trimmed for action, ready to respond to His guidance, and able , at a moment’s notice,   to joyfully step into the flow and let go.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Savior, u nload my soul’s freight that I might live a simple life   for You. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s tu rn again to Romans, chapter 6. In our last lesson, Nancy compared our KF training to an immersion course that is teaching us to live in the new country of karis. The Bible teaches us that the people who live in this new country are no longer afraid of death because their leader, Jesus, has already conquered death.  In the text for this lesson, Paul tells us that we were designed to serve. We cannot help but serve someone. If we abandon one master, we must find another. In our misorientation, we abandoned God and found another master in our Idol Self. We agreed to serve   this Idol’s   illusions and compulsive needs, and we constructed a way of living that perpetuates the arrogant belief that we can cast off all limitations, do exactly what we please, and still be entitled to excellent outcomes. If we observe our behavior, however, we find that no matter how many virtue stories we tell ourselves about our lives, we are not free. We are compelled by unrecognized inner forces that generate a roller-coaster ride of euphoria and self-hate. Paul is encouraging us to choose the slavery that we were designed for. We were designed to serve God.  This is Nancy’s   paraphrase of   Romans 6:12 – 18 .

4  karisfellowships.com   KF39-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  12 Therefore, refuse the rule of misorientation in your body — a rule that tyrannizes you into heeding   the Idol’s   compulsive need to save its life. Your body, as well as the Idol system, is going to die anyway, so there is no point in losing your true life to save it.  13 Furthermore, don’t allow your physical body to become a weapon in the service of  misorientation, assisting the Idol Self to generate more misorientation. Instead use your physical body as a weapon of orientation for God, assisting Him and His purposes as those who have gone beyond death and fear, and are fully alive.   14 In other words, misorientation shall not be your master. Let me explain. You are not living under a legal system, trying to please a misoriented despot. You are living in karis relationship with God and have access to all the privileges of that relationship.   15 So now what? Do we continue to choose misorientation because there is no law or despotic master to punish us? Absolutely not!   16 Perhaps you   haven’t   yet figured out that you will be a slave, whether assisting God or the Idol Self. You are the slave of the one that you listen to and obey. It is your choice either to obey misorientation, which produces death, or to obey God, which orients you and the Creation.   17 But thank God, you who used to be the slaves of misorientation heeded from your hearts the pattern of instruction that was entrusted to you.   18 You were willingly liberated from misorientation and enslaved to orientation.  Take a deep breath.  Paul is letting you know that your slavery is not optional, but your choice of master is. Successful service requires training. Your mission is before you: you are to be a weapon of orientation in this world. As Jesus  trains you, He will regularly invite you to sacrifice your Idol’s hope in the   Glory of Me!   When you start to make that sacrifice, you begin to discover the affirming benefits and ever-developing potential of serving Jesus in your True Self. This discovery does not come simply through learning about meditation techniques or reading the   Toolbox   and   Bible Teaching . You must willingly, humbly, and with effort practice His way of doing things and submit yourself to be trained like a slave.  This is our prayer of commitment:  O Captain, my Captain, make me a weapon of orientation in this world. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water, and you might prepare to take some notes. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider becoming a weapon of orientation in this world.   (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider becoming a weapon of orientation in this world , recognize any reaction you might feel.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF39-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Welcome whatever is happening inside your skin, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow yourself to experience all your thoughts and feelings, without judgment. You might be aware of some resistance or struggle, or you might notice a willingness to explore.   (Pause)   Welcome your experience and the information it brings to you. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing as you   consider becoming a weapon of orientation in this world . What sensations are there?   (Pause)   You might notice what resistance and shutting down or, perhaps, power and trust feel like in your body.   (Pause)   Gently focus your attention on your body as you   consider becoming a weapon of orientation in this world . Breathe . (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider becoming   a weapon of orientation . Are you comfortable about this possibility, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe.   (Pause)   Have you ever tried serving God in the past? What happened?  (Pause)   Observe your experience as just information. You might process your experience with a long exhaling breath or the Dragon Breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome. (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore a new possibility.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit of truth with an open and inquiring mind.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 1  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I become a weapon for God, I let go of being anxious about power and control.  •   As I become a weapon for God, I let go of being anxious about esteem and affection.  •   As I become a weapon for God, I let go of being anxious about what that might entail.  •   As I become a weapon for God, I let go of being anxious about things not going my way.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,

6  karisfellowships.com   KF39-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Thank You for drawing us together for healing and training. Hold us in the power of this new direction as You continue to guide us to our glory and our mission. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to develop our abilities as weapons of orientation, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  For the Christmas and New Year holidays, we will consolidate the regular Karis Fellowships meetings into two mega-meetings. Check the website calendar for dates and times. This is a fun and interesting time when all the karis lifeboats link up and we hear voices from other groups. As always, every active KF member is welcome to attend.  *The NHG book study begins soon. Help those you invite with the registration process and consider facilitating one of the sessions as a karis gift.  (*Except when preparing for the Jubilee Year)  1   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html .   Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.

title: KF40 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF40-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF40 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Our physical goal for the   Three-Part Breath   meditation is to inhale and exhale for an equal amount of time, pausing at the end of each inhale and each exhale. This breathing method trains your mind to control your   body’s re actions to fear and discomfort. It also gives you an opportunity to practice courage, endurance, and living in reality. During this training we will inhale for six counts of one second each, pause for three counts, exhale for six counts, and then pause again for three counts. If you find that you need extra air during this practice, go ahead and take a short inhale, and then return to the count. Continue to maintain a Mona Lisa smile and a relaxed perineum. When you find your mind wandering, gently say to yourself , “ Release thoughts ,” and then   mindfully return to your breath.  To practice the   Three-Part Breath , we inhale by first expanding the abdomen, then the lower ribs, and lastly the upper chest, stopping to pause just short of full capacity. On the exhale, first release the upper chest, then the lower ribs, and lastly the abdomen. Reserve a little air at the end of the exhale to bridge the pause before the next inhale. I will help you pace your breathing for the first minute and then allow you to continue on your own for two more minutes.   Are you ready? Let’s b egin.   Inhale 2-3-4-5-6, pause 2-3, exhale 2-3-4-5-6, pause 2-3.   (Repeat the count for 1 minute)   And now, practice on your own for two minutes.   (Pause for 2 minutes)  Now return to relaxed and quiet breathing as you observe what is going on inside your skin.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Open your eyes and re-engage with your environment and the meeting.   (Pause)   The   Three-Part Breath  massages your internal organs, expands your rib cage, and pumps your lymphatic system. By caring for your body, you teach it to trust you, and when your body can expect your care, it relaxes and begins to heal. As you practice the   Three-Part Breath , you strengthen the power of your will and train your physical body to obey you. Your mind and body can then   return to God’s natural order   of authority in which we,  as God’s creatures, cooperate   with the True Self.  Our hymn for this month is   O Love That Will Not Let Me Go .

2  karisfellowships.com   KF40-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  O Joy that seeks me through the pain,  I cannot close my heart to Thee;  I trace the rainbow through the rain,  And feel the promise is not vain  That morn shall tearless be. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  Let’s be   makrothumos 2   with ourselves as we work on KF Confession 9:  We learn to withdraw from the Idol Self and begin investing in our True Self.  You can learn to pause and ask before reacting to life’s events.   Last week, Nancy suggested using your  Flow Pages   to ask God about everything and, also, to explore a simpler life. Use your   Flow Pages   to list your questions and to tell God what you want. For years, Nancy has made lists of wants and questions to help her explore and define her True Self. Whenever she looks back over these lists, she is astonished at  God’s creative   ability to provide for her, often in unexpected ways, just because she asked.  When you simplify your life, you have more resources available for resisting   the Idol’s chronic   shoulds and claims. So, you might use your pages to explore what you do in a day and what might be motivating you. How much of what you do is driven by a should or a claim — by   your Idol’s law and its fears ? If you are a mastery type, your primary motivation is to win and to have everyone and everything under your control. If you are self-effacing, you are compelled to get caught up   in other people’s business ; you try to rescue them, merge with them, or play the victim. If you are resigned, you might feel driven to resist change or growth by engaging in unproductive and distracting activities. Whatever your neurotic development might be, you can explore this question:   What am I doing to achieve healthier outcomes in my own life and in the lives of others? (Repeat)   Hopefully, by now, no matter what your neurotic tendencies are, you can imagine a healthier outcome and take steps toward that goal.  Once you have asked God and identified the help that you need to simplify your life, you can begin adventuring. Adventuring is an exercise in humility and leads us to new levels of training and discovery, which change our self-perception and, consequently, our life experience. We start becoming something  new. Becoming something new involves change, and change always reveals limitations. Our Idol won’t  like that! It will react to your efforts to change and punish you with self-hate.  Change presents new challenges that will exercise both your humility and your courage. If you are committed to your pride system, doing new things and thinking new thoughts will be much more difficult for you. Pride hates to make mistakes or run into the limitations that adventure inevitably brings. That is why your Idol Self will be screaming at you when you start to break new ground. The good news is that God is eagerly waiting to extend to you His karis gifts when you courageously choose the humility of adventure.  If you force yourself and everyone around you to accommodate your comfort zone, you are simply

3  karisfellowships.com   KF40-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  avoiding the fear and self-hate that come with exploring new territory. You will not find your True Self by remaining in your cozy cage of predictable misery. Adventuring means taking on new challenges and using new skills that you have acquired through hard training. Adventuring might also mean revisiting something that you have struggled with in the past, perhaps an area of failure or fear. It might mean reaching toward a goal without tested skills but with real courage and growing self-confidence. It might mean doing the KF program! By extending beyond your comfort zone, you discover more of yourself and more of God, and as a result, your trust in   God’s ability   to care for you grows. This process of discovery builds the sustaining courage and self-confidence that you need to fulfill the potential of your created design.  Adventuring reveals your weaknesses, and knowing your weaknesses builds your self-confidence. When you know your weaknesses, you can learn to work around them and get help. In the gym or on the track,  you discover your body’s weaknesses through pressing toward the limits of your strength. This pr ocess of productive exhaustion strengthens your muscles. Your soul experiences a similar kind of exhaustion through adventuring. You get to explore your real and imagined weaknesses and can then make choices based o n that evidence. Your soul’s strength is matured through the process of managing and training  those weaknesses. Once you understand this, you and God can work together strategically to develop  your soul’s potential.   When you identify a weakness, get all the help you can to strengthen that weak area. Let me say that again. Get all the help you can to strengthen that area of weakness. Then, with the peace and security of a stronger soul, and with growing self-confidence, you can look forward to the next training opportunity, and cooperate with God, who is eager to prepare you for your next leap forward into real glory.  God opposes the proud, but He invites the humble into new depths of relationship with Himself. 3   Rather  than scrambling to achieve your Idol’s imagined abilities, why not humble yourself, live within your real abilities, and let God do the glorifying? Admit that you don’t know it all. Allow yourself to be trained and  taught. Get help. Adventure into new things and honor the struggle that is an unavoidable component of  growth. As the Idol’s illusions are exposed, you will feel self -hate, but remember that your struggle with self-hate is also a natural part of progress. Humble yourself and admit that you are a beginner, just a little child who is preparing to inherit the kingdom of the heavens.  Our prayer might go something like this:  God of new things, show me the next adventure. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  In KF 37, we looked in the Gospel of Matthew at a famous passage where Jesus tells us to cut off the ways of seeing, the choices of action, and the predilection for paths that lead to misoriented and chaotic outcomes. We learned that we must become like little children, free from prideful illusions and fiercely single-minded in our efforts to grow into the people we were created to be. Next, we turned to Romans 6 where Paul teaches us how to withdraw from the Idol and invest in our True Self. Here is a review of what we have already learned in that chapter:

4  karisfellowships.com   KF40-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1.   God will allow you to dawdle in misorientation until you die. The choice is always yours.  2.   You can choose to plunge into the ultimate immersion course and learn how to live in a new country with Jesus.   It’s   difficult, but very rewarding.  3.   Through the gift of Jesus, your Creator has already invited you to take up your true life and pursue a relationship with Him . It’s up to you to take the next step.  4.   The fear of death has been overcome by Jesus, who conquered death. You are free to adventure without fear when you are connected to Him.  5.   You were created to serve. You either serve God or your Idol Self. You cannot serve both. Whom will you serve?  6.   Your physical body is a weapon whether you use it for God or for your Idol Self. How you use your body is your choice.  7.   If you are a Christian, misorientation is no longer your master. You have been set free to offer your service to God as a karis gift.  Paul is trying to persuade you to turn away from serving the destructive nature of the Idol Self. He begins by invalidating your excuses for choosing to indulge the Idol Self and then reminds you that you build your character through your own choices. You can choose the path that leads to death, or you can choose the path that leads to a life of unimaginable peace, adventure, and blessing. God is for you — for the person He created you to be. He is not against His design. He really is promising to give you your t rue heart’s  desire. He is asking you to do the hard work of orientation for your own sake, for His sake, and for the sake of those you love. You can trust the process.  Let’s finish our study of this chapter   by reading Nancy ’s   paraphrase of   Romans 6:19 – 23 .  19 I speak as one human being to another because of the vulnerability of your Idol Self. You are used to standing beside the Idol, presenting your body as a slave to its muddy motivations and to the misorientation of compelling shoulds and claims, resulting in more misorientation. Now, in the same way, stand beside orientation as if you were its slave, with the result that you become an island of orientation, dedicated to God, surrounded by a sea of confusion.   20 Look at it this way. When you were slaves of misorientation, you were exempt from the work of orientation.   21 And now, ask yourself, “What fruit was born from that slavery, doing those things of which I am now ashamed?” And, indeed, you  should be ashamed because the outcome of those misoriented things is death.   22 But now you have been freed from misorientation and are enslaved to God, and this is your fruit: you become an island of orientation in the sea of confusion, having an eternal quality of life, set free from the anxieties of a time-bound world that is passing away.   23 What you earn as a slave to misorientation is death, but, as a slave to Christ Jesus our Lord, you  receive God’s karis gift of eternal life,   which invites you into deeper and deeper correspondence with Him.  Take a deep breath.  When we think of slavery, we often think of a system that forces people to use their own resources in the service of another with no benefit to themselves. We think of tyrants or masters who use threats, cruelty, and deprivation to motivate their slaves. In first century Rome, however, many slaves were considered part of the household. These slaves were motivated by reward, loyalty, and trust. Loyal slaves had a proprietary and often passionate interest in the ir master’s   honor because t he master’s   honor was theirs.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF40-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  As a slave of Jesus, we are safe and free to adventure, and if we remain connected to Jesus, we can adventure with courage and enjoy   His support. Paul’s goal is to help us relax and thrive in the household  of a new master. This new Master is training us to have the confidence and skills to take up the authority and responsibility of administering His kingdom, living lives that declare His excellence, reputation, and glory.  Whose slave will you be? Will you be enslaved to misorientation and produce fear and death, or enslaved to orientation and gain practical skills as well as honor, love, and the karis gift of eternal life? The choice is yours.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Jesus, my Master, I choose to be Your slave. Show me how. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider becoming the slave of Jesus. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  This may be a difficult focus for you. See if you can try it on for a few minutes during the integration.  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider becoming the slave of Jesus , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you may be experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  As you   consider becoming a slave of Jesus , lightly hold your experience in your awareness without judging it as either good or bad. You might notice a compulsion to resist, to withdraw, or to capitulate. Just observe.   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider becoming the slave of Jesus.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   You might say to yourself,   “ Oh, I recognize that feeling of relief , ”  or you might feel anxiety, irritation, or resistance in your body. You might feel nothing at all. As you consider becoming a slave of Jesus, gently focus your attention on whatever your body is experiencing. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus

6  karisfellowships.com   KF40-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider becoming His slave.   Is that prospect comfortable or uncomfortable, or have you shut down? Just observe.  (Pause)   Do you feel compelled to judge this slavery as good or evil, or a mixture of both? What do you imagine such a life might be like?   (Pause)   Could you be experiencing fear — the fear of loss or missing out, or perhaps the fear of yourself or others?   (Pause)   Observe your experience as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore your pride.  •   Welcome the Holy Spirit of truth and His willingness to support you.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 4  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I consider becoming a slave, I let go of the longing to have my own way.  •   As I consider becoming a slave, I let go of the longing to be admired and respected.  •   As I consider becoming a slave, I let go of the longing to be safe and comfortable.  •   As I consider becoming a slave, I let go of the longing to fulfill my dreams.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank you for drawing us together for training and healing. Sanctify us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our real glory and to the truth of who You created us to be. Lead us into the next adventure this week as we co-labor with You to heal and to fulfill our design and mission for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  *New students are now registering for the NHG book study, and KF members are invited to sign up to help with facilitating at   NHG Facilitator Info .  (*Except when preparing for the Jubilee Year)

7  karisfellowships.com   KF40-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  During the two-week period of Christmas and the New Year, the regular Karis Fellowships meetings will combine into one weekly mega-meeting. Check out the KF   Calendar   for the dates and times of these two  meetings.  1   O Love that Will not Let Me Go   by George Matheson (1842 – 1906),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=sxcnEBn1nA0 ,  www.youtube.com/watch?v=cejtIUBokdo&list=RDcejtIUBokdo&start_radio=1 .  2   See KF6.  3   James 4:6.  4   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html .
