title: KF41 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF41-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF41 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  This month we will learn   Alternate Nostril Breathing . If you want to know more about this technique, you can search the web for   alternate nostril breathing . Here are some of the benefits of this breathing method:  •   Enhances the connection between your mind and your body  •   Revitalizes a tired mind and relaxes you for sleep  •   Improves overall brain function  •   Balances your autonomic nervous system  •   Cleanses your energetic pathways  •   Reduces anxiety and helps you manage your emotions  Alternate Nostril Breathing  Let’s begin.   Assume a meditation posture and breathe naturally for thirty seconds.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now, using your right hand, press your thumb against your right nostril, closing it off as you inhale.   (Pause)  On the exhale, release your thumb and press your index or middle finger against your left nostril, closing it off.   (Pause)   Practice this simple pattern a few times. Explore how you feel when you close off a nostril.  If your sinuses are not clear, breath through your mouth.   (Pause for 20 seconds)  How did   it feel to close off a nostril? Let’s continue to   learn and explore the complete finger pattern. Use the hand and the finger that feel most comfortable for you. Press on one nostril with the thumb as you inhale.   (Pause)   Then release the thumb and press on the other nostril with the finger as you exhale.  (Pause)   Hold the finger in place while you inhale.   (Pause)   On the exhale, release the finger and press with the thumb.   (Pause)   Thumb press, inhale. Finger press, exhale. Hold finger, inhale. Thumb press, exhale. Hold thumb, inhale.   (Pause)   Simply switch nostrils on the exhale. Practice for two minutes at your own pace.   (Pause for 2 minutes, announcing when 1 minute has passed)  Pause. Notice how you feel.   (Pause)   Now return to the meeting.

2  karisfellowships.com   KF41-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  It’s   beneficial to begin your meditation time with a few minutes of   Alternate Nostril Breathing , but this breathing technique can also be used to calm your mind before sleep or to clear your mind for work and creativity. Always keep in mind that KF introduces a variety of tools and methods that you might try. Work with what works for you.  Our hymn is   O Love That Will Not Let Me Go .  O Cross that lifts up my head,  I dare not ask to fly from Thee.  I lay in dust life’s glory dead,  And from the ground there blossoms red  Life that shall endless be. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits,   ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?” )  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  This month we will begin to explore the amazing potential of KF Confession 10:  We honor our limitations and seek lives of gratitude.  Last week, we learned that our adventures help us discover and recover our True Self. Trying new things gives us opportunities to learn how to manage change, which is a natural component of life. Life is flowing on, and when we refuse to adventure, we dissipate this precious resource and squander its powerful flow only to defend the wasteland of our pride and maintain a miserable fortress of illusion. Locked up in that fortress, we cannot stretch our ability to manage the flow of life and, therefore, will feel intense anxiety whenever we perceive a threat, encounter real limitations, or are invited to change. Our anxious minds invent stories of   what if   and   if only . 2   We fear missing out and we fear getting stuck, but we create a fortress that will ensure both of those results!  Limitations threaten our pride system. Hurt pride then triggers our habitual patterns of self-hate, and self- hate lashes us into ways of believing and behaving that we later regret. The beliefs and behaviors that stem from our self- hate do not honor God or His purposes; they simply support the Idol’s survival.  Gratitude goes out the window, and we become disconnected from ourselves, from our community, and from God. Your Idol desperately wants you to stop growing, but with your KF tools, you can manage your self-hate and choose training that will liberate the potential of your True Self. Ask God. Work toward simplicity. Adventure into new territory, and then develop priorities.  When your life is simpler and you are less motivated by the frenzy of the   Idol’s compulsive needs, you  have more resources available for risking adventure. You can then set real priorities that keep your investment in your True Self on track and protect all that you have gained by your efforts. Priorities reveal what you actually value. For example, do you value making a generous impression on Christmas morning, or do you value freedom from debt? Would you spend money on a new wardrobe or an exciting vacation rather than invest in effective healthcare? Are your values in conflict with your limitations? Debt and poor health are limitations that restrict your possibilities. They are most often self-imposed and are a kind of

3  karisfellowships.com   KF41-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  slavery. You can’t go anywhere when your foot is nailed to the ground.   So, the question really is:   Will you restrict your future possibilities for   a little euphoria today, or will you choose to honor today’s limitations  so that you can   invest in tomorrow’s possibilities?   What are your choices telling you about your priorities?  Healthy priorities honor your limitations and become part of your default thinking; they simplify the process of making decisions. Be   makrothumos   with yourself as you work on KF Confession 10. You live in a society that encourages you to mindlessly run around dumping your resources. This affluent culture wants you to believe that you can do it all and deserve to do it all — right now.   It doesn’t want you to be  content with your design and what you are doing, or with what you have and where you are today. Could it be that our society is neurotic?   It’s a ju ngle out there, and you will have to develop priorities in order to confidently and firmly take care of your business.  When we are tempted to make choices based on “as soon as possible”, we can consider the KF version of  the acronym   ASAP — Ask, Simplify, Adventure, Prioritize. In our misorientation, we ignore our limitations and default to destructive patterns of thought and behavior; and in a frantic attempt to escape our anxiety, we compulsively try to make something happen as soon as possible. Now, we are learning to ask, simplify, adventure, and then develop our priorities.  In chapter 5 of   Neurosis and Human Growth , Dr. Horney writes:  The neurotic is a frustrated being — his drives, conflicts, and alienation from self all prevent him from realizing his potential. He feels frustrated because he claims unlimited ability to do it all . 3  When we are neurotic, it is very difficult to identify and defend priorities that will lead us to our oriented development and potential. Priorities are exactly like running a financial budget or counting calories. They are a means of living within the limitations of being a human creature. There is only so much money, ability, time, and health to go around, and you must decide how you will spend those resources. Through asking God, simplifying your life , and adventuring against the Idol’s impos ed and imaginary limitations, you discover your real limitations and can then develop your real priorities.  You are a growing, changing, and unique creature, so your priorities need to be clear, flexible, and tailor- made. Clear priorities will help you direct your life, and flexible priorities can be adjusted to changing circumstances. What do you really want? Your everyday decisions will reveal the answer. Train hard to establish healthy priorities so that you can fight easy when difficult decisions must be made. You are becoming confident about who you are and what God would have you do. Your true life is emerging, and you are finally willing to fight for it.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, show me Your priorities as You help me discover mine. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING

4  karisfellowships.com   KF41-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Let’s look at the end of   a well-known passage in chapter 6 of the Gospel of Matthew. Jesus has been talking to the crowd about serving two masters. He says that you just   can’t do it.   You will love one and hate the other. You cannot serve two masters. That is a limitation.  Who are the masters that Jesus is talking about in this passage? One is God, and the other is mammon. We think of mammon as wealth or money, but mammon is really more about an attitude. Mammon was thought to be the god of avarice or greed, so Jesus is teaching us that greed can rule over us like a god. Our compulsive needs create a kind of greed, and that greed drives us to steal from others in order to allay our anxiety and support our pride. Our unhealthy fear of imagined limitations and deprivation compels us to make up virtue stories about why it is acceptable to snatch and steal from others and avoid  circulating with them. Accomplished greed guarantees the Idol’s survival and temporarily pacifies our  basic anxiety. When greed is accomplished, our Idol can enjoy a moment of self-satisfied pride.  Jesus wants us to give up our greed. He reminds us of what in reality we need today: food, drink, and clothing. By identifying our real needs, Jesus invalidates our virtue stories — those stories that we tell ourselves and others to justify our greed. He exposes the egocentricity lurking behind our choice to fight for, defend, and snatch at things and activities that are not real needs and only serve to maintain our pride. When we simplify our lives and trust God for what we need, we learn to recognize the many gifts of support that are already ours. We learn to be grateful rather than greedy. When we are living in gratitude, everything becomes a gift. Gratitude is the opposite of greed.  In the passage for this lesson, Jesus helps us think through our fears about deprivation and loss in the context of our karis relationship with God. Here is Nancy ’s   paraphrase of   Matthew 6:31 – 34 .  31 Therefore, do not worry saying,   “ What will we eat? ”   or,   “ What will we drink? ” or ,   “ What will we put around our bodies? ”   32 Why would you think that way? The people of this world, who are not in relationship with their Creator, desperately pursue all of these things, but you are the children of God! Our Father of the heavens understands that you need every one of these things.   33 Your business is first of all to pursue like a hunter the kingdom of God and orient your life to His way of doing things. That pursuit alone will yield great benefits, and then God, as your Lord and ally, is able to provide all things for you.   34 Therefore, do not worry about how you will meet your needs for tomorrow. Think of it this way. There is no point in worrying about tomorrow when you only have the power to make oriented choices today. This is a limitation. Tomorrow has its own worries. Mindfully deal with the misorientation of each day as it comes.  Take a deep breath.  In this passage, Jesus is trying to persuade you to give up your greed. He shows you how to arrange your priorities so that you can get what your True Self really wants. As a Christian and a child of God, what is your first priority? Are you seeking   first   His kingdom and His righteous way of doing things? Get into the business of orienting to God as your Lord and become His trustworthy servant and friend. The same energy that you spend on worrying or blaming can be applied to your training in mindful orientation. Orientation is cooperating with your Creator and offering your True Self to Him as a weapon of righteousness. If you are committed to that process, you can trust Him to supply everything else. As you consider your priorities, you might ask the Lord,   “Will this priority help You do what You want to do, and will it help orient me?” (Repeat)

5  karisfellowships.com   KF41-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father of the heavens, I want to make Your kingdom real in my life. Show me how. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider establishing a priority for your life. (Repeat) (Pause)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider establishing a priority for your life , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable. You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Gently hold this consideration of a priority in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push it away, despise it, or dismiss it. Observe whatever tension you may be feeling.   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice how it reacts when you   consider establishing a priority for your life.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   You might say to yourself,   “ Oh, this is what hopelessness feels like in my body . ”   You might feel liberation or permission. You might feel nothing at all. Breathe as you gently observe how your body responds to this priority.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider establishing a priority for your life . What might Jesus say? Just observe.   (Pause)   What do you believe when you consider this priority? Why is this priority important to you?   (Pause)   Observe whatever you are experiencing as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have feelings about all kinds of experiences and priorities. For thousands of years, human beings have felt like you feel when they have considered an area of specific priority.   (Pause)   When a feeling signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than reacting and getting caught up in stories. Breathe, and with a long exhaling breath invite your body to approach the possibility of this priority.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.

6  karisfellowships.com   KF41-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for drawing us together for training and healing. Hold us in the power of new beginnings as You guide us to the truth about our needs. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we cooperate with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with You and Your kingdom, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  *Registration is open for the next NHG book study. Consider setting aside some time to return the gift of facilitating the discussion on one of the chapters.  (*Except when preparing for the Jubilee Year)  1   O Love that Will not Let Me Go   by George Matheson (1842 – 1906),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=sxcnEBn1nA0 ,  www.youtube.com/watch?v=cejtIUBokdo&list=RDcejtIUBokdo&start_radio=1 .  2   Prov. 22:13  3   Karen Horney,   Neurosis and Human Growth   (New York: Norton, 1991).

title: KF42 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF42-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF42 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Last week we started to learn the skill of   Alternate Nostril Breathing . This technique balances your autonomic nervous system, opens new   brain paths, and clears your mind for rest or creative effort. It also relaxes your body and calms your emotions. You can read about this technique on the web and discover more of its great benefits. In our KF training, we practice this breathing method to focus our minds and explore our feelings about limitations.  In our last lesson we practiced   Alternate Nostril Breathing   guided by detailed instructions. In this lesson, however, less instruction will be offered so that you have more time to practice.  Alternate Nostril Breathing  Assume a meditation posture and breathe naturally for thirty seconds, allowing your body to regulate your breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Now, using your right hand, press your thumb against your right nostril, closing it off as you inhale. For the exhale, release your thumb and press   your index or middle finger on your left nostril, exhaling through your right nostril. Inhale through your right nostril and then close it off, exhaling through your left nostril. Basically, you switch nostrils on the exhale. As you experiment with this technique, breathe naturally or use the   Three-Part Breath . We will practice for three minutes. Begin.   (Pause for 3 minutes, announcing each minute as it passes)  And pause. You might begin your meditation time with the   3-Minute Breathing Space   and then move to a few minutes of   Alternate Nostril Breathing .  Our hymn for KF Confession 10 is   O Worship the King . This hymn was written in 1833 by Sir Robert Grant, who served his country as a politician, CEO, lawyer, and governor.  O, worship the King all glorious above,  And gratefully sing His wonderful love!

2  karisfellowships.com   KF42-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Our Shield and Defender, the Ancient of Days,  Pavilioned in splendor and girded with praise. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  We begin to experience real liberty when we practice KF Confession 10:  We honor our limitations and seek lives of gratitude.  Here is a quote from   The Harvard Business Review :  If success is a catalyst for failure because   it leads to the ‘undisciplined pursuit of more’ , then one simple antidote is   the disciplined pursuit of less . Not just haphazardly saying no, but purposefully, deliberately, and strategically eliminating the nonessentials. Not just once a year as part of a planning meeting, but constantly reducing, focusing and simplifying. Not just getting rid of the obvious time wasters, but being willing to cut out really terrific opportunities as well. Few appear to have the courage to live this principle, which may be why it differentiates successful people and organizations from the very successful ones. 2   (Pause)  In our culture, we think of ASAP as an acronym for   ‘as soon as possible’ , implying an urgency that often overrides priorities and ignores the flow .   In the last few lessons, Nancy has encouraged you to think of ASAP in a new way:   Ask, Simplify, Adventure,   and   Prioritize.   Ask God for direction. Simplify your life like a soldier going into battle. Adventure into new territory that may threaten your   Idol’s taboos . Set priorities that honor your discoveries. As the   Harvard Business Review   says, reduce, focus, and simplify for success. Get rid of the obvious time wasters in your life but, also, cut out the really terrific opportunities that do not support your priorities.  Really terrific opportunities can be dangerous; they tempt us to ignore our real limitations and waste our hard-won MATH. We then find ourselves committed to things that require money we   don’t have, abilitie s we   haven’t   demonstrated, time   that’s   committed elsewhere, and a level of health that is not ours. We neglect our self-care, run on too little sleep, allow stress to build up, and drive ourselves back into slavery. If you find yourself regularly following this pattern, you might acknowledge the enslaving hold that your Idol has on you and then begin to tackle it with ASAP.  Realistic goals take into account the person you actually are and set priorities about what you will do with what you already have. Although you may be tempted to support your pride system with illusions of who you could   be or what you would do with what you don’t have,   your real business is to honor your limitations and rejoice in the truth of what you have to work with today. Use well what you already have. The truth of how capable you actually are is revealed in the evidence of how well you handle today.  Your resources are limited, and you will want to use them wisely. Wisdom includes recognizing the limitation of cycles and the natural ebb and flow of the tide. The wisdom of simplicity budgets and

3  karisfellowships.com   KF42-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  allocates resources for those days when the tide goes out. If you build margins between your limitations  and the normal, periodic drain of life’s events, you will be able to make effective use of these inevitable  low tides. Low tides are times to rest, restore, and establish a new working platform. In order to do that, you need to have stored resources.  You only have one life here. What will you do with it? It is your business to budget the real resources that are yours. All human creatures have to consider their resources of money, abilities, time, and health. You only have so much money, so much training, so much time, and so much physical, mental, and emotional energy, or strength. Whenever you are faced with a decision, from the smallest thought about what to eat or wear to the larger issues of retirement planning or raising a child, do the MATH .   M is for money. A is for abilities. T is for time. H is for health. Whenever you make plans for your life or hope to take on a new project or possibility, do the MATH.  In the next few weeks, we will learn to do the MATH and look at how limitations support gratitude and glorious living. This week, you might explore these questions in your   Flow Pages :   In what direction do I want my life to go?   Where is my money, ability, time, and health going today? Where am I in debt? What are my real limitations? What move toward my real glory would I like to make? What is my first priority?  Practice ASAP: Ask for help. Simplify your life. Adventure   and explore. Then,   once the truth about yourself and your situation is revealed, reshape your priorities.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, teach me to honor my real limitations and do the MATH. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  In the Gospel of Luke, chapter 14, Jesus teaches us about limitations. He wants us to remember that we are just creatures with limited resources. It is our job to make the most of those resources, and that takes planning. Our text for this lesson, which we   will read in   Nancy’s paraphrase,   is   Luke   14:25 – 33 . These verses speak about budgeting all of our limited resources.  25 Many people were going forward together with Jesus, and He turned to them and said,  26 “ If anyone comes to Me to be My student and does not hate their own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even their own idealized life, that person is not yet able to become My student.   27 Whoever refuses to take their own cross into their own hands and come after Me does not yet have what it takes to be My student. 28 Look   at it this way. Which of you, when you want to build a tower, does not first sit down and do the MATH to see if you have enough resources for its completion?   29 If you have laid a foundation but are unable to finish the tower because you did not do the MATH, everyone watching you will laugh at you,   30 saying, ‘That idiot began to build and  then did not have the resources   to fulfill his plan!’   31 Or, what king, when he sets out to meet another king in battle, will not first sit down and take counsel to determine whether he, with ten thousand men, has the MATH to encounter the one coming against him with

4  karisfellowships.com   KF42-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  twenty thousand men?   32 And if that king finds that he does not have the MATH, he prepares ahead for the possibilities and sends   his senior ambassadors to the stronger king to ask for terms of peace.   33 So then, if you will not say goodbye to what you depend upon, you are not yet ready to be My student. ”  Take a deep breath.  In this passage, Jesus is essentially talking about doing the MATH before seeking first the kingdom of God and His righteousness. 3   Are you willing to make God and His way of doing things your first priority? If you want to make Him your highest priority, then you have to set everything else and everyone   else at a lower priority. That is what He means when He tells you that if you want to become His disciple , you must hate your own idealized life, your old family systems, your prideful illusions, and whatever you imagine you have control over or claim to own. You must also hate your community when it interferes with or actively opposes your priority to follow Jesus. You can imagine the shock of this teaching in a culture that had very strong feelings about family and possessions . Jesus isn’t   being selfish or harsh when He tells us to hate everyone close to us. He is actually being kind by telling us the truth right from the beginning. Without a strong sense of priority, something or someone   will eventually turn you away   from the   path of orientation.  How and when you are distracted reveals the quality of your allegiance to God and your own trustworthiness. As your allegiance and trustworthiness grow, you will become more sensitive to the effects of misorientation. You will be able to quickly recognize when you have disconnected from God and have stepped out of the flow. That misoriented condition of strain and chaos will feel unnatural and destructive. You will begin to hate it. This is a healthy use of the emotion of hate.  Your Idol Self does not want to accept that you have real limitations . That’s   why this teaching is particularly distasteful and even painful for your Idol. Furthermore, the Idol Self hates the reality that as mortal creatures we spend most of our lives in simple maintenance — sleeping, eating and eliminating, caring for children, working, record keeping, commuting, and making repairs. Simple maintenance does not feel glorious, and the Idol craves feeling glorious.  Jesus encourages you to be wise and do the MATH before you explore any new possibility. He wants to support your success, so He reminds you that you are a creature with real limitations. Learn how to do your MATH.   Assess your real money, abilities, time, and health. Then, based on the real evidence of your limited resources, plan your days to give yourself the best chance to build an increasingly courageous, glorious life that reveals the character of your Creator — a life that cannot be built on the magic of your imagined strengths or idealized dreams. Say goodbye to your pride. Learn to assess your real limitations of money, abilities, time, and health. Then, in the light of that assessment, evaluate your projects. When faced with your real limitations, try gratitude. Those limitations can work for you. Present your puzzles to the Lord. Ask for direction. Simplify by humbly letting go of prideful illusions about yourself and your situation. Adventure into reality, and develop healthy priorities.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord, teach me to do the MATH   for my own life. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”)

5  karisfellowships.com   KF42-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider a limitation that seems restricting or unfair. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider a limitation that seems restricting or unfair , how do you feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.  (Pause)   If you are unaware of having any feelings right now, you can observe your experience with compassion. Breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to simply rest in your awareness. Observe   whatever tension you may be feeling as you   consider a limitation that seems restricting or unfair .   (Pause)   Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider a limitation that seems restricting or unfair.   What sensations are there? Allow your body to talk to you.   (Pause)   You might say to yourself,   “This is what discouragement feels like in my body” or “This is what frustration feels like.”   You might feel relief in your body, or you might feel nothing at all.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to observe those uncomfortable sensations, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  this   limitation that seems restricting or unfair . Are you comfortable or uncomfortable while you observe?  (Pause)   Do you feel compelled to judge this limitation as good or evil? What do you believe about it? What story do you want to tell?   (Pause)   Do you feel a similar restriction in other areas of your life?   (Pause)  Observe whatever you are experiencing as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath or the Dragon Breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to explore your limitations.  •   Welcome the wise Holy Spirit of truth, who is training you to live in reality.  •   Welcome where you are today and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what this limitation reveals.   (Pause for 10 seconds)

6  karisfellowships.com   KF42-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 4  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I am trained by this limitation, I let go of the compulsion to make things go my way.  •   As I am trained by this limitation, I let go of the compulsion to fulfill my family system.  •   As I am trained by this limitation, I let go of the compulsion to defend what is mine.  •   As I am trained by this limitation, I let go of the compulsion to get my dreams magically fulfilled.  (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration .  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank you for drawing us together for this time of training and healing. Guide us by the power of our real limitations into the glory of our unique design. This week, teach us about our MATH as we reorient our lives to flow more effectively in our karis relationships and to further our connection with our True Self and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath. title: KF43 Meeting
content:
karisfellowships.com   KF43-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  KF43 Meeting Version of Teachings  Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity.  “Search me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  I hope that you have taken a few minutes each day to practice   Alternate Nostril Breathing . You may discover that this technique relaxes your body and refreshes your mind. In our stressful world, we all need to learn how to calm our creaturely reactions of fight or flight. We all have work to do, and we want to enjoy the benefits of our work. Techniques that help us to both enjoy our work and work more productively make our lives satisfying and a lot more fun.  Let’s begin with a body scan to connect our minds to our   wise and marvelous bodies. Assume a meditation posture and breathe naturally for twenty seconds, allowing your body to regulate your breath.   (Pause for 20 seconds)  Now turn your attention to your feet and ankles. What sensations do you notice there?   (Pause 20 seconds)  Take a deep breath and move your attention to your calves and knees. Do you notice discomfort, pain, or perhaps twitching? Breathe and observe. Try to relax on the exhale.   (Pause of 20 seconds)  Now begin to observe your thighs and hips. What do you notice? On the exhale, release with the breath any tension or discomfort you find there.   (Pause 20 seconds)  Move your attention to your torso. Scan your abdomen, chest, and back. Observe, and then release with the breath any tension you might find.   (Pause 20 seconds)  Now scan your neck and shoulders, arms and hands. Breathe, adjust, and release.   (Pause 20 seconds)  Observe your face. Breathe and relax any tightness or tension you find.   (Pause 20 seconds)  Begin   Alternate Nostril Breathing , switching nostrils on the exhale. You can breathe naturally, or you might use the   Three-Part Breath   or   the   3-Minute Breathing Space . 1   Practice for three minutes. I will give you one-minute markers.   (Pause for 3 minutes announcing each minute as it passes)

2  karisfellowships.com   KF43-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  And pause. It is beneficial to begin your meditation practice with a few minutes of   Alternate Nostril Breathing.   This breathing technique can also help to clear your mind for work and creativity and to calm your body for sleep.  Our hymn for KF Confession 10 is   O Worship the King.   This hymn praises God for the care that He provides for us through the flow of the Creation.  Thy bountiful care, what tongue can recite?  It breathes in the air, it shines in the light;  It streams from the hills, it descends to the plain,  And sweetly distills in the dew and the rain. 2  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  We are reminded in KF Confession 10 that in order to actualize our potential we have to honor our real limitations:  We honor our limitations and seek lives of gratitude.  WE,   W-E, is a nurturing support group for parents. 3   In   the group’s   1989 newsletter we read:  Becoming who we truly are capable of becoming in the fullest sense could be called the journey of life. Such an on-going, ever-expanding art eludes a tight description and perhaps can only be hinted at as the art of simultaneously being and becoming . . . The person who is adept at becoming will not always be described as happy but will often handle both the joy and the pain of life with acceptance and grace.  Quotes like these help us define the characteristics of the True Self — a fulfilled creature who is both being and becoming at the same time while gracefully accepting the joy and the pain of a real life.  Last week, Nancy introduced the tool of doing the MATH — M-A-T-H. Before beginning any new enterprise, we do the MATH and consider whether we have the Money, Abilities, Time, and Health to accomplish our goals. When we make decisions about our lives, we are setting priorities. Oriented priorities acknowledge that we have limited resources, and by doing the MATH we honor the limitations of those resources.  You cannot do it all, be it all, experience it all, and have it all, but the market economy wants to enslave you by making you believe that you can. Your fear of missing out becomes a primary motivation for playing  the Idol’s game of limitless possibilities. This game deceives you into believing that you can overlook or  push through real limitations — but your real limitations will always win in the end. The search for the   Glory of Me!   is a kind of premeditated disappointment that invites self-hate and leaves you feeling chronically discontented with your life.  In any area of the MATH, we can inherit debt from others or fall into debt by overextending ourselves. As

3  karisfellowships.com   KF43-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  a result, we find ourselves with fewer resources for doing what is really important. Perhaps you are in debt today — whether to your money, your abilities, your time, or your health. In the Proverbs we learn that the debtor is the le nder’s slave , and if you go into debt in any area of the MATH, you will find yourself enslaved. 4   As a slave, you are no longer the driving power in your life; you are forced to submit to the will of your taskmasters. Your unrealistic choices create debt, and with debt come self-generated limitations that you and others must then accommodate. You might actually choose to go into debt to avoid your real glory and the opportunity to explore your real potential. When we are in debt, we are like children entangled in a net that must be cut away before we can explore the fascinating house into which we were born.  The consequences of debt are perhaps best understood in the context of money. No matter how much money we have, we need to handle it as a limitation. Money is a finite resource, which, if used poorly, creates destructive limitations in other areas of the MATH. Budgeting programs can help us maintain our financial priorities. YNAB, an acronym for You Need A Budget, is an effective online budgeting tool for managing uncomplicated financial circumstances. 5   It costs a minimal amount, and there are trial options. The Dave Ramsey course, known as the Financial Peace University, has helped many people find financial freedom from the slavery of debt. You might also explore a free budgeting tool at   www.mint.com . Find  out what works for you. If your finances are complicated or your resources are extensive, you might employ a professional to ground you in the reality of what your money is for and to help you be faithful to your mission. Too much money can deceive you into ignoring other areas of the MATH, causing you to go into debt in those areas. For example, if you can afford to buy expensive products and health  treatments to support your lifestyle and yet continue to ignore your body’s needs, you will eventually find  yourself in debt to your health.  It’s in the Idol’s best interests to resist your efforts to keep track of money and learn how to use financial  resources wisely. Your Idol wants you to feel anxious about money and will encourage you to use money to support its shoulds and claims. The anxious emotions of need and greed pressure you to return to the  Idol’s culture of compulsive spending, snatching, and hoarding, all of which lead to stagnation and  misorientation. With a budget, however, your True Self will have the freedom to explore money within the limitations of reality. You can then learn to circulate your financial resources confidently by earning, spending, saving, and giving.  You will never wear a petite if you are tall, nor can you change your race or genetics; and if you are a man, you cannot become a woman. But within the real and fixed limitations of your design, you have a mission, and you can grow. As you grow, so do your possibilities, and you may find that some of the limitations that at one time you believed to be fixed are now stretching or have even disappeared. Choices that honor your MATH today will lead to more flexibility tomorrow. What may not be possible for you now may become possible in your future. Remember ASAP: ask God and others for help; simplify your life; adventure into opportunities that will stretch your limitations; set your priorities according to the money, abilities, time, and health that are actually yours today. Then make courageous, oriented, real choices that may require some endurance but will cultivate your potential in Christ. A more flexible tomorrow   won’t  materialize by magic, but it might seem like magic when God meets you and supports you in your oriented efforts.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Father, show me how to stretch my limitations. (Repeat)

4  karisfellowships.com   KF43-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING  Let’s look at a prayer from   Proverbs 30:7 – 9   in Nancy’s paraphrase, which blends together her translations  of the original Hebrew and Greek texts.  7 I have asked You, Lord, for two things. Do not withhold this favor before I die.   8 Keep useless idolatry and deceitful business at a safe distance from me. Grant neither deprivation nor excess. Feed me with the bite-size morsels that are my portion and appropriate for my current level of development, teaching me mature self-sufficiency.  9 For if You don’t do this , I might become filled with deceitful ideas and say to myself,   “ I am not accountable to anyone. ”   Or, I might become an impoverished outcast and steal from others, using Your authority deceptively.  Take a deep breath.  We see in this prayer two requests — and only two! That ’ s so simple! The first request is to be set apart into truth and remain connected to reality. The skill of recognizing real evidence and acting on proven principles protects us from deceiving ourselves and being deceived by others. Truth presents one of our great limitations. We cannot stretch the limitations of truth to fit our idealized judgments about how things should be. When we twist the truth or make up a story that supports our judgments and illusions, we are deceiving ourselves. Our misplaced loyalty to our beliefs about what life   should   be prevents us from recognizing what is real. We must then use our precious energy to hide the truth both from ourselves and from others. When reality can no longer be avoided, we must spend more resources cleaning up the mess that we ’ve   created because we ignored the limitations of truth in the first place.  Let’s assume that in an effort to survive you have become adept   at deceiving both yourself and others and are now, consciously or unconsciously, using that skill whenever your pride system is threatened. Your story about threat justifies your choice to deceive. If you want God to protect you from deception, whether in yourself or in others, you will have to learn to live in the truth. We need to develop the courage to deal in truth rather than take refuge in deception, which is one of the cheap habitual shortcuts that our Idol uses to calm our fear and restore our pride. Acting on real evidence and proven principles guides back into the path of orientation energies that we have formerly used for deception. KF training teaches you how to live in reality and gives you tools that help you cooperate with God as He works to keep you safe from deception and lies. If you want to give up the whole world of deceit   and experience God’s protection,  you must learn to live in the truth. That is a limitation.  The second request in this prayer concerns wealth — wealth in money, abilities, time, and health. You can ask God to teach you how to be content with what is offered to you in your present circumstances. Those circumstances are your portion, and they present real limitations that are specifically designed to help you cultivate your own development. Your ongoing training opportunity is to learn how to function productively within those real limitations. As you learn to manage your real limitations, you will forge the courage and authority that you need to access your true inheritance.

5  karisfellowships.com   KF43-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  Right now, let’s   pray and make these two requests to God:  My God and Creator, help me learn to live in the truth so that You can protect me from the fallout of deceit. Feed me with bits of experience that are appropriate for my level of development and teach me how to look after myself. I   don’t   want to extend beyond what I can handle and then wander into the deceptions of my Idol Self, believing that I can be independent from You. On the other hand, I   don’t   want to feel starved or deprived and then find myself in the grip of compulsive needs. I might then be tempted to claim Your authority and judge others as responsible for my suffering. I may even want to blame You!  Take a deep breath.  Compulsive needs are the consequence of the debt we owe to God and to our own soul. Perhaps we   don’t  know that we can actually redeem our debts through oriented living, or perhaps we may simply prefer the habitual shortcuts of snatching and impoverishing ourselves and others. As you learn to use your resources to pay off the debts to your MATH, you will discover that the rate of return is much greater than you can imagine.  We are asking God for a healthy balance between more than enough and more than we can handle. We want to honor our material existence and its real limitations. We do not want to be driven by imagined limitations that justify our compulsive needs and greed.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Guardian of my soul, keep deception far from me and feed me with the portion that is  appropriate for me today.   (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider an uncomfortable area of your life that is your portion today.  (Repeat)   (Pause for 30 seconds)  The   FAITH   Process  Feelings  As you c onsider an uncomfortable area of your life that is your portion today , how does it feel?   (Pause)  Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable.   (Pause)   Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Gently hold your experience in your awareness. You might notice a compulsion to push away or justify

6  karisfellowships.com   KF43-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  thoughts and feelings, or to make up a virtue story. Observe whatever tension you may be feeling as you  consider this uncomfortable area of your life.   (Pause)   Give yourself permission now to explore without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you   consider this uncomfortable area of your life that is your portion.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might recognize what unfairness or longing feels like in your body. You might recognize courage or curiosity.   (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to respectfully observe those uncomfortable sensations, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider this uncomfortable area of your life .   (Pause)   What do you believe when you   consider this uncomfortable area ? What judgments do you want to make?   (Pause)   Do you want to punish or blame yourself, others, or God? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  As you breathe, repeat the word   Welcome .   (Pause for 10 seconds)  (Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement)  •   Welcome this opportunity to safely explore something uncomfortable.  •   Welcome the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, who comforts you with truth.  •   Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made.  •   Welcome what you are learning about yourself.   (Pause for 10 seconds)  Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self. On the exhale, let go. 6  (Pause for 5 seconds after each statement)  •   As I explore my portion, I let go of the longing to force and control.  •   As I explore my portion, I let go of the longing for admiration and affection.  •   As I explore my portion, I let go of the longing for security and comfort.  •   As I explore my portion, I let go of the longing for my imagined outcomes.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration .  Pause. Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for drawing us together for training and healing. Hold us in the power of this new direction as You guide us within our real limitations. Help us do our MATH this week as we co-labor with You to

7  karisfellowships.com   KF43-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self and design, with our community and the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  *The NHG book study has begun. We hope that you will join us in the study to develop your own understanding. You might also participate in karis by returning a gift of facilitation to support the new students. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven.  2   O Worship the King   by Robert Grant (1779 – 1838),   www.youtube.com/watch?v=RAyKmYD2Zg8 .  3   WE is an organization founded by Jean Illsley Clark.  4   Prov. 22:7.  5   www.youneedabudget.com/ .  6   www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html . Examine me and know my thoughts. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity.” (Psalm 139:23– 24)  0:01   OPENING  0:02   PRESENTING  0:06   KARIS CIRCULATION  0:07   GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS  0:08   MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING  Let’s continue   our training in   Alternate Nostril Breathing.   By closing off one nostril we impose a limitation on ourselves that we can explore. Breathing is life support. What does closing off half of your life support feel like? This meditation does a lot of great things for our brains and bodies, but it also gives us an opportunity to explore a little controlled stress.  Let’s begin with a body scan to connect our minds to our marvelous bodies. Assume a meditation posture  and breathe naturally for twenty seconds, allowing your body to regulate your breath.   (Pause for 20 seconds)  Now turn your attention to your feet and ankles. What sensations do you notice there?   (Pause 20 seconds)  Take a deep breath and move your attention to your calves and knees. Do you notice any discomfort, pain, or perhaps twitching? Breathe and observe. Try to relax on the exhale.   (Pause of 20 seconds)  Now begin to observe your thighs and hips. What do you notice? On the exhale, release any tension or discomfort you find there.   (Pause 20 seconds)  Move your attention to your torso. Scan your abdomen, chest, and back. Observe, and then release with the breath any tension you find.   (Pause 20 seconds)  Now scan your neck and shoulders, arms and hands. Breathe, adjust, and release any tension.   (Pause 20 seconds)  Observe your face. Breathe and relax any tightness or tension.   (Pause 20 seconds)  Now we will move to   Alternate Nostril Breathing .  Begin to breathe using alternate nostrils. You can breathe naturally or combine this training with another meditation technique. You may wish to pause at the top and bottom of the breath. Practice for three

2  karisfellowships.com   KF44-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  minutes. I will give you one-minute markers.   (Pause for 3 minutes, announcing each minute as it passes)  Take a deep breath and pause. Notice how your body feels.   (Pause)   How does your mind feel?   (Pause)   In your own meditation time, you might try this method for five minutes, or for as long as you wish, and then explore the results.  Our hymn for KF Confession 10,   O Worship the King , describes our real condition. We are human creatures who are as frail as dust and learning to trust God.  Frail children of dust, and feeble as frail;  In Thee do we trust, nor find Thee to fail.  Thy mercies how tender, how firm to the end,  Our Maker, Defender, Redeemer, and Friend. 1  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”)  0:20   KARIS CONFESSION  0:21   TOOLBOX  KF Confession 10 reminds us of our design and our dependence on our real Creator:  We honor our limitations and seek lives of gratitude.  All of us are subject to the limitations of money, abilities, time, and health. That’s why we are learning to  do the MATH. Doing the MATH helps us set priorities about what we will do with our limited resources. Decision-making is so much easier when we have clearly defined priorities. Priorities allow us to communicate honestly and consistently. We become more certain about our preferences and are not so easily jerked around by our immediate circumstances. For example, a husband and wife went to a Broadway show. The show was well done, but at the intermission they found it easy to make the decision  to go home. Their priority was to feel rested for the next day’s work, and they weren’t willing to jeopardize  their limited health resources by forfeiting their sleep.  Just as we need to be realistic about our health, we need to be realistic about our abilities, which are also subject to limitations. Our mindfulness training equips us to observe our real abilities without making judgments or comparisons. Rather than pursuing what we imagine we could do or think we should do, we can look at what we are already doing and what we can learn today. If you cannot appreciate your real abilities and limitations, you will default to the illusions of your Idol Self — to what you think you could, or should, be or do; you will revert to your search for the idealized   Glory of Me!   If your pride will not allow you to do the MATH, you will make your own life and the lives of those around you unnecessarily burdensome and painful. Be patient with yourself as you explore and develop your real abilities. Humbly, and with an open mind, allow God to train you.  If we are misoriented and not mindful, we voluntarily participate in situations that we are not equipped to handle. Then, when we discover that we are not equal to the task and find ourselves drowning in chaotic emotions and consequences, we try to salvage our pride by imposing neurotic claims on life and on others. We are now in survival mode and on the defensive. Feelings and behavior become extreme,

3  karisfellowships.com   KF44-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  and we are reduced to scrambling around for stratagems that will allow us to maintain our illusions and avoid self-hate.  Mastery types believe that they can accomplish anything with enough willpower or information. When failure threatens, they blame God, others, or circumstances. They completely ignore the facts and imagine ability or success where none is evident. They might, for example, try to teach something when they themselves are not competent in that area. The disparity is apparent to those around them, but they are unable to see it for themselves. If mastery types judge a situation as hopeless, or if their ill-preparedness is exposed, they will assert that God or circumstances have been against them. In their imagined superiority they may claim that they are exempt from any need to prepare and then expect others to accommodate them. They cannot see that they simply are not equal to the challenge.  Self-effacing types ignore their real abilities and sign up for situations that showcase their weaknesses. They need experiences that reinforce their belief that they are losers and victims, so they will undermine their own real development and disregard or abhor their real strengths and potential. They feel compelled to accommodate others in order to elicit love or appreciation based solely on how nice or available they are. Their real abilities lie fallow because for them any self-development feels expansive and terrifying.  Resigned people underestimate their potential because exploring their opportunities would invite change and involve risk and effort. Their fear of personal imposition and loss of freedom compels them to avoid making a karis contribution to their community — a contribution that requires the integration of emotional health with developed ability. Since their emotions are locked up, so are their abilities, and they find themselves living far below the potential of their design.  When you are doing the MATH ,   look at your real abilities. What are you doing successfully right now? What are your antecedents and education? What is your natural design? When your MATH cannot support an undertaking, explore. You might ask yourself:   “ Is this where I belong? Do my design and antecedents support this undertaking? Am I driven by the fear of hurt pride or, perhaps, by compulsive needs? ”   Ask, Seek, and Knock. Get help. Enlist others to help you do the MATH. It is essential for your mission that you develop your real strengths and learn to use them. Your strengths will help you understand your role in the Creation.  Working out of your real abilities helps you flow through life. Think of how much more ability you have since you began KF training! When you grow your abilities, you need fewer resources to do your work. You then have more MATH available for circulating your real gifts and developing your real glory — and you will have more fun in the process.  Our prayer might go something like this:  My Father, help me explore my real strengths and learn how to develop them. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”)  0:30   SHARING  1:00   BIBLE TEACHING

4  karisfellowships.com   KF44-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  In the community of Christ, each one of us is equally necessary. Your abilities may be similar to those of others, but as you exercise your abilities through your own design, the purpose of God is accomplished through you in a unique way. Only you are designed to do what you do.  When we live in the Idol ’s   system, we are driven to achieve an imagined glory that we believe will satisfy our pride and fulfill the longing for the   Glory of Me!   We want what others seem to have, mostly because we do not value what we ourselves have. We may even judge our strengths to be loathsome or worthless because we hate the actual creature that we are — and, of course, we will actively avoid exploring, learning about, and training something that we already hate.  God, however, wants you to discover the glory of His creation. He wants you to reveal the person He created you to be, which is most particularly developed and displayed in the midst of your limitations. Remember that your productive struggle with limitations is very valuable. It is part of your portion, and you can expect your courageous struggle to fulfill its purpose, which is to make you mature, complete, and fully equipped for your mission. 2  In the following passage, Paul wants to help us understand how important it is for each one of us to use our abilities to fulfill our unique design within our particular portion. T his is Nancy’s paraphrase   of   First Corinthians 12:13 – 20 .  13 Let me explain how each one of us, no matter what our backgrounds or social status might be, is equally necessary in the Body of Christ. By one Spirit we all are immersed into one body, whether we are Jews, Greeks, slaves, or freeborn. We are given one Spirit to drink. 14 You can look at it this way: even your own body is not one part, but many parts, and God designed it that way.   15 If your foot should say,   “B ecause I am not the hand, I am not part of the body, ”   the foot does not cease to be part of the body because of that belief.   16 And if the ear were to say,   “ Because I am not the eye, I am not part of the body, ”  the eye does not, just by saying this, cease to be part of the body.   17 If the whole body were an eye, how could it hear? If all the parts of the body were trying to hear, how would the body be able to smell?   18 Just as God intended the different parts of our physical body to cooperate with and complement each other, so He has placed each individual person in the body of Christ to work together with other individuals, each performing their unique function.   19 If those individuals were all one member, where would the fully functioning body be?   20 There are many different backgrounds and social positions, but now that the Spirit has come, all who trust are of one body.  Take a deep breath.  Although Paul is teaching us a principle about the Body of Christ, we can apply the same principle to the entire human community. We are   God’s creature s, and just like all other creatures, we live in an ecosystem and have a part to play in helping the Creation flow efficiently. Those of us who are in Christ, however, have the greatest potential to influence the human community because we are invited to cooperate with God.  God influenced the powerful nation of Egypt through the cooperation of one man, Joseph. You can read this story in the book of Genesis. 3   Joseph was sold as a slave and yet became a ruler in the greatest empire of his time. Joseph had abilities, but as a young man he lacked the character and trustworthiness required to fulfill his mission. His difficult life circumstances could have made him bitter, but he trusted God, his

5  karisfellowships.com   KF44-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  great Coach, to use this suffering as an opportunity for training. At times Joseph must have felt discouraged and abandoned, but through his struggle within the limitations of slavery and prison, Joseph grew up; he became complete, mature, and lacked nothing. Then, when the opportunity came, he was able to confidently step forward with his proven and developed abilities. Joseph had potential in the human community based on his antecedents — his energetic matrix, his family background, and his education, etc. — but it was through the long years of struggle that God developed his character.  If we waste our energy wishing that we were someone we are not and doing something we are not designed to do, we will leave a gaping hole in the flow of Creation. Our necessary mission will not be fulfilled, and the revelation of God that we were designed to express will be lost. As a result, the whole human community will be crippled by our unwillingness to fulfill our design and our God-directed mission.  Doing the MATH helps us achieve balanced lives of increasing ability and stability. When we can flow out of our oriented, unique design, we can more confidently, and with less effort, maximize our MATH for our mission and for God. Our goal is to be like Jesus, not just through displaying His power and claiming His  authority, but by emulating His character and His commitment to doing things God’s way.  Our prayer might go something like this:  Lord Jesus, train my courage for the development of my real abilities. (Repeat)  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”)  1:10   INTEGRATION  Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe.  (Pause for 10 seconds)  Here is our integration focus:   Consider an area of proven ability that you might develop. (Repeat) (Pause for 30 seconds)  The FAITH Process  Feelings  As you   consider an area of proven ability that you might develop , how does it feel?   (Pause)   Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you. They can often be uncomfortable. You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you.   (Pause)  Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Awareness without judgment  Allow your experience to rest in your awareness without judging it. Just observe. You might notice how you react to this area of proven ability.   (Pause)   You might distrust this ability, or you might not value it. Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Inquiry: What is my body saying?  Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you c onsider an area of proven ability

6  karisfellowships.com   KF44-M   ©2021 Nancy Diven  that you might develop.   What sensations are there?   (Pause)   For example, you might recognize what fear of success or fear of hurt pride feels like. You might fear failure. You might even fear making an effort.  (Pause)   If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest. When you are ready, return to respectfully observe the uncomfortable sensations, and breathe.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Talk to Jesus  You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you   consider  this area of proven ability that you might develop . What other areas of your MATH might need your attention first?   (Pause)   What might you fear if you were to develop this area of proven ability? Is your story based on past experience or a family system? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  Heal  God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have   considered an area of proven ability that they might develop .   (Pause)   Think about the terrified disciples just after the crucifixion. 4   You are not alone in your feelings. You are a human creature.   (Pause)   When a fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting. With compassion for all of us who face this challenge, help your body process with a long exhaling breath.   (Pause for 30 seconds)  (Optional)   Continue to breathe while I test for further integration.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”)  1:28   ENDING PRAYER  Dear Father and Creator,  Thank You for drawing us together for training and healing. We want to develop our real abilities for Your purposes and for our own joy and fulfillment. Guide us to our glory and mission as You lead us to the next step in our healing. Help us co-labor with You to train for a more effective flow and a more powerful connection with our True Self and design, with the Creation and our community, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus. Amen.  Take a deep breath.  (If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”)  1:29   ANNOUNCEMENTS  *We are in the NHG season. Be sure to check in with any students that you have invited to the book study and ask how   it’s   going for them. If you wish to return the gift of facilitation, sign up to help with facilitating at   NHG Facilitator Info .
