title: KF45 Meeting
content: KF45 Meeting Version of Teachings Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity\. “Search me, O God, and know my heart\. Examine me and know my thoughts\. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity\.” \(Psalm 139:23–24\) __0:01 OPENING__ __0:02 PRESENTING__ __0:06 KARIS CIRCULATION__ __0:07 GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS__ __0:08 MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING__ I hope that you have taken a few minutes each day to practice __Alternate Nostril Breathing__\. This breathing technique can help relax your body and refresh your mind\. Not every technique works for everyone, so it is valuable to learn what works for you\. We all have business to accomplish, and we all want to enjoy our business as much as we can\. Mindfulness practices help us have a good time, more of the time, in the present time\. Let’s begin with a body scan to connect our minds to our marvelous bodies\. Assume a meditation posture and breathe naturally for twenty seconds, allowing your body to regulate your breath\. *\(Pause for 20 seconds\)* Now turn your attention to your feet and ankles\. What sensations do you notice there? *\(Pause 20 seconds\)* Take a deep breath and move your attention to your calves and knees\. Do you notice anything like discomfort, pain, or twitching? Breathe and observe\. Try to relax on the exhale\. *\(Pause of 20 seconds\) * Now begin to observe your thighs and hips\. What do you notice? As you exhale, release with the breath any tension or discomfort that you find\. *\(Pause 20 seconds\) * Move your attention to your torso\. Scan your abdomen, chest, and back\. Observe, and then with the breath release any tension\. *\(Pause 20 seconds\) * Move to your neck and shoulders\. Breathe, adjust, and release\. *\(Pause 20 seconds\)* Observe your face\. Breathe and relax any tightness or tension that you are holding there\. *\(Pause 20 seconds\)* Now we will move to__ Alternate Nostril Breathing__\. Begin to breathe using alternate nostrils\. You can breathe naturally, or you might use the __Three\-Part Breath__\. We will practice for four minutes, and I will give you a two\-minute marker\.* \(Pause for 4 minutes, announcing when two minutes have passed\)* Pause\. Breathe gently\. Notice how you feel\. *\(Pause\) *Now, open your eyes and re\-engage with the meeting\. Our hymn of gratitude is *Great Is Thy Faithfulness*\. This famous hymn was written by Thomas Obadiah Chisholm, who was born in a log cabin in Kentucky\. He served in Christian ministry until poor health presented to him other opportunities\. Great is Thy faithfulness, O God, my Father; Morning by morning new mercies I see\. All I have needed Thy hand has provided; Great is Thy faithfulness, Lord, unto me\.[\[1\]](#endnote-1) Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”\)* __0:20 KARIS CONFESSION__ __0:21 TOOLBOX __ We are exploring KF Confession 10: We honor our limitations and seek lives of gratitude\. Doing the MATH is exactly like doing a financial budget, but when we budget our MATH, we not only honor the limitations of money, but also the limitations of our abilities, time, and health\. We honor these limitations__ __so that we can determine our priorities and make choices before we find ourselves in situations that demand an immediate or difficult decision\. Our choices are then based on real evidence and not on the illusions generated by our pride system and our fears\. Honoring your limitations helps you communicate more authentically\. Your *yes* becomes a real *yes* based on real MATH, and your *no* becomes a real *no*\.[\[2\]](#endnote-2) People then get to know you for who you really are\. They come to understand your real limitations\. Some people can’t handle their own limitations, so they will not be able to handle yours\. Since they believe that they, themselves, should be above limitations, they demand that you should be too, especially if they crave your immediate and unlimited support\. This is particularly true in families and in organizations that depend on volunteers\. If you have been willing to explore your limitations and have accepted that those limitations are your business, you will be more confident when you let others know where your boundaries lie\. Breathe and connect with your priorities when others and your Idol are imposing their priorities on you\. In Western culture you will need help with budgeting your time\. Use timers and alarms on your phone, your computer, or your watch, and buy individual timers at the store\. When Nancy was parenting her young and very verbal son, she learned to set a timer to limit his chatter\. He was allowed to talk for fifteen minutes, and then Nancy allowed herself thirty minutes of quiet\. A timer gave her son the security of a boundary and an external authority that was not governed by his mother’s whims or imagination\. Both he and his mother agreed to be guided by this outside authority, and they both felt less anxiety\. Nancy’s son learned to relax because he could trust the timer to let them both know when he could talk again\. While he talked, Nancy was able to relax and be more respectfully engaged, knowing that her thirty minutes of quiet was not far away\. By budgeting time in this way, Nancy was honoring both her son’s and her own design and taking into account their current limitations\. When you know where your time is going, you can be more flexible, and you can confidently resist anything that might steal time\. Overbooking is the same as going into time\-debt\. When your schedule is booked too tightly, you have no wiggle room to allow for the reality that events are not always under your control\. You need to budget time for unplanned events, just as you need to save money for unplanned expenses\. Unplanned events are a reality, so add fifteen minutes or even several hours here and there to give yourself margins\. You need to get real about time\. If you are actively adventuring, you will encounter perils, and if you want to pass through those perils peacefully, you will need to have resources in reserve\. Every morning or evening, prepare your plans with prayer\. Budget time for the unexpected\. Ask God to do all that He can do, and ask Him to guide you to do all that you can do\. Planning your day before you begin the day gets the energy flowing in the direction of *your *business and *your* priorities\. Calendars, schedules, and alarms are all tools for planning and budgeting time\. You are a creature with limitations\. You need time to work, and you need time to rest and play\. Balance is what you are looking for, but life will not balance itself\. You have to make choices that will help maintain this balance\. Some seasons and cycles can make greater demands on, or even drain, one or more areas of your MATH, and you will then have to consider how to redistribute your resources in order to bring some stability back into your life\. Go joyfully into that training cycle because the current of the Creation will eventually reward you for your hard work\. Our lives flow in tides, just like the sea\. No sea creature fights the natural cycles of ebb and flow\. Sea creatures take advantage of the flow when it comes so that they can replenish their resources and prepare for the ebb, which will also come\. They circulate or restock according to the season, and flow with the cycles that come and go\. Through their orientation to the Creation, they naturally know how to trust the authority of the tide\. We are creatures, too, but our idolatry resists the natural circulation of the Creation\. We can, however, get back in harmony with the Creation by choosing to honor the real limitations of time and of flow\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Wise Creator, move me into the flow of the Creation\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”\)* __0:30 SHARING__ __1:00 BIBLE TEACHING__ In his letter to the Ephesians, Paul reminds us that Christians have always lived in misoriented cultures\. Today, our culture is busy brainwashing us with the illusion that we can live a life without limitations\. The market economy carefully fosters that illusion because it wants us to spend\. Our society promotes the careless use of resources and then judges the real consequences of that carelessness as unfair\. The Bible makes it clear, however, that no one gets away with anything\. Ignoring your limitations will damage you and your community\. As a Christian, you cannot afford to get caught up in cultural illusions\. Misorientation is all around you, so you must make it your business to defend and train the unique and precious creature that you are\. Let’s look at Nancy’s translation and paraphrase of __Ephesians 5:13–18__\. 13All reprovable things are revealed for what they are when they are exposed to the light\. Or we could put it this way—everything that is revealed becomes a guiding light\. 14For this reason it has been said, “Awake, sleeper\. Arise from the insensible dead and Christ will illuminate you\.” His light will reveal the truth about you, and that truth will guide you to become more like Him\. 15See that you walk around precisely, mindfully, and sharp\-sightedly, not as foolish people without wisdom\. Walk wisely\. 16Walking wisely will buy back the time wasted in time\-debt\. You must take control of your time because the times that we live in are very misoriented, and that environmental misorientation will seek to drive you into misorientation\. 17Since this is true, do not be mindless and egocentric\. Rather, cooperate with what the Lord desires—your orientation\. __18__Stop wasting your resources like a foolish drunk person\. This kind of wasteful mindlessness fractures the soul\. Instead, unify your soul by walking around mindfully and precisely, filled with the Spirit of God\. Take a deep breath\. In this passage, Paul gives us guidance that helps us manage all of our resources, especially the resource of time\. 1. __We must allow every area of our lives to be revealed for what it is__ How are you using your time? Is it possible that you are using your time to save your Idol’s life? 1. __Wake up\! Get real\! Engage\!__ Allow the light of Jesus to shine on your life\. Compare your life with His, and talk to Him about your training for today\. Ask Him what qualities He would like to develop in your life\. 1. __Walk around, but do it carefully and mindfully__ You must take control of how you use your time or else the market economy and your compelling needs will do it for you\. They will steal your time in order to impose their priorities on you\. You know the areas of your life that get hijacked by mindless living\. Plan ahead\. Snatch that time away from the jaws of the market and from your Idol’s mindless craving so that you can use your time for God’s purposes and for your own\. 1. __Cooperate with God__ Rather than fighting against the currents of your life, learn to go with God’s flow and stay connected to His guidance\. The flags of discouragement, frustration, and chronic self\-hate will let you know that you are fighting against the current or swimming against the tide\. On many occasions, Nancy has reluctantly chosen to let go of projects because of limited time\. She has then witnessed God and the community competently manage the necessary projects on their own\. Ask God and others for help, and do your best to create a balance of work and rest in your own life\. It is through engaging with your limitations that you learn to trust God’s ability to support you\. Our prayer might go something like this: *God and Creator, unite my heart to go peacefully with the flow\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”\)* __1:10 INTEGRATION__ Sip some purified water and assume a meditation posture\. Breathe and relax\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Here is our integration focus: *Consider the limitation of time in an area of your life\. \(Repeat\) \(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __The FAITH Process__ __Feelings__ As you *consider the limitation of time in an area of your life,* how does it feel? *\(Pause\) *Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you\. They can often be uncomfortable\. *\(Pause\)* Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Awareness without judgment __ Allow this experience to remain in your awareness as you *consider* *the limitation of time in this area*\. Observe whatever tension you may be feeling as you hold your experience up to the light\. *\(Pause\)*\. Give yourself permission now to explore without judgment, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Inquiry: What is my body saying?__ Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you *consider the limitation of time in this area of your life\. *What sensations are there? *\(Pause\) *Your body is always talking to you\. For example, you might recognize what denial or stress feels like in your body\. Breathe\.* \(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Talk to Jesus__ You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you *consider* *this limitation of time*\. Jesus might be asking if you feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or numb\. Just observe\. *\(Pause\)* Do you feel compelled to judge limitations of time as good or evil? *\(Pause\)* Do you feel entitled to use time in any way you like without adverse consequences? *\(Pause\)* Is this a regular pattern for you? *\(Pause\)* Observe your experience as just information\. You might process with a long exhaling breath or the Dragon Breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Heal__ As you breathe, repeat the word *Welcome*\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* *\(Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement\)* - Welcome this opportunity to explore an area of limited time\. - Welcome the Holy Spirit of truth, who loves the material creature that you are, living in time\. - Welcome your present reality, where you are today\. - Welcome what you are learning about yourself\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self\. On the exhale, let go\.[\[3\]](#endnote-3) *\(Pause for 5 seconds after each statement\)* - As I accept the limitations of time, I let go of the craving to get my own way\. - As I accept the limitations of time, I let go of the craving to gain approval\. - As I accept the limitations of time, I let go of the craving for security and comfort\. - As I accept the limitations of time, I let go of the craving for perfection\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * *\(Optional\) *Continue to breathe while I test for further integration\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”\)* __1:28 ENDING PRAYER__ Dear Father and Creator, Thank You for drawing us together for support and healing\. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as we learn to manage our time\. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co\-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to further our connection with our True Self and mission, with the Creation and our community, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus\. Amen\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”\)* __1:29 ANNOUNCEMENTS__ 1. *Great is Thy Faithfulness* by Thomas Chisholm \(1866–1960\), [www\.youtube\.com/watch?v=dTKIqmdfHSk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dTKIqmdfHSk)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-1) 2. Matt\. 5:37\. [↑](#endnote-ref-2) 3. [www\.camillecaldwell\.com/WelcomePrayer\.html](http://www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html)\. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven\. [↑](#endnote-ref-3)

title: KF46 Meeting
content: KF46 Meeting Version of Teachings Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity\. “Search me, O God, and know my heart\. Examine me and know my thoughts\. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity\.” \(Psalm 139:23–24\) __0:01 OPENING__ __0:02 PRESENTING__ __0:06 KARIS CIRCULATION__ __0:07 GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS__ __0:08 MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING__ KF Confession 11 presents one of our more difficult challenges as we heal: We take responsibility for any damage that we have done\. All of us have inherited debts of misorientation\. The Bible teaches that the misorientation of our ancestors and its effects have been passed on to us, and we have also been damaged by the misorientation of those around us\.[\[1\]](#endnote-1) We, too, have generated misorientation—we have damaged the material world, our communities, and our own lives\. Let’s stop pretending that this isn’t so and get on with the glorious work of redeeming our debts\. The spiritual discipline of meditation strengthens our ability to endure as we take responsibility for the damage we have caused\. __The Sunlight Meditation__ At this point in our training, we have been introduced to a variety of meditation techniques\. As we explore this next confession, we will be reviewing some of those techniques with this added emphasis: we will focus our minds on our foreheads and lift our eyes during the meditation\. Assume a meditation posture and gently close your eyes\. Allow your body to regulate your breathing as you begin __Alternate Nostril Breathing__\. *\(Pause for 2 minutes\)* Pause and relax\. *\(Pause\)* Now, with your eyes closed, imagine that you are sitting outside on a sunny day\. Gently raise your eyes toward the sun without lifting your chin\. You might feel a tiny stretch\. Imagine warmth and light shining down on your forehead\. Try to maintain that sensation throughout this meditation practice\. As you breathe, you can use the__ Maranatha__ __Meditation __to help you focus\. We will practice for three minutes\. Let’s begin\. *\(Pause for 3 minutes\)* Pause\. Take a deep breath and stretch\. Gently open your eyes and re\-engage with the meeting\. Our hymn of gratitude for this confession is *Great is Thy Faithfulness*\. Great is Thy faithfulness, O God my Father, There is no shadow of turning with Thee; Thou changest not, Thy compassions, they fail not\. As Thou hast been Thou forever wilt be\.[\[2\]](#endnote-2) Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”\)* __0:20 KARIS CONFESSION__ __0:21 TOOLBOX__ Here is KF Confession 11 once again: We take responsibility for any damage that we have done\. In this confession, Nancy has used the word *damage*, which can also be understood in terms of debt\. Restoring damage is like paying off a debt\. It often feels tedious and burdensome because we have to expend resources that could be used for pursuing our idealized glory and maintaining the illusion that we can live free from limitations\. We have all created debt through our own choices, and it hurts our pride to admit that life and God won’t magically cancel those debts for us\. Taking responsibility for our debts requires “a long obedience” to a guiding principle, and this obedience is not a wasted effort; we are trained through practicing a long obedience\.[\[3\]](#endnote-3) When we do the MATH, the final resource to consider is our health\. Each human being is a matrix of soul, mind, emotions, and material body\. If we neglect the limitations of that design, we will go into health debt\. Waking up to the consequences of this neglect has brought many of us to Karis Fellowships\. Nancy includes your health under KF Confession 11 because she believes that all of us have damaged our health in some way\. God is inviting you to come to Him with the reality of your health and the real limitations that it presents\. Without health—whether physical, mental, emotional, or spiritual—you cannot live a glorious life, but if you co\-labor with God as your Guide and Physician, you can seek and rescue that which was lost\. Your mind and soul have the capacity to comprehend the glory and love of God, and your body is the vehicle through which that glory and love are revealed\. You are the evidence of the unseen reality of your Creator, and for His sake you need to restore your health\. To do that you will need help\. Getting help requires spending other resources in the MATH\. For example, you need money to hire help, and you must allocate time to develop the abilities and habits to care for the health of your body, mind, and soul\. It’s never too late to improve your health\. People experience compromised health for a number of reasons\. We may, for example, have been born with poor health, or we may have been damaged by adverse circumstances\. That is all part of living in a messed\-up world\. However, we can improve compromised health for the glory of God\. In fact, health limitations may be the resistance you need to build the strong CORE muscles of a trustworthy character\.[\[4\]](#endnote-4) Perhaps, one day, God might step into the material world and heal you, but in the meantime, as you live within the limitations of the health that is yours today, you can show Him that you are trustworthy\. Take responsibility for your physical health and well\-being\. You might visit alternative practitioners who can help you heal naturally and avoid future health problems\. Illness often robs us of the money, ability, and time that we need to find and explore solutions, so explore your options before you are in a health crisis and running scared\. Then, when you or someone you love gets sick, which is a certainty in this world, you will know where to go for help\. The struggle to find your healing path strengthens your CORE—your courage, your orientation, your commitment to reality, and your endurance\. Before you find your path, you will have to expend some of your resources exploring your possibilities\. Losses in the process are natural\. They are part of your struggle and part of your training\. With oriented eyes, learn to see loss as a natural result of living within limitations\. Limitations narrow your playing\-field, focus your efforts, and train you in efficiency\. Value these limitations for their part in helping you learn to ask, simplify, adventure, and set priorities\. Spend time with people who are recovering their health\. Ask, seek, and knock\. Talk to those who are already involved in recovery\. Just as you would seek out a skilled doctor or plumber, you will need to look around for a skilled alternative practitioner or therapist\. Alternative healers can often be found through the referral network of health\-food stores, gyms, and yoga studios\. Search for them on the web, but be sure to examine their reputation and skill set before you decide to pay for their services\. You might ask KF members to recommend practitioners and therapies\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Jesus, open my eyes so that I might follow You on the path to optimal health\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”\)* __0:30 SHARING__ __1:00 BIBLE TEACHING__ In this lesson, we will learn from a woman who unsuccessfully pursued her healing for twelve years\. She spent her limited resources of money, ability, and time—in essence her life—going to doctors, but she could not find a cure\. Some of us know what she went through\. Nancy has spent over forty years pursuing her healing\. During that time, she has experienced miraculous healing, and she has also found substantial healing through conventional and alternative medicine\. Through enduring that long struggle, Nancy gained the self\-confidence that she has today\. She learned to appreciate her efforts and clarify her priorities\. She also learned where her character lacked a strong CORE\. Without those years of struggle, Karis Fellowships would not exist\. This is Nancy’s translation__ __of __Luke 8:43–48__\. 43And there was a woman in the crowd who had been hemorrhaging for twelve years\. She spent her life going to doctors and none of them were able to heal her\. 44She came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His robe\. Immediately, the bleeding stopped\. 45“Who touched me?” Jesus asked\. Everyone denied it, and Peter said, “Master, this whole crowd is pressing up against you\.” 46But Jesus told him, “Someone touched me, for I felt healing power go out from me\.” 47When the woman saw that her actions were not hidden, she began to tremble and fell to her knees before Jesus\. The whole crowd heard her declare that she was the one who had touched Him and that she had been immediately healed\. 48“Daughter,” He said to her, “your trust has made you whole\. Go forward in peace\.” Take a deep breath\. In this passage, we might notice how the sick woman took responsibility for her physical damage, or debt, and through that process found Jesus\. She was an unusual woman living outside the common roles of her society\. Like many members of Karis Fellowships, she was driven by desperate need to abandon the conventions of her culture and pursue the healing that only comes from a relationship with Jesus\. 1. __She had already put lots of effort into her healing__ Before Jesus healed her, the woman had already made her physical healing a priority, and that priority was factored into all of her life decisions\. 1. __She was very assertive about the importance of her health__ This suffering woman was no longer a passive recipient of the ministrations of doctors\. She believed that her health was her responsibility, and she did not let pride, conventions, social roles, or her fears stand in her way as she pursued health\. 1. __She had learned courage and endurance while making oriented choices in the real world__ Her ill\-health was a reality\. The long years of living with debilitating health had taught her courage, orientation, how to grapple with reality, and endurance\. When she saw her opportunity in Jesus, she used her CORE muscles to grab Him\. 1. __She had learned to be honest and speak her reality with self\-confidence__ It’s scary to touch the unseen and get instantly healed\. Another world opens up to you, like the ability to fly when you have unwittingly fallen out of the nest\. Through the long years of struggle, this woman had trained herself to act in the moment according to her beliefs, despite her fear\. She was able to honestly answer Jesus with humility and truth without worrying about what others might think or how they might judge\. 1. __Jesus said that her faith, or her action based on her trust, had saved her__ The woman’s choices in the material world were the evidence of what she believed in her heart\. This partnership of ideas and action made her whole\. The Greek word for *whole* is commonly translated as *saved*\. Wholeness comes when we live congruently as the children of God—when our choices reflect our oriented beliefs\. We are then unified and complete\. We are glorious\. 1. __Her choices made her healing happen__ Perhaps the most important lesson that we can learn from this story is that the woman’s will, and not the will of Jesus, makes her healing happen\. She is healed after her character has developed and her desires have become clear and focused\. Through her long struggle, she has acquired a taste for action, so when her opportunity comes, she is ready to act\. She reaches out to Jesus based on her trust in Him\. Jesus commends this congruence of belief and action, which brings her peace\. Her internal conflict is finally resolved\. She is saved, unified, and complete, and her physical health in the seen world now reflects the unseen reality of her soul\. Make your health a priority\. Restore your own spiritual, physical, mental, and emotional health so that you can journey forward in peace\. No one can do it for you\. You must take action and learn how to touch Jesus for yourself\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Jesus, help me train today so that one day I might touch You and become whole\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”\)* __1:10 INTEGRATION__ Sip some purified water and, if you wish, prepare to take some notes\. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Here is our integration focus: *Consider an area of health—whether spiritual, physical, mental, or emotional—that continues to invite restoration\. \(Repeat\) \(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __The FAITH Process__ __Feelings__ As you *consider an area of health—whether spiritual, physical, mental, or emotional—that continues to invite restoration*, how does it feel? *\(Pause\) *Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you\. They can often be uncomfortable\. *\(Pause\)* Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __Awareness without judgment __ Allow your experience to rest in your awareness as you *consider this area of limited health\.* You might notice a compulsion to make up a virtue story or to push away thoughts and feelings\. We often flush away thoughts and feelings before they have a chance to teach us\. Observe whatever tension you might be feeling, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Inquiry: What is my body saying?__ Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you *consider this area of health that continues to invite restoration\. *What sensations are there? *\(Pause\) *Your body is always talking to you\. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe\. For example, you might recognize what denial or hopelessness feels like in your body\. You might feel inspired\. Breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Talk to Jesus__ You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you *consider this area of health—whether spiritual, physical, mental, or emotional—that continues to invite restoration*\. Do you judge the need for restoration as good or evil? *\(Pause\)* What do you believe when you think about this area? What story do you want to tell? *\(Pause\)* Are you afraid of something? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Heal __ As you breathe, repeat the word *Welcome*\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* *\(Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement\) * - Welcome this opportunity to explore your health\. - Welcome the gentle Holy Spirit of truth as He seeks to heal and make you whole\. - Welcome the present reality of your health and the progress you have made\. - Welcome what you are learning about yourself\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self\. On the exhale, let go\.[\[5\]](#endnote-5) *\(Pause for 5 seconds after each statement\)* - As I begin to honor my health, I let go of the longing to have things go my way\. - As I begin to honor my health, I let go of the longing for self\-satisfaction and admiration\. - As I begin to honor my health, I let go of the longing for security and comfort\. - As I begin to honor my health, I let go of the longing for perfection\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* *\(Optional\) *Continue to breathe while I test for further integration\.* * Pause\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”\)* __1:28 ENDING PRAYER__ Dear Father and Creator, Thank You for drawing us together to learn and to heal\. Hold us in the power of new vision as You guide us to wholeness\. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we cooperate with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to further our connection with our mission, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus\. Amen\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”\)* __1:29 ANNOUNCEMENTS__ \*If you are the Karis Link to someone in the NHG study, be sure to check in with them and see how they are doing\. If they wish to join KF, help them understand that they must meet the requirements of attendance and completed homework\. You might attend one of the NHG lessons yourself to refresh your understanding of your own process\. You can check the website for the schedule and contact numbers\. *\(\*Except in the Jubilee Year\)* 1. Num\. 14:18\. [www\.adamsetser\.com/blog/2015/5/9/a\-long\-obedience\-in\-the\-same\-direction\-the\-meaning\-of\-life\-from\-friedrich\-nietzsche\-and\-king\-solomon](https://www.adamsetser.com/blog/2015/5/9/a-long-obedience-in-the-same-direction-the-meaning-of-life-from-friedrich-nietzsche-and-king-solomon)\.
