title: KF47 Meeting
content: KF47 Meeting Version of Teachings Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity\. “Search me, O God, and know my heart\. Examine me and know my thoughts\. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity\.” \(Psalm 139:23–24\) __0:01 OPENING__ __0:02 PRESENTING__ __0:06 KARIS CIRCULATION__ __0:07 GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS__ __0:08 MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING__ We are exploring KF Confession 11: We take responsibility for any damage that we have done\. KF Confession 11 is perhaps the most difficult confession to put into practice\. Nancy hopes that the meditation techniques that you are learning will strengthen you for this task\. All of us have inherited debts of misorientation, and we ourselves have generated debt\. We have damaged the material world, our communities, and our own lives\. We need to be reminded of these facts so that we can take responsibility for our present outcomes and get on with the glorious work of redeeming our debts\. In this lesson, we will be reviewing some of our KF meditations while lifting our eyes and imagining that the sun is shining on our face\. __The Sunlight Meditation__ Take a meditation posture\. Gently close your eyes and begin __Alternate Nostril Breathing\.__ Practice for one minute\. *\(Pause for 1 minute\)* Pause\. Keep your eyes closed and return to normal, relaxed breathing\. Through your KF training, you have learned that the events in your life are not the problem\. Misorientation is the problem, and misorientation is caused by your reactions to those events\. Now let’s return to the __Lectio Divina__ meditation using a passage from the Gospel of Mark\. Our text is a little longer than usual, and I will read it twice during the next minute\. Allow the meaning to soak into your soul\. Let’s begin\. *Do you not see that what goes into a person from the outside cannot defile that person?* *What defiles you is what comes out of you\.[\[1\]](#endnote-1)* *\(Pause for 1 minute, repeating the passage after 30 seconds\) * Hold this Scripture in your mind while you gently lift your eyes\. You might feel a tiny stretch\. Imagine what light and heat from the sun might feel like on your face\. For two minutes, try to maintain that sensation as you continue to meditate on our text\. *Do you not see that what goes into a person from the outside cannot defile that person?* *What defiles you is what comes out of you\.* *\(Pause for 2 minutes, repeating the passage after 1 minute\)* Pause\. Take a deep breath, and you might like to stretch your whole body\. Gently open your eyes and re\-engage with the meeting\. During the next thirty seconds, jot down anything you learned or felt during this meditation\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* Our hymn, *Great Is Thy Faithfulness, *describes the trustworthy flow of created cycles: Summer and winter, and springtime and harvest, Sun, moon and stars in their courses above, Join with all nature in manifold witness To Thy great faithfulness, mercy and love\.[\[2\]](#endnote-2) Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”\)* __0:20 KARIS CONFESSION__ __0:21 TOOLBOX __ Misorientation is revealed through the poor quality of our relationships\. When we live in misorientation, we first damage ourselves\. Others who are in relationship with us are then forced to accommodate that damage, which in turn damages them\. As a result, energy that could be used for the development of their True Self is hijacked into accommodating our misorientation\. One of the most important goals of Karis Fellowships is to help you rebuild the relationships in your community\. You can only do that if you are restoring and developing your True Self\. Think about your own relationship problems\. How often are your relationships damaged because of your insecurities, your pride and self\-hate, and your egocentric needs and greed? Taking responsibility for the damage that you have done begins with taking responsibility for your own orientation\. You cannot rebuild damaged relationships if you continue in your own misorientation\. So, at this point, you might still need to focus on training your True Self rather than looking for ways to rebuild a relationship\. Pia Mellody, a therapist and author who specializes in the treatment of codependency, suggests that we ask ourselves this question: *Would I talk to or treat a person that I am just getting to know in the way that I am treating this person who is close to me?[\[3\]](#endnote-3) \(Repeat\)* You might ask yourself, “Would I shout at, make demands on, or be rude and sulky with a person I have just met? Would I ignore them, shame them, or impose my opinions on them?” Most probably the answer is no\. When you ask yourself these questions, you show your willingness to humbly consider the possibility that you are abusing someone close to you\. You can invest in your relationships by developing habits of positive interaction, such as demonstrating good manners no matter how you feel, speaking words of appreciation and gratitude no matter how you feel, and offering small services no matter how you feel\. Here is another tool: when you have indulged in a misoriented interaction with another person, you might need to withdraw and reorient to your True Self and to God by doing a worksheet or intervention\. After you have examined the pride and fear that drove you to participate, you might return to the person involved and ask if they would be willing to consider with you how the interaction could have been more oriented and productive\. Another tool for building positive interaction is called SET—S\-E\-T—which stands for Support, Empathy, and Truth\.[\[4\]](#endnote-4) In all your communication with others, you can generate a more positive flow by showing support and empathy before sharing your truth\. Learning to do this is not easy without mindfulness training\. Using S\-E\-T might feel awkward and inefficient at first, but with practice you will be able to go through the steps quickly and with growing confidence\. The positive energy that you bring to the encounter is more effective than a perfect technique\. __S stands for Support__ Encourage the person by acknowledging their value in your eyes\. Sometimes people are just looking for the reassurance that you don’t hate them as much as they hate themselves\. You don’t always need to say something\. Sometimes support can be expressed by taking a few moments to simply listen while another person expresses their reality\. When you support others in their distress, you let them know that you value them and will try to understand, rather than judge, what they are experiencing\. __E stands for Empathy__ Just listening or making supportive noises is not enough to move a relationship forward\. That’s why all the steps of S\-E\-T are important\. If someone is distressed, you can show them that you are aware of their feelings\. You might try to restate what they have said, perhaps using their own vocabulary, to assure them that you are trying to understand\. If you are helping a small child, you might try drawing a picture to help them talk about their feelings\. Sometimes, people, and especially children, just need to hear words that describe what they are experiencing\. By offering these words, you let them know that they are not alone in their feelings\. __T stands for Truth__ When you have shown others support and empathy, they might be less defensive when you speak your truth moderately\. It is important to learn to stop blaming others and telling them who you think they are or what you think they are doing\. You now know that you are not qualified to judge what is going on in someone else, so the truth that you speak will be about you and not about them\. You need to let others know, in a moderate way, what is going on inside you, and if they are willing to listen, you may even be able to explain your choices\. Here is one formula you can try: *When you say \(or do\) \[\. \. \.\], I feel \[\. \. \.\] because I believe that \[\. \. \.\]*\. *\(Repeat\)* For your own statement, fill in the blanks\. Communicating your feelings in this way helps you take responsibility for your own reality and may help someone else understand you better\. If others can’t listen to you without having strong reactions, you might try writing them an email, following the steps of S\-E\-T: Support, Empathy, Truth\. An email provides a natural boundary that protects you from the recipient’s chaotic feelings and self\-defensive reactions\. Writing gives you a chance to state your reality clearly and gently, and it gives the other person as much time as they need to calm down and review your thoughts before they respond\. By sending an email, you at least give them the opportunity to consider the option of offering an honest and respectful response\. Before you send that email, you might invite someone you trust to read it and help you think through what you want to say\. Keep your email short and to the point\. Avoid any dramatic or judgmental language\. Now that you have tools to help you make choices out of your True Self, give your relationships a chance to heal\. When you were living in misorientation, you weren’t trustworthy in your relationships because you were not offering an authentic expression of yourself\. When you live out of your True Self, you are finally honest and fair\. You are on firm ground\. You become a person that others can trust\. By offering your reality, you adventure into real relationships that have within them the power to release potential and change lives\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Lord Jesus, help me heal damaged relationships by offering my True Self\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”\)* __0:30 SHARING__ __1:00 BIBLE TEACHING __ Last week, we learned about the woman with the hemorrhage who took responsibility for her health and made it a priority by directing her resources of money, abilities, and time toward solving her problem\. Through her long years of struggle, she developed active courage and endurance\. When the time was ripe, her mature courage, orientation, and endurance allowed her to seize her opportunity with Jesus\. Now we will look at __Ephesians 4:28–32__\. This is Nancy’s translation with a little paraphrase\. 28I say to the one who has been stealing—stop stealing\. Instead, labor to the point of fatigue for the practical good things so that you may have something to share with others who are in need\. 29Let no rotten and worthless reasoning proceed out of your mouth; rather, when there is a need, build up the community by saying the good that you know so that you give a karis gift to those who are listening\. 30And do not cause pain to the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were enclosed and sealed to be, one day, ransomed in full\. 31Let all bitterness of temper, passion, wrath, outcry, and railings against others be lifted off you, together with all damaging misorientation\. 32Become kind—doing useful things to benefit each other—full of compassion and karis invitations to others, even as God, through the gift of Christ, karissed you\. Take a deep breath\. When you were living in misorientation, you were stealing from your community and from God in order to support your Idol Self\. Now, your days of worthless reasoning that caused so much turmoil are over, and you are laboring, often to the point of fatigue, to develop your True Self so that you might serve your community according to your design\. Out of this growing potential, you will be able to offer kindness and practical help to others\. That offering is a karis gift to the community, and it shows God that you are trustworthy\. Ultimately your karis gift is to God, and your trustworthiness invites Him into more relationship with you\. In the __TAT__ intervention,[\[5\]](#endnote-5) you are guided to ask forgiveness for the damage that you have caused by your “rotten and worthless reasoning”\.[\[6\]](#endnote-6) Your disharmony has damaged God’s purposes, and it has harmed the community\. Self\-hate often expresses itself through bitterness, wrath, and blaming others\. These feelings and choices let you know that you are misoriented\. In spite of such feelings, you can engage your will and choose to be kind by doing useful and helpful things with compassionate understanding\. This is one way that we can lose the life of our Idol for Christ’s sake, and in losing it you offer to the community the karis* *gift of your True Self—the self that is cooperating with God\. Through you, God extends a karis invitation to your community\. When you give the gift of your True Self, you are demonstrating that you are a child of God; you are following the example of your heavenly Father, who gave the gift of His True Self to redeem this messed\-up world\. He put aside His very just wrath and offered us Jesus as a karis gift\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Father, I want to offer Your karis to others\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”\)* __1:10 INTEGRATION__ Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes\. Assume your meditation posture, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Here is our integration focus: *Consider a relationship in your life that has been damaged\. \(Repeat\) \(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __The FAITH Process__ __Feelings__ As you *consider a relationship in your life that has been damaged*, how does it feel? *\(Pause\) *You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you\. *\(Pause\)* Recognize with compassion whatever you may be experiencing, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __Awareness without judgment__ Allow your experience to rest in your awareness as you *consider this damaged relationship*\. You might notice a compulsion to justify your position or to push away oriented reasoning\. *\(Pause\) *Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are\. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Inquiry: What is my body saying?__ Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you *consider a relationship in your life that has been damaged\. *What sensations are there? *\(Pause\) *Your body is always talking to you\. For example, you might recognize what anger, shame, guilt, or hurt feels like in your body\. *\(Pause\)* If your sensations are uncomfortable, you can move your attention to an area of your body that is not reacting, and rest\. When you are ready, return to observe the uncomfortable sensations, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __Talk to Jesus__ You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you *consider this damaged relationship*\. Jesus might ask if you feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or numb? Just observe\. *\(Pause\)* Do you judge this damage as good or evil? *\(Pause\)* Have you often found yourself in a damaged relationship? *\(Pause\)* Are you experiencing hurt pride or fear? *\(Pause\)* Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Heal __ God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have felt just like you feel when they have damaged their relationships\. You are a human creature\. *\(Pause\)* Feelings are just chemical reactions in your body bringing you information\. With training, you can choose what you will do with that information\. *\(Pause\)* Rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting, you can breathe with compassion for everyone living with damaged relationships\. Help your body process through a long exhaling breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* *\(Optional\) *Continue to breathe while I check for further integration\. Pause\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”\)* __1:28 ENDING PRAYER__ Dear Father and Creator, Thank You for bringing us together for healing and training\. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to the truth about our relationships\. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co\-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to further our connection with our True Self and design, with our community, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus\. Amen\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”\)* __1:29 ANNOUNCEMENTS__ \*If you have invited someone to the NHG study, be sure to ask them how the study is going for them\. *\(\*Except in Jubilee Year\)* 1. Mark 7:18\. [↑](#endnote-ref-1) 2. *Great is Thy Faithfulness* by Thomas Chisholm \(1866–1960\), [www\.youtube\.com/watch?v=dTKIqmdfHSk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dTKIqmdfHSk)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-2) 3. [www\.google\.com/search?q=Facing\+Codependence](https://www.google.com/search?q=Facing+Codependence&stick=H4sIAAAAAAAAAONgFuLSz9U3MKnMy8pIVkKws7WkspOt9JPy87P1E0tLMvKLrEDsYoX8vJzKR4yh3AIvf9wTlvKZtObkNUY3LjyKhTS42FzzSjJLKoXkuPikkKzTYJDi4ULi8wAAtC2yyI4AAAA&npsic=0&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwjO4tqT6YfZAhVI4YMKHfLHDMQQ-BYINQ&tbs=kac:1,kac_so:1)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-3) 4. [www\.chrisakins\.com/communicating\-effectively\-in\-difficult\-situations/](http://www.chrisakins.com/communicating-effectively-in-difficult-situations/)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-4) 5. See KF25\. [↑](#endnote-ref-5) 6. Eph\. 4:29 in Nancy’s translation\. [↑](#endnote-ref-6)

title: KF48 Meeting
content: KF48 Meeting Version of Teachings Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity\. “Search me, O God, and know my heart\. Examine me and know my thoughts\. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity\.” \(Psalm 139:23–24\) __0:01 OPENING__ __0:02 PRESENTING__ __0:06 KARIS CIRCULATION__ __0:07 GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS__ __0:08 MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING__ We have the opportunity to rebuild our foundations with KF Confession 11: We take responsibility for any damage that we have done\. Training to be still and silent in body and mind lays the foundation that we need for growing into our potential\. We can apply this skill when we feel frustrated, compelled, or anxious, and when we or others make mistakes\. In KF we are learning to spend more time observing and less time talking\. This is one of the reasons that we adhere to time restraints in our sharing\. When we share moderately and efficiently, we exercise restraint and show respect for our listeners\. Meditation helps us learn to dwell without words\. In his vision, the Apostle John witnessed a worship ceremony in heaven that included thirty minutes of silence\.[\[1\]](#endnote-1) Silence during worship today would drive most Christians crazy\! As we learn to be silent, we no longer use words to suppress our anxiety or to keep God at a comfortable distance\. Silent minds let go of words, images, or sensations and come to the place of pure connection with God\. This might be the connection that Paul talks about in First Corinthians: “Now we see through a mirror of riddles, but then we will see face to face\.”[\[2\]](#endnote-2) When our minds learn to dwell without words, we come face to face with God\. In this lesson, we will revisit __Centering Prayer[\[3\]](#endnote-3)__ while practicing the __Sunlight Meditation__\. Take the meditation posture\. Lift the top of your head so that your neck is somewhat straightened\. Lower your chin a little and let your shoulders fall back\. Gently close your eyes and keep them closed throughout this meditation\. Allow your body to regulate your breathing as you begin one minute of __Alternate Nostril Breathing__\. *\(Pause for 1 minute\)* Now, let go of __Alternate Nostril Breathing__ and move to __Centering Prayer__\. Allow a centering word, which may be a phrase, a word, or an image, to float to the surface of your mind\. *\(Pause for 5 seconds\)* As you breathe, bring your word to mind, then let it go and rest in the stillness\. If your mind wanders, use the word and your breath to re\-collect yourself*\. \(Pause for 30 seconds\)* Now, gently lift your eyes toward the middle of your forehead and feel a slight stretch in your eye muscles\. You might find it helpful to imagine that you are looking at the inside of your forehead\. Breathe\. If you need to recall your mind, use your word*\. \(Pause for 30 seconds\)* Imagine that the sun or a lamp is shining into your eyes\. *\(Pause\)* Imagine what the light and heat would feel like on your forehead\. Breathe\. Practice dwelling silently in the light for two minutes\. Use your word to recall your mind\. *\(Pause for 2 minutes, announcing when one minute has passed\)* Pause\. Take a deep breath and stretch\. Gently open your eyes and re\-engage with the meeting\. Our hymn of gratitude and mercy is *Great is Thy Faithfulness*\. Pardon for sin and a peace that endureth, Thine own dear presence to cheer and to guide; Strength for today and bright hope for tomorrow, Blessings all mine, with ten thousand beside\![\[4\]](#endnote-4) Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”\) * __0:20 KARIS CONFESSION__ __0:21 TOOLBOX__ KF Confession 11 helps us learn new habits: We take responsibility for any damage that we have done\. Last week we explored SET—S\-E\-T—which stands for Support, Empathy, and Truth\. These three steps will help you communicate more effectively with others\.[\[5\]](#endnote-5) Each Idol type struggles with at least one area of SET__\.__ Mastery types resist supporting others\. Resigned types suppress any effort toward empathy\. Self\-effacing types wish to avoid telling the truth\. In your early KF training, you learned how to take responsibility for the damage you have done to yourself\. This damage can be physical, mental, emotional, or spiritual and is often the result of self\-hate\. In addition, you carry inherited debt, or damage, from others, and what you do with that debt is also your responsibility\. Now that you have begun your journey of discovery and have some tools to facilitate your own healing, you can take responsibility for dealing with the damage done to you by others\. Whatever that damage might be, you can thrive within your design and your present limitations\. You can learn from the woman with the hemorrhage, and you can also take Dr\. Horney’s advice, which is to get all the help you can\. Get all the help you can as you continue to train for your opportunity to touch Jesus\. Hopefully, by now, you have come to understand that all misorientation causes damage\. In misorientation you step out of harmony with God and the Creation, and by willfully using your unique power and authority to serve the Idol, you injure God’s design and obstruct His purposes\. You know this, and that is why you are working hard to free yourself from misorientation\. As you become more oriented, you will begin to see how your marvelous power can be used to help orient your community\. Even when you have not actively participated in damaging the community, you can be an agent of healing and change\. You can learn to take active responsibility for guiding others toward orientation by being careful and mindful about how you live your life\. The positive results in your community will encourage you to keep pursuing the path of your own orientation\. Who knows what might be possible? This vision of hope and influence widens your horizon as you boldly explore territory that you, and perhaps others, have never seen before\. Our example is Jesus, the progenitor of our faith\. He never did any damage to anyone and yet He continually worked to restore damage\. He paid for debts that were not His own\. Although He was not actively trying to restore everyone and everything all the time, the quality of His life gave everyone He met the opportunity to restore and be restored\. We are His ambassadors, and He calls each of us to participate in the same adventure\.[\[6\]](#endnote-6) Nancy used to think that she was called to restore everyone and everything all of the time\. It was a terrific burden, and she used that story as an excuse to avoid her own development\. She did not understand that her own restoration and development was her first priority\. You cannot restore the Creation without first restoring yourself\. Restoring yourself will take time and resources, and depending on how much damage has been done, you may find that in the first months, or even years, of KF training you will need to invest most of your resources in your own healing\. God wants everyone to have an abundant life, and by living a real life, you can co\-labor with Him to make His desire a reality in this material world\.[\[7\]](#endnote-7) Real lives reveal God’s goodness in all the ups and downs of life—when the tide comes in and when the tide goes out\. As you live your life fully engaged with reality, you can work with God to help others live abundantly\. Helping others is not meant to be a one\-way street; when you help the community to live abundantly, abundance circulates back to you\. There are as many ways to influence a community and circulate gifts as there are people\. You might clean houses, manage employees, or work as a volunteer\. You might be designed to lead a large community, perhaps as a politician or a pastor\. If you are a parent, you have the potential to exert far\-reaching influence by teaching your children to circulate within the family\. Circulating children become circulating adults who are complete, mature, and fully equipped to change the world\. If you are tearing down or stealing from others, you are participating in damage and harming yourself\. If, however, you are contributing to the MATH—the money, abilities, time, and health—of your community, you are helping your community to live abundantly, and by helping your community to live abundantly, you are helping yourself\. You might be working in a job that is dishonest, poisonous, or greed\-driven and drains the resources of the community, but you can fight the good fight to change that culture\. You become an agent of positive change not through judgment and hostility but by working hard to live a holy life and cheerfully refusing to participate in evil\. Now that you have worked hard on your orientation, you will want to protect it\. So, cheerfully refuse to participate in evil\.[\[8\]](#endnote-8) Our prayer might go something like this: *Captain of the hosts, I want to be ready for the mission of abundance\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”\) * __0:30 SHARING__ __1:00 BIBLE TEACHING__ In Romans chapter 12, Paul teaches us how to restore and support the Christian community\. He gives us further guidance in chapter 13, so you might like to read both chapters together\. Taking responsibility for damage that we have done is a great gift to those we have damaged and, also, to ourselves—and when we co\-labor with God to restore damage that we did not actively cause, we give an even greater gift\. This greater gift flows out of the growing wealth of Christ within us\. In Karis Fellowships, we are participating in each other’s healing and restoration, and through that effort we are helping God heal the world\. This is Nancy’s translation of the last verse of chapter 12\. *Do not allow yourselves to be conquered by injury; rather, conquer injury by living in active good\.[\[9\]](#endnote-9) \(Repeat\)* Now let’s put this verse in its context and see what Paul means when he tells us to conquer the power of injury with active good\. Here is Nancy’s translation of __Romans 12:17–21__\. __17__Never render harm in return for harm*\. *Consider in advance what would be a virtuous response in the eyes of all people\. 18If it is possible, be peaceable with everyone through accessing the resources of your own inner peace\. 19You who are blessed with God’s love, do not punish anyone, but leave a place for God’s wrath, for it is written: “Punishment is Mine”, says the Lord\. “I, Myself, will pay it back\.”[\[10\]](#endnote-10) 20Instead, “when someone who hates you is hungry, supply them with bits of something to eat; if thirsty, furnish them with drink\. For when you do this, you heap burning coals upon their head\.”[\[11\]](#endnote-11) 21Do not allow yourselves to be conquered by injury; rather, conquer injury by choosing active good\. Take a deep breath\. “Conquer injury by choosing active good\.” This sentence summarizes what Paul is saying in our passage\. Let’s look at four points that we can learn from his teaching\. 1. __Violated legal systems__ We can see in this passage, and also at the end of Romans 13, that our constant temptation is to react in a misoriented way to whatever we perceive as injury or harm\. When events or people violate our claims and hurt our pride, our perceptions become distorted, and we judge that violation and hurt as personal injury\. 1. __Circulate goodness__ As the people of God, even when we are damaged by another person’s choices and actions, we do not retaliate by returning evil for evil or harm for harm\. Paying back is simply a means of defending our pride system\. Paul is not telling us to be doormats, however; he is encouraging us to circulate active goodness for our own sake\. 1. __Consider in advance __ KF training prepares us to respond to every situation in an oriented way and helps us put into practice Paul’s injunction to consider in advance what would be a virtuous response\. Let’s get real\. Injury from others is a fact of life\. How will you choose to handle it? If you are living in active orientation, you will be able to recognize and then transcend the violations of your legal system and the injuries to your pride\. The resources that you have been wasting in pride protection can then be redirected toward the creative management of real assault from others\. 1. __Protect yourself__ Sometimes another person’s self\-hate is so extreme that you will need to protect yourself from that person\. Proverbs 22:3 and 27:12 teach us to foresee injury and take steps to protect ourselves\. Most people are addicted to anxious fears, rage, chaos, and drama, all of which cause injury, and the media encourages and exploits that addiction\. Wise people, however, have learned through experience how to seek peace and protect themselves in an oriented way\. They are able to consider in advance what might be a virtuous response in difficult situations\.[\[12\]](#endnote-12) Seek counsel and support\. Learn to prepare yourself with orientation and protect yourself with goodness before you find yourself conquered by injury\. Some years ago, Nancy realized that she could not maintain a peaceful life if she continued in a certain friendship\. For nearly a year, her friend had been mindlessly blaming others for the chaotic outcomes that she herself created\. When the friend finally dropped the relationship, Nancy was able to let her go, but she regretted that she had not confronted the problems in the friendship sooner\. Her self\-effacing neurosis had imposed taboos that blocked her ability to be honest and care for herself\. She compulsively showed her friend empathy and support but could not choose the active good of sticking to her own business, courageously defending her own boundaries, and moderately sharing her own reality\. This active good might have helped her friend avoid further injury to herself and others\. Instead, the friend was conquered by both imagined and real injuries and became the arsonist of her own wildfires\. Nancy spent months chasing her around with a bucket of water while she ran around with a torch\. Nancy’s misorientation in the service of her Idol undermined her ability to foresee the evil and protect herself\. When the Idol feels injured, its first response is to retaliate out of self\-hate\. Allowing yourself to be mastered by self\-hate will start fires, but you are learning to consider in advance how to protect yourself and respond to every injury, whether real or imagined, with orientation\. Do not allow injury to conquer and enslave you, forcing you to retaliate, manipulate, or retreat\. Rather, conquer the injury by choosing active good\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Prince of Peace, help me conquer injury with active good\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”\) * __1:10 INTEGRATION__ Sip some purified water, and prepare to take some notes\. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Here is our integration focus: *Consider an uncomfortable situation in your community\. \(Repeat\) \(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __The FAITH Process__ __Feelings__ As you *consider* *an uncomfortable situation in your community*, how does it feel? *\(Pause\) *Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you\. They can often be uncomfortable\. *\(Pause\) *Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __Awareness without judgment__ Allow your experience to rest in your awareness\. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them\. Accept with compassion that your pride might be hurt\. Just observe your experience as you *consider* *this uncomfortable situation*\. *\(Pause\) *Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are\. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Inquiry: What is my body saying?__ Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you *consider* *this uncomfortable situation in your community\. *What sensations are there? *\(Pause\) *Your body is always talking to you\. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe\. For example, you might recognize what obsession, frustration, or passive aggression feels like in your body\. Breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Talk to Jesus__ You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you *consider* *this uncomfortable situation in your community*\. Do you judge the situation as good or evil? *\(Pause\) *What do you believe? What story do you want to tell? *\(Pause\)* Are you afraid of something—perhaps of hurt pride or self\-hate? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Heal __ As you breathe, repeat the word *Welcome*\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* *\(Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement\) * - Welcome this opportunity to explore how you can be more trustworthy in your community\. - Welcome the gentle Holy Spirit of truth, who works toward peace\. - Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made\. - Welcome what your community is teaching you about yourself\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self\. On the exhale, let go\.[\[13\]](#endnote-13) *\(Pause for 5 seconds after each statement\)* - As I help heal my community, I let go of the longing for power and control\. - As I help heal my community, I let go of the longing for care and admiration\. - As I help heal my community, I let go of the longing for safety and survival\. - As I help heal my community, I let go of the longing for perfection\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* *\(Optional\) *Continue to breathe while I test for further integration\.* * Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”\) * __1:28 ENDING PRAYER__ Dear Father and Creator, Thank you for drawing us together for healing and training\. Hold us in the power of this new direction as You guide us toward our real glory and authority\. Set us free with the truth about our lives as You lead us to the next step in our healing\. Help us co\-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to become more trustworthy for our own sake, for the sake of the community, and for Your sake so that the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus may be seen in this world\. Amen\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”\) * __1:29 ANNOUNCEMENTS__ The next Karis Fellowships training cycle begins in March\. KF Admin requests that all current members register now on the website for the next KF cycle to make the registration tasks easier\. 1. Rev\. 8:1\. [↑](#endnote-ref-1) 2. 1 Cor\.13:12\. [↑](#endnote-ref-2) 3. [www\.centeringprayer\.com](http://www.centeringprayer.com/)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-3) 4. *Great is Thy Faithfulness* by Thomas Chisholm \(1866–1960\), [www\.youtube\.com/watch?v=dTKIqmdfHSk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dTKIqmdfHSk)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-4) 5. [www\.chrisakins\.com/communicating\-effectively\-in\-difficult\-situations/](http://www.chrisakins.com/communicating-effectively-in-difficult-situations/)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-5) 6. 2 Cor\. 5:20\. [↑](#endnote-ref-6) 7. Matt\. 6:10\. [↑](#endnote-ref-7) 8. Rom\. 12:21\. [↑](#endnote-ref-8) 9. Rom\. 12:21 in Nancy’s translation\. [↑](#endnote-ref-9) 10. Deut\. 32:35\. [↑](#endnote-ref-10) 11. Prov\. 25:21–22\. [↑](#endnote-ref-11) 12. Rom\. 12:17\. [↑](#endnote-ref-12) 13. [www\.camillecaldwell\.com/WelcomePrayer\.html](http://www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html)\. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven\. [↑](#endnote-ref-13)

title: KF49 Meeting
content: KF49 Meeting Version of Teachings Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity\. “Search me, O God, and know my heart\. Examine me and know my thoughts\. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity\.” \(Psalm 139:23–24\) __0:01 OPENING__ __0:02 PRESENTING__ __0:06 KARIS CIRCULATION__ __0:07 GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS__ __0:08 MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING__ We may now be ready to enter into stillness using the __Sunlight Meditation __without blending it with other meditation practices\. Assume a meditation posture\. Sit upright and straighten your neck by dropping your chin a little\. Gently close your eyes\. Begin with two minutes of __Alternate Nostril Breathing__\. *\(Pause for 2 minutes\)* Now, let go of __Alternate Nostril Breathing__\. Focus on your breath and your forehead\. If your mind wanders off into images or words, say to yourself, “Release thoughts,” and then draw your focus away from mental activity\.[\[1\]](#endnote-1) Return to stillness, and with your eyelids closed, gently turn your eyes upward as if you were looking at something close to your forehead\. Breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* When you are ready, imagine that the light of the sun or a lamp is shining onto your forehead and into your eyes\. If you wish to pace your breathing, inhale and exhale for the same amount of time\. For example, you might inhale for six counts and pause for three counts, and then exhale for six counts and pause for three counts\. When you are comfortable with the rhythm of your breathing, you can let go of counting\. If your mind wanders, say to yourself, “Release thoughts,” and then gently draw your attention back to the light\. Continue for two minutes while you rest in the stillness and gaze into the light\. *\(Pause for 2 minutes\)* Pause\. Take a deep breath and gently open your eyes\. Stretch and re\-engage with the meeting\. Our hymn for the final month of the KF training cycle is *Be Thou My Vision*\. This hymn was written in the 6th century by an Irish Christian poet, Dallan Forgail\. Be Thou my Vision, O Lord of my heart; Naught be all else to me, save that Thou art; Thou my best Thought, by day or by night, Waking or sleeping, Thy presence my Light\.[\[2\]](#endnote-2) Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”\) * __0:20 KARIS CONFESSION__ __0:21 TOOLBOX__ KF Confession 11 helps us build new foundations: We take responsibility for any damage that we have done\. 1. __We first make efforts to restore the damage that we have done__ We can now tell the Lord that we are ready to take responsibility for the damage that we have done to our minds, our bodies, and our spirits\. We begin with self\-care and the hard work of redirecting our own lives toward habitual orientation\. Once that process is in motion, we turn our attention to our relationships\. We examine our behavior and our choices by asking ourselves, “Would I treat a stranger the way I am treating this person?”* *Our answer to that question may help us determine whether we are abusing that person\. We can then begin the essential work of changing our behavior, which will in turn initiate the rewarding process of healing our relationships\. Once our close relationships have begun to move toward orientation, we can make efforts to restore damage in our wider community\. If we have stolen from our community, we can take steps to repair the damage by offering karis gifts\. 1. __We are invited to restore damage wherever we meet it__ All of us have been damaged by other people\. Now, we need to step out into the adventure of healing that damage\. We can either feel cheated, judge our situation as unfair and live in retaliation, or we can respond to God’s invitation to restore harmony by co\-laboring with Him to heal the damage that has been done to us\. If our community has been damaged by others, we may be ready to take up the mission to overcome the injury with active goodness\. We can do this in our jobs and through volunteer work, or simply by spreading goodwill wherever we go and in whatever situation we find ourselves\. We can learn to smile as a habit\. A smile is a gift\. 1. __We help to restore the damaged Creation__ The Creation encompasses everything from the cells in your body to the planets in the universe\. The Creation is you and everything around you\. God reveals His glory through the entire Creation, animate and inanimate\. If, however, we damage that glorious Creation by our egocentric choices and steal from the lives of future generations, how will those generations recognize His glory and experience His marvelous gifts and beautiful goodness? The truth is that each one of us is part of the ecosystem of the entire Creation, so if the Creation is not functioning well, all of us are damaged\. When we are misoriented, we live in an *ego\-*system of craving and selfishness rather than in an *eco\-*system of flow and cooperation\. By using our mindfulness training, we can observe how we treat the Creation, and just as we are beginning to clean up our own lives, we can, little by little, start helping to clean up our world\. We can learn to use less, reuse what we have, and recycle what we don’t use\. We might pick up a piece of litter and put it in the trash\. That’s a humble thing to do, but through this humble action we invite the karis of God into our lives\. Learn how you might help clean up the earth\. Just as you would start to clean up your own life by taking one small step, choose one small action that will help restore the Creation, and then turn that action into a mindful practice\. It might be your mission to prevent cruelty to other creatures or to help clean up our water, food, and air\. It’s all spiritual work if done in partnership with God and through the True Self\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Creator, show me a small step that will help heal Your Creation\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”\) * __0:30 SHARING__ __1:00 BIBLE TEACHING__ We might make KF Confession 11 one of our goals for this year: We take responsibility for any damage that we have done\. Let’s look at __Romans 8:16–23__\. This is Nancy’s translation, with a little paraphrase for clarity\. 16The Spirit Himself is a witness with our spirit that we are the children of God\. 17If children, we are heirs—heirs indeed of God\! And not only that, but fellow\-heirs with Christ, so we suffer with Him and jointly glorify Him, revealing His nature through our suffering\. 18And with that understanding, I consider that whatever suffering there may be at this present moment is not even worth evaluating compared to the glory that God intends to reveal in us\. 19We are creatures living in a material world, and that material world fully expects, and even eagerly anticipates, the revelation of the sons of God\. 20For the Creation was put on hold, not by choice, but by the one who subjected it, in the hope 21that the Creation itself will also be set free from slavery to deterioration and released into the liberty of the real glory of the children of God\. 22For we know that up to this time, we, with the whole Creation, groan and suffer as if in the pains of childbirth—23not just as sufferers, but rather as those who, groaning within themselves as in the labor of birth, produce the firstfruits of the Spirit\. We wait patiently and purposefully to be made sons, when our whole person will be ransomed and unified\. Take a deep breath\. In this passage, Paul teaches us that the whole point of our suffering in this life is to reveal our glory as heirs of God together with our Lord Jesus\. When we choose to productively endure suffering, God can reveal through us the character of Jesus and the glory of our True Self\. Together with the rest of Creation, we are suffering from the natural pain of birth as we move into the position of power and authority prepared for the sons and heirs of God\. Every aspect of the Creation eagerly anticipates our coming and the revelation of our glory\. When we become the people God intended us to be, the whole Creation will be liberated with us\. We and this material world labor together in the real hope that one day everything about us will be ransomed and made whole\. Paul teaches that the Creation, with its material limitations, is actually supporting us in this process\. By cooperating with the real limitations, cycles, and design of the Creation, we make use of the support that the Creation offers to us rather than struggling against that support\. We waste so much energy fighting our birth because in our misorientation we hate any process that we cannot control\. We want to live our lives as immature womb\-children, so we refuse to learn to trust God and are unwilling to submit to His training\. We have already decided how life should be and who we want to be, and we are averse to going into the not\-knowing where we might experience some suffering\. Right now, we are still in the process of birth\. We do not yet see what we can become, but we have hope—just as God has hope—that if we participate in this process, we will all get to find out who we were meant to be\. Think of the Creation, which includes your origins, body, and personality, as an ally, a friend who supports you in your birth\. The limitations and seeming oppositions of the Creation are actually helping to move you toward your destiny—the destiny of becoming a son of God with all the rights of a son’s inheritance\. Yes, this process is difficult, just as childbirth is difficult, but the oriented outcome is the regeneration of an independent, glorious, and powerful creature—YOU\! You are the son who has chosen this training and is preparing for the delights and responsibilities of the glorious authority that belongs to the heirs of God\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Father, train me to enter into my inheritance with joy\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”\) * __1:10 INTEGRATION__ Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes\. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Here is our integration focus: *Consider entering into the delights and responsibilities of your inheritance\. \(Repeat\) \(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __The FAITH Process__ __Feelings__ As you *consider* *entering into the delights and responsibilities of your inheritance*, how does it feel? *\(Pause\) *Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you\. They can often be uncomfortable\. *\(Pause\) *Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __Awareness without judgment__ Allow your experience to rest in your awareness\. Step back and observe whatever you may be experiencing as you *consider entering into your inheritance*\. *\(Pause\) *Feelings and passing thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are\. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Inquiry: What is my body saying?__ Bring your attention to your body and notice what it is doing when you *consider* *entering into your inheritance\. *What sensations are there? *\(Pause\) *Your body is always talking to you\. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe\. For example, you might recognize what joy or despair feels like in your body\. Breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Talk to Jesus__ You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you *consider* *entering into the delights and responsibilities of your inheritance*\. Do you feel comfortable or uncomfortable with this idea, or perhaps confused or dismayed? Just observe\. *\(Pause\)* Do you judge delight or responsibility as good or evil? *\(Pause\) *When you think about this inheritance, what limitations or lack of limitations do you imagine? *\(Pause\)* Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath or the Dragon Breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Heal__ As you breathe, repeat the word *Welcome*\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* *\(Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement\) * - Welcome this opportunity to explore the hope of your inheritance in Christ\. - Welcome the gentle Holy Spirit, who desires to train you for that inheritance\. - Welcome your present reality—where you are today and what your potential might be\. - Welcome what you are learning about yourself\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self\. On the exhale, let go\.[\[3\]](#endnote-3) *\(Pause for 5 seconds after each statement\)* - As I am trained for my inheritance, I let go of the craving for power and control\. - As I am trained for my inheritance, I let go of the craving for esteem and affection\. - As I am trained for my inheritance, I let go of the craving for security and superiority\. - As I am trained for my inheritance, I let go of the craving for perfection\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* *\(Optional\) *Continue to breathe while I test for further integration\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”\) * __1:28 ENDING PRAYER__ Dear Father and Creator, Thank You for inviting us to train together to receive our inheritance\. Hold us in the power of this new understanding as You guide us to our real glory and to all that You intended us to be\. Help us co\-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to further our connection with our true glory, with our mission, with the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus\. Amen\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”\) * __1:29 ANNOUNCEMENTS __ The KF training cycle begins again in March\. If you would like to join us for the next cycle, please register now on the website\. If you know people who have graduated from the book study within the last year and have either not joined or dropped out of the Fellowships, you might wish to invite them to register for KF again\. Simply let them know, as a courtesy and a gift, that the new cycle is due to begin\. If they are interested in KF training, you might help them register on the website\. 1. “Let go, relax, and know that I am God” \(Psalm 46:10\)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-1) 2. [www\.youtube\.com/watch?v=ihJAJA4ibEs](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ihJAJA4ibEs)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-2) 3. [www\.camillecaldwell\.com/WelcomePrayer\.html](http://www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html)\. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven\. [↑](#endnote-ref-3)

title: KF50 Meeting
content: KF50 Meeting Version of Teachings Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity\. “Search me, O God, and know my heart\. Examine me and know my thoughts\. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity\.” \(Psalm 139:23–24\) __0:01 OPENING__ __0:02 PRESENTING__ __0:06 KARIS CIRCULATION__ __0:07 GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS__ __0:08 MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING__ KF Confession 12 is the heartbeat of our redeemed life in Christ: We circulate our true resources, reconnecting to our Creator and to the Creation\. We are approaching the end of the Karis Fellowships training cycle\. You might like to review the meditation and mindfulness methods that we have practiced and choose one that works for you\. Pursue your meditation practice diligently\. You will gain the greatest benefits if you practice for at least twenty minutes in the morning and twenty minutes later in the day\. You may wish to practice the same method for one year, or you may wish to practice the method offered in the lesson\. It’s your meditation practice\. Do whatever works for you\. This month we will practice a meditation called __Waiting on the Lord__\. This meditation blends easily with other meditation practices or it can stand alone\. In this lesson, we will briefly prepare using __Alternate__ __Nostril Breathing__ and the __Sunlight Meditation__\. Take a meditation posture\. Straighten your neck and lower your chin a little\. Imagine that your spine is like a radio tower, with the pole of your head reaching toward the heavens and your tailbone reaching toward the earth\. Gently close your eyes and begin with two minutes of __Alternate Nostril Breathing__\. *\(Pause for 2 minutes\)* Pause, and allow your shoulders to drop back into a relaxed position\. Scan and observe your body\. Do you notice any tightness or pain? Breathe, and release with the exhale any tension in your body\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * Now, with eyelids gently closed, lift your eyes and imagine the sun or a lamp shining onto your forehead\. Breathe\. Imagine that you are looking through your forehead into the light and that the light is pouring into your face as you breathe\. *\(Pause for 1 minute\)* At some point, perhaps later if not right now, you might imagine that you are gazing into the face of Jesus or into the glory of God\. For one minute, just breathe and gaze while you wait before the Lord\. *\(Pause for 1 minute\)* Pause, and gently open your eyes\. Take a deep breath and return to the meeting\. Our hymn for this meditation is *Be Thou My Vision*\. Be Thou my Wisdom and Thou my true Word, I ever with Thee and Thou with me, Lord; Thou my great Father, I Thy true son; Thou in me dwelling, and I with Thee one\.[\[1\]](#endnote-1) When you practice this meditation, you might also consider Isaiah 40:31\. But those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength; They shall mount up with wings like eagles; They shall run and not be weary; They shall walk and not faint\. God promises these great benefits to those who learn to wait on Him\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”\)* __0:20 KARIS CONFESSION__ __0:21 TOOLBOX__ Let’s listen again to our final KF Confession of purpose and mission__:__ We circulate our true resources, reconnecting to our Creator and to the Creation\. Last month, we talked about taking responsibility for the damage we have done\. Now, we can learn to co‑labor with God to redeem our debts and give back what we have stolen\. We can also give karis gifts that help repair damage we did not cause\. By circulating gifts, we help God heal not only ourselves but also this world\. What does it mean to circulate gifts? The gifts that we give come out of the storehouse of our true resources\. God designed each of us to have our own supply of resources, but in our misorientation we refuse to access and develop them\. Through our efforts toward orientation, we discover that we have much more to give than we realized\. The Idol cannot be generous with its resources\. It is not self\-sustaining, nor is it connected to the Creation, so it must crave and snatch to support itself\. Our True Self, however, flows in harmony and correspondence with the Creation, giving and receiving as naturally as we breathe and as the tide flows\. When we are oriented, we let go in order to receive, and in this way we nourish and circulate our own life force\. Just as our heart pumps blood through our bodies, so we pump the energetic flow of the Creation; as a result, we thrive\. We are the heart that keeps the Creation circulating, so the moment that we hoard or grab, the heart of the Creation stops beating\. It takes effort and training to learn to pump efficiently and with joy, so particularly at the beginning of your work, you might feel like you are making a lot of effort but only gaining small benefits\. In past lessons we talked about damage in terms of debt\. If your immediate outcomes seem like a poor return on the hard work that you are investing, you are simply experiencing the evidence that you are still deep in debt\. The deeper you are in debt, the longer it will take to produce discernible, oriented results\. It takes time and a great deal of effort just to begin the process of orienting your life, and it takes even more time and effort, as well as developed CORE muscles, to effect beneficial changes in the material world\. As you continue to be courageous and oriented, live in reality, and practice endurance, you will see increasing evidence of powerful and positive change in your life\. Whenever we try to use our newly acquired skills and benefits to actualize the unfulfilled dreams of our idealized glory, energetic circulation stagnates\. If, however, we focus on the next step in the dance of life, forgetting all that we have formerly relied upon to support our pride, we are carried along in the harmonious and oriented flow of Creation\. With our hearts set on winning the race, we press forward to discover our potential in Christ\.[\[2\]](#endnote-2) Our True Self grows stronger when we circulate today, and it atrophies when we are satisfied with our stories of yesterday’s generosity, miracles, or judgments\. Our natural habitat is a place of circulation where we receive and let go, today, in the flow\.[\[3\]](#endnote-3) The flow of karis circulation is exactly like dancing with a partner\. If you have ever tried to learn the waltz, you know that the first steps can feel awkward\. When the music starts flowing, you can barely keep up\. You courageously endure the shame of stepping on someone else’s toes and the pain of presenting your own toes to be stepped on\. Then, after a great deal of practice, you suddenly catch the music and are able to dance\. You feel exquisite joy over your brief accomplishment and are momentarily distracted by euphoria\. You might even stop dancing so that you can take some pride in your accomplishment, but in doing so, you disconnect from the present moment\. The music flows on, but you have stopped dancing\. You have allowed prideful attachment to your achievements or fear of failure to interfere with the next step\. You cannot cling to old things and, at the same time, flow into new opportunities\. Your goal is to enjoy the present moment of harmony and then allow it to disappear into the joy of the next moment of harmony\. With practice, your whole life becomes a series of joyful dance steps that follow the music of the flow\. As you allow one step to pass, you turn your attention to the next step and experience the unique harmony that it brings\.[\[4\]](#endnote-4) There is no hoarding or clinging; if you want to stay in the dance, you have to let go\. You have to let go of former glory, and you also have to forgive yourself for not making the grade\. If, however, you are struggling to let go of the pride of past achievements and the self\-hate of former failures, be compassionate toward yourself\. It takes time and effort to learn new skills and to train your CORE muscles so that you can dance\. Whenever you use energy to nurse resentment and maintain grudges, you are hoarding energy that is intended to flow\. Forgiveness releases misoriented energy and circulates a gift\. Jesus told us to bless our enemies rather than resenting them because He wants us to gain the benefits of circulation\. When you forgive, you allow misoriented energy to go back to whoever is responsible for it\. You are then free to joyfully embrace your next step\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Great Teacher of the flow, I want to learn how to dance\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”\)* __0:30 SHARING__ __1:00 BIBLE TEACHING__ KF Confession 12 is the law of Christ’s kingdom and our path to real glory: We circulate our true resources, reconnecting to our Creator and to the Creation\. Let’s look at Nancy’s translation of __Luke 6:31–38__\. In this passage, Jesus is teaching His followers the principle of karis circulation\. 31And just as you want people to do to you, do the same to them\. 32If you show agape love to those who love you, what karis is that to you? Look at it this way: even misoriented people love those who love them\. 33And if you do good to those who do good to you, what karis is it to you? Even misoriented people do that\. 34And if you lend to those from whom you hope or expect to receive, what karis is it to you? Even the misoriented lend to the misoriented in order to receive the same things in return\. 35Instead, love your enemies and do good and lend, expecting nothing from them in return\. Then your reward will be abundant, and you will be revealed as the sons of the Most High, your Father, because He does active good and is kind to those who are hurtful and against karis\. 36Become merciful, just as your Father is merciful and has pity\. 37Do not judge, and you will in no way be judged\. Also, do not condemn, and you will not be condemned\. Release, and you will be released\. 38Give, and others will give into your open arms a true measure, already pressed down, already shaken and running over\. This is how it works: in whatever proportion you measure out your resources, the same proportion will be measured back to you\. Take a deep breath\. Jesus begins His teaching about karis by reminding His disciples of what is often called the Golden Rule: “Do for others what you want them to do for you\.”[\[5\]](#endnote-5) Give in proportion to your MATH­—your money, abilities, time, and health\. Learn to open your arms, and then watch for the response from others, from the Creation, and from God\. Learn to trust\. Karis is more than being kind to those who have already shown kindness to you\. Karis requires the ingredient of trust\. If you show kindness to those who have shown kindness to you, you do not have to trust them to return a benefit; you have already received a benefit\. Similarly, if you lend or give to another person with the expectation of a particular return, you are not in a trusting karis relationship; you are in a contract based on the law of mutual expectations\. Contracts are necessary in the market economy, and people set them up because they don’t trust each other\. A contract is intended to bind another person and exact a premeditated return\. If you do something for someone else and then feel disappointed with their response, you know that you have an expectation\. You are not in karis; you are in a contract\. Oriented people look forward to what returns to them in karis circulation\. They confidently anticipate that God and others will respond with invitations to build relationships of deeper trust, leading to greater opportunities\. Can you see how increased trust brings more freedom, not only to you but also to the whole community? Poised for the next joyful step, oriented people continue to practice A\-S\-A\-P—Ask, Simplify, Adventure, Prioritize\. Every gift they give is an adventure and an exploration of gratitude\. They throw their gift into the flow and then watch to see what happens\. Karis relationships are built on trust and mutual generosity\. God invites you into karis relationship by giving you a great gift—the restoration of your soul—and by returning a gift, you invite God into more relationship\. If you want a karis relationship with anyone, you have to respond with gifts that are proportionate to your MATH and to your gratitude\.__ __Your response is a gift that says, “I value my relationship with you, not the return I expect from you\.” When you see how others respond, you learn a lot about the quality of your relationships, and you find out how much others value you\. Whenever you give out of karis, you go into the not‑knowing\. You can always trust that there will be a response to your gift, but you cannot know what that response will be, and in karis you do not attach to an expectation of what it should be\. When gifts are returned, you become so rich within your True Self and in your relationship with God and others that you would rather bless your enemies than hold grudges against them\.[\[6\]](#endnote-6) Forgiveness and letting go become natural and easy in the rich flow of circulation\. Holding a grudge is like refusing to dance because someone has stepped on your toe\. Oriented people would rather dance\. Jesus is showing you in this passage that you are too rich to live like those who demand that others reciprocate in a certain way\. Misoriented people can only go as far as exchanging mutual expectations\. Their demands are based on law and contract, not on karis\. Contracts and law are based on distrust; the purpose of karis, however, is to build trust\. All of us are afraid to trust, and that makes karis a lot scarier and more challenging, but only karis can reveal the glory of God and the real glory of you\. In karis, we give because of who we are—the sons of the Most High, who have an inheritance in this world and in the next\. We give to see what will happen, knowing that all of our giving is ultimately a gift to God in karis response to all that God has given to us\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Lord Jesus, teach me to let go and get in the flow\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”\)* __1:10 INTEGRATION__ Sip some purified water and prepare to take a few notes\. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Here is our integration focus: *Consider letting go of something, perhaps a grudge or a gift\. \(Repeat\) \(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __The FAITH Process__ __Feelings__ As you *consider letting go of something, perhaps a grudge or a gift*, how does it feel? *\(Pause\) *Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you\. They can often be uncomfortable\. *\(Pause\) *Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __Awareness without judgment__ Gently hold in your awareness whatever you may be experiencing when you *consider letting go*\. You might notice a compulsion to justify or to simply dismiss thoughts and feelings\. Try to hold your experience up to the light and mindfully observe whatever you may be experiencing\. Breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Inquiry: What is my body saying?__ Breathe, and bring your attention to your body\. Notice what it is doing as you *consider letting go of something, perhaps a grudge or a gift\. *What sensations are there? *\(Pause\) *Your body is always talking to you\. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe\. For example, you might recognize what greed, offended pride, fear, or release feels like in your body\. Breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Talk to Jesus__ You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you *consider* *letting go of something\.* Does that feel comfortable or uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe\. *\(Pause\)* Does the thought of letting go of this thing feel good or bad? *\(Pause\) *What are your reasons? What story do you want to tell? *\(Pause\)* What do you fear or hope for? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Heal __ As you breathe, repeat the word *Welcome*\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* *\(Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement\) * - Welcome this opportunity to explore what you might let go\. - Welcome the gentle Holy Breath of truth, who wants to teach you how to circulate\. - Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made\. - Welcome what you are learning about yourself\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self\. On the exhale, let go\.[\[7\]](#endnote-7) *\(Pause for 5 seconds after each statement\)* - As I learn to circulate, I let go of the craving to hoard and control\. - As I learn to circulate, I let go of the craving to support and defend myself\. - As I learn to circulate, I let go of the craving for security and self\-sufficiency\. - As I learn to circulate, I let go of the craving for idealized glory\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* *\(Optional\) *Continue to breathe while I test for further integration\. Pause\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”\)* __1:28 ENDING PRAYER__ Dear Father and Creator, Thank You for drawing us together to train and to heal\. Hold us in the power of circulation as You guide us to our true glory\. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we co\-labor with You to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to further our connection with our True Self and design, with our community and the rest of Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus\. Amen\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”\)* __1:29 ANNOUNCEMENTS__ The spring KF training cycle always starts in March\. If you are interested in joining the next KF training cycle, please register now on the website\. New NHG graduates will be joining us, and you might pray for them as they make this transition\. If you have invited someone to the NHG Study, please plan to support them by attending the upcoming KF Introductory Meeting\. Thank you for all your efforts to live in karis with Karis Fellowships\. 1.
