Heb\. 3:13\. [↑](#endnote-ref-3) 4. 2 Cor\. 5:17\. [↑](#endnote-ref-4) 5. [en\.wikipedia\.org/wiki/Golden\_Rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Rule)\. [↑](#endnote-ref-5) 6. Luke 6:28, 35\. [↑](#endnote-ref-6) 7. [www\.camillecaldwell\.com/WelcomePrayer\.html](http://www.camillecaldwell.com/WelcomePrayer.html)\. Adapted for Karis Fellowships by Nancy Diven\. [↑](#endnote-ref-7)

title: KF51 Meeting
content: KF51 Meeting Version of Teachings Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity\. “Search me, O God, and know my heart\. Examine me and know my thoughts\. See if there is any way in me that causes pain, and lead me in the ways of eternity\.” \(Psalm 139:23–24\) __0:01 OPENING__ __0:02 PRESENTING__ __0:06 KARIS CIRCULATION__ We always begin the next Karis Fellowships training cycle in March\. Everyone who wishes to continue with KF must register in order to have access to the KF website and community\. If you haven’t registered already, take a minute right now to register, either on the KF website or through the link in your email\. Let’s just pause and breathe while members register\. *\(Pause 1 minute\)* Registering now will remove a burden from the hard\-working KF admin team and will also keep you connected to the website\. If KF admin does not receive your registration, the system will disconnect you and move you to the “inactive” list\. __0:07 GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS__ __0:08 MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING__ When we practice KF Confession 12, our trust in the karis relationship with God grows: We circulate our true resources, reconnecting to our Creator and to the Creation\. Scientific research attests the benefits of mindfulness training and meditation\. Hundreds of studies have shown that these practices strengthen our immune system, increase mental focus, promote a sense of well\-being, and decrease symptoms of depression and anxiety\.[\[1\]](#endnote-1) Meditation, in particular, improves self\-esteem and fosters self\-acceptance, leading to greater esteem and acceptance of others\.[\[2\]](#endnote-2) You can imagine how these benefits improve your ability to productively manage your relationship with yourself and with others—and even your relationship with God\. Our practice for this month is __Waiting on the Lord__\. The goal of this meditation is to learn to wait, simply wait, before the Lord\. You might feel that this is a waste of time and wonder, “What is this waiting doing for the Lord? What is it doing for me? Doesn’t God want me to get up, get on with my work, fix the world, and become glorious?” Yet there are many verses in the Bible that encourage us to learn to wait on God\. John Milton, the great 17th century English poet, wrote his extraordinary epic poem, *Paradise Lost,* after he had lost his sight\. Blindness could have destroyed his career as a writer and, also, could have restricted his contribution to the community\. So, how did he manage such a crushing limitation? He managed his limitation and even thrived because he knew this truth: God is not interested in our search for an imagined glory; He is interested in teaching us to wait on Him and trust\. Listen to these words written by John Milton: “Doth God exact day\-labor, light denied?” I fondly ask\. But Patience to prevent that murmur soon replies: “God doth not need either man’s work or His own gifts; Who bear His mild yoke, they serve Him best\. His state is kingly\. Thousands at His bidding speed and post o’er land and ocean without rest\. They also serve who only stand and wait\.”[\[3\]](#endnote-3) Take a deep breath\. “They also serve who only stand and wait\.” When things don’t go our way, the struggle to be patient is just as difficult for us today as it was for Christians hundreds of years ago\. When light or clear direction is denied, our human tendency is to be discontent\. We want to fight our limitations because we imagine that they restrict our happiness and potential and interfere with our service to God\. Developed patience does not murmur against God, however\. It understands that in waiting—in exercising patience—we also serve\. We may not become famous poets, but by learning to wait productively, we choose to trust the creative power of the Holy Spirit, who is able, even in our present darkness, to reveal the glory of God\. __Waiting on the Lord__ Assume a meditation posture\. With your head reaching toward the heavens and your tailbone reaching toward the earth, close your eyes and begin with one minute of __Alternate Nostril Breathing__\. *\(Pause for 1 minute\)* Pause, and allow your shoulders and arms to drop into a relaxed position\. Now, as you breathe, observe your body\. Can you allow your muscles to relax and release tension? Breathe, and invite your body to let go with the exhale\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* Keeping your eyes closed, look up at the inside of your forehead\. Imagine that you are looking into a light that is pouring into your face\. *\(Pause\)* As you inhale, you might explore pulling energy up from the earth through your tailbone, filling the spinal column and brain\. Then, as you exhale, allow the energy to drain back into the earth\. Practice for one minute\. *\(Pause for 1 minute\)* At some point, you might imagine that you are gazing into the face of Jesus or into the glory of God\. Just silently absorb, wait, and breathe for one minute\. *\(Pause for 1 minute\)* Pause, and gently open your eyes\. Take a deep breath and re\-engage with the meeting\. Our hymn for the last month of our training is *Be Thou My Vision*\. Be Thou my battle Shield, Sword for the fight; Be Thou my Dignity, Thou my Delight; Thou my soul’s Shelter, Thou my high Tower: Raise Thou me heavenward, O Power of my power\.[\[4\]](#endnote-4) Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”\)* __0:20 KARIS CONFESSION__ __0:21 TOOLBOX__ Last week, we touched on the idea of flow\. When we start living from our True Self and are able to maintain our connection to the Creator and the Creation, karis gifts begin to flow toward us\. Our response is to send gifts back out into the Creation\. By doing so, we keep the karis connection with our Creator circulating and flowing\. This is a very exciting, surprising, and fascinating process through which we build a relationship with God based on gratitude and trust\. Everything that you have is a gift from God, and when you respond by returning gifts to God, you pump the energetic flow of the Creation\. Perhaps in last week’s meeting you understood something of the purpose and promise of living in the flow of circulation\. Just like in a dance, we accomplish one step with joy and then immediately give ourselves to the next step without any judgment about how it should be or what we should receive in return\. Without doubt, our energy has been damaged by the misorientation of others\. However, acting like a human filtering system, we can cleanse that misoriented energy through our lives and choices and return oriented energy to the Creation\. As a friend of God in karis relationship, you become the means of liberating others; you conquer injury with active good\.[\[5\]](#endnote-5) One way of doing this is to circulate the gift of forgiveness\. You forgive by letting go of the debt that you hold against yourself or against others—and, also, any debt that in your misorientation you hold against God\. God sends rain on both the oriented and the misoriented, and when you walk in orientation and forgiveness, flowing in the freedom of your relationship with Him, you too will send rain on both the oriented and the misoriented, watering every thirsty soul that you touch\.[\[6\]](#endnote-6) In the flow of circulation, there are seasons of giving and seasons of guarding, so it’s important to learn when to let go and when to hold on\. Hoarding any area of the MATH—whether money, abilities, time, or health—supports the Idol and cuts off circulation\. That is called greed\. On the other hand, indiscriminately scattering your MATH exhausts your resources\. That is called dissipation\. Those resources are then no longer available for oriented circulation\. There is misorientation, and there is wisdom\. Misorientation serves our fears and seeks to save our pride\. Oriented wisdom serves love and seeks to bring everything into harmony\. When we circulate wisely, we invest in lives and situations that are moving toward orientation\. Prudent giving is a component of karis\. Perhaps you are learning to give with discretion and not out of compulsion\. A budget can help you give wisely despite your compulsive feelings\. Budgets honor your limitations, help you set priorities, protect you from compulsive giving or hoarding, and make provision for authentic generosity\. You can then confidently develop the habit of watching for opportunities to support others who are making an effort to be on God’s team\. By supporting such people, you support God, and by supporting God, you support yourself\. As you practice A\-S\-A\-P—Ask, Simplify, Adventure, Prioritize—and adjust to what you learn in your experiments, you will stop frittering away the gifts of your MATH on instant gratification and image management\. Frittering is a way of avoiding your true glory and mission\. Learn to see where the energy is flowing and use your gifts to get on board\. How are you circulating your MATH? How do you feel when called upon to offer your MATH without any expectation of personal return? How do you feel when you choose not to give? What are your principles of circulation? What priorities guide your giving? In our next lesson, we will look at some principles of circulation that may help you establish your priorities\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Show me today where You are working, Lord, so that I might offer a karis gift to You\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”\)* __0:30 SHARING__ Next week will be our last lesson in the KF cycle and traditionally, during the presenting time, members share how they support their community or what they do for a living\. You might also prepare for the sharing time by reviewing your Meeting Preparation Guides and highlighting a few of the beneficial changes you have experienced this past year\. __1:00 BIBLE TEACHING__ The purpose of the KF Confessions and our training is to lead us to the new level of trust expressed in KF Confession 12: We circulate our true resources, reconnecting to our Creator and to the Creation\. Let’s read __First Peter 4:1–11 __in Nancy’s translation, which includes a little paraphrase for clarity\. This passage summarizes the goal of our training\. 1Therefore, since Christ has suffered in the material experience, arm yourselves also, like soldiers, with the same understanding, because those who suffer in the material experience have made an end of misorientation\. 2They are therefore able to live the rest of their time in the material existence no longer reacting to the compelling needs and cravings of humanity but, instead, responding to the desires of God\. 3Look at it this way: In your former life, you spent plenty of time working hard to achieve the goals of misoriented people while those same people made you bear wanton violence toward yourself and others\. They encouraged you to live egocentric lives filled with unexamined longings, unrestrained addictive behaviors, mindless gratifications, and all the activities of serving and worshipping your own Idol Self and theirs\. 4They are now surprised and think you very strange because you no longer choose to run with them into the same wasteful enthusiasms, which by their character and outcomes slander God\. 5They will give an account of their actions to the One who carries the responsibility and is also ready to judge the living and the dead\. 6This is how it works: the good news is preached even to those who are dead so that the quality of their choices can be revealed and examined\. They are dead according to the flesh of humanity, but the good news is told even to those who are dead so that they might live according to the Spirit of God\. 7For the fulfillment of all things is near\. Therefore, come to your senses; be mindful and not drunk in your prayers\. 8Above all, exercise agape love purposefully and intentionally among yourselves, because agape covers much misorientation\. 9Be hospitable to one another without grumbling about it\. 10Since you have received a gift from God, be like excellent household stewards and circulate that gift by serving each other\. Karis giving is beautiful and intricate, like an embroidered work of many colors\. 11If one of you has something to say, speak with mindful consideration as if you were speaking an oracle of God\. If one of you serves or ministers, don’t do it to indulge the pride and the illusions of the Idol’s imagined glory, but do it out of the strength that God supplies so that as we express Jesus Christ in this world, God may be glorified in everything and in every way, to Whom is the glory and the mastery forever and forever\. Amen\. Take a deep breath\. The main point of this passage is this: productive suffering is part of the process of learning to effectively circulate\. When we suffer, we learn to endure, and our endurance produces character that is mature, complete, and lacks nothing\.[\[7\]](#endnote-7) If we lack nothing, we have the freedom to circulate\. If you choose to follow Jesus, you can expect to suffer; suffering will always accompany your move toward orientation\. You are in a birthing process, and through productive suffering you learn to cooperate with your own birth\. You have spent plenty of time fulfilling the compulsive strivings of your culture and background, and these strivings have caused you to suffer unproductively\. It is now time for you to live in the oriented flow of new birth\. The energy of this flow is agape love, which is manifested in how we interact as a karis community\. We interact by offering to each other the gifts that God has given to us, and this giving weaves together a beautiful and intricate environment that nurtures and supports our healing and our growth\. This wholesome environment is not something we can enforce or control with legal systems, and that’s why it baffles those around us who have not yet come alive in karis\. It’s time to stop trying to save your Idol’s life by defending and maintaining your pride system\. When you humbly participate in karis circulation, you are circulating with God\. You are on His side\. Through this circulation, God’s generous and magnanimous attributes are displayed to a stagnant and fearful world, inviting those who live there to reconnect with their Creator\. Everyone has gifts to give, and if you are giving and receiving encouragement and giving and receiving gifts, you are in the flow of karis circulation\. Everything you do as an expression of karis honors and glorifies your Creator\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Great Giver of karis gifts, help me get into the flow of Your circulation\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”\)* __1:10 INTEGRATION__ Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes\. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Here is our integration focus: *Consider stepping into the karis flow\. \(Repeat\)* *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __The FAITH Process__ __Feelings__ As you *consider* ­*stepping into the karis flow*, how does it feel? *\(Pause\) *Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you\. They can sometimes be uncomfortable\. *\(Pause\) *You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you\. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __Awareness without judgment__ Gently allow your experience to rest in your awareness\. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them\. Observe without judgment whatever thoughts or feelings go by as you *consider stepping into the karis flow*,* *and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Inquiry: What is my body saying?__ Breathe and bring your attention to your body\. Notice what it is doing when you *consider* *stepping into the karis flow\. *What sensations are you experiencing? *\(Pause\) *You might recognize what curiosity, the fear of loss, or the fear of losing control feels like in your body\. Breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Talk to Jesus__ You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you *consider* *stepping into the karis flow\. *Do you judge the karis flow as good or evil, interesting or scary? *\(Pause\)* What do you believe when you consider stepping into the flow? What story do you want to tell? *\(Pause\)* What area of trust in God might you explore? What scares you or bothers you about karis? *\(Pause\)* Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Heal__ As you breathe, repeat the word *Welcome*\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* *\(Pause for 8 seconds or one long breath after each statement\) * - Welcome this opportunity to explore the circulation of living in faith\. - Welcome the Holy Breath, who is constantly circulating\. - Welcome your present reality and the progress you have made\. - Welcome what you are learning about yourself\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Now, as you breathe, you might use the following statements as a confession to the Lord and turn away from the Idol Self\. On the exhale, let go\.[\[8\]](#endnote-8) *\(Pause for 5 seconds after each statement\) * - As I step into the karis flow, I let go of the craving to control my future\. - As I step into the karis flow, I let go of the craving to support my self\-esteem\. - As I step into the karis flow, I let go of the craving for predictable comfort and safety\. - As I step into the karis flow, I let go of the craving to have things go my way\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * *\(Optional\) *Continue to breathe while I test for further integration\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”\)* __1:28 ENDING PRAYER__ Dear Father and Creator, Thank You for drawing us together to train our trust and heal our fears\. Sustain us as we explore the terrors of karis flow while You guide us to our goal\. Lead us to the next step in our healing this week as we respond to Your invitation to orient our lives to karis and to strengthen our trust in You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus\. Amen\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”\) * __1:29 ANNOUNCEMENTS__ We always begin the next Karis Fellowships training cycle in March\. Everyone who wishes to continue with KF must register in order to have access to the website\. If you have invited someone to the NHG Study, please plan to support them by attending the upcoming KF Introductory Meeting\. 1. title: KF52 Meeting
content: KF52 Meeting Version of Teachings Karis is an invitation to a relationship based on mutual generosity\. This is our KF prayer using Nancy’s Bible translation: “Examine me, O God, and discover my heart\. Run experiments on me and become intimate with my fearful thoughts\. See if there is any hurtful or idolatrous way in me, and lead me in the ways of eternity\.” \(Psalm 139:23–24\) __0:01 OPENING__ __0:02 PRESENTING__ In this last meeting of the training cycle, we would all like to get an idea of what God is doing in the world through you\. Traditionally, during the presenting time, we each briefly share what we do for a living and how we support the wider community\. Feel free to pass, if you wish\. __0:06 KARIS CIRCULATION__ Everyone who wishes to continue to have access to the KF website must re\-register\. Completing your registration now will keep you connected to the website and remove a burden from the hard\-working KF admin team\. If KF admin does not receive your registration, the system will disconnect you and move you to the “inactive” list\. __0:07 GUIDELINES & LIMITATIONS__ __0:08 MINDFULNESS & MEDITATION TRAINING__ Sit or stand with the crown of your head reaching toward the heavens and your tailbone reaching toward the earth\. Begin with __Alternate Nostril Breathing__ for one minute\. *\(Pause for 1 minute\)* Now, allow your shoulders and arms to drop into a relaxed position\. As you breathe, observe your body\. Are there any areas of tension that you might allow to rest? *\(Pause\) *Breathe, and let your body soften on the exhale\. Relax your face\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __Waiting on the Lord__ With your eyes closed, imagine that you are looking through your forehead and into the light\. Imagine that the light is pouring into your eyes\. As you inhale, you might explore pulling energy up from the earth through your tailbone, filling your spinal column\. As you exhale, allow the energy to drain back into the earth\. Practice for one minute\. *\(Pause for 1 minute\) * At some point, perhaps right now, you might imagine that you are gazing into the face of Jesus, or into the glory of God\. Just silently absorb and breathe for one minute\.* \(Pause for 1 minute\) * Continue to breathe as you listen to these verses from Psalm 36 in Nancy’s translation: 8They drink their fill from the overflow of Your house, And You give them to drink from the river of Your delights\. 9For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light\. 10O continue Your kindness to those who know You, And Your faithfulness to the oriented heart\.[\[1\]](#endnote-1) Pause, and gently open your eyes\. Take a deep breath and re\-engage with the meeting\. *\(Pause\)* Our hymn for this last confession is *Be Thou My Vision\.* High King of Heaven, my victory won; May I reach Heaven’s joys, O bright Heaven’s Sun\! Heart of my own heart, whatever befall, Still be my Vision, O Ruler of all\.[\[2\]](#endnote-2) Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this training?”\)* __0:20 KARIS CONFESSION__ __0:21 TOOLBOX__ Let’s listen once again to our final KF Confession: We circulate our true resources, reconnecting to our Creator and to the Creation\. In these last few lessons, we have introduced the idea of flow\. As we circulate our true resources, we keep the flow moving\. We learned in KF30 that there are two levels of karis\. At the first level, we lay the foundation of trust, which is necessary for any karis relationship\. This level has three steps\. By practicing these steps, you show God that you are serious about developing your relationship with Him and that you intend to learn to be trustworthy\. At this first level, you train to: 1. __Obey kingdom law:__ learn God’s kingdom law of orientation and obey it\. 2. __Cultivate more orientation:__ learn what orientation feels like and looks like, and mindfully act in ways that cultivate it\. 3. __Choose life:__ avoid misoriented behavior\. When you practice these oriented steps, you give a gift to God and to others, and you give your True Self a drink from the overflow of God’s house\.[\[3\]](#endnote-3) The outcome, or effect, of pursuing orientation is predictable—over time, you will create a life that is more stable, more productive, and more secure\. The second level of karis is where the adventure really begins\. You begin planting seeds with hope, but without attaching to expectations\. At this level, you learn to: 1. __Love your neighbor as yourself: __treat very well those who support you\.[\[4\]](#endnote-4) 2. __Do good to the trustworthy community:__ support members of the community who are investing in their true glory\. 3. __Act with kindness toward the world: __offer gifts of care and support to those outside the trustworthy community\.[\[5\]](#endnote-5) When we are healthier and more oriented, we are no longer driven by the fear of losing our Idol’s life and can observe events without judgment\. We mindfully acknowledge the Idol’s efforts to control us, but we refuse to participate in the damage it causes\. We remember what we really want: we want to enjoy more love and more life, and we want to be more capable of handling whatever life brings\. When we make choices oriented toward achieving those desires, we become more trustworthy\. We also learn more about God, which increases our trust, and we reveal that growing trust by courageously circulating our MATH—our money, abilities, time, and health\. We circulate and then watch with anticipation to see what God will do\. The outcome or effect of your circulation at this second level of karis is unpredictable; you cannot foresee what glorious things God will return to you\. You just start drinking from the river of His delights, and in His light you see more and more light\. You can never swallow too much of that river, and there is no end to what His light can reveal\. Circulation begins with letting go\. We stop living an egocentric life and allow our resources to flow toward a real need or a real joy\. We become someone’s neighbor\. Rather than waiting for others to give to us, we initiate the ecosystem of circulation\. We develop the empathy required to know what another person needs or what would bring them joy\. Offering joy is just as valuable as meeting a need\. Before we have time to talk ourselves out of it, we let our resources flow to that person\. We do something; when we see our chance, we act\. By letting go of our resources, we let go of trying to save the life of our Idol—we let go of meeting the compulsive needs of our pride system, and we let go of trusting the Idol’s dictates\.[\[6\]](#endnote-6) Our life then becomes evidence of our trust in God and His trust in us\. How does that work? As we learn to trust God, we develop a magnanimous heart that responds to its own opportunities to circulate\. Being magnanimous doesn’t mean that we let go of all of our MATH all of the time\. We still budget and prioritize, but we do not make our MATH another rigid legal system, so we can choose to stretch the comfort zone of our MATH to meet a need or a joy\. This demonstrates our trust in God and gives Him the opportunity to demonstrate His trustworthiness toward us\. Our choice shows God that we are trustworthy and willing to learn more trust\. This ongoing cycle of circulation with God allows resources to flow away from us, but it also allows resources to flow toward us\. When we refuse to be motivated by greed and fear, our arms are open to give and receive\. The resources of the Creation are then free to flow back and forth in a natural cycle\. By allowing the tide to go out, we invite the tide’s return\. As we invest our MATH, we gain even more\. Through entering into circulation, we experience an ever\-increasing vitality that brings with it more and more joy\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Father, I am willing to let go and get into the flow\.* *\(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Toolbox?”\)* __0:30 SHARING__ You might want to share an area of your life that has positively changed during this year of KF training\. __1:00 BIBLE TEACHING__ Every bit of guidance from the Bible, every call to love, and every declaration of your potential as a child of God is an invitation to respond with oriented action and trust\. Your response is called faith\. Faith is what it takes to fulfill the greatest commandment, which is to love God with all of our being and to love our neighbor as we would love ourselves\.[\[7\]](#endnote-7) In the passage for this lesson, a lawyer asks Jesus which commandment is the greatest\. Jesus responds with an answer that stirs up the lawyer’s self\-hate because Jesus emphasizes action, not simply knowledge\. The lawyer is proud of his scriptural knowledge, but Jesus challenges him to translate what he knows into action\. The lawyer then feels anxious and tries to justify his inaction by asserting that the commandment is too vague for anyone to follow\. He takes refuge in semantics by asking Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?” Nancy wants to point out something in this passage that might surprise you\. We are often taught that the neighbor is the one who was left for dead, the needy one\. That is not what Jesus says\. Jesus tells us that the neighbor is the one who has compassion and helps the one who has fallen into the hands of robbers\. Neighbors take action on our behalf\. The ones who take action on our behalf are the ones we are commanded to love as ourselves\. Let’s read __Luke 10:25–37__ in Nancy’s translation\. To help our understanding, Nancy has used the phrase *the one near* instead of the word *neighbor*\. 25And look, a certain expert in law stood up testing Jesus\. He said, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?” 26Jesus said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?” 27The lawyer replied, “You shall love the Lord your God out of the source of your desires, and from within your whole conscious self, your whole strength, and all of your intelligence; and you shall love the one near you as you would love yourself\.” 28Jesus said to him, “You have answered correctly\. Do this, and you will live\.” 29But the expert in law, wishing to support his pride, said to Jesus, “And who is the one near me?” 30Jesus replied, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and he fell among thieves\. They stripped off his clothes and beat him, wounding him, and then they disbanded, leaving him half\-dead\. 31By coincidence, a priest was going down the same road and saw the crime victim\. Far from going near him, he went to the opposite side of the road to pass him by\. 32A Levite who was coming down to that place also saw the wounded man and, in just the same way, passed by on the other side in order to get as far away from him as possible\. 33A Samaritan who was on a journey came upon the victim and, seeing him, felt compassion\. 34And he came near to him, bandaged his traumas, pouring upon them soothing oil and healing wine\. He lifted the man onto his own beast and, leading him to a place to rest, took an interest in him\. 35On the next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper \(the one who receives everyone\), and he said, ‘Take an interest in this man, and whatever more you spend, when I return, I myself will repay you\.’ 36Now, in your opinion, which of these three people became the one near*—*or the neighbor—to him who was overwhelmed by thieves?” 37The expert in law said, “The one who acted mercifully toward him\.” Jesus said to the lawyer, “Go on your way, and you yourself do likewise\.” Take a deep breath\. Notice that the neighbor is not the religious leader or the person who claims special spiritual authority based on antecedents\. Jesus teaches us that our neighbor is the one who comes near\. The neighbor rescues and helps us when we have been set upon by robbers who have exploited and abused us for their own gain\. We might look back on our lives and think to ourselves: “If it wasn’t for that person and their gifts to me, where would I be?” If you shudder at the thought of where you might be, then you have found your neighbor\. Your neighbors are those who extend themselves and offer their own MATH on your behalf, not because you deserve it or because you made the first gesture, but because karis neighbors know how to love\. They are the instrument of God’s love in your life\. When your neighbor offers you a karis gift, God uses that gift to invite you into deeper karis relationship with Him\. Their gift becomes God’s gift; He works through them to benefit you\. So, when you respond to your neighbor with a gift of your own, you are responding to God\. When out of gratitude you offer something costly to your neighbor, you are saying to God: “I am ready to be in a growing relationship of trust—a relationship that requires courage for adventure, an ever\-developing orientation, a commitment to reality, and new levels of endurance\. I want a relationship that will help me step up to my design and purpose, and will train me to receive my inheritance\. I am ready to declare the glory that is mine in Christ Jesus\.”* *Your neighbors are those people who take action to support you in that marvelous process of becoming God’s trustworthy friend\. How you respond to your neighbor declares to heaven your real intentions\. Offer gifts to those who have rescued and supported you, and then become a neighbor to others by taking the initiative to circulate with them\. Follow the example of the Samaritan\. Show mercy to someone who has been set upon by robbers in this misoriented and destructive culture\. Become God’s karis gift and see what happens\. Our prayer might go something like this: *Lord Jesus, I am ready to become a neighbor\. \(Repeat\)* Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the Bible teaching?”\)* __1:10 INTEGRATION__ Sip some purified water and prepare to take some notes\. Assume a meditation posture, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 10 seconds\)* Here is our integration focus: *Consider who might be your neighbor\. What could it look like to love your neighbor as yourself? \(Repeat\) \(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __The FAITH Process__ __Feelings__ As you *consider* *what it might look like to love your neighbor as yourself*, how does it feel? *\(Pause\) *Your feelings are yours to teach you about yourself, to guide you, and to train you\. They can often be uncomfortable\. *\(Pause\) *You can learn to recognize and honor your feelings without allowing them to master you\. Recognize with compassion whatever you are experiencing, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\) * __Awareness without judgment__ Allow your experience to rest in your awareness\. You might notice a compulsion to push thoughts or feelings away, to judge them, or to justify them\. We often flush our feelings and thoughts from our awareness before they have a chance to teach us\. Observe whatever tension you may be experiencing as you *consider what it might look like to love your neighbor as yourself*\. *\(Pause\) *Feelings and fleeting thoughts are not right or wrong; they just are\. Give yourself permission now to explore them without judgment, and breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Inquiry: What is my body saying?__ Breathe, and bring your attention to your body\. Notice what it is doing when you *consider* *what it might look like to love your neighbor as yourself\. *What sensations are there? *\(Pause\) *Your body is always talking to you\. You may not understand its language right now, but you can observe\. For example, you might recognize what hoarding or what curiosity feels like in your body\. Breathe\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Talk to Jesus__ You might imagine that you are leaning back in the safe and loving arms of Jesus as together you *consider* *what it might look like to love your neighbor as yourself\.* Do you feel comfortable, uncomfortable, or are you shutting down? Just observe\. *\(Pause\)* Do you judge loving your neighbor as yourself as good or, perhaps, as evil because it scares you? Like the lawyer, you may feel skeptical or defensive, or you may be full of excuses\. *\(Pause\) *What do you believe about your neighbors, those who have supported and even rescued you? Observe your responses as just information, and breathe with a long exhaling breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* __Heal __ God created us to have all of these feelings, and for thousands of years human beings have been feeling like you feel when they have *considered* *loving their neighbor as they love themselves*\. You are not alone in your feelings\. You are a human creature\. *\(Pause\) *Feelings are just chemical reactions in your body bringing you information\. With training, you can choose what you will do with that information\. *\(Pause\)* When a fear or judgment signals you through the body, you can focus on your body and your breath rather than getting caught up in a story and reacting\. Breathe, and with compassion allow your body to process this experience with a long exhaling breath\. *\(Pause for 30 seconds\)* *\(Optional\) *Continue to breathe while I test for further integration\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about the integration?”\)* __1:28 ENDING PRAYER__ Dear Father and Creator, We are very grateful for this year of training together\. Hold us in the power of this karis understanding and continue to guide us to our glory\. As we co\-labor with You, reveal the truth of who You created us to be with all of our potential in Christ\. Help us to reorient our lives for a more effective flow and to flourish in our connection with our True Self, with our community and the rest of the Creation, and with You, for the glory and honor of our Lord Jesus\. Amen\. Take a deep breath\. *\(If time permits, ask, “Does anyone have comments or questions about this meeting?”\)* __1:29 ANNOUNCEMENTS__ This is the last meeting in the Karis Fellowship training cycle\. We hope to hear your voices next week as we welcome new members into our community and begin the cycle again\. All current KF members who wish to join us, please register on the website\. 1.
